OpenAL: render 3D audio binaurally (HRTF) for headphones. Off by default: OpenAL Soft would otherwise auto-enable it on any output that reports itself as headphones, which many people hear as muffled. Takes effect after restart.

Acoustics prototype (#683): in-world sounds get a room reverb estimated from rays cast around the listener, and are muffled when a wall or the ground is between you and them. Needs ray tracing (RenderVKRayTracing on a GPU with ray queries); otherwise it does nothing. Streams, media and voice stay dry. Takes effect immediately.
Acoustics (#683): reverb (wet) level in a fully enclosed room, 0 = no reverb, 1 = full. Outdoors stays dry regardless.
Acoustics (#683): how strongly a blocked line of sight muffles a sound, 0 = never, 1 = strongest (about -7 dB overall and -20 dB at high frequencies).

Acoustics (#683): how much a blocked line of sight also muffles the sound's send to the room reverb (a sound outside a sealed room only excites it through the walls). 0 = old behaviour (blocked sounds still ring the room fully), 1 = the send is filtered like the direct path.

Acoustics (#683): tilts how absorbent rooms are judged to be, -1 = harder and livelier (longer, brighter reverb) .. 0 = as measured .. 1 = deader (shorter, warmer, quieter tail). Scales the estimated absorption by 0.35x at -1 and 2.8x at +1. Takes effect immediately.

Acoustics (#683) GPU cost: trace the 64 room-estimate rays every Nth frame (1 = every frame). Source occlusion rays still run every frame. The room estimate is smoothed over seconds, so 3 is inaudible.
Acoustics (#683) GPU cost: how far (metres) the room-estimate rays look. Rays that reach nothing within it count as open area. 60 = the original range.

Acoustics (#683) GPU cost: beyond this distance (metres) the acoustics rays count alpha-mask cut-outs (leaves, hedges, fences) as hit without reading their alpha texture (conservative: blocked). 1000 = always alpha-test (original behaviour). Alpha-blend surfaces are always tested.

Acoustics (#683): transparent surfaces block and reflect sound by what you would see -- a fully transparent face or texel lets sound through, anything even slightly visible (a window, a glass wall or roof) blocks it like glass: rooms behind glass reverberate, a glass roof is not open sky, a sound outside a closed window is muffled (less than through a wall). Alpha-mask surfaces with a hard physical material (stone / metal / glass / plastic) block as solid screens; other alpha-mask surfaces stay soft foliage. Off = alpha-blend geometry is ignored by the acoustics rays (previous behaviour). Takes effect immediately.

Acoustics (#857): every in-world sound gets its own room estimate (rays cast around the sound), so a sound in another room gets that room's reverb and only reaches your room through the opening. This many of the most audible are re-measured at least every 0.2 s, the rest at least every 0.5 s (as the ray budget allows). 0 = off (every sound shares your room's reverb, the previous behaviour). Takes effect immediately.

Acoustics (#857) GPU cost: rays per frame for the per-sound room estimates (16 per sound, so 16 / 32 / 48 / 64 = 1-4 sounds per frame in turn; each ray also casts one visibility ray to you). Smoothed over about a second per sound.

Acoustics (#857): extra reverbs (0-3) for sounds in other rooms; sounds are grouped by how their rooms sound. Needs an audio device with at least 2 effect sends per source (OpenAL Soft has them). Each zone costs one more reverb in the audio mixer. 0 = sounds in other rooms only reach your room's reverb.

Acoustics (#858): how much a path around a corner or through a doorway (found by one-bounce rays) takes back the muffling of a sound whose straight line is blocked, 0 = off (blocked is blocked), 1 = full.

Acoustics (#858) GPU cost: how many blocked sounds (0-4) per room-ray frame get the doorway / corner search from your room's rays (64 short rays per sound); the most audible ones about every 0.1 s, the rest at least every 0.5 s. 0 = only the per-sound rays and the guided search find such paths.

Acoustics (#858) GPU cost: path queries per frame (0-128; each one or two short rays) for sounds heard around corners and through doorways. Paths found are kept and re-checked every frame for the 6 most audible blocked sounds (every 0.25 s for the rest), so a door closing cuts them within about 0.1-0.2 s; the rest of the budget searches for new paths (guided toward openings and earlier paths, including two-bounce paths into the next room). Together with AudioAcousticsSourceRoomRays at most 128.

Acoustics (#858): how far a blocked sound heard through a doorway or around a corner moves toward that opening in the stereo image, 0 = stays at its true direction, 1 = fully at the opening. The distance (and so the level) is unchanged.

Acoustics (#683 phase 1): measure the room reverb by tracing sound rays that bounce around the scene on the GPU (decay per frequency band, early reflections and their direction, how much sound escapes through openings) and blend the reverb toward what was measured, by how well it converged. Off: the reverb is estimated from the room rays alone. Needs AudioAcoustics and ray tracing. Takes effect immediately.

Acoustics (#683 phase 1) GPU cost: bouncing rays traced from the listener per bounce frame (64-1024, in steps of 64), every AudioAcousticsRoomInterval frames. More converge faster; the results are averaged over about a second either way.
Acoustics (#683 phase 1) GPU cost: reflections followed per bouncing ray (1-8). Each one costs a ray and a shadow ray back to the listener.

Acoustics (#683 phase 1) GPU cost: how many sounds in ANOTHER room (among the AudioAcousticsSourceRooms most audible) get their own bouncing rays per bounce frame, so that room's measured reverb is heard through the door (0-4). The most overdue go first. 0 = only the listener's room is measured.
Acoustics (#683 phase 1) GPU cost: bouncing rays per sound with its own room measurement (64-256, in steps of 64).
Acoustics (#683 phase 1) debug: add the bounce pass's detail (diffuse / specular returns per ray, the pan vectors sent to the reverb, each measured source room) to the acoustics log line every 10 s.

Acoustics (#683 early gain): sound reflected toward you within a few tens of milliseconds of the direct sound makes that sound louder -- a sound inside a metal horn is louder in front of the mouth, a sound in a small hard room a little louder. Traced on the GPU from each of the most audible sounds toward the listener; the part the room reverb already plays is left to the reverb. Off: the direct level is the occlusion / diffraction model alone. Needs AudioAcoustics and ray tracing. Takes effect immediately.
Acoustics (#683 early gain) GPU cost: how many of the most audible sounds get their reflected energy measured (0-64; a few per bounce frame in turn, each at most every 0.1 s). 0 = none.
Acoustics (#683 early gain) GPU cost: rays traced from a sound toward the listener per measurement (64-256, in steps of 64). Averaged over about half a second either way.
Acoustics (#683 early gain) GPU cost: reflections followed per ray (1-8; 2-4 covers the early sound). Each costs a ray and a shadow ray to the listener.

Acoustics (#683 early gain): reflections arriving up to this many milliseconds after the direct sound count toward its loudness (0-200). 50 ms is about how long after the direct sound a reflection still fuses with it (heard as the sound being louder, not as an echo); later energy is the reverb's.
Acoustics (#683 early gain): the most reflections may raise a sound above its plain level, dB (0-12).

Acoustics (#683 early gain): the share of a sound's early reflections the room reverb already plays when the sound is in your room (0-1); only the rest is added to the sound itself. Outdoors the reverb plays none of it. Lower = sounds in rooms get louder.

Acoustics (#897): low frequencies build up near hard surfaces -- about +3 dB per close wall at the listener and at the sound (a wall +3, an edge +6, a corner +9 dB), fading out farther than about half a metre. 0 = off, 1 = full. Uses the room rays already traced; needs AudioAcoustics, ray tracing and an OpenAL device with 3 auxiliary sends (OpenAL Soft).

Acoustics (#930): lying snow absorbs sound. Where the weather's snow lies (its snow depth grids: top faces and the faces under a drift, not walls above it or ground under a roof), an acoustics ray's hit takes snow's absorption by depth (a dusting nothing, 10 cm or more full): fresh snow very absorbent, packed snow (footprints, tracks) harder, wet / melting snow between snow and water. Shorter, quieter reverb and weaker ground reflections outdoors in snow, less early-gain boost and boundary bass from snowy floors; heavy snowfall adds a little air absorption. 0 = ignore snow (as before), 1 = full. No effect without snow or with the weather off. Needs AudioAcoustics and ray tracing.

Acoustics (#953): with your ear under water (the camera, or the avatar with MediaSoundsEarLocation), crossfade to an underwater profile: sounds in the air above come through the surface (AudioAcousticsWaterBoundaryLoss), every in-world sound is a little duller (hearing under water), and the room reverb plays at the speed of sound in water (shorter, denser). It replaces the old fixed 5x underwater distance falloff. Off: the old falloff; the boundary loss still applies. Needs AudioAcoustics and ray tracing. Takes effect immediately.

Acoustics (#953): loss in dB for a sound on the other side of the water surface (a sound under water heard from the air, or a sound in the air heard under water). The air / water surface lets only about 0.1 % of the sound energy through: about 30 dB. Applied to the sound and its reverb sends, crossfaded as either end crosses the surface; no change when both are on the same side. 0 = off. Needs AudioAcoustics and ray tracing.

Acoustics (#953): extra loss in dB at high frequencies (about 5 kHz) through the water surface, on top of AudioAcousticsWaterBoundaryLoss (ripples, bubbles and grazing paths take the highs first). 0 = the same loss at every frequency.

How snapshots saved to disk are named, without the extension. Tokens: {name} the base name chosen on the first save, {date} YYYY-MM-DD, {time} HHMMSS, {region} the current region, {w} and {h} the image size, {n} the counter (the first free number, so {n:3} gives 001, 002 ...). A name that already exists is never overwritten: the counter moves on (a pattern without {n} gets _2, _3 ...). Example: {name}_{n} gives Snapshot_1, Snapshot_2. Empty = the default.

Smooth jagged edges in world snapshots (Snapshot floater "Antialias (slower)"): the snapshot is rendered several times with tiny camera offsets and averaged (RenderSnapshotTemporalFrames sets how many). Off: one frame, as before. Depth snapshots and snapshots with the interface are never affected.

Vulkan: how many slightly offset frames a world snapshot averages when SnapshotAntialias is on (supersampling; the scene is frozen across them). More = smoother edges and less noise, each frame costs one full render at the snapshot size. 0 = off (one frame, the old behaviour); at most 64. Default 16. Live snapshots larger than the window (#873) accumulate at least this many jittered live frames (at least 4 per output pixel, at most 64).

Vulkan (#1093): snapshots larger than the window (accumulated from jittered live frames) are sharpened ONCE on the averaged result with the same contrast-adaptive filter as the live view, at RenderCASSharpness times this scale. The individual samples are never sharpened (that brought back the grain, #932). 1 = the live view's strength (default); 0 = off (the softer pre-#1093 look); above 1 = stronger. Window-size snapshots are unaffected.

Vulkan (#1093): the width of the reconstruction filter of an accumulated snapshot follows the samples per output pixel (0.5 output px at 4 per pixel, down to 0.3 when dense) instead of a fixed 0.5. Off = the fixed 0.5 (softer). Window-size snapshots are unaffected.

Vulkan (#1093): while an accumulated snapshot renders its samples, textures use a sharper mip level by log2(1 / upscale) (2x: -1, 4x: -2; at most -3), so the shot keeps the extra texture detail it can resolve. Restored right after the shot. Off = the live view's bias. Window-size snapshots are unaffected.

Vulkan (#873): take snapshots with the old OFFSCREEN renderer (the world re-rendered at the snapshot size) instead of from the live view. Off (default): snapshots come from the main render path -- exactly what the view shows, at or below the window size the finished frame resampled, above it jittered live frames accumulated. For A/B comparison and as a fallback. 360 snapshots and "No post-processing" always use the offscreen renderer.

Vulkan (#873): freeze the world (as Freeze World, Ctrl+Shift+F) while a snapshot larger than the window accumulates its jittered frames. 0 = never (moving pixels are rejected by motion vectors and taken from the last frame), 1 = for shots 2x the window and above (default), 2 = always.

Vulkan (#873): the largest factor over the window a snapshot is accumulated at from jittered live frames (1-8, default 4). Larger snapshots are accumulated at this factor and scaled the rest of the way.

Vulkan (#873): while the Snapshot floater is open, frame the part of the view a snapshot with a different aspect ratio from the window keeps (snapshots crop the live view; they never re-render with another field of view).

Develop > Cache > Extract Cache Store Record (#714): the record to extract, as "<uuid> [kind] [variant]" (kind = gputex, j2c, asset, mesh, cluster or a number; default gputex). GPU-ready: no variant, chain or chain-mask = the whole mip chain assembled from its records (#865); a number = one record (bit 0 mask use, bit 8 per-level layout, bits 9-13 level log2, 0 = the tail; 0 / 1 = an old whole-chain record). Written to the logs folder

Keep the asset cache (sounds, animations, notecards, scripts, gestures, settings, materials, GLTF, landmarks, wearables, meshes) in the cache store (#715: one crash-safe store at <cache>/store, meshes as one record per part) instead of one sl_cache_*.asset file per asset in <cache>/cache. Existing files are converted in the background after login (and served meanwhile). Off: the old per-file cache (its files are left alone). Also used automatically when the store cannot be opened. Applies at the next start

Keep the cluster LOD cache in the cache store (#715: kind cluster, page reads by range, budget RenderVKClusterCacheMB) instead of one .clod file per mesh face in <cache>/clusterlod. Existing files are converted in the background after login. Off: the old per-file cache. Also used automatically when the store cannot be opened. Applies at the next start

Keep the GPU-ready texture cache in the cache store (#715: one compressed, crash-safe store at <cache>/store) instead of one .gtx file per texture in <cache>/gputex. Existing .gtx files are converted in the background on the first start with the store. Off: the old per-file cache (its files are left alone). Also used automatically when the store cannot be opened. Applies at the next start

Keep the J2C texture cache in the cache store (#715: one crash-safe store at <cache>/store, sharing the textures budget with the GPU-ready cache, #705) instead of texture.entries / texture.cache / one body file per texture in <cache>/texturecache. The old cache is converted in the background (newest first; textures not converted yet are still read from it). Off: the old cache (what is left of it; the store's J2C records stay but are evicted first). Also used automatically when the store cannot be opened. Applies at the next start

Cache metrics (#715): minutes between "CacheMetrics" blocks in the log (hit rate, read latency, writes, evictions, footprint per cache and backend; one key=value line per row). 0 = only at shutdown and from Develop > Cache. The session summary <logs>/cache_metrics_<time>.json is written at shutdown either way

Cache store: threads that decompress large records (GPU-ready textures) after a reader has read them, below normal OS priority so rendering keeps the cores. 0 = auto (a quarter of the CPU threads, 1 to 4); otherwise 1 up to half the CPU threads. Applies at the next start

Cache store: threads that read records from disk and check them (decompression of large records runs on CacheStoreDecodeThreads). 0 = auto (1 on a hard disk; on an SSD an eighth of the CPU threads, 2 to 4); otherwise 1 to 16. Applies at the next start

Cache store (#715): seconds between periodic index snapshots while something changed (0 = only at exit). The snapshot only speeds up the next start; a crash just rescans the newest segment data. Applies at the next start

Vulkan: space at altitude. The higher the camera, the thinner the air: above GMDXSpaceStart the sky darkens to deep navy and black, haze thins, the sun turns into a sharp white disc, stars and the Milky Way show by day and a thin blue band of air lines the horizon. Off: the sky is the same at every height. Changes live.
Vulkan, GMDXSpaceAltitude: the camera height in metres where the air starts to thin (below it nothing changes). Changes live.
Vulkan, GMDXSpaceAltitude: the camera height in metres where the sky has its near-space look (held above). Changes live.
Vulkan, GMDXSpaceAltitude: how far toward the near-space look the sky goes at GMDXSpaceFull, 0 to 1 (1 = black sky, 0.5 = a dark blue one). Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: brightness of the catalogue stars (the Yale Bright Star Catalogue's 9096 stars at their real places, brightness and colours), on top of the sky's own star brightness. 1 = default, 0 = no stars. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: the latitude the night sky is seen from, in degrees (north positive): the celestial pole stands this high over the north horizon and the stars turn about it with the sun. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: the season of the night sky, as the sun's ecliptic longitude in degrees (0 = March equinox, 90 = June solstice: a northern summer night with the Milky Way's core in the south, 180 = September, 270 = December). Changes live.
Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: how much the stars twinkle (more near the horizon, where their colours also flicker apart). 1 = default, 0 = steady stars. Changes live.
Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: brightness of the Milky Way (ESO/S. Brunier's panorama) in a dark night sky; twilight and moonlight wash it out. 1 = default, 0 = none. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: brightness of the dark sky's own glow: the dark navy that keeps a moonless sky from pure black, and the airglow's faint green-grey tint low over the horizon. Twilight and moonlight wash it out. 1 = default, 0 = none (a black sky). Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: brightness of the zodiacal light, sunlight off the solar system's dust: a faint warm cone over the horizon on the sun's side after dusk and before dawn. 1 = default, 0 = none. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: brightness of the planets Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn, steady points of their own colours on the stars' path of the sun (Venus and Mercury only near the sun, at dusk and dawn). They move on the real calendar from night to night; the season (GMDXNightSkySunLongitude) places the Earth. 1 = their real brightness next to the stars, 0 = none. Range 0 to 4. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: how often shooting stars cross a dark night sky. 1 = a few a minute (a quarter of the photo studio's meteor rate, RenderMeteorSpawnInterval, which with RenderMeteorsEnabled and RenderMeteorMaxCount still applies); none by day or in bright twilight, fewer under a bright moon. 0 = none. Range 0 to 4. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: a meteor shower. Many more shooting stars (up to 9 times as many with the radiant overhead), most flying away from one point, the radiant of the shower nearest the season (GMDXNightSkySunLongitude): the Perseids in August, the Geminids in December, and so on. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: how many satellites glide across the sky after dusk and before dawn: faint steady points that shine while sunlight still reaches them high up and fade out as they pass into the Earth's shadow. 1 = one every 40 seconds or so (at most 6 at once), 0 = none. Range 0 to 4. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: brightness of the faint smudges beyond the stars at their real places: the Andromeda galaxy, the Orion nebula, the Pleiades' blue haze, and in southern skies the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds. Twilight and moonlight wash them out like the Milky Way. 1 = default, 0 = none. Range 0 to 4. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: the faintest stars drawn, as a magnitude: fainter ones fade out (over half a magnitude). 8 = every star of the catalogue (default), 6.5 = what the eye sees in a dark sky, 3 = only the brightest 170 or so, the constellations' outlines. Range 3 to 8, step 0.1. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: size of the stars (and planets and satellites) on screen; their peak brightness is kept, so bigger stars also look brighter. 1 = default (as sharp as the screen allows). Range 0.5 to 3, step 0.05. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: colour saturation of the night sky: the stars' and planets' colours, the Milky Way and the deep-sky glow. 1 = their real colours (default), 0 = all white / grey, 2 = twice as colourful. Range 0 to 3, step 0.05. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: turns the Milky Way along its own band, in degrees, moving its bright core away from Sagittarius (the stars stay where they are). 0 = the real sky (default). Range -180 to 180, step 1. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: tilts the Milky Way's band about its core, in degrees, so it crosses the sky at another angle (the stars stay where they are). 0 = the real sky (default). Range -90 to 90, step 1. Changes live.

Vulkan, GMDXPhysicalNight: a game look for the night sky on top of the other night sky settings: brighter, bigger and more colourful stars, a much brighter Milky Way with its faint outskirts lifted, more shooting stars, stronger deep-sky glow and zodiacal light. 0 = the real sky (default). Changes live.

Vulkan: alpha-masked world surfaces (paths, decals, foliage cards) are drawn this many millimetres closer to the camera, so a path or decal mesh built just above the ground does not flicker against it (the Vulkan renderer stores vertex positions on a 16-bit grid that can close a 1-2 mm gap; GL keeps them exact). Larger values let masked faces show through by that much. 0 = off. Changes live.
Vulkan (GMDXAlphaMaskPullMM): extra pull in millimetres per metre of camera distance.

Vulkan (GMDXAlphaMaskPullMM): cap of the grazing-angle factor (1 / cos of the angle between the surface normal and the view) that widens the pull on surfaces seen edge-on, such as a path ahead of you. 1 = no widening.

Draw avatars while they load instead of LL's loading cloud: the system body shows as far as its appearance has arrived (bakes not here yet in plain grey, the rest as they decode) and attachments as their meshes arrive, and no cloud particles are made. Off: the loading cloud until the avatar is fully loaded (LL's behaviour).
Loadouts: the quick-swap keys of slots 1-4, ;-separated, in menu shortcut syntax (control|alt|shift|key); an empty entry is unbound. Set them in Loadouts > Categories > Key...
Loadouts window: close it after Equip.

Instant replay: keep the last GMDXReplaySeconds of the window (UI included) encoded in memory on the GPU's H.264 video encoder, so Combat > Save Replay (Alt+F10) can write them to an MP4. Costs a frame copy and a small conversion per captured frame, about 100 MB of video memory and up to GMDXReplaySeconds x GMDXReplayBitrateKbps of system memory.
Instant replay: seconds kept in memory and saved (5 to 300). A saved clip starts on the keyframe at or before that many seconds ago, so it can be up to a second longer.
Instant replay: the window is scaled down to this height for the video (aspect kept). Takes effect immediately and starts a new buffer.
Instant replay: frames captured per second at most (10 to 240). Starts a new buffer when changed.
Instant replay: record the viewer's own sound (world, UI, music, media, voice; never the microphone or other programs) into the replay.
Instant replay: video bitrate in kbit/s (1000 to 200000). Memory used = seconds x bitrate / 8. Starts a new buffer when changed.
Instant replay: folder for saved clips. Empty = the Videos folder's GunMetal-DX subfolder.

Mini-map background painted by the viewer in the OCOL map look (OCOL's map tile renderer): the terrain at a 64 m texture repeat, lit by a north-west sun with cast shadows and contact shading, and the water coloured by its depth with a shore band. Off: LL's pre-2024 painted terrain. Not used while a world map tile is shown (GMDXMiniMapUseMapTile).
World Map: draw this grid's captured region maps (mini-map menu, Region Map) over the map's own tiles, at 512 px, for the regions on screen. Off: the server's map tiles only.
Mini-map background: a region's captured map (mini-map menu "Capture Region Map...") when there is one, instead of the painted terrain or the world map tile.
Region map capture: render the map with sun shadows. Off, nothing casts a shadow (flat, even daylight). Set in the Capture Region Map window.
Region map capture: paint the water in the OCOL map look (deep to shallow by depth, shore band, foam) instead of capturing the in-world water. Set in the Capture Region Map window.
Region map capture: save maps exactly lossless (JPEG 2000 reversible, about 27 MB for 4096 px) instead of visually lossless (about 14 MB). Set in the Capture Region Map window.

Region map capture: the map shows what is below your altitude plus this many metres (never below the region's highest hill). 50 m clears most roofs and trees on the ground; lower it in a skybox so the roof stays out. Set in the Capture Region Map window.
Region map capture: the longest wait (seconds) for the region to finish loading before the map is rendered with what has arrived.

Mini-map background. Off: painted by the viewer from the region's terrain and water, as LL and Firestorm drew it before 2024 (the terrain textures, or the PBR terrain materials' colours). On: the region's world map tile from the server, with the painted terrain shown while the tile is loading or when the region has no tile.
Mini-map: hide the window's minimize, tear-off and close buttons (mini-map menu, View). It still closes from its toolbar button or the World menu.
Mini-map: draw the marks (right-click the map > Add Mark Here; gmdxminimapmarks.cpp).
Mini-map: show the region coordinates under the cursor (and a mark's name over a mark).
Mini-map: draw the zones (right-click the map > Draw Zone; gmdxminimapmarks.cpp).

Mini-map: draw the marks, zones and pings that people in your region share with you through their GunMetal-DX Helper (gmdxmapshare.h); those object chat lines are then hidden. Only from the people in your map share list (Send To, ticked or not) and the members of the groups you send to (your worn group while GMDXMapShareMyGroup, the ticked groups); anyone else's line stays chat text, and a mark or zone from them asks (Accept / Always / Deny / Mute); their pings are never drawn. Off: shares stay plain chat text and are not drawn.
Mini-map: shared map lines also stay in the nearby chat as plain object chat (for checking what was sent).

Map shares and pings can be sent (gmdxmapshare.h): the #GunMetal-DX Helper is worn while this is on, and says each one privately (llRegionSayTo) to the people you send to who are in your region; nobody outside your region ever gets one. Off: the helper comes off unless another feature uses it, and nothing can be sent. Receiving needs no helper.
Mini-map: how long a received ping shows on the mini-map and over the world, in seconds (3 to 60, as in Preferences > Combat > Pings).

Mini-map and World Map: a ping arrives as a radar blip (gmdxmapshare.h): a flash and three rings spreading out in the ping's colour, then its dot fades away over the ping's life (GMDXPingSeconds); the marker over the world pulses the same way as it appears. Off: one ring a second for its first 2 seconds, and it fades over its last 1.5 seconds.
Mini-map: a short sound (UISndChatPing) when someone's ping arrives.

The ping wheel's key (map_ping_wheel, default Shift+B; gmdxpingwheel.h): let go within this many milliseconds, it sends a plain Ping where it went down; held longer, a wheel of Ping / Enemy / Rally opens and letting go on a slice sends that kind (in the middle: nothing). 50 to 2000. Set in Preferences > Combat > Pings.

Internal (llviewerinput.cpp): your key_bindings.xml was moved over to the ping wheel once: Shift+B, which pinged an enemy, opens the ping wheel where it still had that old default, and the wheel got Shift+B where it was free. Set back to 0 to do it again at the next start.
Mini-map: new zones are drawn with dotted lines (Draw Zone > Dotted Lines; a zone's own Zone Line changes it too).
Mini-map: the fill of new zones, 0 none, 1 the zone's colour, 2 black and yellow caution stripes, both see-through (the last Zone Fill picked).
Mini-map: the colour of new zones, 0 red, 1 orange, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 cyan, 5 purple (the last Zone Colour picked).
Mini-map: opacity of the map (its background and region images), 0.1 to 1. The compass, avatars and overlays stay solid. Set from the mini-map menu, Background > Opacity.

Mini-map, Show Whole Region with the map rotating (Rotation menu): 0 (default) = turn around me, round (a radar centred on the avatar); 1 = turn around me, square; 2 = turn the whole region about its centre, shrunk so all of it fits at any angle (no zoom).

Mini-map compass while the Whole Region map rotates (Compass Style menu while rotating): 1 (default) = edge pills, the map fills the view; 0 = gunmetal frame, the map shrinks inside it. The heading tape is north-up only.

Mini-map "Show Whole Region": the whole region the avatar is in, fitted to the mini-map, north at the top, with nothing outside it (no neighbouring regions, objects, avatars or parcel lines). The map cannot be zoomed or panned while it is on (MiniMapScale is kept for when it is turned off), and resizing the mini-map keeps it square. The compass is drawn in the style GMDXMiniMapCompassStyle picks.

Mini-map compass in "Show Whole Region" mode (GMDXMiniMapWholeRegion). 0 = gunmetal frame: a metal border around the map with the eight directions and tick marks in it. 1 = edge pills: the map fills the mini-map, the eight directions in small rounded labels at its edges and corners. 2 = heading tape: the map fills the mini-map, a strip across the top shows the camera's heading.

Mini-map (and the People panel's map) "Hide avatars high above me": avatars more than GMDXMiniMapHideAboveMeters above your own height get no dot, no hover info and cannot be picked by a right-click, e.g. people sitting on build platforms during combat. An avatar the viewer only knows as "1020 m or higher" (unknown altitude) is hidden whenever you are below 1020 m, whatever the height.
Mini-map: with GMDXMiniMapHideAbove on, how many metres above your own height an avatar must be to be hidden (250 to 1000).

Mini-map "Only Render Physical Objects" (with "Render Objects" on): instead of the static object layer, draws every physical object (the Physical property, e.g. bullets and other dynamic objects; not attachments) as a dot with a short trail along its velocity, updated every frame. Physical objects at rest are not shown.

Rez effects: what objects do when they appear. 0 none, 1 Tron (a cyan wireframe scan, then the textured surface fills in), 2 fire (burns into view), 3 hologram, 4 voxel assemble, 5 3D printer, 6 transporter, 7 a random one of the ticked effects per object. The object is always there and solid from its first frame: the effect only paints its surface.

Rez effects: what objects do when they disappear. 0 none, 1 ember burn, 2 disintegrate, 3 ash on the wind, 4 glitch out, 5 implode, 6 a random one of the ticked effects per object, 7 Tron de-rez, 8 shatter. A removed object keeps drawing only for the effect: no shadow, no clicks.

Rez effects: seconds an effect takes (Tron: the fill scan; its wireframe scan takes 0.6 of this; the 3D printer takes about 5.8x this, 8 s at most, and the transporter 1.5x, 6 s at most). Disintegrate takes 1.8x this, ash, Tron de-rez and shatter 2x; a de-rez lasts 1.2 s at most.

Rez effects: play the rez-in only for objects whose textures are still loading when they first show (the wireframe covers the white blobs). Off: every object that appears plays it. Avatars and attachments always play it.
Rez effects: avatars and what they wear (attachments, rigged mesh included) play the effects too. A leaving avatar just goes; an attachment taken off plays the de-rez.
Tron rez-in: how brightly the wireframe and the scan line glow (0 = no glow, 1 = default, up to 4).
Tron rez-in: wireframe line width on screen, in pixels (0.5 to 5).

Rez effects: on damage-enabled land (where you stand), shorten every effect to 0.25 s at most, and the 3D printer and transporter rez-ins keep the object whole and solid (paint only) instead of hiding what is not built yet.

Rez effects: a two-part rez-in plays its first part, then holds there, idling, until the object's textures have loaded for you (an avatar: its appearance, LL's fully loaded), and only then plays its final part. Tron holds its wireframe, the hologram its projection, voxel its blocks, the 3D printer before its final layers (kept warm, then cooling into the real surface), the transporter its sparkles, fire its smouldering shell. Every rez-in still ends within 30 s of its start. Never on combat-safe land. Off: Tron waits at most 2 s, the others never.

How the edit selection is drawn. 0 Classic: LL's silhouette for prims and sculpties, Firestorm's softer wireframe for mesh, rigged mesh, avatars and trees. 1 Outline: a screen-space outline of everything (outer contour and visible face edges). 2 Wireframe: every triangle edge of everything, Slipstream's original look.
Rez effects: the Tron rez-in is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the fire rez-in is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the hologram rez-in is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the voxel assemble rez-in is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the 3D printer rez-in is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the transporter rez-in is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the ember burn de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the disintegrate de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the ash on the wind de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the glitch out de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the implode de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the Tron de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: the shatter de-rez is in the random mix.
Rez effects: glow colour of the Tron rez-in.
Rez effects: glow colour of the fire rez-in.
Rez effects: glow colour of the hologram rez-in.
Rez effects: glow colour of the voxel assemble rez-in.
Rez effects: glow colour of the 3D printer rez-in.
Rez effects: glow colour of the transporter rez-in.
Rez effects: glow colour of the ember burn de-rez.
Rez effects: glow colour of the disintegrate de-rez.
Rez effects: glow colour of the ash on the wind de-rez.
Rez effects: glow colour of the glitch out de-rez.
Rez effects: glow colour of the implode de-rez.
Rez effects: glow colour of the Tron de-rez (its glow strength and line width are the Tron ones).
Rez effects: glow colour of the shatter de-rez (its cracks, glassy tint and glints).

Inventory (#350, reads only): when several queued AIS item fetches share a parent folder, fetch that folder once (category children, depth 0) instead of one item request each, as LL's LLInventoryFetchItemsObserver does. FALSE restores one request per item.

Inventory (#350, reads only): forced item refetches (sent after every item a copy or give creates) wait up to this long so several from one folder can be coalesced into one folder fetch. Ordinary item fetches never wait. 0 disables the wait; maximum 5.
Inventory (#350): minimum number of queued item fetches in one folder before they are replaced by one folder fetch (LL uses more than 7). Minimum 2.
Inventory (#350): only coalesce when the folder holds at most this many times as many objects as items wanted from it, so a few items in a big folder stay single requests.
Inventory (#350): never coalesce item fetches into a fetch of a folder with more than this many objects.

Inventory folder copy (#353): create the links of each copied folder with one AIS CreateInventory request per SLInventoryCopyLinkBatchSize links (as LL does for outfits), checking that every link was created. FALSE restores one request per link.
Inventory folder copy (#353): links per AIS CreateInventory request when SLInventoryCopyBatchLinks is on. 1 to 100.

Inventory folder copy (#353, client only): per copied object, mark the destination folder changed and let the end-of-frame inventory notification refresh views, instead of notifying all observers once per object.

Inventory item copies (#353, TESTING): put up to SLInventoryCopyBlocksPerMessage queued copies into one CopyInventoryItem message (one InventoryData block and CallbackID per copy; pacing and per-copy confirmation unchanged). LL's viewer always sends one block per message, so this is off until verified on a test account.
Inventory item copies (#353): InventoryData blocks per CopyInventoryItem message when SLInventoryCopyMultiBlock is on. 1 to 16.

Inventory item copies (#538): how many CopyInventoryItem requests may await the server's reply at once; further copies wait in order and go out as replies arrive. The simulator silently drops large bursts. Minimum 1.

Keep running the filter/arrange pass every frame for inventory panels that are not visible (old behaviour, ~1 ms per hidden panel per frame). Off: hidden panels still pre-build their views at the 1 ms hidden budget but only filter once shown.

Debug: every inventory cache lookup (folder-for-type, base outfit link, COF link checks, worn ids, drag cargo facts, ...) also recomputes the uncached answer and logs an "InventoryCacheVerify" WARNING on any mismatch. Slow; for test sessions only.

Conversations (#371): an incoming IM or group chat only creates its session; its conversation panel is built the first time it is opened (toasts, the conversations list and unread counts work without it). FALSE builds the panel for every new session, as before.

Conversations (#369): a chat history holds a window of at most SLChatWindowMessages messages; scrolling to its top or bottom pages more in (live messages from memory, earlier sessions from the log) and drops as many at the other end, so frame time stays flat however long the conversation. FALSE keeps every message in the document, as before. Applies to conversations opened afterwards.
Conversations (#369): most messages a windowed chat history (SLChatWindowedHistory) holds at once. 50 to 2000.

Conversations (#371): messages read from a chat log per page, off the main thread. A conversation first shows two pages of its history; scrolling to the top of a windowed chat history reads one more. 10 to 500.

Allow swimming: in deep water the avatar floats at the surface (flying is switched on and held there), dives while crouch/down is held, rises back when released, and walks out onto land. Needs flying to be allowed. Swim animations come from the AO.

Swap turning and strafing on the default movement keys outside mouselook: A/D and the Left/Right arrows strafe, and with Shift held they turn. Only the default A/D/arrow bindings are swapped; custom key bindings are left alone. Mouselook, sitting and the free camera are unaffected.

On: moving backwards (S / down arrow) on the ground keeps the avatar facing forward (when running backwards, only in your own view) and the built-in AO plays its Walking Backwards animation. Off: the avatar turns round to face its travel, walking or running, and the AO plays its forward Walking animation. Without the AO overriding walk, Off leaves the viewer default.

Look-at sync (#902): send where your avatar looks (a direction only) to other Slipstream viewers, so they can turn your mesh body's own neck and head. Off by default. Never sends while LL's "Don't send my Look At target" is on or the AO holds your head. Wears the #Slipstream Helper while on.

Look-at sync (#902): restart another avatar's look-at layer when it is driven but applies nothing for 3 seconds (an unbound or stuck motion; at most 5 times per avatar). Off: only log it ("#PoseLookAt stuck").

#Slipstream Helper (#902): retry an unavailable helper on its own (after 30 s, doubling to 5 minutes), not only on a region change or when a feature is switched on again; FIND's timeout counts only time after the avatar and inventory are there; the attach budget resets once the helper is ready. Never retries after you took the helper off, put it in the Trash, or its script failed to compile. Off: the old behaviour.

Look-at sync (#902): the longest a look-at line (keep-alives included) waits for the helper queue to drain before it goes out anyway, in seconds. 0 = wait as long as it takes (the old behaviour, which could hold every line while pose data streamed).

Look-at sync (#902): how strongly your avatar turns toward what you look at (0..1), sent with your look-at
Look-at sync (#902): seconds a head takes to settle onto a new look-at target and to fade in or out (0 = no easing); sent with your look-at so others see your preference

#485: wall-clock budget per frame (ms) for region idle updates (terrain patches, object cache visibility, creating objects from the object cache). Applies even with NewObjectCreationThrottle disabled (-1) and right after a teleport; only behind the login / teleport progress screen is LL's 1 s used. NewObjectCreationThrottle (> 0) caps the count per region per frame on top of it.

Wall-clock budget per frame (ms) for destroying dead objects (LLViewerObjectList::cleanDeadObjects). Dead objects leave every lookup, the GPU scene and the object list at once; their destructors run from a backlog within this budget (at least one per frame; 4x while the backlog is over 4096 objects or 2 s old), so an avatar leaving with its attachments no longer stalls one frame. A region being deleted destroys its own pending objects at once. 0 = destroy everything in the frame it died (LL).

Parcel audio (#892): the media plugin hands the parcel stream's decoded audio to the viewer (shared-memory ring) and the viewer plays it through OpenAL: as one stereo source with no effects when the parcel has no speakers (or ParcelAudioSpeakers is off), else through the in-world speakers. A change restarts a playing stream. Off: the plugin plays the stream to the system device itself, exactly as before (no speakers). Statistics every 10 s under the "ParcelAudio" log tag.

Debug (#960): with ParcelAudioCapture on, the media plugin attaches the audio ring but discards every frame, i.e. a capture that delivers nothing. The viewer should then fall back to the plugin's own output a few seconds after the stream starts playing (one WARNING under the "ParcelAudio" log tag) and the stream stays audible. Read at the next stream start. Not saved.

Parcel audio (#892): play the parcel stream from the parcel's in-world speakers ([slspk ...] hover-text tag, doc/parcel_speakers_protocol.md) as positioned sounds with distance falloff and room acoustics. Finds the speakers of the parcel you are on and checks each one's owner / group with one object-properties request. Turning it on also turns ParcelAudioCapture on. Off: no speaker discovery and no requests.

Parcel audio speakers (#892): about once a second every playing speaker's position in the stream is measured against the shared timeline; one further off than this (ms) is re-joined at the next 50 ms chunk boundary (a short gap in that speaker). Doppler (moving listener) legitimately shifts speakers: while you move faster than 1 m/s only offsets over 50 ms are fixed. 0: measure and log only.

Parcel audio speakers (#892): Doppler pitch shift on the speakers while you (or they) move. Off (default): no shift -- walking past speakers in different directions no longer detunes them against each other (chorusing) or drifts them apart in time; position, falloff, cones and room acoustics are unchanged, and other in-world sounds keep their Doppler. On: OpenAL's Doppler, as for other sounds.

Parcel audio speakers (#892) with room acoustics: the speakers' reverb sends keep their level over distance (a diffuse field: a reverberant hall's reverb is about as loud everywhere in it; outdoors the room reverb stays low). Level = the speaker's vol x the room's reverb (wet / decay from the acoustics estimate) x how the speaker's room couples to yours. Off: a speaker's reverb falls with distance like any in-world sound's (the reverb's initial decay over the distance).

In-world sounds: a script's sound radius (llSetSoundRadius) becomes a soft maximum -- the sound keeps falling off as real inverse distance (-6 dB per doubling, as it always does here) and fades out over the last 15 % of the radius instead of cutting off at it. Sounds without a radius are unchanged. Off: exactly the previous behaviour.

Parcel audio (#892): what you hear on a parcel with speakers while out of range of all of them. 0 = what the parcel's [slspk outside=...] tag says (default: silence), 1 = always the stream as a quiet stereo bed (-12 dB), 2 = always silence.
Parcel audio (#892): how many speakers play at once (1..32, default 16), the ones loudest at your position. Speakers in range beyond it are skipped (logged once per change).
Parcel audio (#892): seconds of the captured stream kept queued in OpenAL (1.0..2.5). More survives longer frame hitches without a gap; the stream starts this much later.

Use the GPU-driven particle pipeline (LLCleanParticleStore): CPU feeds one emitter descriptor per source and the GPU owns emission, simulation, and rendering. When off, falls back to LL's legacy CPU particle simulation + rendering.

Vulkan: extra blend-to-mask demotion beyond LL's. A blend face whose texture has at most this fraction (0..1) of partial-alpha pixels (alpha 17..239) is drawn as alpha-MASK (opaque wherever alpha > the cutoff). 0 = off, LL behaviour: only LL's strict test (canRenderAsMask: under ~2% mid-range alpha, no glow, opaque tint) demotes. Values above 0 turn soft-alpha content such as light shafts and glass opaque. Live

Vulkan: alpha-blend legacy (Blinn-Phong) material faces that are shiny (specular exponent or env intensity, or legacy shininess) and whose texture has an alpha channel stay in the alpha-blend bucket instead of being auto-demoted to alpha-mask / opaque, so LL's glare shows their specular highlights and shiny reflections on transparent texels (clear glass that shows only its glints, #470). Off = the previous demotion (A/B for ordering of shiny binary-alpha foliage). Takes effect as faces re-register

Select-to-diagnose (Vulkan clean ingest, #88): when the edit selection changes, log one "VKIngestDiag" INFO block per selected object (every linkset member) with its face list, decode/capture/slot/LOD-group/instance state, rigged routing and GPU spin, then a one-line summary of what is NOT in the GPU scene. Only runs on selection changes.

Vulkan CPU: compare and stream the material-UV and terrain-record blobs only after the material store re-copied them (or their GPU buffer is new), instead of comparing the full blobs every frame. 0 = the old every-frame compare.

Vulkan CPU: run the texture-residency lap every frame on its own entry point, and the full material texture resolver only when material-side work is pending (changed or unsettled materials, budget-starved resolves, media, self/HUD), plus a 30-frame safety pass. Fixed texture sets (projectors, particles, water, sky) refresh on change or every 8th pass. 0 = the old behaviour (full resolver nearly every frame).

Vulkan: a material whose emissive MAP is not resident yet (loading, tier-2 cache read pending, image budget starved, re-resolving after a recycled material id or a spell off screen) emits nothing until the map arrives. Off = the old behaviour: the shaders emit the bare emissive factor while the map is missing, so an emissive mask (factor 1, mostly black map) lights the whole face solid white with bloom for those frames. Bisect switch; takes effect as materials re-resolve.

Testing (#876): act as if the driver were Intel's Windows one, so automatic pipeline compile concurrency is capped to 1 on any machine (logs the same "Pipeline compiles: 1 at a time" line). RenderVKPipelineCompileThreads above 0 still overrides.

Testing (#1064): a pipeline name exactly as a crash log prints it after "crashed while compiling pipeline:" (e.g. "mProbeTracePipe (ProbeRt)"). Each start treats the previous session as having crashed while compiling it on this driver: the first start gives it a strike, the second quarantines it (it is not compiled; a notification says so). Read at startup only; clear it after testing. The quarantine lives in user_settings/vk_pipeline_quarantine.txt (delete it, or change its driver line, to clear).

Testing (#1064): a pipeline name exactly as a crash log prints it after "crashed while compiling pipeline:". The viewer CRASHES ON PURPOSE when it starts compiling that pipeline, through the real crash handler and compile-crash marker: two such crashes quarantine the pipeline and the third start runs without it. Read at startup only; clear it after testing.

Vulkan diagnostic: a face whose material names a base-colour map that is not resident (still loading, image budget, missing, or a material cleared while it was being drawn) shades MAGENTA instead of the bare base factor (solid white on most faces). Visible in the lit view and RenderVKDebugView 1. Takes effect as materials re-resolve. Pairs with the VKWhiteBase log lines (RenderVKDebugWhiteBaseLog)

Vulkan diagnostic: log (VKWhiteBase, at most 8 lines per 2 s) when a live material LOSES its resolved base-colour map (with the texture, reason and the object / avatar drawing it), when an instance switches material (with the descriptor fields that differ -- what flips a face's material), when a dead material is revived, and when a stale dead verdict would have cleared a material still in use. Counts are always in the VKTexUpload summary line (white_base, revived, clear_refused, mat_flips)

Vulkan (#772): reflection probes are recaptured only on CHANGE -- a probe is scheduled only when never captured, a static change (edit, new / removed object, terrain) reaches its capture, its environment changed, moving dynamic contents are inside (at RenderVKProbeDynamicRefreshSec), or past RenderVKProbeSafetySec; otherwise no capture, filter or encode runs. False = the old scheduler (one face every frame forever, by age).

Vulkan (#772): the realtime reflection probe (detail Realtime / Raytraced) skips a frame when it is the probe captured last frame, nothing changed in its capture range, and no dynamic contents move inside (still avatars: every RenderVKProbeRealtimeStillSec). Only with six realtime faces per frame. False = capture every frame.

Vulkan (#772): the planar mirror skips its capture while the camera and mirror are static and nothing in the reflected view changed (no static change, mover, avatar or particle emitter in it, no environment / light / shadow change), up to RenderVKMirrorIdleMaxSec. False = the old behaviour (RenderHeroProbeUpdateRate only).
Vulkan (#772): longest a static planar mirror keeps its capture under RenderVKMirrorIdleSkip (animated water, textures, flexi and clouds refresh at least this often).
Vulkan (#772): an idle reflection probe is recaptured at least this often (seconds), changed or not.
Vulkan (#772): after login / teleport / region crossing, for this many seconds the probe safety age is RenderVKProbeSettleSafetySec (textures and LODs are still streaming in).
Vulkan (#772): the probe safety age (seconds) during RenderVKProbeSettleSec after an arrival.

Vulkan (#772): a change that repeats at the same place within this many seconds (a colour-cycling script, a re-registering prim), and every motion sphere (mover start / settle, pose and seat refreshes), is held as moving dynamic content for this long after its last occurrence (probes refresh at RenderVKProbeDynamicRefreshSec, once more when it expires) instead of a static content change every time. 0 = every change is static.

Vulkan (#772): a probe with a repeating in-place change inside (RenderVKProbeChurnSec: colour cycling, a re-registering prim) is refreshed every this many seconds while it repeats, once more when it stops.
Vulkan (#772): a probe with MOVING dynamic contents inside (movers; avatars for Dynamic probes) is refreshed every this many seconds while they move, once more when they stop or leave.
Vulkan (#772): an avatar counts as moving (for probe / mirror change tracking) when its render position moved more than this (m) since the last frame.
Vulkan (#772): the realtime probe refreshes every this many seconds while still dynamic contents (an avatar animating in place) are inside. 0 = every frame.
Vulkan (#772): the realtime probe is captured at least this often (seconds) under RenderVKProbeRealtimeIdle.

Vulkan (#772): a change outside a probe influence volume dirties it only when at least this wide (radians, radius / distance) from its origin and inside its capture far clip. 0 = any change inside the far clip.
Vulkan (#772): environment drift (light / ambient / sun lanes) past this since the last snapshot marks every probe env-dirty; they refresh nearest first, RenderVKProbeEnvTrickleSec apart.
Vulkan (#772): an environment change past this since the last snapshot (a jump: environment switch) makes every probe capture stale at once (the old reset).
Vulkan (#772): minimum seconds between two environment-drift probe refreshes (0 = back to back).
Vulkan (#772): log a probe recapture line (captures per second by reason, idle frames, realtime / mirror skips, change lists, probe GPU ms with RenderVKGpuTimers) every this many seconds. 0 = off.

Vulkan: reflection-probe discovery cadence (#478, GPU-driven probes). The GPU re-bins the static instances into its 16 m automatic-probe occupancy grid every N frames (at once when the region set or agent region changes); cells whose content changed are re-placed on the GPU (up to 64 per frame). Manual probes arrive through a registration hook with a slow CPU safety scan (a slice of the object list per frame). 0 = re-bin every frame, and scan 2048 objects per frame.

Vulkan diagnostic (#478): every ~2 s log one line (VKGpu) of the GPU-driven reflection probes' counters -- occupied / placed 16 m cells at the last re-bin, placements this frame and still queued, resident cube slots, the scheduled and realtime jobs' slots. Read back asynchronously (a 64-byte copy, three frames late); off = no copy at all. Placement and scheduling never read anything back.

Vulkan RT (B8): skip the rig copy + rigged BLAS refit of an avatar group whose skinned world positions did not change this frame (GPU pose held, root unmoved, skin meta unchanged). 0 = off (refit every group every frame), 1 = unchanged avatars only, 2 = also refit avatars farther than RenderVKRigRefitFarMeters every 2nd frame and small on-screen ones every 2nd..4th (RenderVKRigRefitFullPx; their RT shadows lag up to N-1 frames, and such avatars never self-shadow in RT -- classified with hysteresis, "no-self-shadow (throttled)" in the RT log -- so their stale geometry cannot shadow their own current surface). Counter rt_rigRefitSkipped.
Vulkan RT (B8): with RenderVKRigRefitGate 2, avatars whose bounds are farther than this from the camera (m) have their rig copy + rigged BLAS refit every 2nd frame. 0 = never throttle by distance.

Vulkan RT (B8, crowd perf): with RenderVKRigRefitGate 2, an avatar's rig copy + rigged BLAS refit runs every frame while its bounds are at least this tall on screen (px), every 2nd frame below it, every 3rd below half, every 4th below a quarter (capped by RenderVKRigRefitMaxPeriod; staggered per group). Your own avatar and the protected set (RenderVKRiggedProtect*) always refit. Throttled avatars' RT shadows lag by up to N-1 frames. 0 = distance rule only (RenderVKRigRefitFarMeters).
Vulkan RT (B8): the longest refit period (frames) RenderVKRigRefitFullPx may give a small on-screen avatar (1 = no screen-size throttle).

Vulkan RT (#1007): with RenderVKRigRefitGate 2, refit far / small on-screen avatars' rigged BLAS on a cadence (RenderVKRigRefitFarMeters every 2nd frame, RenderVKRigRefitVeryFarMeters every 4th, RenderVKRigRefitFullPx by screen size; staggered per group). Off = every avatar refits every frame its pose changed, and none loses RT self-shadowing (A/B). The held-pose proof and the pose skip (RenderVKRigRefitPoseThreshold) are separate. Live.

Vulkan RT (#1007): with RenderVKRigRefitCadence, avatars farther than this (m, and past RenderVKRigRefitFarMeters) refit their rigged BLAS every 4th frame (capped by RenderVKRigRefitMaxPeriod). Never your own avatar or the protected set. 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan RT (#1007): rigged BLAS POSE SKIP. A group's rig copy + refit is skipped while its avatar's pelvis-relative pose moved less than this (m, summed per frame since the group's last refit: joint translation + rotation x 0.5 m, measured on the GPU) -- the threshold holds within 10 m of the camera and grows linearly with distance beyond. Avatar-local groups only, never your own avatar; capped by RenderVKRigRefitPoseMaxStale. The BLAS and the positions hit shading reads stay one consistent (slightly old) pose. 0 = off. Live.
Vulkan RT (#1007): the most frames in a row the pose skip (RenderVKRigRefitPoseThreshold) may leave a rigged group's BLAS unrefit (max 8; 0 = pose skip off). Live.

Vulkan RT (F1): build the TLAS with ALLOW_UPDATE and refit it in place (MODE_UPDATE) on most frames; a full build every RenderVKTLASRebuildFrames and whenever the instance count, record buffer, repack generation, rigged plan, RT radius changes, the camera jumps or instances wait to enter. Instances entering the RT radius join at the next full build. 0 = full build every frame (the old path, without ALLOW_UPDATE). Counters rt_tlasRefit / rt_tlasRebuild / rt_tlasDeferred.

Vulkan RT (F1): with RenderVKTLASRefit, at most this many frames between full TLAS builds (bounds refit quality decay and the delay before newly eligible instances cast RT shadows). 1 = build every frame.

Vulkan CPU: reuse the ray-tracing rigged plan (candidate walk, owner/mask grouping sort, rig entries, BLAS geometries) while its inputs are unchanged: rigged-row plan fields, the contents of the slots it read, LOD groups, repacks, skin meta, avatar visibility/tier bits and counts. 0 = rebuild it every frame.

Vulkan CPU: self-attachment priority ingest settles per object. After a full lap over the worn objects only the ones still pending (decode / capture / mesh fetch in flight) are revisited each frame, with a backoff for any that stay pending; the whole outfit is re-walked every 30 frames at a low budget, and at once when the outfit changes. Texture priority boosts still cover every worn object every frame. 0 = the old lap-level settle (any one pending object kept every worn object re-ingested every frame).

CPU: write the own avatar's wearable visual params into the avatar only while it can matter (appearance morph running, a wearable changed, appearance editor open) plus every 32 frames, instead of every frame. 0 = every frame (LL behaviour).

Vulkan CPU: the easing visibility / camera distance stamped on worn attachments each frame (it only decides whether a scripted local move of the attachment glides) comes from the wearer -- one position per avatar per frame, frustum test on a sphere covering avatar and attachment -- instead of recomputing every attachment's object position. 0 = per-attachment object position.

Vulkan CPU: ingest-sweep pre-signature. A settled static object whose cheap pre-signature (volume, detail, load state, LOD, TE/face counts, GPU LOD band, LOD distance ratio) is unchanged skips the heavy pre-steps (updateDistance/calcLOD, mesh setVolume, face-list resync); attachments, animesh, movers, flexis, sculpties and pending meshes stay heavy, edits clear the pre-signature, and every object gets a heavy visit every 4 laps. Mesh setVolume runs only when there is something to adopt. The sweep also idles while the camera moves as long as no LOD band changed. 0 = the old behaviour.

Vulkan: multiplier on the texture resolution the GPU cull requests for on-screen faces (0.25 - 4). 1 = one texel per screen pixel at the face's nearest point (the decode then rounds up to the next mip, so the shown mip is never magnified); 2 = one mip sharper, 0.5 = one mip softer. The texture memory budget still governs.

Vulkan texture residency: seconds a texture's on-screen demand is held before its image may shrink (mips dropped on the GPU) after it leaves view. Longer = fewer re-reads from the GPU-ready cache when the camera turns back, at the cost of VRAM held for unseen textures. Under texture pressure the hold is 0.25 s regardless. Default 2

Vulkan texture residency: while VRAM is not under pressure (no texture step, no VRAM ladder rung, no recent allocation failure), seconds a texture that left view keeps its resident size before its image may shrink to its target, so turning back costs no GPU-ready cache re-read. Bounded by the texture budget: when the held images' extra bytes do not fit, the ones longest out of view shrink first; under pressure the hold stops at once (RenderVKTexHoldSec applies). 0 = off. Default 300

Vulkan: per-frame time budget (ms) for the incremental texture residency scan (a rolling cursor over the shared texture images; demand hold, decode demand, per-bias budget sums). A full lap takes as many frames as the budget needs.
Vulkan: per-frame CPU budget (ms) for new/upgraded texture image uploads; leftovers carry to later frames
Vulkan: per-frame CPU budget (ms) for re-checking existing materials' texture bindings (sliced walk)

Vulkan: evaluate other avatars' animation on the GPU (keyframe sampling, LL's pose blend, joint hierarchy -> joint world table; clean_anim.comp). The motion controller bookkeeping and procedural motions stay on the CPU. Off = LL's CPU path for every avatar.

Vulkan GPU animation: an animesh worn as an attachment by a GPU-animated avatar takes its root from the wearer's attachment joint as the GPU evaluated it THIS frame (clean_anim.comp second dispatch), instead of the CPU's readback copy of that joint (a few frames old: the animesh trailed the body in fast animations). Off = CPU root (A/B). Live.

Debug: every 120 frames log (VKAnim) each attached animesh's frame alignment with its wearer: order_lag (frames the wearer's skeleton was behind when the animesh placed itself, want 0), gpu_follow (root from the wearer's GPU joint this frame), cpu_attach_rb_age (age of the CPU's readback copy of the attachment point). The same readout shows in the DebugAnimatedObjects hover text ("attach align"). Live.

Vulkan GPU animation validation: every 300 frames up to 4 GPU-animated avatars also run LL's full CPU path from the same pre-blend pose, and the GPU joint world matrices are diffed against it (log tag VKAnimCmp).

Vulkan GPU animation (#257): reuse each GPU-animated avatar's cached pose-export structure (per joint, the ordered joint states LL's pose blender would blend) while its motion set, priorities and joint states are unchanged, skipping LLPoseBlender::addMotion / exportAndClear; only weights, keyframe times and procedural values are re-read each frame. Off = full export every frame (A/B: SECTIONS counters av_animExportFull / av_animExportIncr / animExportUs / animMotionUs, VKAnim "pose export" log line).

Debug for RenderVKAnimIncremental: about 1 in 8 cached pose exports per frame also run LL's full addMotion + export path; the blender calls and the resulting GPU blend inputs are compared bitwise, the full result is used, and mismatches are logged (tag VKAnimIncr, at most once per second; counters animVerify / animVerifyMismatch).
Vulkan: skip pre-skinning and drawing rigged meshes / worn attachments of avatars whose padded animated bounds (and sun-swept shadow volume) are outside the view frustum.
Vulkan: render planar mirrors (objects flagged Mirror, LL hero reflection probes) when RenderMirrors is on. The nearest visible mirror gets a reflected-view capture each frame.

Vulkan (#860; needs ray tracing and deferred lighting): RAY-TRACED MIRRORS. On: the selected mirror (RenderVKMirrors) is no longer rendered a second time from the reflected camera; instead every screen pixel the mirror covers casts one perfect-mirror ray at the full render resolution, lit like the RT reflections (sun / moon with a shadow ray, local lights, projector shadow rays per RenderVKRTMirrorsHitShadowRays, probes at the hit, sky on a miss), with avatars and worn attachments when the mirror is Dynamic (as the planar capture). Cost follows the mirror's on-screen size instead of a full scene render. Known gaps vs the planar capture: particles are not reflected (not in the ray-tracing scene); alpha-blended surfaces seen in the mirror are lit cheaply (ambient + unshadowed sun, up to 4 layers); no glow. Falls back to the planar capture while ray tracing stands down (VRAM pressure / RT budget), on cards without ray tracing, and in snapshots. Off (default) = the planar capture (A/B). Live. GPU timers: g_mirror_rt (c_mirror_rt on the async queue) vs the planar c_mirror; VKMirror log line on each mode change

Vulkan (RenderVKRTMirrors): the longest mirror ray, in metres (1 .. 4096). A ray that hits nothing within it shows the sky along its direction. Longer = farther scenery in the mirror, slower rays outdoors. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTMirrors): the most projector shadow rays a mirror ray's hit may cast (0 .. 4; the brightest ray-traced projector shares there get one, the rest light the reflection unshadowed). Default 4: projector shadows in a mirror look like the main view's under all but the densest stage rigs. Lower = cheaper under many shadowed projectors. Live

Vulkan: gate the planar mirror capture on a hardware occlusion query of the mirror's probe box against the main view's opaque depth (read back a frame slot later, no stall). While the selected mirror is fully occluded its capture is skipped. FALSE = always capture (A/B).
Vulkan: mirror capture resolution as a fraction of the window (0.25 - 1). Lower is cheaper but softer.

Vulkan texture residency: the highest global texture mip bias (each step halves texture resolution) the VRAM budget or pressure mode may apply WITHOUT an actual allocation failure. The per-process heap budget shrinks while another GPU-heavy application (e.g. a game alt-tabbed to) holds VRAM; uncapped, that drove every texture to thumbnail size. A real out-of-memory still allows up to 7

RAM (#698): emergency reserve -- system memory held back (committed) and freed on the first failed allocation, so the failing job's cleanup, logging and the next frames have headroom. Re-acquired after memory has been comfortable for 20 s. 0 = no reserve. Max 1024.
RAM (#698): how many times a decode / mesh load that failed for lack of memory is retried (with 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s backoff) before it is dropped and logged. A dropped asset is eligible again later.

RAM (#698): after an allocation failure, the memory governor treats memory as CRITICAL for this many seconds (extended by each further failure): decode and cache budgets drop to their floors and retained CPU texture copies are trimmed at once. Restores on its own.

Debug (#698): system-memory fault injection -- every Nth hooked allocation (image decode, mesh unpack, clean mesh decode, mesh cache read, VK store fill) fails as if out of memory (0 = off). Tests that running out of RAM retries / drops instead of crashing.

Debug (#595): Vulkan fault injection -- every Nth runtime device-memory allocation fails with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY (0 = off). Soft (degradable) requests only unless SLVkInjectAllocFailHard is on. Tests that running out of video memory degrades instead of crashing.

Debug (#697): Vulkan fault injection for the non-allocation out-of-memory paths -- every Nth call at an instrumented site (world frame vkEndCommandBuffer / vkQueueSubmit2, vkCreateImageView of soft images, soft descriptor set allocation) returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY without calling the driver (0 = off). Tests that a dropped frame / skipped resource is survived.
Debug (#595): SLVkInjectAllocFail also fails HARD (required) allocations -- this aborts by design; it finds runtime allocation sites that are still fatal.

Vulkan (#403): share the GPU with other Slipstream viewers running on it. Each viewer publishes its video memory use to a small file in the user app dir (vram_peers) and sizes its own automatic budget to a fair share of the card, borrowing room the others don't use and giving it back when they need it. Temporary and automatic: no setting is changed. Off = each viewer sizes itself from the OS budget alone (on Windows that lets two viewers oversubscribe the card and page).

Vulkan texture compression: textures are block-compressed on the GPU when they upload, cutting texture video memory 4-8x. 0 Off (uncompressed RGBA8), 1 High quality (BC7, best of modes 6/5/1 per block), 2 Balanced (BC7, fast mode 6/5 encoder), 3 Max savings (BC1 for opaque colour at 4 bits per texel, BC3 for alpha), 4 Adaptive (per texture: BC1 / BC3 where the encoder measured it good -- RenderVKTexAdaptiveMinPSNR -- else BC7 high quality; avatar textures BC7; BC1 / BC3 for textures shown below full resolution, RenderVKTexAdaptiveReducedCheap; decided only when a texture uploads, never re-encoded because the camera moved). Alpha-less normal maps use BC5 at every level. Media, small and light/particle/water/sky textures stay uncompressed. Textures up to RenderVKTexSmallHQDim texels always use the High quality encoder (except at Max savings, where they get the per-texture choice). Live: resident textures re-encode progressively, no restart. Set once automatically (first launch of a version with the setting, or a new graphics card): Adaptive on every card that supports BC compression (version 1 set High quality on cards with 16 GB or less and Off above; users who never picked a level move to Adaptive once); never changed automatically again (RenderVKTexCompressionDefaultApplied)

Testing aid (#675): run the Vulkan 1.2 + extensions fallback (VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering, VK_KHR_synchronization2, VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state, SPIR-V 1.5 shaders) even on a device that supports Vulkan 1.3. Not saved; set it on the command line (--set RenderVKForceApi12 1) or with the environment variable SLIPSTREAM_VK_FORCE_API12=1. Requires a restart

Which graphics card Slipstream renders on: "auto" (default: the most capable type that meets the requirements -- discrete, then integrated) or the stable id of a Vulkan device as listed in Preferences > Graphics > Advanced (the device UUID, or vendor-device id when the driver reports none). If the chosen card is missing or does not meet the requirements Slipstream falls back to Automatic for that run and tells you; the setting is kept. Requires a restart

Vulkan texture compression: version of the one-time hardware default of RenderVKTextureCompression already applied (0 = never). Internal marker; the default is applied again only on a graphics card change or when this version is raised

Vulkan texture compression: the RenderVKTextureCompression level the one-time hardware default last wrote (99 = never). Internal: a level equal to it counts as not chosen by the user, so a later default change can still reach it

Vulkan texture compression: images whose largest side (at upload) is at most this many texels always use the High quality BC7 encoder at Balanced and Adaptive (they cost little memory and are where the faster formats fail); at Max savings they get the per-texture content choice. 0 disables the rule

Vulkan texture compression: GPU time per frame the texture encoder aims for. The per-frame encode budget (RenderVKTexEncodeBudgetMP) and re-encodes per pass (RenderVKTexReencodePerPass) are scaled down from their caps when the measured encode time runs over this, and back up when well under. 0 = no adaptation (the caps are used as-is)

Vulkan texture compression, Adaptive level: a texture keeps BC1 (opaque) / BC3 (alpha) only when that encoding measured at least this PSNR in dB against the original, its smooth (gradient) areas at least this + RenderVKTexAdaptiveSmoothMarginDB, and no more than 1% of its blocks have a visible error; otherwise it is stored BC7 high quality. Higher = more textures on BC7 (more memory, fewer artefacts). Applies at each texture's next upload; measures are kept, so changing it re-measures nothing

Vulkan texture compression, Adaptive level: extra PSNR (dB) BC1 / BC3 must reach over a texture's smooth blocks (gradients, skin, sky: where BC1 bands) above RenderVKTexAdaptiveMinPSNR, when smooth blocks are at least 5% of the texture

Vulkan texture compression, Adaptive level: textures the residency system uploads below their full resolution (small or far on screen) use BC1 / BC3 whatever their content verdict; back at full resolution they follow the verdict. Off = the verdict applies at every size

Vulkan texture compression: remember per-texture facts across sessions in the cache folder (vk_texcomp_decisions.bin, keyed by texture UUID): the Adaptive level's measurements, avatar textures, one-colour and unused-alpha textures -- textures measured once skip the measuring encode afterwards. Cleared with Clear Cache. Read at startup
Vulkan texture compression: textures (at their resident size) smaller than this many texels on a side stay uncompressed

Vulkan texture compression: megatexels encoded per frame at most (High quality BC7 counts 3x); a cap -- the encoder scales it down to hold RenderVKTexEncodeTargetMs on slower GPUs. New uploads beyond it go uncompressed and are re-encoded later; format switches continue next frame
Vulkan texture compression: device-local block scratch ring in MB (encoded blocks wait here for their copy into the texture; read at startup)
Vulkan texture compression: cap in MB of the reused pool of uncompressed staging images the encoder reads from (read at startup)
Vulkan texture compression: resident textures re-encoded per frame at most after a RenderVKTextureCompression change; a cap, scaled like RenderVKTexEncodeBudgetMP (RenderVKTexEncodeTargetMs)

Vulkan: cut-out (alpha mask) textures such as grass, leaves, fences and hair keep the same amount of solid area in their smaller, distant versions, so they no longer thin out or let layers behind show through with distance. Changing it re-uploads the affected textures over the next few seconds

Vulkan diagnostic: log whether the faces of a selected object are cut-out (alpha mask) surfaces that get the distance-preserving texture treatment, and every 30 seconds list the textures it was applied to

Vulkan: textures whose whole image is one colour are stored as a single texel (lossless). 0 off, 1 only once the full-size image was seen to be one colour, 2 also when the sharpest decode so far is one colour (re-checked if a sharper decode arrives)
Vulkan: size (MB) of the persistent host-visible staging ring texture uploads sub-allocate from (uploads that don't fit use a dedicated buffer). Takes effect on restart.

Vulkan: projector (spot light) shadows. 0 off, 1 shadow maps (atlas, RenderVKProjShadow*), 2 ray traced: one shadow ray per pixel per shadowed projector against the scene TLAS, no shadow-map atlas rendered (RenderVKRTProjShadowMax / RenderVKRTShadowSoftness / RenderVKRTShadowBias). 2 needs the ray tracing foundation (RenderVKRayTracing + VK_KHR_ray_query at startup); without it 2 falls back to 1 (logged once). Switchable live. Also requires RenderShadowDetail >= 2 (LL: sun + projector shadows).

Vulkan: maximum projectors shadowed per frame (1-32), picked by brightness x apparent size with hysteresis. The atlas is sized for max(this, 16) at startup (16: 128 MB, 32: 256 MB incl. the static cache); raising it past that needs a restart.
Vulkan: projector shadow cell size x4 in texels (cell = this / 4, 256-2048; 8 cells per row; tile = 1, 1/2 or 1/4 cell by screen coverage). Restart to apply.
Vulkan: a cached projector shadow tile is re-rendered at least every N frames even if nothing in its cone changed (safety net).
Vulkan: projector shadow tiles whose cone holds an avatar refresh their avatar layer every N frames (1 = every frame; cheap: cached static depth copy + rigged draws).
Vulkan: a MOVING projector (e.g. stage lights) re-renders its shadow tile at most every N frames (1 = every frame). Between renders the shadow lags the light slightly but stays consistent.
Vulkan: projector shadow receiver offset along the surface normal, in shadow-texel footprints (x (0.5 + grazing)). Raise if lit faces show acne; lower if light leaks right behind thin casters.
Vulkan: projector shadow receiver offset toward the light, in shadow-texel footprints. Large values let light leak through thin walls right in front of the receiver.

Vulkan (#567): a moved-queue pose refresh invalidates the projector shadow tiles around the object only when it actually changed the object's instance pose (0 = every refresh invalidates, the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan (#567): cached projector shadow tiles are invalidated by the instance store itself -- new, released and shadow-relevantly re-registered instances (geometry, routing, mask material, static pose; not colour or UVs), at the old and the new place -- instead of by every changed-object re-registration (a colour cycle re-rendered every tile around it). 0 = the old changed-queue spheres. Live.

Vulkan (#567): while the frame is slower than RenderVKRiggedLodTargetFPS (the same soft load state as RenderVKProjShadowDynamicBudget), at most this many MOVING projectors whose tile is not a full cell re-render their shadow per frame, stalest x most influential first (projectors lighting the area near the camera always do); the rest lag a few frames. 0 = no limit. Live.

Vulkan (#567): projector shadow tiles that re-render their static casters in the same frame are culled this many at a time in ONE GPU cull (each tile keeps its own frustum and caster-size test; the result is the same as culling them one by one) instead of one cull plus a pipeline drain per tile. 2..8; 0 or 1 = every tile culled alone (the old path). A tile whose casters overflow its share of the batch is re-rendered alone a few frames later. Live.

Vulkan (#567): at most this many projector shadow tiles re-render their static casters per frame for a SOFT reason (something changed in the cone, the change list overflowed, the periodic safety refresh), stalest x most influential first; the rest keep their cached shadow and re-render over the next frames. Spreads bursts (every tile dirtied at once) over several frames. Projectors lighting the area near the camera (full-cell tiles), new tiles and moved lights are never held. 0 = no limit. Live.

Vulkan (#567): a projector whose frustum moved less than this many shadow-tile texels since its cached tile was rendered keeps the tile (interpolation drift / float noise); the shadow lags by under this much. 0 = any change re-renders. Live.
