Vulkan (#567): moving objects, GPU target-omega spinners and worn attachments are DYNAMIC shadow casters: cached projector shadow tiles keep them out of their static layer and redraw them in the per-frame overlay, so a moving object no longer re-renders every tile around it. An object rejoins the static layer after being still this many seconds. 0 = off (every move re-renders the static tiles around it, the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan (#567): with cached sun / moon cascades (RenderVKShadowUpdate 1 or 2) and the dynamic-caster split (RenderVKShadowMoverSettleSecs > 0), a cascade's static layer re-renders only when needed -- the view outgrew it, the light turned by RenderVKShadowLightMoveTexels texels, a static change touched it, or RenderVKShadowCacheRefreshFrames passed -- instead of every 1/2/4/8 (or 4/16/32) frames; moving objects, avatars and particles are drawn on top every frame. No effect in Realtime (0). Live.
Vulkan (#567): event-driven cascades re-render when the sun / moon direction has turned enough to move a point at the cascade's reach by this many shadow texels since its last render. Live.
Vulkan (#567): safety net -- an event-driven cascade re-renders at least every N frames (catches anything no event reports, e.g. a mesh LOD that streamed in). Live.

Vulkan (#825, frame pacing): with the event-driven cascade cache (RenderVKShadowEventCache), a far sun cascade (2 / 3) re-rendered for a static change, the light's slow drift or the safety refresh waits while another far cascade re-renders (or the scheduled reflection probe filters) that frame, at most this many frames -- one far cascade per frame instead of two stacked; projector tiles due for the same reasons wait one frame behind a far cascade. View outgrowth, light jumps and invalidations always render at once; cascades 0 / 1 are never held. 0 = off (the old stacking). Live.

Vulkan diagnostic (#825): every 5 s log (VKShadowReg) what produced the instance-registration spheres that re-render cached shadow cascades / projector tiles (shadowEvChgRegister): spheres per second and by camera distance, the reasons (new / released / pose / spin / LOD group / flags + bits / bounds / material, and how many the shadow-relevance rules dropped) and the top emitting objects. Off = no cost. Live.

Vulkan (#567, diagnostics): with RenderVKGpuTimers on, split c_shadows / c_projshadow into per-cascade and per-tile sub-marks (c_sun_cull, g_sun_draw, g_sun_overlay, c_proj_records, c_proj_cull, g_proj_static, g_proj_copy, g_proj_dyn...). Off by default. Live.
Vulkan: cull shadow casters whose shadow cannot land in the visible part of their cascade (view-slice planes the light can't cross), and sub-texel casters.

Vulkan: shadow casters smaller than this many shadow-map texels of their cascade are skipped (0 = keep all): static and moving casters, worn attachments and avatars (by the avatar's bounds), per cascade. Live.
Vulkan: every ~600 frames, compare the GPU-generated skin palettes against the CPU reference math for up to 64 skins and log the max difference (VKSkinPal). Validation aid for the GPU palette path.
Vulkan diagnostic: log the touch SurfaceInfo (face, ST, UV, position, normal, binormal) sent with every ObjectGrab / GrabUpdate / DeGrab (VKTouch).

Vulkan: on a region crossing, re-base the clean pipeline's agent-space state (instances, particles, SSR history) by LL's origin shift. Off = old behavior (previous sim's objects overlay the new one until re-registered), for A/B.

#568: incremental teardown of a removed region (dropped from the ring, DisableSimulator, a left neighbour). The region is delisted at once; its objects are then killed in slices of this many ms per frame (at least one object), then its object cache is saved, then it is deleted -- one step per frame. 0 = the old synchronous teardown in the frame it is removed (A/B).

#568: per-frame time budget (ms, at least one per frame) for object cache I/O completions -- a region's cache read landing, which sends the region handshake reply the simulator waits on before it streams that region's objects. They run on the cache's own queue every frame (login included). 0 = the shared main-loop work queue (old behaviour, A/B).

Vulkan (#568): keep the clean instance store in a stable render-world frame across region crossings. A crossing then only changes the frame offset: no instance is rewritten, re-boxed or re-uploaded (one GPU pass moves the GPU rows), and cached shadow cascades, projector tiles, TAA history and the ray-tracing TLAS are re-based instead of reset. Off = the legacy per-crossing rebase of every instance (A/B).

Vulkan (#568): with RenderVKStableWorldFrame, re-anchor the render-world frame on the agent region once it is farther than this (m, along x or y) from the anchor, keeping stored positions near the camera within float precision (2048 m: below 0.12 mm). A re-anchor is a CPU-only pass over the instance store (no GPU work). 0 = re-anchor on every crossing.

Vulkan: moving (active) objects are drawn at LL's eased drawable pose -- the same pose the seated avatar and the camera follow -- instead of the raw network/interpolated object position. Off reproduces the old vehicle stutter (#96). Live.

Vulkan: early (async) damped moves -- the seat a driver sits on, every avatar, the tracked camera focus object -- get this frame's visibility before LL's easing runs, so they are damped like LL/Firestorm instead of snapping to each interpolated network pose. Off reproduces the unsmoothed vehicle handling (#180). Live.

Vulkan: also use the GPU target-omega spin for physical, moving or sat-on linksets (old behaviour). Off (default): those take LL's eased drawable pose like Firestorm, so a turning vehicle's root and its scripted children (steering wheel, gauges) are smoothed (#180). Live for newly posed objects.

Vulkan: while seated on an object (else for the selected linkset), log one VKVehicleDiag line per frame (frame dt, root pose vs the uploaded GPU pose, root eased-vs-target and instance-vs-eased rotation, GPU spin, moved-queue slice, avatar and camera offset in the seat frame) plus up to 8 'child' lines for animated children (instance vs eased and eased vs target rotation, refreshed this frame). Diagnostic for vehicle stutter (#96) and snappy scripted motion (#180).

Vulkan: every 2 s, log (VKPhysicsDiag) the avatar-physics collision volumes (LEFT_PEC, RIGHT_PEC, BELLY, BUTT) of your avatar, or of the avatar named in RenderVKDumpAvatar: position, default, default + all volume morphs, joint override, position before overrides, whether an animation holds it, and the physics params' current offsets. Diagnostic for #207.

Vulkan: every 2 s, log a VKMoverDiag summary of the moved-object queue (backlog, drained per frame) and, for the objects within 32 m that moved most, how often their GPU pose actually changed per second against the frame rate, with their velocity (LL interpolates only objects that have one). Diagnostic for choppy scripted motion.
Vulkan: log (throttled, VKHudDiag) what the clean pipeline does with HUD prim pose and colour/alpha changes. Diagnostic for HUDs that don't update.
Vulkan: hide / fade in-world name tags and hover text whose anchor point is behind world geometry (one scene-depth test per label, as LL's depth-tested tags). Off: in-world text always draws on top
Default Alt+Shift shortcuts (e.g. Alt+Shift+H, hide HUDs) are moved to Ctrl+Alt+Shift, for keyboards where Alt+Shift switches the input language. Your own custom bindings are never changed (#948)

Vulkan diagnostics: log HUD hover text (llSetText on HUD prims) every 2 s -- how many are queued / visible, and for each drawn line its HUD position, projected window coordinates, depth and the matrices used

Vulkan: coarse shading for the alpha-blend pass (VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate). 0 = auto (2x2 at 1440p and up, 2x1 below while a temporal resolve runs: TAA, FSR or DLSS; every pixel shaded when none does), 1 = every pixel shaded, 2 = one shade per 2x1 pixels, 4 = one per 2x2. Coverage, depth and blending stay per pixel; TAA resolves the coarse pattern. Dense stacked foliage at high resolution is the target. Switchable live; ignored on GPUs without per-pipeline shading rates

Vulkan: content-adaptive coarse shading for the OPAQUE lit pass (VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate attachment, VRS tier 2). 0 = auto (adaptive from 1440p up, off below), 1 = off (every pixel shaded), 2 = adaptive at any resolution, 3 = force 2x2 everywhere (cost bound for A/B, visibly coarse). Per screen tile (8-32 px, the GPU's rate tile) a compute pass (GPU sub-mark c_vrs_rate) picks 1x1, 2x1, 1x2 or 2x2 from last frame's reprojected luminance gradients, motion and depth edges. Coverage, depth and edges stay per pixel; alpha-mask (cutout) faces, rigged meshes, alpha, water and the HUD always shade every pixel. Needs the depth pre-pass split (TAA, SSAO or the RT shadow mask on). RenderVKLitDebugMask 4096 shows the rates. Switchable live; ignored on GPUs without the rate attachment

Vulkan opaque VRS (RenderVKOpaqueShadingRate): Weber threshold of the luminance-gradient error per tile direction (perceptual 0..1 luminance step, relative to the tile's mean + 0.05). Higher = coarser shading on more of the screen. Live
Vulkan opaque VRS: threshold relaxation per render pixel of motion per frame beyond the first (capped at 3x). Moving content tolerates coarser shading. 0 = motion ignored. Live
Vulkan opaque VRS: a tile whose receivers span more than 1 + this depth ratio (a silhouette over far background) stays at full rate. 0 = no depth-edge guard. Live

Vulkan, cost A/B for the lit world fragment shader (read the g_lit_static GPU sub-mark with RenderVKGpuTimers on). Sum of bits, live, main view only (probe / mirror captures always shade in full); 0 = normal. 1 local lights off, 2 projector shadows off (visibility 1), 4 reflection probes off, 8 probes: default probe only, 16 SSR off, 32 sun/moon shadow off, 64 RT shadow mask: nearest texel (no depth-aware 4-tap upsample), 128 haze / water fog off, 256 normal / ORM / emissive maps off, 512 legacy shiny env off, 1024 SSAO read off, 2048 planar mirror off, 4096 shading-rate overlay (2x1 red, 1x2 green, 2x2 blue), 8192 PBR environment specular as before #872 (no normalization to the diffuse ambient, unfiltered sky fallback). Also affects the alpha and water passes, which share the lighting code

Vulkan (roadmap phase 2): master switch for the queue-overlap changes -- RenderVKOverlapMaskAO, RenderVKOverlapGodRays, RenderVKOverlapTlas, RenderVKOverlapParticles, RenderVKProbePrivateCull, RenderVKProbeEarly. Off = the pre-phase-2 barrier placement and pass order exactly, for A/B and bisecting. No visual difference either way

Vulkan (phase 2, needs RenderVKPreciseBarriers): SSAO and the ray-traced shadow mask share one depth transition after the depth pre-pass and run interleaved (trace beside SSAO, temporal beside blur H, spatial beside blur V) instead of two serial chains; the mask's history copies move ahead of the pre-pass. Off = sequential. Occlusion culling forces sequential

Vulkan (restart required): persist the compiled graphics / compute pipelines to vk_pipeline_cache.bin in the cache directory, so later launches skip the ~20 s world-pipeline compile. The file is validated (viewer version, GPU, driver, pipeline-cache UUID, CRC) and discarded on any mismatch. Off = compile everything every launch (an in-memory cache is still used within the session). To purge it: Clear Cache in Preferences, or delete vk_pipeline_cache.bin from the cache directory while the viewer is closed

Vulkan (#642 cluster LOD, experimental): draw rigged mesh as clusters with a continuous, screen-error-driven level of detail (a DAG of meshlets streamed in fixed pages) instead of the whole-mesh rigged LOD controller (#561 / #613). Off (default) = nothing of the cluster path exists and every current path is unchanged; the old controller also stays the path for GPUs that cannot run this one. Takes effect live. The GPU features its faster tiers use are enabled at startup whenever the GPU has them and they are inert while unused (RenderVKClusterDeviceFeatures), so switching it on mid-session runs those tiers at once; only device-generated commands and the partitioned TLAS need it on at startup (the tier log line says so). Tiers and stats: the 'Cluster LOD' and 'CLOD' log lines.

Vulkan cluster LOD (#743, testing): caps every cluster capability (raster: 0 draw-indirect with vertex pulling, 1 uint8 indexed draw-indirect, 2 mesh shaders; command generation: 0 draw count, 1 device-generated commands; uploads: 0 staging copies, 1 indirect copies, 2 GPU decompression; ray tracing: 0 per-cut BLAS, 1 cluster acceleration structures, 2 + partitioned TLAS; atomics: 0 32-bit, 1 64-bit) at this tier so every fallback can be tested on the newest card. -1 = the best each capability supports on this GPU. Live (the next frame uses the new tiers; every change logs the 'Cluster LOD tiers' line); the startup log shows the native tiers

Vulkan cluster LOD (#743, startup): which cluster LOD GPU extensions the device enables while RenderVKClusterLOD is off at startup, so turning it on mid-session can use them without a restart. 0 = none (the device exactly as before cluster LOD: use it if a driver misbehaves); 1 = those that change nothing while unused (uint8 indices, indirect copies, GPU decompression, cluster acceleration structures, 64-bit atomics); 2 = also mesh shaders (the extension is inert, but the renderer then makes its draw descriptor set visible to mesh / task shaders). RenderVKClusterLOD on at startup enables everything the GPU has regardless (including device-generated commands and the partitioned TLAS, which are startup-only). Restart to change

Vulkan cluster LOD (#642): the pixel tolerance of the cluster cut -- a cluster is drawn when its simplification error projected on screen is at most this many pixels and its parent's is more. 1 = visually identical to full detail at that distance. The tolerance controller (#749) raises it under GPU-time or VRAM pressure (2 / 4 / 8). Range 0.05 .. 1024: a very large value (e.g. 1024) forces the coarsest DAG levels, down to a handful of triangles per face, for testing

Vulkan cluster LOD (#749): the tighter pixel tolerance for protected avatars (your own and the nearest), instead of an exemption list. Range 0.05 .. 1024 (set it as high as RenderVKClusterTolerancePx to force the coarsest levels on protected avatars too)

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748): the pixel tolerance of the ray-tracing cut (coarser than the raster one, with hysteresis: a cut change costs an acceleration-structure rebuild on GPUs without cluster acceleration structures). Range 0.05 .. 1024

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748): what ray tracing traces for the meshes the cluster path draws. 0 = the legacy per-LOD / rigged BLAS even with cluster LOD on (the fallback for first-generation RT cards); 1 = the cluster RT cut (cluster acceleration structures where the GPU has them, else per-cut BLAS rebuilds; RenderVKClusterForceTier tests each); 2 = as 1, and on GPUs with partitioned TLAS (VK_NV_partitioned_acceleration_structure) the TLAS is partitioned for the session (read at startup: changing 1 <-> 2 needs a restart) Default 1 (2026-10-14): 2 is EXPERIMENTAL and off by default -- its partitions were filled in instance-id (arrival) order, so every partition's bounds overlapped most rays and traversal was far slower (god rays 35x, RT shadow mask 6x at Baltimare vs 1). Since 2026-10-22 the partitions are SPATIAL (RenderVKClusterPTLASPartition 1, grid cells of RenderVKClusterPTLASCellM); keep 2 opt-in until a fixed-camera A/B against 1 shows it no slower.

Vulkan cluster LOD ray tracing, partitioned TLAS (RenderVKClusterRT 2 at startup only): how instances are assigned to partitions. 0 = by instance id (the original; ids are arrival order, so every partition spans the scene: rays visit most partitions -- measured 3-35x slower traces, 2026-10-14). 1 = SPATIAL (default): the grid cell of the instance's translation (RenderVKClusterPTLASCellM) hashed into up to 1024 partitions; disabled records, instances larger than a cell and a full partition's overflow go to the global partition. A change re-creates the PTLAS (one full write). Logged at creation and on the 10 s Cluster RT line (writes to global).

Vulkan cluster LOD ray tracing, spatial partitioned TLAS (RenderVKClusterPTLASPartition 1): the grid cell edge in metres (8 .. 1024). Instances whose largest axis scale exceeds it go to the global partition. A change re-creates the PTLAS.

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748): the RT cut of a mesh is evaluated from a reference camera position that follows the real camera only once it moved more than this fraction of the distance to the mesh, so the RT cut changes far less often than the raster cut (fewer acceleration-structure rebuilds, steadier ray-traced shadows). 0 = follow every frame

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748): on GPUs without cluster acceleration structures (per-cut BLAS tier), the most per-mesh BLAS rebuilds per frame for changed RT cuts (the previous BLAS stays in use until its replacement is ready)

Vulkan cluster LOD (#747 / #748): avatars drawn by the cluster path cast and receive ray-traced shadows (and show in ray-traced probe captures) from their cluster cut -- the cut the main view draws, skinned every frame -- instead of their legacy rigged geometry (1, default). 0 = they keep the legacy rigged BLAS (the receiver lift RenderVKClusterShadowLiftScale then hides the LOD mismatch). An avatar whose cluster RT data is not ready in a frame keeps its legacy BLAS for that frame. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748): static meshes drawn by the cluster path (RenderVKClusterStatic 2) are ray traced on their own cluster cut (1, default: the most important ones that fit the cluster RT memory -- the rest keep their legacy BLAS, which they trace at their legacy LOD). 0 = every static mesh keeps its legacy BLAS in RT (A/B: RT traversal / memory of the static cluster path). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748 static pass): the cluster BLAS of static meshes traced on their cluster cut are persistent (on, default): each lives in a heap block and is rebuilt only when its RT cut or one of its CLAS changes -- a still camera builds none, and while a new cut is not ready the previous BLAS keeps tracing. Off = every static cluster BLAS is rebuilt every frame with the rigged ones (A/B). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (static cut perf pass): the RT cut of a static mesh on the cluster path is never finer than the raster draws it -- its tolerance is the larger of RenderVKClusterRTTolerancePx and this x RenderVKClusterTolerancePx x the cluster LOD pressure level's multiple (x1 / 2 / 4 / 8; the level, not its easing, so cuts change only when the level steps). 1 (default) = the main view's rule; larger = coarser RT statics than the raster; 0 = the fixed RT tolerance (the old behaviour, A/B). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (static cut perf pass): the budget of the static CLAS arena of the cluster RT path, MB. 0 (default) = a quarter of the cluster RT memory (RenderVKClusterRTMemoryMB), 64 .. 512 MB. The static admission threshold keeps the most important statics inside it (the rest trace their legacy BLAS). Before it the arena took all the room the cluster RT memory left (about 1.1 GB at a crowded venue). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): 1 = the RT cut and the rigged acceleration structures of avatars on the cluster path that never self-shadow in RT (the no-self-shadow throttle tag: far / small on screen, never your own) follow their own schedule; every other avatar stays exact every frame, and with none of them traced the cadence costs nothing: each avatar re-selects its RT cut on its distance band's period (RenderVKClusterRTRigPeriod*), copies it forward in between and keeps its CLAS (its RT pose lags by at most that period); mid / far avatars trace a coarser cut (RenderVKClusterRTRigTol*) and rebuild only the clusters whose pose moved. 0 = the A/B: every avatar re-selected and rebuilt every frame on the raster's cut (the behaviour before; default since the first cut flickered self-shadows on untagged avatars). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): distance (m) under which an avatar is in the NEAR band (its period RenderVKClusterRTRigPeriodNear, multiplier RenderVKClusterRTRigTolNear). A 10 percent dead band around each edge. Live
Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): distance (m) from which an avatar is in the FAR band; between NearM and this: MID. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): frames between RT cut selections of a NEAR avatar (1 = every frame: the raster's cut, rebuilt every frame unless still). Capped by RenderVKClusterRTRigMaxStale. Live
Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): frames between RT cut selections of a MID avatar (staggered across avatars). Its RT pose lags by up to this many frames. Live
Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): frames between RT cut selections of a FAR avatar (staggered across avatars). Its RT pose lags by up to this many frames. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): RT cut tolerance of a NEAR avatar, as a multiple of the raster's (1 = the raster's cut: the traced surface is the rasterized one, no self-shadow mismatch, shared welded skinning). 1 .. 64. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): RT cut tolerance of a MID avatar, as a multiple of the raster's (above 1: fewer clusters to skin and build, own unwelded skinning; only for avatars that never self-shadow in RT, and capped at 0.1 m past the raster cut's error so their receivers still recognise their own surface). 1 .. 64. Live
Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): RT cut tolerance of a FAR avatar, as a multiple of the raster's (see RenderVKClusterRTRigTolMid). 1 .. 64. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): the most frames an avatar's RT geometry may lag its pose: caps every period, and a cluster kept because its pose barely moved is rebuilt once its acceleration structure is this old. 1 .. 120. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1008 rigged RT cadence): a due mid / far avatar whose cut did not change rebuilds a cluster only when one of its vertices moved more than this fraction of the cut's own error at the avatar's distance since the cluster was built (0 = rebuild every cluster of a due avatar). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1011): the rigged RT cut's bookkeeping. 1 (default): the main view's cluster selection hands each avatar mesh's cut summary and the clusters' ranks to the RT build (no per-cluster re-gather, arena slots in a stable order) and the per-avatar arena admission runs in parallel. 0 = the A/B: the RT build re-gathers the shared cut itself and places clusters in arrival order. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1011): rigged cluster RT CLAS reuse (needs RenderVKClusterRTRigRank). 1 (default): an avatar whose RT cut did not change keeps its slots and the shared (welded) skinning, and a cluster's acceleration structure is rebuilt only when its vertices moved: past RenderVKClusterRTRigReuseEps for avatars that shadow themselves, past RenderVKClusterRTRigPoseEps of the cut's error (at most RenderVKClusterRTRigMaxStale frames) for avatars tagged no-self-shadow. 0 = the A/B: every cluster of a changed avatar is rebuilt every frame. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#1011): metres a self-shadowing avatar's cluster vertices may move before its RT acceleration structure is rebuilt (RenderVKClusterRTRigReuse). Default 0.00002 (20 um, float noise of the eye-relative skinning); clamped to 0.001. 0 = only bit-identical positions are reused. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (last step of the avatar migration): an avatar drawn by the cluster path whose LEGACY pre-skinned vertices nothing reads this frame -- shadow cascades, projector tiles, mirror and probe faces draw it from the shared rig cut, the GPU pick from its clusters, RT traces its cluster cut (confirmed for a few frames), it is not selected, no wireframe -- gets no legacy pre-skin, weld, RT rig copy or legacy rigged BLAS, so skinning cost follows the cluster cut. Any consumer still on the legacy path keeps the whole legacy work for that avatar (never half). The CLOD A/B log line reports what was skipped and why avatars were kept. 0 = always run the legacy work (A/B). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#748): VRAM for the cluster ray-tracing structures (cluster acceleration structures, cluster BLAS, partitioned TLAS) and the per-cut BLAS. 0 = automatic: a third of the ray-tracing budget, 64 MB .. 3 GB (a share: small cards keep a small cap); manual values are clamped to 64 MB .. 3 GB

Vulkan cluster LOD (#746): VRAM for the cluster page pool (80 KB pages; the coarsest pages of every registered mesh stay resident, finer ones stream in on demand and are evicted least-recently-used). 0 = automatic from the VRAM budget. Capped below 4 GB
Vulkan cluster LOD (#746): the most cluster page data uploaded to the GPU per frame (MB). Pages not uploaded yet draw their coarser parent meanwhile, never a hole
Vulkan cluster LOD (#744): disk space for built cluster meshes (cache/clusterlod, one file per mesh face; least recently used out first). 0 = no disk cache (meshes are rebuilt every session)

Vulkan cluster LOD (#744): render-thread time per frame (ms, 0.25 .. 8) for the cluster mesh builder's bookkeeping -- finished builds and copying the source of newly admitted ones. The builds themselves (clusterize + DAG + pages) run on RenderVKClusterBuildThreads background threads at full speed, nearest avatars first, so a crowd's backlog drains in seconds without stalling the frame
Vulkan cluster LOD (#744): worker threads that build cluster meshes. 0 = automatic (a quarter of the CPU threads, at least 1)
Vulkan cluster LOD (#746): seconds a registered cluster mesh no visible instance uses keeps its GPU pages before they are freed (free on liveness)

Vulkan cluster LOD (#749): relative tolerance margin before a cut coarsens again (temporal stability under TAA / FSR): the LOD camera lags the camera by up to this x 2 m (and the projection allows for that distance, so detail is never lost), the projection scale coarsens only after falling this far. 0 = none

Vulkan cluster LOD (#745, debug view): 0 off, 1 colour by cluster, 2 colour by DAG level, 3 highlight clusters drawn as a fallback for a missing finer page (red; green = own level), 4 the cluster draw with its real materials, 5 seam view (#798): red = a cluster of a level that simplified the face's open border (the weld seam to the next mesh loses vertices there), orange = the same drawn as the fallback of a missing finer page, grey = border intact, 6 weld view (#798): per skinned cluster, grey = no weld candidate, green = candidates welded, cyan = every candidate already seamless (left alone, #798 no-op), yellow = some welded or seamless / some with no partner, red = candidates but none welded (no other mesh within RenderVKRigWeldDistance in the pairing space), blue = rejected by skin weights / max gap only. Any non-zero value also draws the selected clusters as an overlay in the G-buffer (rigged meshes of avatars on the cluster path skinned; those of avatars still on the legacy path in rest pose)

Vulkan cluster LOD weld probe (#798, one-shot; resets to 0): 1 = the avatar on the cluster path nearest the view centre (not yours), 2 = yours. Logs (ClusterWeldProbe) per mesh the weld candidates the legacy slot flags vs the ones the cluster builder flags, how many pair with another mesh at the rest pose / in bind space (a CPU replica of the weld rules), the nearest other-mesh distance of the unpaired ones, the pairs per mesh pair and a few near misses.

Vulkan cluster LOD RAM: while the cluster path owns rigged meshes, free the mesh store's CPU copy of a rigged mesh face once its cluster DAG is on disk (the .clod write landed); it is fetched back (re-decoded, or re-requested from the mesh repository) when legacy or a rebuild needs it. Off = keep every copy (new releases only; e.g. for RenderVKClusterWeldProbe). Live.

Vulkan cluster LOD (#798): while the cluster path owns rigged meshes, the creator LOD every rigged mesh loads, whatever its screen size (0 lowest .. 3 highest; the asset's highest when it has fewer). The cluster DAG built from it supplies every coarser level, so 3 costs download / RAM for the source, not draw detail; creators match the seams between meshes (body parts, clothing) on LOD 3 only -- a lower source leaves those seams unwelded. Legacy path: LL's screen-size LOD as before.

Vulkan cluster LOD (#747): avatars (rigged meshes) drawn by the cluster path in the main view. Per avatar, only when every one of its rigged meshes has a resident cluster mesh (never half cluster, half legacy). 0 never (rest-pose debug overlay only); 1 yes, whenever the cluster depth pre-pass pipelines exist for the raster tier in force (#749: the cluster draws are in the pre-pass, so motion vectors, SSAO and the RT shadow mask see them; without those pipelines only while nothing reads the main view's pre-pass per pixel); 2 always (A/B testing). Shadows, probes, mirror, RT and picking keep the legacy rigged path (their #749 cluster views are selection-only). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#747 / #1010): limit of the skinned cluster arena in MB. The arena holds the skinned vertices (+ previous positions for motion vectors) of the clusters in the current cut of the avatars drawn by the cluster path (~2.3 KB per cluster), allocated as the cut needs them, up to this limit. 0 = auto: 1/16 of the GPU's video memory budget (128 MB .. 4 GB). VRAM pressure lowers the effective limit temporarily (the setting is untouched). When a crowd's cut does not fit, the least important avatars (small on screen first, your own last) are drawn coarser, each avatar whole; if even the coarsest cuts do not fit, the least important avatars are hidden whole for that frame -- never some of an avatar's parts. Logged as "CLOD skin arena" every 10 s. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD rigged weld (#826): pair once, apply per frame. A character's weld pairs (made in its rest pose) are stored per skinned cluster vertex and re-applied every frame its pose changes -- no rest-pose evaluation, weld-grid insert or partner search -- until a cluster of it enters the cut, its rest row changes (shape, joint overrides, owner), a candidate has more than one partner mesh, or the pairing parameters change (then that character searches again, as before). 0 = every re-skinned character searches every frame (A/B). Logged on the CLOD skin line (pairs cached / invalid / searched). Live.

Vulkan cluster LOD skinning (2026-10-14): reuse a skinned cluster's arena slot (character space) while its character's pose is provably held (GPU animation held frame / static deform pose: LLCleanAnimStore::slotPoseClean, skin meta unchanged, a refresh every 64 frames) -- only clusters new to the cut are skinned (with RenderVKRigWeld: a held character with any new cluster is re-skinned whole, so its seams weld symmetrically). 0 = re-skin every cluster every frame (A/B). Logged in the CLOD skin line (reused / skinned, characters held). Live.

Vulkan cluster LOD rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld on the cluster cut): ceiling (65536-2097152) of the weld's entry list (one entry per cluster copy of every open-boundary vertex of the drawn avatars). The list follows the read-back demand below this ceiling (80 B per entry + 8 B of grid, in 64K-entry steps); an avatar whose candidates do not fit in a frame is not welded at all that frame (never half an avatar, which would light one side of a mesh join differently from the other). Logged in the CLOD skin line (weld demand / peak / cap). Live.

Vulkan cluster LOD (#747 / #611): simplification error factor for avatars with two or more cluster rigged meshes (layered body + clothing). 2 = each layer keeps half the pixel tolerance, so body and clothing errors together stay within one tolerance (poke-through between layers bounded by it). 1 = no layer protection. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD, rigged alpha-blend meshes (hair cards, lashes, sheer layers) on the cluster path: the largest pixel tolerance their cut may use. The GPU-pressure controller can raise the main tolerance to 8+ px; alpha meshes keep at most this (their instance tolerance scale is lowered), because a coarser level of thin cards / many small disconnected parts removes whole cards (thinner, patchier hair) long before it would show on an opaque surface. A pruned group renders only where its whole patch projects under this many pixels (2 px: a 5 cm card cluster at ~30 m at 1440p). The RT cut follows (same instance scale). 0 = no cap (the opaque tolerance). Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#747 fallback): ray-traced shadow receivers on an avatar drawn by the cluster path whose ray-traced geometry is still its LEGACY rigged BLAS that frame (RenderVKClusterRTRigged 0, RenderVKClusterRT 0, or its cluster RT data not ready) start their shadow rays this many times the cut's error bound (main tolerance x distance / px per metre) off the surface, so the legacy geometry never shadows the coarser surface on screen. Avatars traced on their cluster cut are not lifted (they cast from the surface the raster draws). 1 = the bound; 0 = off (hard-edged self-shadow patches return at high tolerances on legacy-traced avatars); up to 4. Live

Vulkan cluster LOD (#745): static (non-rigged) mesh faces on the cluster path. 0 off; 1 selection, streaming and stats run for them and RenderVKClusterDebug draws them as an overlay; 2 EXPERIMENTAL: the cluster path draws them in the depth pre-pass (#749: AO, RT shadow mask, motion vectors) and the deferred G-buffer, and the legacy main-view cull skips them (no GPU pick for them yet)

Vulkan cluster LOD (#749): the other passes that get a cluster selection of their static meshes (their own error metric and tolerance): bit 1 sun shadow cascades, 2 reserved (reflection probe faces: no cluster view until they draw cluster statics -- the selection-only view was removed as dead work, #748 perf pass), 4 the mirror. 0 = main view only. Whether those passes also DRAW the cluster path is RenderVKClusterViewDraw

Vulkan cluster LOD (#702 integration): the passes besides the main view that draw what the cluster path owns, instead of the legacy geometry. Bit 1 sun shadow cascades, 2 projector shadow tiles, 4 the mirror, 8 reflection-probe faces (CPU-scheduled dynamic captures), 16 the GPU cursor pick. Switched avatars come from ONE shared skinned cut (the main view's LOD, un-culled for the avatars those passes draw); cluster static meshes (RenderVKClusterStatic 2) from the cascades' / mirror's own selections (RenderVKClusterViews). A pass whose bit is off, or whose cluster data is not ready this frame, keeps its legacy draws for those objects (never half). Mirror / probes: plain-lit frames only (a ray-query lit frame keeps them legacy). 0 = main view only (the previous behaviour)
Vulkan cluster LOD (#745): cull clusters against the previous frame's Hi-Z pyramid in the main view (needs RenderVKOcclusion2Phase or RenderVKOcclusionCull, which build it)

Vulkan device-loss diagnostic (#845 / #917; restart required): create the device with robustBufferAccess and, where supported, VK_EXT_robustness2 (robustBufferAccess2, robustImageAccess2, nullDescriptor), so every pipeline's out-of-range or null descriptor reads return zero instead of faulting. If a device loss stops with this on, a descriptor read was out of range or unbound; if it persists, the fault is a raw device address or freed memory. Costs some GPU time. Logged at startup as 'debug robustness'

Vulkan async compute (#845 / #917; live): the scene depth (ATTACHMENT / READ_ONLY) and the scene HDR + glow (UNDEFINED -> GENERAL) layout transitions around the async SSAO / RT mask and deferred lighting segments are recorded on the graphics queue right before the fork and after the join, instead of inside the compute-only command buffers. On (default) = no attachment-compression transitions on a queue without a graphics engine (the Windows device losses with the async queue on); off = the previous in-segment barriers (A/B testing)

Vulkan (roadmap phase 3a; restart required): the second queue the async-compute work runs on. 0 = none (single queue, every resource EXCLUSIVE: the pre-phase-3 device), 1 = a dedicated compute-only queue family when the GPU has one (NVIDIA / AMD: the async-compute hardware queues; buffers and sampled / storage images are then created CONCURRENT across both families and barriers recorded for that queue drop their graphics stages), else a second queue of the graphics family, 2 = always a second queue of the graphics family (no CONCURRENT sharing; also allows RenderVKAsyncPost). At the default (1) with RenderVKAsyncCompute -1, the per-GPU automatic default may create no second queue (see RenderVKAsyncCompute); setting this to 0 or 2 disables that automatic default (to force the queue on, set RenderVKAsyncCompute to 1). Logged at startup as 'Async compute queue'

Vulkan (roadmap phase 3a): master switch for running compute work on the async compute queue (RenderVKAsyncComputeQueue) beside the graphics queue, with timeline-semaphore fork / join points. -1 (default) = automatic, per GPU architecture, decided at startup: ON for NVIDIA Turing and newer and AMD discrete GPUs (GCN / RDNA), OFF for NVIDIA Maxwell / Pascal / Volta (no documented concurrent graphics + compute benefit before Ampere; Windows device losses), AMD RDNA2 (RX 6000) on AMD's own driver (#845), AMD integrated GPUs, Intel (all), other vendors and NVIDIA on non-NVIDIA drivers (untested). Automatic off means no second queue at all (the pre-phase-3 device), so setting 1 then needs a restart. Applies only while RenderVKAsyncComputeQueue is at its default; the decision and its reason are logged at startup ('VKAsync: auto -> ...') and shown in About and the device-lost report. 1 = on whenever a second queue exists, 0 = off: everything recorded on the graphics queue exactly as before (the recorded command stream is the phase-2 one; live). Each workload has its own switch: RenderVKAsyncRTBuild, RenderVKAsyncMaskAO, RenderVKAsyncGodRays, RenderVKAsyncVolumetrics, RenderVKAsyncPost, RenderVKAsyncProbeRT, RenderVKAsyncDeferredLighting. No effect without a second queue, on snapshots / offscreen renders, or with RenderVKPreciseBarriers off. Research and sources: research/ASYNC_COMPUTE_BY_ARCH.md

Vulkan (phase 3a, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute): BLAS builds / refits, the rig copy and the TLAS build run on the async compute queue while the graphics queue records the alpha sort, readbacks, particles and the main-view depth pre-pass (moved ahead of the shadow / probe / mirror views for this; the RT build's cull inputs are shared with those views' culls, so they wait for it). Off = recorded on the graphics queue. The pre-pass move (and so most of the overlap) needs the split pre-pass (RenderVKDepthPrepass with AO, motion vectors or the RT mask) and occlusion culling off; otherwise the build only overlaps the alpha sort / readbacks / particle compute

Vulkan (phase 3a, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute and RenderVKOverlapMaskAO): the RT shadow mask (trace, temporal, spatial) and SSAO (+ blurs) run on the async compute queue from the finished pre-pass depth, while the graphics queue renders the reflection-probe faces and the planar mirror; pass 1b waits on them. Off = recorded on the graphics queue

Vulkan async compute (RenderVKAsyncCompute): run the deferred lighting compute (RenderVKDeferredLighting) on the async queue beside the early reflection-probe face raster. The G-buffer pass then follows the early depth pre-pass and the planar mirror is recorded before the probe faces (the lighting samples it). Needs the early pre-pass (an async RT build or async SSAO / RT mask this frame) and RenderVKProbeEarly; GPU sub-marks c_defer_light / q_defer_light. -1 (default) = automatic: on when the async queue is a dedicated compute-only family (NVIDIA / AMD async-compute hardware queues; RTX 5090 4K: 14.5 vs 15.5 ms GPU), off on a second graphics-family queue or without one (including when RenderVKAsyncCompute's per-GPU automatic default created no async queue); the resolved value is logged at startup ('VKAsync: deferred lighting on the async queue'). 1 = on whenever an async queue exists, 0 = the lighting compute on the graphics queue right before the sky (g_defer_light). Live

Vulkan (#978, phase 1; with the deferred lighting on the async queue -- RenderVKAsyncDeferredLighting --, RenderVKAsyncLayoutsOnGraphics and ray-traced GI on, RenderVKGI): 1 (default) = the async lighting chain (q_defer_light) ends after the GI trace + its denoiser, and the graphics queue no longer waits for it right after the reflection probe faces: it first records the acoustics trace and forks the volumetric fog / ray-traced probe face segments, then waits for the chain in pass 1b right before the combine (BASE + LOCAL / COMBINE), which it runs itself. The GI trace starts exactly as early as before (its inputs: this frame's G-buffer, TLAS, projector tiles and the ReSTIR emissive build at the chain's head; it cannot run beside the RT reflections or the ReSTIR pass, which share its buffers). Same frame's GI (no added latency). Timers: g_join_gi = the graphics queue's wait for the chain, q_gi_beside = graphics work done beside it, q_gi_hidden = chain time not waited for, g_defer_tail = the combine on graphics. 0 = the old order (graphics waits at g_join_defer after the probe faces; the combine inside q_defer_light). Live

Vulkan (#978, phase 2; ray-traced GI on, RenderVKGI): 1 = ONE FRAME OF GI LATENCY. The combine (BASE + LOCAL / COMBINE) uses LAST frame's GI, reprojected to this frame's camera (a disocclusion, a teleport / camera cut or a resize takes the GI radiance cache there, else the reflection probes), and this frame's GI trace + radiance-cache resolve + GI denoiser run AFTER the combine on their own async compute segment (q_gi_lag) beside the rest of the frame (sky, alpha depth, particles, god rays, pass 2, motion blur, the TAA / DLSS / FSR resolve), joined right before the SSR copy / bloom (g_join_gi_lag: ~0 when it fit). The async lighting chain (q_defer_light) then holds only the shadows + reflections + RT reflections, which the graphics queue still waits for before the combine (g_join_gi). Costs while on: a depth snapshot (4 B / render pixel) and a copy of the GI state for the forward pass (32 B / cache slot: 8 MB at 2^18); the asynchronous god rays stay on graphics on such frames. Builds on RenderVKGIEarlyTrace's split (on whenever this is). Timers: q_gi_lag, g_join_gi_lag, q_gi_lag_hidden = the GI time not waited for. 0 (default) = phase 1 exactly (same frame's GI). Live

Vulkan (phase 3a, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute and RenderVKOverlapGodRays): the god-ray march and its temporal pass run on the async compute queue while pass 2a (pre-water alpha + particles) rasterizes; the composite waits on them. Off = recorded on the graphics queue

Vulkan (#718, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute): the volumetric fog's froxel passes (inject, light, temporal, integrate) run on the async compute queue beside pass 1b; the opaque apply at the start of pass 2 waits only for them. Off = recorded on the graphics queue.

Vulkan (phase 3a, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute): the deferred reflection-probe filter (mips + GGX filter) runs on the async queue beside the HUD / UI, joined at the start of the next frame. Its mip chain uses image blits, so it only works on a graphics-family async queue (RenderVKAsyncComputeQueue 2); on a dedicated compute family it stays on the graphics queue

Vulkan (phase 3a, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute and RenderVKProbeEarly): the ray-traced reflection-probe faces (RenderReflectionProbeDetail 3) run on the async compute queue beside pass 1b (the main lit pass), joined before the frame-end probe filters. Works on any async family (compute only). Off = recorded on the graphics queue at the start of pass 1b

Vulkan: frame pacing. The main loop waits for the frame-in-flight slot it will render into at the very START of the frame (before input, object updates and animation; timed as vk_paceWait), so each frame's simulated time step begins right after the GPU frees a slot. Off = the wait happens mid-frame inside the swapchain acquire (vk_acquireWait), after the world was already advanced: the CPU runs up to a frame ahead and then stalls about two GPU frames, so displayed frames carry uneven time steps (micro-stutter on a steady GPU). Live

Vulkan, diagnostic: the present mode used with vsync off (RenderVSyncEnable 0). 0 = MAILBOX (no tearing; falls back to IMMEDIATE, then FIFO), 1 = IMMEDIATE (may tear; falls back to MAILBOX, then FIFO). For uneven frame pacing under a compositor that paces MAILBOX on its own cadence (seen on Windows). Live (recreates the swapchain); the chosen mode is logged as 'Swapchain recreated'

Vulkan (roadmap phase 3b, needs RenderVKAsyncCompute): frame pipelining. Each frame's GPU front end (instance / joint / geometry streams, GPU animation, buffer fills, main cull, light + probe clusters, frame info, skin palettes, pre-skin) runs on the async compute queue and waits only for the previous frame's graphics work up to its last reader of those buffers (after its HUD, or after its probe capture when the faces are recorded late) -- not for the previous frame's tail (probe filters, UI, present) or this frame's uploads, which it overlaps. Forces RenderVKAsyncPost off. Frames with buffer growth, the first frame after a non-pipelined one and offscreen renders record the front end on the graphics queue. GPU timers: q_frontend (the segment), q_fe_hidden (the part not waited on by graphics). Off = the phase-3a recording exactly. Default off until validated with sync validation

Vulkan god rays (#208): composite the shafts after every transparent (water, post-water alpha, post-water particles: the end of pass 2), so glass, water and alpha-blended surfaces no longer cover shafts in front of them. With RenderVKReactiveMask off and TAA on, the composite goes right after the water instead (before TAA's reactive reference copy), so post-water alpha still covers it there. Shafts behind glass / water are no longer in the refraction copy. Off = the old order (after pre-water alpha, before the refraction copy)

Vulkan (phase 2, needs RenderVKPreciseBarriers): the god-ray composite keeps its place in the blend order (RenderVKGodRaysAfterAlpha) but in its own short rendering scope, so only the composite waits for the march and temporal pass and the alpha / water raster before it runs beside them. Off = the march blocks pass 2a

Vulkan (phase 2, needs RenderVKPreciseBarriers): the TLAS build's release to its consumers (ray-query FS / compute) is recorded at the first consumer (probe faces, mirror, RT mask, pass 1) instead of right after the build, so work in between (alpha sort, particles, shadow tiles, pre-pass, probe culls) is not held behind the acceleration-structure build. Off = released right after the build

Vulkan (phase 2, needs RenderVKPreciseBarriers): the particle sim / sort chain's release to its draws is recorded at the first particle draw (cascades, mirror or pass 2a) instead of right after the compute, so draws recorded in between are not held behind it. Off = released right after the compute

Vulkan (phase 2, needs RenderVKPreciseBarriers): reflection-probe capture faces cull into their own buckets and counters (as the planar mirror does) instead of reusing the main cull's after the main and HUD draws consumed them. Needed by RenderVKProbeEarly. Off = shared buffers (about 5 x instance capacity x 20 bytes less VRAM)

Vulkan (phase 2, needs RenderVKPreciseBarriers + RenderVKProbePrivateCull): record the probe capture faces before the mirror and pass 1 (after the shadow cascades / projector tiles they sample) instead of at the end of the frame, so their culls and raster overlap other work. The filter into the probe arrays stays at the end of the frame, so the main view samples the same probe data as before. Off = whole capture at the frame end

Vulkan GPU timers (RenderVKGpuTimers): write the per-pass and named sub-mark timestamps. Off = only the first and last timestamp of the world recording (the frame total), so the timer queries cannot serialize overlapped work while measuring it

Vulkan: alpha-blend surfaces write depth where they are near-opaque (alpha >= 0.99) at the end of the opaque pass, so blended layers hidden behind solid foliage / hair texels are skipped by the early depth test instead of shaded and blended (dense foliage stacks 4-10 layers per pixel). Soft edges blend as before. Off = every blended layer is shaded

Vulkan (#731): alpha-blended surfaces are depth-tested against the opaque scene with a small metric tolerance, so a blended layer lying on a surface (a baked-shadow / decal layer a fraction of a millimetre over a road) draws instead of flickering against it under TAA / FSR jitter. World geometry only: avatar alpha (rigged mesh, worn attachments) always uses the strict test (#742 / #750). Off = strict test (the blended fragment must not be behind the opaque surface)

Vulkan (#731, RenderVKBlendDepthTol): base tolerance in millimetres -- how far behind the opaque surface (along the view ray, before the grazing-angle factor) a blended fragment still draws. Must exceed the vertex quantization of large meshes (about 1-2 mm on 64 m faces); larger values let blended faces show through thin walls by that much
Vulkan (#731, RenderVKBlendDepthTol): extra tolerance per metre of camera distance (metres per metre; 0.0001 = 0.1 mm per m)
Vulkan (#731, RenderVKBlendDepthTol): cap of the grazing-angle factor 1 / |N.V| that widens the tolerance on surfaces seen edge-on (1 = no widening)
Vulkan (#731): tint magenta the blended fragments that lay behind the opaque surface and drew only because of RenderVKBlendDepthTol

Discord status (#205): show that you are in Second Life on your Discord profile (Rich Presence), through the local Discord app. Nothing is sent before login; the status is cleared on logout. The Show settings choose what else is shown. Applies live
Discord status: show the region you are in. Never shown while RLVa @showloc is active, nor (with SlipstreamDiscordHideMatureLocation) in Moderate / Adult regions. Applies live
Discord status: show what you are doing (Standing, Sitting, Flying, Away, Busy). Applies live
Discord status: show your avatar name (display / username per your name settings). Never shown while RLVa @shownames or @shownametags is active. Applies live
Build > Texture: keep the Blinn-Phong face tint and the PBR base color tint in sync (a tint change on one is applied to the other). Applies live

Discord status: add a "Teleport to me" button that opens your location as a maps.secondlife.com SLURL. Requires SlipstreamDiscordShowRegion and follows the same location hiding rules; Second Life main grid only. Applies live
Discord status: hide the region and the teleport button while you are in a Moderate or Adult region. Applies live
Discord status: the Discord application (client) id the status is published under. Empty = Discord status unavailable in this build

Caps the regions the viewer connects to a square ring around the agent's region: N regions on each side, so 2 = 5x5 (25 regions), 1 = 3x3, 0 = own region and its 8 neighbours only (the minimum for crossings); max 8. Also a hard cap on the number of connected regions, (2N+1)^2, except the agent's region and its 8 neighbours (needed for crossings). A backstop to SLNetDrawDistanceMax, which decides what the simulator enables. Neighbours outside the ring are refused; live regions left outside it leave when their simulator disables them. Applies live

Disconnects a neighbour region (never the agent's own region, nor a region next to it that still has a circuit) that has sent no packets for this many seconds: its simulator has dropped our child agent without a DisableSimulator, so its objects would otherwise stay rendered but dead. 0 = off

Paces new neighbour region connections: at most one new circuit per this many milliseconds (nearest first), instead of bursts on every crossing. The agent's region and its 8 neighbours are never delayed. 0 = no pacing. Live

Network draw distance cap in meters: the most the viewer asks the simulator for (AgentUpdate Far), independent of the render draw distance. The simulator gives the agent a presence in every neighbour region within this distance and sends objects out to it, so a large value multiplies server-side work on every region crossing. Rendering still uses the full draw distance. Clamped to 64..512 m: the viewer never asks for more than 512 m whatever the render draw distance (0 = 512). Live

While the agent moves faster than SLNetDrawDistanceFastSpeed (boosted flight, vehicles), limit the network draw distance to a lead-time based value: speed x SLNetDrawDistanceFastLeadSeconds + SLNetDrawDistanceFastMargin, clamped to SLNetDrawDistanceFastMin..SLNetDrawDistanceFastMax (and never above SLNetDrawDistanceMax or the render draw distance). Neighbour regions then come up about that many seconds before their border at any speed, without asking the simulator for everything at the full draw distance on every crossing. Off = fast movement uses the normal network draw distance. Live

Fast movement network draw distance (SLNetDrawDistanceFastLimit): seconds of warning wanted before a neighbour region's border; the network draw distance is speed x this + SLNetDrawDistanceFastMargin. Live
Fast movement network draw distance (SLNetDrawDistanceFastLimit): meters added to speed x SLNetDrawDistanceFastLeadSeconds. Live
Fast movement network draw distance (SLNetDrawDistanceFastLimit): lower bound in meters, so diagonal neighbours are still up at moderate speed. Live
Fast movement network draw distance (SLNetDrawDistanceFastLimit): upper bound in meters (SLNetDrawDistanceMax and the render draw distance still apply). Live

How fast, in meters per second, the network draw distance (AgentUpdate Far) comes down when its target drops (fast movement starting, SLNetDrawDistanceMax lowered). Lowering it at once made the simulator drop neighbour regions we already had, which were then re-sent as we approached. A lower render draw distance still applies at once. 0 = at once. Live

Horizontal speed in m/s above which (for 1 s) the network draw distance follows speed (SLNetDrawDistanceFastLimit); it returns to normal after 3 s below 60% of this. Normal flight is well under it; boosted flight and vehicles are over. 0 = never. Live

Both mouse buttons walk: while holding the left mouse button on your own avatar to steer (normal camera, not the third-person shooter camera), also holding the right button walks forward, like the forward key (runs or flies per your current mode). The right click is then used for walking and opens no context menu. Applies immediately

At startup, warn in plain language when Slipstream is running on something that is not the computer's real graphics driver (a translation layer such as Microsoft's Direct3D 12 "Dozen", a software renderer, an integrated GPU while a discrete one exists, a discrete GPU without a working Vulkan driver). The warning always offers Continue anyway. FALSE skips the dialog (the check is still logged). Applies at the next start
The graphics setup (device name | driver version | vendor) for which "don't show this again" was chosen in the driver check dialog. A different device or driver version shows the dialog again

Verbose logging: also write the renderer / ingest / asset telemetry (periodic summaries, per-object traces) to the log. Off keeps the log to startup and system info, warnings, errors, crashes and any diagnostics you turn on explicitly (section log, GPU timers, *Diag settings). Applies immediately

Freeze World (World menu, Ctrl+Shift+F): stop the world clock -- avatar animation, object motion / interpolation / target omega, particles, texture animation, water, sky, clouds -- while the camera, UI and your own movement keep running. Not persisted

Folder for decoded sounds (the WAV file each played sound is decoded to). Empty = a "sounds" folder inside the cache folder. Created if missing; if it cannot be written, the default is used and a warning is logged. Applies on the next start
Disk space for decoded sounds, in MB (32 - 4096). When a new sound is decoded past this budget, the least recently played sounds are deleted (they are decoded again if needed). Applies immediately

Keep decoded sounds between sessions, so sounds heard before play without being decoded again. Off = the sound cache folder is emptied when the viewer exits (and at startup, in case the last session crashed). Clear Cache empties it either way

GPU-ready texture cache (#274): keep the block-compressed mip chains the Vulkan renderer made in a "gputex" folder inside the cache folder, so textures seen before load from disk without a full JPEG2000 decode or a re-encode. Applies immediately (off: nothing is read or written; the files stay until evicted or Clear Cache)

#715 diagnostics: track GPU-ready cache reads per texture (read counts and times, bytes read vs bytes uploaded, the residency downgrades / frees and texture pressure between reads) and log a "GpuTexReadDiag" summary every 60 s (rereads with and without a VRAM drop in between, reads-per-texture histogram, top rereaders). Off: no tracking. Applies immediately
Disk space for the GPU-ready texture cache, in MB (256 - 65536). Past this budget the least recently used textures are deleted (they load from the regular texture cache again). Applies immediately

Texture memory: with SlipstreamTextureMemoryMode Auto, machines with less system RAM than this (GB, nominal) keep no reusable decoded texture copies -- textures reload from the GPU-ready disk cache, as in Prefer disk cache. 0 = off

Texture memory (#405 / #707): decoded texture copies exist only while a feature needs them (media, UI uploads, previews, Save As, appearance editing, a pending GPU upload); the GPU and the disk caches hold the rest. 0 = Auto (world textures additionally keep their copy in RAM while memory is plentiful, for the fastest re-upload; dropped when it gets tight), 1 = Prefer disk cache (lowest RAM: no optional copies -- reload from the GPU-ready disk cache, else the J2C cache). Never changed automatically; Auto behaves as Prefer disk cache on machines with less RAM than SlipstreamTextureDiskBelowRAMGB
New prim defaults (#466): rez new prims from the Build tool at the size in SlipstreamNewPrimSizeX/Y/Z instead of 0.5 m
New prim defaults (#466): X size in metres of a newly rezzed prim (0.01 - 64), used when SlipstreamNewPrimSizeEnabled is on
New prim defaults (#466): Y size in metres of a newly rezzed prim (0.01 - 64), used when SlipstreamNewPrimSizeEnabled is on
New prim defaults (#466): Z size in metres of a newly rezzed prim (0.01 - 64), used when SlipstreamNewPrimSizeEnabled is on
New prim defaults (#466): make prims rezzed from the Build tool phantom
New prim defaults (#466): make prims rezzed from the Build tool physical
New prim defaults (#466): make prims rezzed from the Build tool temporary
New prim defaults (#466): texture (asset UUID) put on every face of prims rezzed from the Build tool. Empty or null: keep the default plywood

Vulkan retained UI: each floater's drawing is recorded and replayed until it changes, instead of re-running all of its view code every frame. Floaters draw live while hovered, focused or being dragged; content changes, moves, UI scale and font atlas changes re-record them, plus a staggered safety refresh (RenderUIRetainedRefreshMs). Off = every floater draws live every frame

Retained UI: a floater holding keyboard focus is recorded and replayed like any other; only its focused control (caret, typing) is drawn live each frame. A focus change re-records. A focused control its parent draws by hand falls back to drawing the floater live. 0 = focused floaters always draw live.

Retained UI: a hovered floater draws live only while the mouse moved within this many milliseconds (hover highlights follow the mouse); a resting mouse's hover state is recorded once and replayed. 0 = hovered floaters always draw live.

Vulkan retained UI: a recorded floater is re-recorded at least this often (ms, staggered +-25%), catching content that changes without reporting it (list cells, timers, voice indicators). Lower = livelier background floaters, more CPU
Vulkan: every ~5 s log each hitch-recorder section's steady-state average (ms and count per frame) -- the before/after instrument for CPU optimizations

Vulkan reduced-detail avatar tier (replaces LL impostors): avatars ranked past RenderAvatarMaxNonImpostors (the "max fully rendered avatars" slider; 0 = unlimited) still draw normally but cast no shadows (see RenderVKReducedAvatarShadows), animate at RenderVKReducedAvatarAnimFPS and LOD out sooner (RenderVKReducedAvatarLODScale). Never your own avatar.

Vulkan reduced avatars: animation (motion evaluation / GPU pose blend) updates per second; the pose is held in between (root motion stays per-frame). Staggered per avatar. 0 = every frame. Applies only below RenderVKReducedAvatarAnimMaxPx on-screen height; larger reduced avatars follow the screen-size ladder (RenderVKAvatarAnimFullPx), and near / large ones animate every frame (#725).

Vulkan reduced avatars: the fixed RenderVKReducedAvatarAnimFPS rate applies only to reduced avatars shorter than this on screen (pixels, 10% hysteresis). Taller reduced avatars animate at the screen-size ladder's rate (RenderVKAvatarAnimFullPx: every frame at and above it), and any avatar within RenderVKAvatarAnimScreenMinM of the camera every frame (#725).

Vulkan: off-screen (hidden) avatars other than your own never evaluate a pose; they hold their frame (no pelvis ground probe, head offset or footstep ray casts) and run the motion controller's hidden bookkeeping (stopped / loading motions) this many times per second, staggered per avatar. Their root still moves every frame. 0 = bookkeeping every frame (frames are still held).

Vulkan reduced avatars that cast no shadow: pre-skin their rigged meshes into a persistent cache in the avatar's pelvis frame, only on frames their pose changes (RenderVKReducedAvatarAnimFPS ticks, skeleton edits), and place the cached vertices with the pelvis's current transform every frame.
Vulkan reduced avatars: multiplier on the LOD factor of their rigged mesh and worn attachments (1 = no bias; 0.5 = switch LOD at half the distance, i.e. at most one level coarser at range).

Vulkan: draw the classic system avatar body (head, upper / lower body, eyes, eyelashes, hair, skirt) of every avatar, self included. Off = avatars show only their attachments (mesh bodies keep rendering; an avatar without a mesh body shows only what it wears). Avatar menu > Show System Avatar Bodies.

Vulkan system avatar body: skip each body part whose baked texture LL treats as invisible (IMG_INVISIBLE: hidden by an alpha layer / mesh-body alpha mask) in every pass. Off = draw every part (A/B; the hidden ones are then discarded per pixel).
Vulkan reduced avatars: still cast shadows (sun cascades, projector shadows, ray-traced shadows). Off = they only receive shadows.
Vulkan reduced avatars: also reduce any avatar farther than this many meters, whatever its rank (0 = rank only).
Vulkan: evaluate other avatars' animations at a reduced rate when they are small on screen (root motion stays per-frame)

Vulkan animation LOD: on-screen avatar height (pixels) at and above which animation is evaluated every frame; below it every 2nd frame, below half every 3rd, below a quarter every 4th (GPU animation, RenderVKAvatarAnimScreenLOD: 30 / 20 / 15 FPS)
Always log one line (section breakdown + GPU waits, rate-limited to one per 2 s) for any frame longer than this many ms; 0 = off (#700)
When the previous session did not end cleanly, keep its log as logs/Slipstream-crash-*.log and retain this many (0 = do not keep) (#700)
Vulkan: log a per-section breakdown of frames that spike well above the running average (hitch attribution)
Vulkan: log per-pass GPU timings (timestamp queries) every ~5 s (diagnostic)

Vulkan lit-pass trim (forward and deferred lighting, alpha / water / particles too): a local light whose attenuated colour at a surface point is below this linear radiance is skipped there (no shadow / gobo fetch), fading out smoothly over [cutoff, 2 x cutoff] so no edge shows where its falloff tail ends. 0 = off (LL behaviour). Live

Smooth terrain (#211): draw the terrain as a smooth surface through its height samples (a monotone bicubic: it passes through every sample and never overshoots) instead of flat triangles, subdivided near the camera (RenderVKTerrainSmoothDetail) with seamless distance LOD. Picks, foot planting and parcel lines follow the drawn surface; the simulator still collides with the flat one, which differs by less than one metre cell's rise. Off = the faceted terrain exactly. Live

Smooth terrain (RenderVKTerrainSmooth): finest subdivision built near the camera. 0 = smooth normals on the 1 m height grid only, 1 = 0.5 m cells (out to ~120 m), 2 = 0.25 m (out to ~56 m), 3 = 0.125 m (out to ~12 m). Each level also keeps the coarser ones further out. Live

Vulkan lit-pass trim (forward and deferred lighting, alpha / water / particles too): blend only the N reflection probes with the largest final weight per pixel (manual-over-automatic mix included), renormalized, instead of every candidate of the pixel's cluster (up to 24 + the default probe, two cube fetches each). 1..4; 0 = all candidates (LL behaviour). Pixels with N or fewer candidates are unchanged. Live

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (sun / moon mask, RT projectors, RT probe faces): alpha-blend casters follow LL's shadow-pass alpha rule (shadowAlphaMaskF.glsl) -- a texel at 0.88 alpha or more is solid, an opaque caster (with RenderVKRTTranslucentSplit the soft-shadow disc rays test the alpha-blend casters for these texels, so they get soft penumbrae like any opaque caster); below that the caster passes translucentTransmit of the light with RenderVKTranslucentShadows (nothing below 0.05), else LL's own result (nothing under texture alpha 0.598 or alpha 0.05, a flat 50% otherwise). 0 = every blend texel dims by (1 - alpha) (the previous behaviour). Live

Vulkan ray tracing: alpha-blend faces whose face alpha is at most 1/255 (100%-transparent faces of builds) are left out of the TLAS (was 0.05; faint but visible glass stays so the RT acoustics block sound on it). LL casts no shadow from them; in the TLAS every shadow ray crossing one paid a non-opaque candidate (alpha test, texture fetch) to find a hole. Fullbright faces stay (LL's shadow pass ignores their face alpha). Such faces no longer show in ray-traced probe faces / RT debug views (they are invisible). 0 = keep them (previous behaviour). Live (applies at the next TLAS build)

Vulkan ray-traced soft shadows (sun / moon mask, RT projectors): adaptive sampling already stops after the two outermost disc rays when both are fully lit or fully blocked. With this tolerance it also stops when the two rays AGREE on a partial value within it -- light through the same translucent caster (pool water, glass), where the remaining rays only repeat the same transmittance at the price of another candidate walk each. Only matters with RenderVKRTTranslucentSplit off (with the split the disc rays never see translucent casters, so they are always 0 or 1). 0..1, in visibility units (0.0625 = 1/16); 0 = off (previous behaviour). Live

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (sun / moon mask, RT projectors, RT probe faces, RT god rays, inline RT in the alpha / forward pass): the standard opaque / translucent split. The soft-shadow disc rays trace only the OPAQUE caster set (alpha-blend casters excluded by their TLAS instance mask, except with RenderVKRTBlendShadowParity their texels at alpha 0.88 or more, which count as opaque here and are skipped by the transmittance ray; alpha-mask cut-outs keep their alpha test), so they stay 0 / 1 and the adaptive early-out works under glass and water; ONE extra ray per receiver and light, along the light's centre direction over the alpha-blend casters only, multiplies in their transmittance (coloured with RenderVKTranslucentShadows; LL thresholds with RenderVKRTBlendShadowParity), and is skipped where the opaque rays are all blocked. The penumbra size comes from opaque blockers only. Look: a translucent caster's shadow edge / texture is projected from the light's centre (sharp) instead of averaged over the disc. With this on, RenderVKRTShadowAdaptiveTol has no effect (the disc rays are binary). 0 = every disc ray walks every translucent candidate it crosses (previous behaviour). Live

Vulkan ray-traced reflection probe faces (RenderReflectionProbeDetail 3): the sun shadow ray of each traced hit takes alpha-blend casters at their texture's mean colour / alpha (coarsest mip) instead of the texel at the hit (face UVs, triangle fetch, ray-cone LOD per candidate). The capture is GGX-filtered, so texel-level translucent shadow detail is invisible there. 0 = texel-accurate (previous behaviour). Live

Vulkan (#615): render targets whose lifetimes never overlap share one memory block -- the deferred G-buffer (dead once the lighting compute has read it) and the HDR bloom pyramid + cross-filter buffers (first written after the TAA / FSR resolve), about 17 B per display pixel (~35 MB at 1080p, ~140 MB at 4K). The log line "render targets: N MB -> M MB" shows the saving. Off = separate allocations. A change re-creates those targets on the next frame. Offscreen renders (snapshots, 360) always use separate allocations. Live

Vulkan: deferred lighting for the main view's opaque / alpha-mask / rigged surfaces (phase 5.2). Pass 1b writes a G-buffer (albedo, normals, roughness-metal / gloss, glow, emissive / specular: 20 B per pixel; GPU sub-marks g_gbuf_static, g_gbuf_rigged) and a compute pass lights it (g_defer_light) with the same lighting code as the forward pass (sun + shadows, local lights, probes, SSR, SSAO, mirror, haze). Off = the forward lit pass (g_lit_static, g_lit_rigged). Alpha, water, particles, the HUD, probe / mirror captures always shade forward (snapshots follow RenderVKSnapshotDeferred); debug views (RenderVKDebugView), Highlight Transparent, the shading-rate overlay, overdraw stats and ray-query lit frames (RT shadows without RenderVKRTShadowMask) fall back to forward. Needs the depth pre-pass split (SSAO, TAA or the RT shadow mask). Live

Vulkan: how the deferred lighting compute (RenderVKDeferredLighting) runs. 2 (default) = AUTO, per GPU class (#824): the split below on GPUs with hardware ray tracing (where it was tuned, and which the RT shadow merge / projector stochastic / hybrid RT reflection paths need), the uber kernel on GPUs without it (Pascal and older, Polaris / Vega / RDNA1, integrated: a GTX 1080 at 4K lit 0.7-2.0 ms faster with the uber kernel); decided once per session and logged ("VKDeferSplit: RenderVKDeferredSplit 2 (auto)"). 1 = split by the data each part reads: a shadow resolve (sun cascades / RT mask, projector atlas -> a visibility buffer), a reflection resolve (probe blend, SSR, planar mirror, legacy env -> a reflection buffer) and a combine (G-buffer + both buffers + tiled local lights -> HDR + glow); ~20-25 % faster than the uber kernel (RTX 5090). Its pipelines compile with the world pipelines at login. 16 B per render pixel of intermediates (12 B with RenderVKDeferReflectHalfRes; + 8 B mono / 16 B colour projector slots while shadowed projectors are in view; below render scale 1 the 16 B share the G-buffer / bloom alias block with RenderVKAliasTargets), created on first use and freed only when this setting or RenderVKDeferredLighting is turned off; if VRAM refuses them the uber kernel lights those frames and the allocation is retried (1 s, backing off to 30 s; log: "VKDeferSplit: intermediates ... refused"). 0 = one uber kernel (shadows, probes, SSR, local lights and haze in one program: ~128 registers). Debug views, RenderVKLitDebugMask and snapshots always use the uber kernel. Same image within the intermediates' precision. Live

Vulkan split deferred lighting (RenderVKDeferredSplit 1; #827): 1 (default) = the combine step is split by feature. A tile pass (beside the shadow / reflection resolves) builds each 16x16 tile's light mask and lists the tiles any local light reaches; a BASE kernel lights every pixel without local lights (sun / moon + shadow, ambient, reflections, emissive, haze: about half the combine's registers, so far higher occupancy on register-bound GPUs such as Pascal) and stores per pixel how strongly the final colour responds to local light; a LOCAL kernel then runs the local-light walk over the listed tiles only (indirect dispatch) and adds its sum onto BASE's result. Same image up to float rounding (the pre-local colour passes the RGBA16F target once more on lit pixels). +4 B per render pixel (the gain, ~32 MB at 4K) + a small tile list, allocated the first time this is on and kept until split lighting itself is freed (turning this off frees nothing, so a live toggle is safe). GPU timers: g_defer_classify / _shadow / _refl / _base / _local (c_ on the async compute queue). 0 = one combine kernel (A/B reference). Live

Vulkan split deferred lighting (#823): 1 (default) = when nothing casts on the deferred surfaces this frame -- sun / moon shadows off (the setting or the sun below the horizon), no shadowed projector in view, no merged RT shadow pass -- the SHADOW resolve pass is not recorded: the combine / BASE kernels take the sun visibility from the volumetric cloud layer directly (exactly what that pass stored with shadows off; 1.0 without clouds), visibility reuse is off for those frames, and the fused feature split (RenderVKDeferClassifyFused) dispatches the tile classification alone. With the sun spec key at 0 (RenderVKSpecPipelines) the combine never loads the visibility buffer at all. Saves the pass's G-buffer decode + store (~0.8 ms at 4K on a GTX 1080). 0 = the pass always runs (A/B; same image). GPU timer: g_defer_shadow / c_defer_shadow (feature split, classify unfused) reads ~0 while skipped. Live

Vulkan feature-split deferred lighting (RenderVKDeferredFeatureSplit 1; #831): 1 (default) = the tile classification (which tiles get the local-light pass, and their light lists) runs inside the shadow pass, one 16 px tile per workgroup, instead of as its own full-screen pass. 0 = the separate classification pass beside the 8x8 shadow pass. Same tile lists, same image; a performance A/B. GPU timers: g_defer_shadow_cls (1) vs g_defer_classify + g_defer_shadow (0); g_defer_prep = the barriers before them (c_ on the async compute queue). Live.

Vulkan: how the deferred lighting (uber kernel and the split combine) finds each pixel's local lights. 2 (default) = froxel masks: the light pass (after the light clusters) marks, for every light, the screen tiles x depth slices its range can reach (sphere vs each cell, projector frustums too) in a 256-bit mask per cell -- built from the lights alone, no pixel depth read, lossless (every one of the up to 256 lights has its bit) -- and each lit pixel walks its own cell's lights; no per-tile light test, depth reduction or barrier inside the heavy lighting kernel. Tiles of 16-128 px (the power of two nearest render height / 32: 64 px at 4K) x 48 slices, 32 B per cell (~3 MB at 4K). 1 = the light grid: a separate compute pass per frame builds every 16x16 pixel tile's light mask from the tile's surface depths (~1 MB at 4K), the lighting kernels read it. 0 = the in-kernel test: each lighting workgroup tests every light against its 16x16 tile (three barriers per tile). All three give the same image (each walks a superset of the lights that reach the pixel, in light-index order). Shader clock (RenderVKShaderClockLighting): the lighting kernels' light-set lookup is stage "froxel" ("grid" / "tile_*" for 1 / 0); the froxel build's GPU time is pass c_light_froxel. Live

Vulkan deferred lighting (uber kernel and the split combine; #815): 1 = with a per-tile light mask (RenderVKLightCulling 0 or 1) each 16x16 workgroup copies the position / radius, colour / falloff and projector flag of every light its tile mask holds into shared memory once (one light per thread, 8 KB per workgroup), and every pixel's light walk reads them from there instead of two dependent global loads per candidate light. Same lights, same order, same values: the image is bit-identical. 0 (default) = every pixel loads them from the light buffer (A/B reference). No effect with RenderVKLightCulling 2 (the default) (froxel cells are per pixel). Shader clock: the copy is charged to stage "grid" / "tile_lights". Live

Vulkan split deferred lighting (RenderVKDeferredSplit 1): 1 (default) = the reflection resolve runs at half resolution -- one probe walk per 2x2 pixel block for the irradiance and the soft (rough) specular, upsampled in the combine with a depth-plane + normal aware bilinear filter -- plus a full-resolution pass for the SHARP pixels only (roughness / 1 - glossiness below RenderVKDeferReflectSharpRough, so every SSR surface; a strong planar-mirror weight; legacy shiny (env) faces; fullbright shiny), which keep exact per-pixel reflections. ~4x fewer probe walks on rough surfaces; reflection intermediates 8 instead of 12 B per render pixel. 0 = every pixel at full resolution (A/B reference). Live (the intermediates are re-created)

Vulkan split deferred lighting (RenderVKDeferredSplit 1): 1 (default) = alpha-blended world faces lying ON an opaque surface (decals, onion-skin layers, coplanar signs: view depth within 4 mm + 0.1 %, normal within ~25 deg) take the sun and shadowed-projector visibility the lighting's shadow pass resolved for that surface instead of filtering the shadow maps again. Everything else (foliage, glass, hair) shades as before. Costs 4 B per render pixel (the surface's depth + normal, written by the shadow pass). 0 = every blended fragment filters its own shadows (A/B reference). Live (the intermediates are re-created)

Vulkan (RenderVKDeferReflectHalfRes): perceptual roughness below which (legacy: 1 - glossiness) a pixel's specular reflection is evaluated per pixel instead of upsampled from the half-resolution blocks. Clamped to 0.11 .. 1 (SSR surfaces, roughness <= 0.1, always stay per pixel; 1 = every glossy pixel per pixel, only the irradiance at half resolution). Higher = sharper glossy reflections, more full-resolution work. Live

Vulkan ray-traced reflections (#859; needs ray tracing and deferred lighting). 1 (default) = HYBRID: screen-space reflections stay primary; where SSR has no confident answer (a miss, off screen, behind an occluder, or a smooth surface SSR does not trace) on a surface smoother than RenderVKRTReflectionsRough, rays against the scene (avatars included, alpha-blended surfaces composited in front of the hit) replace the reflection-probe share. The SSR and planar-mirror shares are unchanged. Split deferred lighting traces only the pixels SSR left to the probe (none on an empty screen); the uber kernel (RenderVKDeferredSplit 0) pre-traces every smooth pixel. Alpha-blended surfaces and water get theirs at half resolution (RenderVKRTReflectionsForward). Stands down (probe fallback, setting untouched) while the VRAM pressure ladder or the RT memory budget has taken ray tracing away. 0 = off (probe fallback only). 2 = reserved (full ray-traced reflections; currently off). Live. GPU timers: g_defer_rtrefl_trace, g_defer_rtrefl (resolve), g_defer_rtrefl_pre (uber)
