Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): perceptual roughness (legacy: 1 - glossiness) below which a pixel the screen-space reflection left to the probe gets a ray-traced reflection. Glossy surfaces get a footprint-sized spatial filter of the neighbouring rays (the GGX lobe x the hit distance), so their reflection blurs with roughness and distance; the splice fades out over the top quarter of the range (no hard edge). Clamped to 0.02 .. 1. Lower = fewer rays. Ray density per block: RenderVKRTReflectionsSharpRough / _Scale / _RayBudget; distance: RenderVKRTReflectionsMaxRecvDist. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): the longest reflection ray, in metres (1 .. 1024). A ray that hits nothing within it keeps the reflection probe (which holds the far field and the sky). Shorter = cheaper rays. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting): ray-traced reflections on alpha-blended surfaces (glass, windows) and water too. A compute pass finds the front-most alpha-blend / water layer per 2x2 pixel block with a camera ray and traces its reflection; the forward shaders use it in place of the probe where SSR has no answer. Costs a half-resolution camera ray over the blend / water geometry every frame plus the reflection rays. Live. GPU timer: part of g_defer_rtrefl_trace

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): alpha-blended surfaces (glass, alpha hair / clothing, blended foliage) appear in ray-traced reflections: up to 4 nearest layers in front of the hit, lit cheaply (ambient + unshadowed sun), composited front to back. 0 = reflections see through them. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting): the ray density floor -- the densest level a frame may use; RenderVKRTReflectionsRayBudget can only make a frame sparser. Density is chosen per 2x2 pixel block from its smoothest candidate. 0 = full density everywhere (one ray per candidate pixel: the old behaviour). 1 (default) = adaptive: blocks with a candidate smoother than RenderVKRTReflectionsSharpRough (mirrors, puddles, legacy shiny env faces) keep one ray per candidate pixel, every other block one ray (its first candidate pixel). 2 = one ray per 2x2 block everywhere. A block's single ray is filled to its other candidates by the resolve filter from the rays on the same plane (normal + depth). The rays of each 8 px tile are packed into the first lanes of its workgroup, so half density roughly halves the trace's GPU time, not only its ray count. Uber frames (RenderVKDeferredSplit 0) always trace full density. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, RenderVKRTReflectionsScale 1): perceptual roughness (legacy: 1 - glossiness; legacy shiny env faces count as 0) below which a 2x2 block's smoothest candidate keeps full ray density (one ray per candidate pixel); blocks whose candidates are all rougher get one ray per block. A mirror inside a block therefore never loses rays. Wet surfaces (#783) settle near 0.12: half density; very wet flat ground (0.09) and puddles (0.02): full. Clamped to 0 .. RenderVKRTReflectionsRough (0 = no block keeps full density). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): the farthest reflecting surface (receiver), in metres from the camera, that gets a ray-traced reflection. Farther pixels keep the screen-space reflection + probe result and cost no ray or tile work (they are never marked as candidates); the ray-traced share fades out over the last 20 % of this distance, so there is no visible ring. Independent of RenderVKRTReflectionsMaxDist (the ray's own length). Applies to the uber pre-trace too; not to the forward / water layer (RenderVKRTReflectionsForward). Clamped to 1 .. 4096. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting): the most reflection rays per frame, as a fraction of the render pixels (0.25 = a quarter of them: ~2.07 M at 4K). The reflect passes count what each density level (RenderVKRTReflectionsScale) would cast; the trace then takes, on the GPU (no readback, no stall), the densest level at or above the floor whose count fits -- first every block to one ray per 2x2 except the mirror blocks, then the mirror blocks too. Pixels are never dropped: a frame over budget even at one ray per 2x2 block casts that. Back to a denser level only once it fits 80 % of the budget (no level flicker at the boundary). The chosen level, the would-be ray counts and the rays cast appear in the VKGpu timer log ("RT reflections over N frames") while RenderVKGpuTimers is on. 0 = no budget. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting): trace the reflection rays from a compacted RAY LIST. On (default): a selection pass picks each listed 8 px tile's rays (the same density / budget / strength decisions) and appends them to a list, then the trace runs one lane per ray in full warps. Off: the old in-tile trace, one 64-lane workgroup per listed tile tracing that tile's few rays (at a scene full of weak reflectors ~2 rays per tile, so its cost followed the listed tiles, not the rays). Same rays, same images; GPU timers: c_defer_rtrefl_sel + c_defer_rtrefl_trace (on) vs c_defer_rtrefl_trace (off). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1 with RenderVKRTReflectionsRayList on): trace the reflection rays as three kernels -- the traversal, the hit's material (surface, textures, weather) and its lighting (sun ray, local lights, environment, blend layers) -- handing each other per-ray records (112 B per ray, sized for RenderVKRTReflectionsRayBudget x the render pixels -- a quarter of them without a budget: ~100 MB at 1440p with the default budget), so each kernel holds only its own working set. Rays past the records' capacity are traced by the single kernel. Same image up to the record's rounding (normals 2 x 16-bit octahedral, colours fp16). 0 = the single trace kernel (also the fallback while the records cannot be allocated). GPU timers: c_defer_rtrefl_trace + c_defer_rtrefl_mat + c_defer_rtrefl_light (+ c_defer_rtrefl_tail). Live.

Vulkan ray tracing, diagnostic (#1128 GPU hangs in a ray-query kernel): run the ray-query kernels through their HANG BEACON twins -- the RT reflection list trace, forward pass and queued blend layers, the visibility queue's walk (RT / GI hit rays, GI reuse), the shadow core's sun / light-sample walks and VIS tails (queued and fused), the GI trace (fused and split). Before every ray query a lane writes its pixel, the walk about to start (kind, ray mask) and the query's origin / direction / interval into host-visible memory (about 100 MB of system memory while on), and marks itself done when it finishes. If the GPU is lost, the device-lost report names every lane left inside a query (the culprit traversal), the kernels that started in the last frame and the reflection trace's dispatch. The twins compile in the background when this is first switched on (the normal kernels run until they land; then a few frames pass before the twins are bound). Slower while on (every query writes to system memory). Off: nothing changes. Not saved. Live.

TEST MACHINES ONLY -- HANGS THE GPU ON PURPOSE (device lost, the viewer closes). With RenderVKRTHangBeacon on and its kernels bound: for one frame the first ray-query beacon kernel to run records a known query in its lane 0 (site 0xf000, origin (1, 2, 3), direction (0, 0, 1), interval [0, 4]) and then never finishes, to check that the device-lost report reads a hung lane's beacon on this GPU / driver (it must list that lane IN QUERY). Any frame with ray tracing on (shadows, reflections or GI) triggers it. Cleared when used. Not saved.

Vulkan diagnostic (#1128): when the driver offers it (VK_EXT_device_fault deviceFaultVendorBinary), ask for its own binary crash dump and, on a graphics device loss, write it to the logs folder (gpu_fault_vendor_binary_*.bin) for the vendor's crash-dump tool -- the one record that can say where hung GPU threads were in a hang that names no address. The startup log says whether the driver offers it. May cost a little GPU time while on (driver bookkeeping). Takes effect after restart. 0 = off.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): the most projector shadow rays a ray-traced reflection hit may cast (0 .. 4). Every light in range of the hit still lights it; of the ray-traced projectors covering it, only this many -- the ones contributing the most light there -- get a shadow ray (opaque casters only: alpha-blended beams and glow cards are not tested), the rest light the reflection unshadowed, as reflection probes always do. Without the cap a club with dozens of ray-traced stage lights cast dozens of shadow rays per reflection ray. Higher = more exact projector shadows inside reflections, slower. The VKGpu timer log's "RT reflections" line shows what the hits paid ("hit shading: ..."). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): 1 (default) = the reflection rays ask the hardware to cull single-sided back faces during traversal, instead of meeting them and skipping them in the shader (a candidate test, or a whole re-trace past an opaque back face). It reaches only the instances the TLAS marks cullable -- single-sided alpha-mask foliage and single-sided avatar meshes / worn attachments (RenderVKRTFoliageTransmission, RenderVKRTRiggedFacingParity) -- which the shader would have skipped anyway, so the reflection looks the same; walls, floors, terrain, water, alpha-blend and double-sided surfaces keep the shader's rule (the sun shadow rays need them two-sided). 0 = the shader's rule only (A/B). The VKGpu timer log's "RT reflections" line reports the re-traces per ray ("trace cost: ... backface retraces/ray"). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1 with ray-traced GI, RenderVKGI): what a ray-traced reflection HIT reflects in turn. 1 (default) = one occlusion ray (up to 4 km: only a true miss counts as open sky) along the hit's own mirror direction: where it escapes, the reflection probes / sky stand there (open metal outdoors unchanged); where it meets a surface (opaque, terrain, alpha-mask cut-outs and alpha-blend faces by their opacity), the GI radiance cache at the hit (RenderVKGICache; nothing without a cell) -- so mirrors facing each other inside a closed room go dark with the room instead of a sky-lit hall of mirrors. The hit's own ambient follows RenderVKGIHitAmbient (0 none, 1 the probes, 2 the cache else the probes, 3 the cache else none). 0 = the old rule: every hit takes the probes / sky, unoccluded (A/B). Costs one short opaque ray per reflection hit on GI frames (GPU timer g_defer_rtrefl_trace). Live

Vulkan RT reflections under GI (with RenderVKRTReflectionsHitOcclusion): the haze between a shiny surface and what its reflection hits is sky light; scale it by whether the hit sees the sky, so a sealed room's reflections carry no sky-lit haze (a mirrored wall inside a closed box stays dark). 0 = the haze everywhere (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan RT reflections: a reflection ray whose first surface is the back of a one-sided opaque face at most 2 m behind it started inside a solid (a shiny surface at a room's corner, a hair inside the neighbouring prim) -- it stops there and reflects black instead of passing through the wall and showing the world outside (lit lines along the corner seams of a sealed room, which screen-space reflections then spread over the walls). One-sided faces seen from behind farther back are still passed, as the camera's view does. 0 = always pass them (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan RT reflections debug view: each ray-traced reflection shows where its hit's light comes from, as shares of the hit's total -- RED the ambient term (GI radiance cache / probes / sky ambient, per RenderVKGIHitAmbient), GREEN the environment (specular / shiny) term, BLUE the haze in-scatter between the surface and the hit, WHITE local lights + emission. Brightness = the hit's total light (x4). Pixels in normal colours were not ray traced. Live.

Vulkan debug view (RenderVKRTReflections 1): every ray-traced reflection shows where its hit's environment came from instead of its colour (tinted by the reflecting surface's own colour): GREEN = the hit's occlusion ray escaped to the open sky (nothing within 4 km: probes / sky along it), RED = blocked (GI radiance cache, or black), CYAN = blocked, but only farther than RenderVKRTReflectionsMaxDist (counted as an escape before 2026-10-23), orange between = partly (through alpha-blend faces), YELLOW mixed in = the reflection grazed or crossed the hit's surface (smooth / normal-mapped shading) and its occlusion ray was bent back onto the side it arrived from, WHITE = no occlusion test (GI or RenderVKRTReflectionsHitOcclusion off, water, fullbright hits), BLUE = the reflection ray hit nothing (the reflecting pixel's own probe / sky env); MAGENTA mixed in = alpha-blend layers in front. Pixels in their normal colours are not ray traced (screen-space reflection, probes, or too rough). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): how the reflection rays alpha-test cut-out (alpha-mask) surfaces -- eyebrows, lashes, hair cards, leaves, grass. 0 (default) = like the main view: the test samples the texture at ONE render pixel's footprint (not the wider footprint a sparse ray or a rough receiver blurs its colour over), with the main view's mip bias and its per-mip coverage boost (RenderVKAlphaMipCoverage), so thin cut-outs on plain alpha mips (Bakes on Mesh) stay in the reflection. 1 = the old rule (the colour footprint's mip, no coverage boost; A/B: thin cut-outs can vanish). 2 = always the finest mip (A/B). 3 = every alpha-mask surface solid, no alpha test (A/B: a cut-out that is still missing never reaches the test -- culling, mask class or geometry, not alpha). With GPU timers on, the VKGpu "RT reflections" line reports "avatar mask cand: tested/ray, rejected, rescued by coverage". Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1): 1 (default) = SIZE-CLASS SEGMENTS. Static opaque objects smaller than RenderVKRTReflectionsSmallSize carry their own ray-tracing class, and a reflection ray first traces up to the distance where such an object would cover less than RenderVKRTReflectionsSizeFootprintPx reflected pixels (the ray cone: one render pixel at the reflecting surface, spreading with the pixel angle and the surface roughness), then -- only if nothing was hit -- traces the rest of its length without them. Sharp mirrors therefore keep every small object to hundreds of metres; rough floors drop them a few metres out, where they would be blurred to nothing anyway. Alpha-blended layers in the reflection skip small objects past the same distance. Shadows, probes, acoustics and every other ray still see all objects. 0 = every ray traces every class over its whole length (A/B). The VKGpu timer log's "RT reflections" line reports it ("size segments: ..."). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, RenderVKRTReflectionsSizeClasses): the size bound, in metres, of the small object class: a static opaque object whose bounding-box diagonal is below it is small. Only static opaque objects are classed (avatars, attachments, alpha-masked and alpha-blended objects are not; alpha-blended reflection layers test their own bounds against it). 0 = no small class. Clamped to 64. Live (objects re-class on the next frame)

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, RenderVKRTReflectionsSizeClasses): how many reflected pixels a small object (RenderVKRTReflectionsSmallSize) may still cover where reflection rays stop seeing it. The ray cone gives each reflection ray its pixel footprint along the ray; small objects drop out past the distance where the size bound equals this many footprints. 1 (default) = once they are below one reflected pixel. Higher = drops them nearer (cheaper, may lose small detail in rough reflections); lower = keeps them farther. 0 = use the fixed RenderVKRTReflectionsSmallDist instead. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, RenderVKRTReflectionsSizeClasses, RenderVKRTReflectionsSizeFootprintPx 0): the fixed distance, in metres along a reflection ray, past which small objects (RenderVKRTReflectionsSmallSize) are no longer traced. Ignored while RenderVKRTReflectionsSizeFootprintPx is above 0 (the footprint rule, which keeps small objects in sharp mirrors). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting): 1 (default) = the reflection ray density falls smoothly with the surface roughness instead of in 2x2 block levels. Below RenderVKRTReflectionsSharpRough a pixel keeps the density RenderVKRTReflectionsScale gives it today (mirrors unchanged); from there it falls about linearly to RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityMin at the RT roughness cutoff (RenderVKRTReflectionsRough). Which pixels cast is an even ordered-dither pattern (no visible blocks), and a cell whose pattern pixel is not reflective hands its ray to a reflective pixel of the same cell, so edges and thin features keep rays. The resolve filter gathers from the nearest rays (about 1 / sqrt(density) pixels apart) on the same surface. RenderVKRTReflectionsRayBudget scales every density down evenly (never below one ray per 2x2 for full-density pixels). 0 = the 2x2 block levels (A/B). The VKGpu timer log's "RT reflections" line reports it ("density gradient: ..." and the ray density bands). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityGradient 1): the ray density at the roughest ray-traced surfaces (roughness at RenderVKRTReflectionsRough), as rays per pixel. 0.015625 (default, 1/64) = about one ray per 8x8 pixels; their reflections are blurred by the resolve anyway. Clamped to 1/256 .. 1. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityGradient 1): the shape of the density ramp from RenderVKRTReflectionsSharpRough to RenderVKRTReflectionsRough: density = mix(max, RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityMin, t^curve), t the roughness position along the ramp. 1 (default) = linear; below 1 the density drops sooner (cheaper), above 1 it stays high longer. Clamped to 0.1 .. 10. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityGradient 1, #859 noise): ray density for CURVED receivers. A receiver whose surface normal turns quickly across the screen (a railing, chrome trim, a small rounded fitting) gets enough rays that neighbouring rays stay within this many degrees of each other's normal, so the resolve can fill the pixels between them: density = (normal change per pixel / this)^2, up to one ray per pixel -- above the floor (RenderVKRTReflectionsScale), the roughness and the strength densities, which describe flat surfaces. Before it such receivers got the sparse lattice of a flat surface (one ray per 4x4 or 8x8 pixels), most of their pixels found no ray on their own surface and kept the probe: a speckle of traced and probe pixels that crawled with the camera jitter. Large gently curved surfaces (car bodies, columns seen from afar) are unaffected. Edges (creases over ~75 degrees, depth steps) do not count. Costs rays only on curved receivers (the budget still applies); the mark pass reads 4 neighbours per candidate. 0 = off (the previous densities). Default 12. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting, #859 noise): 1 (default) = the RT reflection resolve accumulates its result over frames. The rays are sparse (RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityGradient / _Strength) and taken at jittered pixel centres, so each frame reconstructs a slightly different reflection where it varies quickly across the screen -- read as noise, which DLSS / TAA cannot hold because a reflection moves with its virtual image, not with the surface. Each pixel takes its history from where the REFLECTED IMAGE was last frame (the view ray continued past the surface by the hit distance), checked to lie on the same surface plane; on curved, bumpy or rough surfaces (and when that check fails) from where the surface itself was. The history is clamped to this frame's neighbourhood (no ghosting past what the current rays support) and blended 20 % new per frame; teleports / camera cuts reset it. Costs 16 bytes per render pixel of VRAM (two history layers; 15 MB at 1280x720, 133 MB at 3840x2160) and a few texel reads per reflective pixel. Not used where DLSS Ray Reconstruction takes the reflections raw (RenderVKDlssRawSignals bit 4). 0 = off (no history; the RT targets are re-created on a change). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting, #859 noise): 1 (default) = the RT reflection resolve weighs each neighbouring ray by how close its REFLECTION DIRECTION is to the pixel's own (within the surface's glossy lobe), not only by whether it lies on the same plane, and adds specular anti-aliasing: a receiver whose shading normal varies within a pixel (normal maps, small curved objects) gets its reflection averaged over the directions its pixel covers instead of one point sample per pixel that changes with every camera jitter offset (shimmer on bumpy polished floors at grazing angles, sparkle on chrome). The trace's ray cone also widens by the receiver's curvature, so hit textures are sampled at the matching mip. 0 = the previous resolve (plane + 25 degree normal gate, own ray only on sharp surfaces). Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1, split deferred lighting): 1 (default) = ray-traced reflections follow how VISIBLE a pixel's reflection is, not only its roughness. Each reflective pixel gets a strength: the share of its final colour the traced reflection can change (PBR: the Fresnel reflectance at the view angle, so grazing angles keep rays; legacy shiny: 0.5 x intensity^2 x its Fresnel, as the shading mixes it in; legacy specular maps: specular x glossiness / 4; each times the share SSR and the planar mirror leave to the environment). Below RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthCut the pixel casts no ray and keeps SSR + the probe; above it the ray density (RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityGradient) falls from its roughness value at RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthFull to RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityMin at RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthMin, and the traced reflection fades in between the cutoff and the minimum (no visible edge). Never more rays than without it. 0 = roughness only (the previous candidates and densities). The VKGpu timer log's "RT reflections" line reports the candidates, mean strength by type and the cut count; RenderVKDebugView 28 shows the densities. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflectionsStrength 1): the reflection strength at and above which a pixel keeps the full ray density its roughness gives it. 0.25 (default): metals, mirrors and strongly shiny surfaces. Clamped above RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthMin, at most 1. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflectionsStrength 1): the reflection strength at and below which a pixel's ray density is RenderVKRTReflectionsDensityMin (the density rises about linearly from here to RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthFull). The traced reflection also fades in from RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthCut up to this strength. 0.03 (default). Clamped to RenderVKRTReflectionsStrengthCut .. 1. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflectionsStrength 1): below this reflection strength a pixel casts no reflection ray and keeps SSR + the reflection probe (a head-on legacy shiny-low face is about 0.008). 0.02 (default); 0 = only the strength-scaled density, nothing cut. Clamped to 0 .. 1. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKRTReflections 1; #869): 1 = WORLD-SPACE LIGHT RESERVOIR GRID for the ray-traced reflection hits. Once per frame a compute pass (GPU timer c_light_regir) fills a camera-centred grid of cells (RenderVKLightGridCellSize, RenderVKLightGridLevels) with light samples drawn in proportion to each light's unshadowed reach into the cell (brightness x distance falloff x projector cone; RenderVKLightGridReservoirs per cell), from this frame's lights, so moving and colour-cycling lights are always current. A reflection hit then evaluates only RenderVKLightGridPicks of them (resampled for the hit's position and normal, weighted so the average is the exact light sum) instead of every light in range; a cell reached by no more lights than that evaluates them all exactly, and a hit whose reflected pixel covers less than RenderVKLightGridFootprintCm (close sharp mirrors) keeps the exact walk. The sun / moon, probes and ambient stay exact. Rough reflections get some noise, smoothed by the reflection resolve's spatial filter. 0 (default) = every light in range of a hit is evaluated (A/B reference). The VKGpu timer log's "RT reflections" line reports it after "hit shading:" (grid=..., hit split, candidates per cell, picks, changed lights, memory). Fixed 8.5 MiB buffer, allocated the first time it is turned on. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKLightGrid 1): local lights fully evaluated per ray-traced reflection hit that samples the light grid (1 .. 4). Each pick takes the projector shadow-ray budget (RenderVKRTReflectionsHitShadowRays) like an exact light. Higher = less noise, slower. A grid cell reached by no more lights than this evaluates all of them exactly. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKLightGrid 1): light samples stored per grid cell (2 .. 16), drawn stratified in proportion to each light's reach into the cell; the hit picks among them. Higher = the hit's choice is better informed (less noise) at a little more cost per hit and build. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKLightGrid 1): edge of the light grid's finest cells in metres (0.125 .. 16, default 1). The grid is a camera-centred clipmap of 32 x 32 x 16 cells per level, each level's cells twice the size of the one inside it (RenderVKLightGridLevels levels). Smaller = samples fit their spot better (less noise) but the grid covers less. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKLightGrid 1): nested levels of the light grid (1 .. 4, default 4). With the 1 m default cell: 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 m cells, the outermost reaching +-128 m across and +-64 m up and down around the camera. Reflection hits outside the grid keep the exact light walk. Live

Vulkan (RenderVKLightGrid 1): a ray-traced reflection hit whose reflected pixel covers less than this many centimetres there (the ray cone at the hit: a sharp mirror up close) keeps the exact light walk, so close-up mirrors stay noise-free. 0 = every hit samples the grid. Live

Vulkan: offscreen snapshots (Snapshot floater, world / world+HUD / depth) light their opaque surfaces with the same deferred lighting path as the main view (RenderVKDeferredLighting), so a snapshot matches the live view. Off = snapshots take the forward lit pass (the pre-2026-10 behaviour; A/B for snapshot-vs-live differences). The G-buffer is re-created at the snapshot size for the shot and back at the window size on the next frame.

Depth-only passes (sun shadow cascades, projector shadows, the depth pre-pass, the alpha-blend depth pass, the shadow translucency layer; static, rigged and cluster LOD draws) use a reduced vertex shader that computes only the position (+ the alpha test's UV / material / tint / flags) instead of the full world VS with its normal / tangent / motion / lighting outputs: far fewer registers, so higher occupancy in vertex-bound shadow passes (biggest on older GPUs). Bit-identical depth to the full VS (same source lines, invariant position), so the EQUAL passes after the pre-pass still match. Live A/B: both pipeline sets are built; the next frame picks the set. The pre-pass variants that also write normals / motion (AO / TAA frames) get their own slim VS too: only the normal frame / world + previous position their fragment shader reads (no colour, cel, pick, terrain record).

Deferred-lit frames pre-pass DEPTH ONLY (+ motion vectors with TAA / FSR): the G-buffer pass writes the normals anyway, so the pre-pass no longer runs the normal fragment shader, and ambient occlusion moves to after the G-buffer pass, reading the G-buffer normals (G1: the shading normal and the smooth vertex normal). The lighting consumes AO in its final (combine) step only. Forward-lit frames, and frames whose effects (FX) read the pre-pass normals, keep the depth + normal pre-pass. 0 = the depth + normal pre-pass in every AO / TAA frame (as before). Live A/B.

#1088: how the passes after the depth pre-pass (lit main pass, deferred G-buffer, probe-face mask passes) test depth. 0 (default) = an ordered compare (greater-or-equal under reversed-Z) without depth write: hidden fragments still fail it exactly as with EQUAL, but a surface whose depth comes out one rounding step nearer than the pre-pass's still shades -- some drivers (AMD Windows, Vega iGPUs) compute positions slightly differently per pipeline, which with EQUAL left thin dark lines along triangle edges and holes in alpha-masked text. 1 = exact EQUAL (as before). The compare is dynamic state: no recompile, early depth rejection unchanged. The terminator-triangle and avatar-id passes keep EQUAL (they have no alpha test). Live A/B.

With RenderVKPrepassDepthOnlyDeferred: ambient occlusion (after the G-buffer pass) runs on the async compute queue, overlapping the deferred lighting's shadow and reflection resolves on the graphics queue; the combine step waits for it. 0 = AO inline on the graphics queue before the lighting (A/B for GPUs where async compute does not overlap well). Needs RenderVKAsyncCompute and split deferred lighting (RenderVKDeferredSplit); otherwise AO runs inline. Live A/B.

!!! DO NOT TURN THIS OFF. !!! Turning it off switches to an old forward fallback that is about 2.5x slower in busy places (measured 91 -> 38 FPS) AND disables ambient occlusion and the ray-traced shadow mask (avatars lose AO and soft RT shadows). Leave it ON (TRUE). The fallback is scheduled for removal (#640). Technical: depth-only pre-pass over the opaque + alpha-mask draws before the lit main pass, which then depth-tests EQUAL so every visible pixel is shaded once; its depth / normals / motion also feed AO, the RT shadow mask, VRS and Hi-Z occlusion.

Diagnostic: an avatar's user name, display name or UUID. Logs the Vulkan ingest state (faces in scene, LODs, textures/bakes, alpha mode) of every attachment it wears, once per value (VKIngestDiag). Clear it to reset.
Diagnostic (#610): log, at most once per second, avatar collision-volume pick hits with their distance from the avatar (a ghost hit far from it = stale volumes) (VKPickDiag).

GPU raster cursor pick (#702 / #704) diagnostics: log every click pick (hover picks up to 4 per second) with its answer (to the exact ray / trailing / none), the candidate draws and fragments, any depth-window paging, and the object it chose with its claim; plus a per-second summary of exact / trailing / unanswered picks, picks answered between frames and pages (tag VKPick).

GPU raster cursor pick (#702): a click's async pick (pickAsync: tools, focus, grab, build) whose exact GPU answer is not in yet waits for it -- the per-frame request asks for the click's pixel, the pick (and the input after it) is held 2-4 frames, nothing blocks -- instead of a blocking answer between frames behind the frames in flight (~1.5 GPU frames). Held at most 8 frames, then answered between frames as before. Picks made synchronously inside a click (pickImmediate) still answer between frames when needed. Live

Vulkan temporal pipeline (#84) debug switch: turns on temporal anti-aliasing (per-instance previous transforms, motion vectors from the depth pre-pass, Halton(2,3) sub-pixel jitter of the main view, and the TAA resolve before the tonemapper) regardless of RenderFSAAType. The normal way to enable it is RenderFSAAType 3 ("TAA" in Preferences). TAA replaces FXAA / SMAA while on. Motion vectors need RenderVKDepthPrepass (without it the resolve falls back to camera-only motion).

Vulkan TAA (#84) debug view, replacing the resolved image: 1 = red reactive mask (transparents / particles over the scene after water, history weight reduced), green history rejected (off-screen, reset, disocclusion by depth), blue history weight; 2 = the motion the resolve used (|x|, |y| pixels / 8); 3 = below native render scale, the resolve without rectification (history not clipped to the current neighbourhood; a real image, for bisecting upscale jitter); 4 = how far rectification pulled the history (grey x8); 5 = the current frame's share of each pixel (grey x5); 6 = the water mask (#204: blue = water, reprojected on the water plane; red in it = its history rejected; grey = not water). The real resolve keeps running underneath every view (history stays valid); views 4 and 5 are measured against this frame's resolve, so they are approximate.

Vulkan RT shadow mask (B5): skip copying the 4-layer projector history when the previous mask frame had no ray-traced projector records (it is then never sampled). 0 = copy every frame (old behaviour). Switchable live

Vulkan RT shadow mask (F3a): ping-pong temporal history. Two history slots and two mask descriptor sets alternate per mask frame, so last frame's temporal output IS this frame's history: no per-frame history copies (acc sun, 4-layer acc proj, ids, depth, meta: ~300 MB of traffic at half-res 4K); the trace writes its ids / depth plane a second time into the history slot instead. 0 = the copy path (RenderVKRTMaskSkipIdleProjHistory applies there). A switch drops the history for one frame. Switchable live

Vulkan RT shadow mask diagnostic: at most every 10 s, one log line (VKRTMaskDiag) with how many of an 8x8 grid of surface texels the sun shadow covers at each stage of the mask (one-frame trace, temporal accumulation, final mask), the history length, the frame info's sun shadow mode as the GPU saw it, and the renderer's sun / mask state. Costs a few tiny GPU copies on the sampled frame. Live

Vulkan temporal (F6): rigged previous-frame positions (motion vectors) come from LAST frame's pre-skin output -- a 2-slot position history plus a per-instance table of where each instance's skinned range was -- instead of a second skin-palette dispatch over last frame's joints and a second skin per vertex. Instances new / back in view, or whose LOD or skin changed, get previous = current for one frame (camera motion only); re-skinned reduced-avatar cache items take their old cached pose under last frame's pelvis. 0 = re-skin with last frame's palettes (old path). Switchable live Default off: measured +0.28 ms c_preskin / GPU total on the worst-case foliage sim (RTX 5090, 2026-10-02) -- the history writes cost more than the second skinning pass they replace.

Vulkan GPU pre-skin (clean_preskin.comp, #822): a rigged work item with at least this many vertices first copies its skin's bone palette (110 joints x 48 B = 5.2 KB) into workgroup shared memory, so each vertex's four joint fetches no longer wait on its weight load through the cache hierarchy (a dependent-load chain per vertex). Smaller items read the palette buffer per vertex as before (the copy would cost more than it saves). Bit-identical output. 0 = never stage (A/B). GPU timer: c_preskin. Live

Vulkan (I-6): the world passes' full-resolution glow attachment uses the packed B10G11R11 float format (4 B/px) instead of RGBA16F (8 B/px) when the device can blend and sample it. The target is zero almost everywhere and nothing reads its alpha; precision drops to 6/6/5 mantissa bits before the TAA glow resolve / 512x512 blur chain (which stay RGBA16F), so bloom / glow are visually the same but not bit-identical. Packing glow into the HDR target's alpha is not possible: glow is an RGB (display-encoded colour x glow) term blended with its own coverage. Read at startup (restart to switch)

Vulkan (C7): with GPU avatar animation, copy and stream only the CPU joint-table rows the animation compute reads -- this frame's CPU-evaluated (mode 0) avatars -- and only those that changed, instead of copying and streaming the whole table (216 matrices per avatar) every frame. The renderer's copy is kept as a mirror of the GPU table; a re-created table is streamed in full. 0 = whole table every frame. Switchable live

Vulkan (C8): rate of the rolling self-heal slices that re-check rows on top of the dirty runs -- instance rows re-copied / re-streamed (and so re-copied to the previous-instance store and re-visited by texture demand, material refs and RT), the RT rigged-set re-check and the material-reference re-check. 0 = off (dirty runs only), 1 = low (instances n/256 min 16 per frame, RT max(256, n/256), material refs max(256, n/256)), 2 = the old rates (n/64 min 64, 2048, max(2048, n/32)). Switchable live

Vulkan leak watching: once a minute, log a detailed per-store dump (VKMem detail) of the clean stores -- materials, terrain records, skins, particle emitters, instances, bindless textures, animation keyframe arena -- with live / free / pending-retire / high-water / capacity counts, lifetime freed / reused totals and CPU / GPU bytes. The one-line VKMem stores summary is logged every 5 s with RenderVKMemoryLog regardless. 0 = off

Vulkan ingest (C9): time budget (ms) for draining the changed-object queue each frame, on top of its 96-object cap; at least 8 objects are processed per frame (HUD objects first). 0 = the count cap only

Vulkan ingest (C9): after the changed-object queue re-registers an object, record its fresh ingest signature (plus the face-bounds and incomplete-object steps of a full sweep visit) instead of erasing it, so the registration sweep's next visit does not re-register the whole object a second time. Its heavy pre-steps (LOD, volume) still run on that visit. 0 = erase (old behaviour). Switchable live

Vulkan (F9): depth-test the main-view sky against the depth pre-pass (EQUAL at the reversed-Z far plane, no write), so only uncovered pixels run the sky shader. 0 = full-screen sky with no depth test (old behaviour). Same image either way. Switchable live

Vulkan debug: FALSE drops the sun-glow term (haze_glow) from the atmospheric haze on surfaces, alpha, particles and water. The sky's own sun glow is unaffected. For checking whether a glow seen on geometry comes from the haze. Not saved.

Vulkan (F11): skip the pre-water refraction copy (a full-resolution HDR copy) when no water surface can be in view: the main frustum's height range misses every region's water height (skyboxes above the draw distance, looking up), or the Water render type is off. 0 = copy every frame (old behaviour). Switchable live

Vulkan (F8): in the main-view alpha-blend draw pair, the vertex shader collapses what the fragment shader would only discard -- single-sided faces in the cull-front (back-face) draw, and the water surface in both draws -- so they are never rasterized. Same image. 0 = old behaviour. Switchable live

Vulkan (F10): fill the GPU cull's per-reason reject histogram (one same-address atomic per rejected instance and per emitted draw, in every cull) and log it with the per-bucket draw counts (VKFunnel CULL / CULLREASON) plus the skinVerts* / shadowRigDropped / rigCache* hitch counters. Off: only the two reasons the renderer acts on (rigged capacity, skin cache full) are counted. Switchable live

Vulkan (B1 / F4a): RenderCASSharpness sharpens once -- RCAS on the TAA resolve when it runs, else CAS in the final pass (it used to do both, and RCAS also ran without TAA). The output dither then moves into the tonemap whenever the tonemap is the last full-screen pass (no FXAA / SMAA, no LDR glow), so the final pass (and its full-resolution LDR round trip) is skipped unless vignette, grain, CVD, lens distortion, previews, the reference still or the scopes need it. 0 = the old double sharpening and always-on final pass. Switchable live

Vulkan debug (#1075 layered stereo, step 0: the A/B gate): hash the world image at capture point 1 (after the final pass: world only, no selection outline, HUD or UI) every frame through a small readback ring, and log it (tag VKFrameHash, FRAMEHASH lines) when it changes and every 600 frames while it holds; also log the recorded-stream signature (FRAMESIG: the sub-mark names in order) when it changes. For a desktop A/B hold a fixed camera with TAA off and time / weather frozen, then compare two logs with scripts/perf/vk_ab_compare.py. Costs one full-image copy per frame while on. Switchable live

Vulkan debug (#1075 layered stereo, design step 8): render the desktop world as this many views (1 = normal; 2 = stereo: both eyes as layers of one multiview recording, RenderVKDebugStereoIPD apart; up to 4), the window showing view 0. The decisive test of the layered path without a headset: with IPD 0 every layer must equal the single-view image (RenderVKDebugFrameHash logs one FRAMEHASH per layer). Effects not yet converted to layers are off while it is above 1. Read at startup (restart to apply); ignored in VR

Vulkan debug (#1075 layered stereo, the desktop N = 2 mode, RenderVKDebugViewCount 2): the eyes' separation in millimetres, along the camera's right axis, each eye with the camera's own projection. 0 = every view is the camera itself -- the decisive equality test (layer 0 == layer 1 == the single-view image). Ignored in VR (the headset's located eyes). Switchable live

Vulkan VR (#1075 layered stereo, A/B): the headset's hidden-area mesh (XR_KHR_visibility_mask) is laid into each eye's depth at the near plane before the pre-pass, so the pixels the lens never shows are rejected by every depth-tested pass instead of shaded. Off = every eye pixel is shaded (the old cost). No effect on the desktop or without the extension. GPU timer: g_vr_vismask. Live, not saved

Vulkan (B2 / F4c): skip the colour half of the per-frame previous-frame copy (scene -> SSR source, a full-resolution HDR copy) when nothing reads it: screen-space reflections off and no legacy non-TAA RCAS (RenderVKSharpenOnce 0). The depth half and every layout transition stay. SSR waits one frame for a fresh copy when switched on. 0 = always copy. Switchable live

Vulkan (B9): sort main-view alpha-blend buckets past the 4096-draw single-workgroup cap with a multi-workgroup bitonic sort (recorded while the alpha counts read back near the cap; 2x headroom). Without it, draws past 4096 in a bucket were appended unsorted to the post-water set. 0 = the old cap. Switchable live

Vulkan (#835): rigged alpha-blend draws sort by the centre of their posed box pulled a quarter of its extent toward the camera (LL's alpha face distance), so nested layers of one mesh (fur / onion-skin shells over a solid base) keep one order, the enclosing layer drawn last. 0 = the centre alone (1.3 beta 13: such layers swapped order frame to frame and flickered). Live

DEBUG (Vulkan, #238): use the 2048-draw alpha-sort variants (about 20 KiB of compute shared memory) even when the device could run the 4096-draw ones (about 36 KiB). Devices with less than that maxComputeSharedMemorySize (AMD GCN / Polaris: 32 KiB) always use them. For testing the fallback; takes effect after restart.

Vulkan (#565): storage format of the reflection-probe radiance cube arrays, for an in-world comparison. 0 = RGBA16F (8 B/texel, the reference). 1 = RGB9E5 shared exponent (4 B/texel; weak on saturated colours next to dim ones). 2 = R11G11B10 float (4 B/texel; banding on smooth gradients, slight hue shift on greys). 3 = BC6H (1 B/texel, GPU-encoded after each scheduled capture; the default sky probe and the realtime probe stay uncompressed RGBA16F; 4x4 block artifacts on mirror-like surfaces). Unsupported formats fall back (3 -> 1 -> 0, 2 -> 0) with a log line. Default is 1 (RGB9E5). Changing it re-allocates the probes and re-captures them all (no restart); resolution (RenderReflectionProbeResolution) is independent.

Vulkan (#238): realtime reflection probe faces rendered per frame. 6 = all six faces + filter every frame. 1-5 = a rotating subset per frame, filtered once all six are done (lower GPU load per frame; the probe refreshes every 6/N frames). 0 = auto: 2 on AMD GCN 1-4 / Polaris (whose driver can TDR on the six-face capture), 6 elsewhere.

Vulkan ingest worker: prim tessellation + tangents and the capture preparation (interleave, bounds, index checks) of async-decoded meshes run on worker threads; the render thread commits the results to the mesh store at the start of the ingest tick (before the frame's store fill) and re-ingests the waiting objects. Flexi prims, sculpts and local meshes stay synchronous. 0 = capture inline (old path).

Vulkan CPU overlap: run the clean-store -> renderer CPU-mirror fill (instance dirty runs, geometry repack, material / LOD-group copies) on a worker thread while the main thread buffers the UI, joining before the texture resolve and command recording. vk_fillJoinWait shows main-thread time still spent waiting for it. 0 = fill inline on the main thread.

Vulkan: the self-heal registration sweep drops to its idle rate (1/8 slice + budget) when a full lap's own visits found fewer than ~2% changed objects (signature changes / new objects), instead of judging by the global instance-upsert count -- which every mover, animesh and scripted change in a busy sim keeps high, holding the sweep at full rate forever. 0 = the old rule.

Vulkan: full-detail avatars beyond RenderVKAvatarAnimNearM evaluate animation at 30 FPS and beyond RenderVKAvatarAnimFarM at 15 FPS (staggered per avatar; their position still updates every frame). Your own avatar and animesh are never throttled. 0 = every frame.
Vulkan: camera distance (m) beyond which full-detail avatars animate at 30 FPS (RenderVKAvatarDistanceAnimRate).
Vulkan: camera distance (m) beyond which full-detail avatars animate at 15 FPS (RenderVKAvatarDistanceAnimRate).

Vulkan (GPU animation): full-detail avatars also evaluate animation at a reduced rate by on-screen height -- every frame at and above RenderVKAvatarAnimFullPx, 30 FPS below it, 20 FPS below half, 15 FPS below a quarter (the slower of this and RenderVKAvatarDistanceAnimRate wins; 10% hysteresis). Never within RenderVKAvatarAnimScreenMinM of the camera, never your own avatar or animesh. Their root still moves every frame. Counters avPxAnimSkip / avPxAnimEval.

Vulkan debug (#725): log every other avatar's animation-rate transitions (VKAnimRate: rate, reason near / large / px / dist / reduced / hidden / exempt, on-screen height, camera distance, pixel area, reduced-tier rank; at most once a second per avatar) and show the current rate in the avatar's hover text.

Avatar animation debug (#631, stuck rest pose): every 15 seconds, log each other avatar's animation state (VKAnimState: visibility and why, overall appearance, last pose evaluation, signaled vs playing animations and the state of each one's motion, GPU animation mode / slot / seed / export, unresolved rigged skins). Lines for avatars that look stuck are tagged SUSPECT. Refresh Animations always logs the avatar's state, with or without this setting.
Vulkan: avatars closer to the camera than this (m) always animate every frame, whatever their on-screen size (RenderVKAvatarAnimScreenLOD).

Vulkan A/B bench: set TRUE to start. Steps RenderVKBenchSetting through RenderVKBenchValues (RenderVKBenchSeconds each, RenderVKBenchCycles rounds, first RenderVKBenchSettle s after each switch discarded), logs per-value frame avg / p50 / p99 / FPS / GPU wait / GPU total / RenderVKBenchSubs sub-marks under the VKBench log tag, restores the setting and clears itself. GPU numbers need RenderVKGpuTimers.
Vulkan A/B bench: the setting to step (Boolean, U32, S32, F32 or String).
Vulkan A/B bench: comma-separated values to step RenderVKBenchSetting through (e.g. 1,3,0).

Vulkan A/B bench: comma-separated names to average per value -- GPU sub-marks (g_lit_static, pr_rt_face, c_rtmask, q_async_busy ...) and/or CPU section timers from the section log (sweep_total, vk_sync_total, ui_draw, LL_idle_total, renderFrame ...).
Vulkan A/B bench: seconds per value (min 2).
Vulkan A/B bench: seconds discarded after each switch (pipeline builds, history resets, timer latency).
Vulkan A/B bench: rounds through the value list (interleaved, so scene drift averages out).

Vulkan TAA (#204): anti-flicker at native resolution. A pixel whose history has stayed valid for several frames widens its rectification box by up to this many sigma and takes a smaller share of each new frame, so thin / distant geometry stops shimmering between jitter phases. 0 = off (the plain 1-sigma box); higher = steadier but slower to follow changes without motion vectors. Clamped to 0..3. Switchable live

Vulkan TAA: resolve the per-face glow target with the scene (same motion, rejection and share; its own clip box) into a display-sized history that the HDR bloom extract and the LDR glow read. Off = they sample the raw jittered render-resolution target, so glowing faces and their surroundings shimmer (worse with RenderVKRenderScale below 1). Its cost is inside the p_taa GPU timer: toggle to measure. Switchable live

Vulkan TAA (#84, #204): material texture mip bias while the main view is jittered (RenderFSAAType 3 / RenderVKTAA / render scale below 1), in mips; negative = sharper. The resolve averages the extra detail over the jitter phases; too negative and fine high-contrast texture detail (distant brick, fences, foliage) aliases and shimmers. Below native the render scale's log2 is added on top. Clamped to -2..1. Switchable live

Vulkan (#226, testing): when non-zero, the video memory pre-checks for setting-driven allocations (reflection probe resolution / count, shadow quality, RT shadow resolution, projector shadow atlas) treat the device-local budget as at most this many MB (current usage stays real), so the revert + notice path can be tested on a big card. Also caps the budget the VRAM pressure ladder (#282) and the texture budget measure, to test the ladder on a big card. 0 = the real budget.

Vulkan (#695, testing, needs restart): in UMA mode (an integrated GPU with a carve-out, or RenderVKDebugForceUma), treat the carve-out (device-local) heap budget as at most this many MB, so the spill of device-local allocations to the shared host heap and the combined budget can be tested with a 512 MB carve-out on any card. 0 = the real budget.

Vulkan (#695, testing, needs restart): treat this GPU as an integrated (UMA) GPU -- the VRAM budget becomes the device-local heap + a share of the system-memory heap (RenderVKUmaSharedRamPercent), texture pools go to the larger of the two and device-local allocations spill to system memory once the device-local heap is full. With RenderVKDebugFakeCarveoutMB 512 this simulates a Ryzen APU on a discrete card (slow: system memory over PCIe).

Vulkan (#84): show the motion-vector target instead of the image (enables motion vectors without jitter). Hue = screen direction, brightness = speed (full at 16 px per frame), black = no motion or sky. A still camera leaves the static world black and colours only moving objects and spinners; any camera motion colours everything.

Vulkan (#118): photographic motion blur. Things that move on screen streak along their motion: another avatar flying past, and (at half strength by default) the world when you fly or drive fast. Turning or orbiting the camera does not blur by default, and what the camera follows (your own avatar) stays sharp. Runs on the scene before TAA / FSR, which smooth out its sampling noise; without either it uses a fixed, stable pattern. Costs a little GPU time even when nothing moves (about 18 bytes read/written per pixel); more where things move. Uses the depth pre-pass motion vectors (keeps them on with TAA off: about 4 bytes per pixel plus the previous-transform history) and about 16 bytes per pixel of its own working images, freed when off. Off by default. Live. Supersampled snapshots render a frozen world (no blur); single-frame snapshots carry the live motion.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur): exposure time in seconds -- how long a streak is. Scaled by the frame time (at most 8 frames of motion), so the look does not depend on the frame rate. 1/60 s (default) = a 180-degree shutter at 30 FPS; 1/30 s = twice as long; 0 = no blur. Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur): longest blur, as a radius in pixels of a 1080-line image (scaled to your resolution, so the look is the same at any size; the streak can be twice this long). 1-64, default 24. Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur): samples per pixel along the blur (4-32, even; default 16). Short blurs use fewer automatically. More = smoother long streaks without TAA / FSR, at a higher cost where things move (none where nothing does). Single-frame snapshots use twice as many. Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur): how much turning the camera blurs (mouselook, turning, orbiting, zooming), 0-2. Default 0: the view stays sharp while you look around, the sky never blurs. 1 = physically correct. Only ever removes blur the motion really has (never adds any). Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur): how much moving the camera blurs the world (flying, driving, walking), 0-2. Default 0.5: a fast flight streaks the scenery with half the physical blur -- noticeable and cinematic without smearing every step you walk. 1 = physically correct. What the camera follows (your own avatar) stays sharp whatever this is. Live.
Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur): how much things that move by themselves blur (other avatars, vehicles, moving and spinning prims), 0-2. Default 1 = physically correct. Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur) debug view, replaces the image: 1 = tiles (16 px; upper-left half of each tile its fastest pixel, lower-right half the blur that tile samples along; hue = direction, brightness = length; dim tiles skip the blur entirely), 2 = what moves (red = camera turning, green = camera moving, blue = the object itself; raw, before the strength settings). 0 = off (default). Not saved. Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur, #836): the uniform-motion shortcut (a plain box blur with no depth test) only runs on a tile when every tile its blur can reach moves at the same speed, not just the 8 tiles around it. Off = the old 3x3 check: with a max radius over 16 px the box reads tiles nobody checked and smears still things (your own avatar, a prim) into square tile-sized blocks around them. 1 = on (default). Live.

Vulkan motion blur (RenderVKMotionBlur, #836): weight each blur sample by 1 / (1 + its exposed brightness) (Karis), so a few very bright samples (emissive / fullbright surfaces, far above white before tonemapping) cannot swamp the average and bleed their colour into things next to them. Areas of one brightness blur exactly as before; bright moving streaks come out a little dimmer. 1 = on (default). Live.

Vulkan (#574): rigged vertex welding. After the GPU pre-skin, open-boundary vertices of one avatar's rigged meshes (body, head, hands, feet, add-ons) that coincide in bind space get one shared position and, below RenderVKRigWeldNormalAngle, one shared normal (tangents re-orthogonalized), closing seams and hairline gaps under animation and the lighting line across joins. Never across avatars or onto static geometry; only boundary edges (a hem lying over a body interior is not welded). Draws, shadows, probes, RT and picking all see the welded vertices. VRAM: about 9 MB at the default RenderVKRigWeldMaxVerts (freed when off). Live.
Vulkan rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld): pairing distance in millimetres, in bind space (the meshes' rest pose; 0.05-10).

Vulkan rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld): welded vertices share their normal only with neighbours within this angle in degrees (0-180); larger differences are deliberate hard edges and keep their own normal (the position is still shared).

Vulkan rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld): a pair is left alone when its skinned vertices are further apart than this, in centimetres (0.1-50): meshes whose weights move them apart for real are not pulled together.

Vulkan rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld, crowd perf): avatars whose bounds are shorter than this on screen (px) are not welded -- their seams are sub-pixel there. Your own avatar and the protected set (RenderVKRiggedProtect*) always weld. 0 = weld every avatar. Counter rigWeldSkipAv.

Vulkan rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld): most boundary vertices welded per frame (rounded up to a power of two, 4096-1048576); past it vertices are not welded (logged as dropped, VKRigWeld every 30 s). 64 B + 8 B of grid per entry. Mode 1: the most boundary vertices of one discovery (the avatars discovered in a frame).

Vulkan rigged welding (RenderVKRigWeld, #641): 0 = rediscover the weld pairs every frame by a bind-space hash search (the original #574 path, for A/B); 1 = decide each avatar's pairs once, at its rest pose with its own shape (re-decided only on attach / detach, outfit, shape, joint overrides, rigged LOD switches and weld setting changes, asynchronously), and per frame only average the listed pairs. Governs the cluster LOD weld too (#798): 1 = pairs at each avatar's rest pose (per-avatar rest rows rebuilt on the same shape / joint-override triggers, searched per frame on the cut), 0 = bind space. Live.

Vulkan rigged welding, mode 1 (#626): two vertices are welded only when their skin weights overlap at least this much (sum over the avatar joints of the smaller of the two weights: 1 = they deform identically, 0 = no joint in common; 0-1). Keeps cavities and onion-skin layers weighted to other joints from being welded shut. Changing it re-decides every avatar's pairs.

Vulkan rigged welding, mode 1 (#641): capacity of the weld pair pool, in welded vertices (records) over all avatars (4096-2097152). 72 B each on the GPU (9.4 MB at the default). Avatars whose list finds no room are not welded (VKRigWeld log, every 30 s: "no pool space").

Vulkan (#632): avatars whose animation is not re-evaluated every frame (distance / screen-size animation rate, the reduced tier, hidden avatars at RenderVKHiddenAvatarFPS) keep their rigged meshes pre-skinned in avatar-local (pelvis) space in the skin cache (RenderVKReducedAvatarSkinCache), shadows and ray tracing included. On frames their pose was held, their pre-skin, weld and ray-traced BLAS refit are skipped; only the avatar's transform moves them. Counters rigHeldSkinAv / rigHeldSkipAv. Off = only the reduced no-shadow tier uses the cache (as before). Live.

Vulkan (#167): after the depth pre-pass, build a Hi-Z pyramid from its depth and skip pass-1 drawing of static opaque/mask objects that are completely hidden behind it (exact for the current frame: no popping). Needs RenderVKDepthPrepass. Counters occlTested / occlCulled appear in the hitch-log averages. Experimental, off by default.

OFF by default for now: in open outdoor scenes it measured ~3 ms a frame SLOWER at 4K on a GTX 1080 (the extra pre-pass phase + Hi-Z build + test cost more than it culls); scene-adaptive on/off is tracked in a ticket. With it and RenderVKOcclusionCull off no Hi-Z is built, so RenderVKClusterOcclusion is idle too. Vulkan: two-phase Hi-Z occlusion culling of the main view (clean_occl2.comp). The depth pre-pass first draws the static objects that were visible last frame (phase 1, plus every avatar), builds a Hi-Z pyramid from that depth, tests every static opaque / mask / alpha-blend draw against it, then draws the newly revealed ones (phase 2). Hidden objects leave the pre-pass, pass 1 and the alpha passes; the result is exact for the current frame (no popping), last frame only decides what goes first. Supersedes RenderVKOcclusionCull. Needs RenderVKDepthPrepass. On a camera cut (teleport, region crossing, sit / stand, camera preset, big jump: the TAA history-reset signal) the frame skips the two phases, draws the plain pre-pass and seeds the visibility list from its frustum set, so the next frame culls normally. Counters occl2Tested / occl2Culled / occl2Revealed / occl2P1 / occl2AlphaTested / occl2AlphaCulled / occl2Reset / occl2CutSkips; GPU sub-marks c_occl_split, c_occl_seed, g_prepass (phase 1), c_hiz, c_occl_p2, g_prepass_p2. Measured (RTX 5090, 4K): GPU -0.26 to -0.64 ms inside buildings, about +0.03 ms in an open view, no hitches.

Vulkan (diagnostic, restart required): enable VK_KHR_pipeline_executable_properties and create every pipeline with CAPTURE_STATISTICS, then log one "VKPipeStats" line per pipeline and shader stage with every statistic the driver reports (registers, spills, instruction count, subgroup size, ...; vendor-specific) plus the pipeline's name and shader modules. Can slow pipeline creation and bypass the pipeline cache on some drivers; off = no effect at all

Vulkan (diagnostic, restart required): enable VK_KHR_shader_clock (shaderSubgroupClock) and run the deferred lighting kernels (uber and every split pass) as instrumented twins that read the subgroup clock at each stage boundary (G-buffer decode, sun visibility, projectors, atmosphere, probes, SSR, mirror, shading, local lights, haze, stores, tile phases); logs "VK shader clock" lines every ~5 s with cycles per pixel per stage and each stage's share of the kernel. The instrumented kernels are slower and use more registers than the production ones (read the shares, not the totals); off = the production kernels, no effect at all

Vulkan: count lit fragment-shader invocations in the main opaque pass (atomic counter on even frames, FS-invocation pipeline-statistics query on odd frames) and log shaded fragments / screen pixels ("overdraw factor") with the GPU timers, or on its own every ~5 s (diagnostic)
Vulkan: bypass exposure/tonemap and show the clamped linear HDR scene sRGB-encoded (diagnostic)

Vulkan tonemap (#820): the tonemap pass's whole post-exposure tail -- colour grade linear stage, tonemapper and its mix, split toning, sRGB encode, legacy gamma, and the display-space grade (hue shift, the user 3D LUT, tone curves) -- baked into a 3D lookup table (RenderVKTonemapLutSize^3, RGBA16F) over a log shaper of the exposed colour, re-baked by a tiny compute pass only when the grade / tonemapper settings change, and read with one tetrahedral lookup (4 texel fetches) per pixel. Dynamic exposure, bloom, lens effects and the dither stay per pixel. Error against the direct path (offline, 48^3): <= 1.2/255 on greys and natural colours; extreme saturated HDR colours near the gamut edge up to a few /255. 0 = always per pixel (A/B reference); 1 (default) = only while the colour grade (Lightbox) is on, where the per-pixel tail is expensive; 2 = always (the plain tonemapper too: measure with the exposure + tonemap GPU timer before making it the default). Live

Vulkan tonemap LUT (RenderVKTonemapLut, #820): the table's edge (16..64; 48^3 x 8 B = 864 KB). 32 halves the bake and the footprint (grey-axis error up to ~3/255 with Khronos Neutral); 64 tightens the gamut-edge error. A change re-creates the table (one device wait). Live
Vulkan: log a one-line VRAM summary (per-heap used/budget, allocation count, renderer categories) every ~5 s.

Vulkan (#550): built-in cel shading -- toon lighting (banded sun / moon and local lights, flattened ambient, rim light, specular step) plus outlines, on the surfaces RenderVKCelScope selects. Off by default; live

Vulkan (#549 / #550): what cel shading applies to. 0 the whole scene, 1 every avatar (rigged mesh, system bodies and worn attachments; animesh included), 2 only your own avatar, 3 only the avatars picked with the avatar context menu (Cel shade this avatar; this session), 4 friends. Changing it needs no re-ingest (per-avatar selection bitset on the GPU)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): lit levels of the toon N.L ramp for the sun / moon and local lights (1 = two-tone, 2-8 more steps)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): width of each band edge as a fraction of a band (0 = hard steps, 1 = smooth); also softens the rim edge
Vulkan cel shading (#550): flattens the ambient / probe lighting toward one luminance (0 = as lit, 1 = flat), keeping its colour
Vulkan cel shading (#550): colour of the fill light on the shadowed side of toon-lit surfaces
Vulkan cel shading (#550): strength of the shadow-side tinted fill (0 = none, 1 = as bright as the lit side)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): rim light strength at grazing angles (0 = off)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): rim light width (0..1 of the grazing range)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): strength of the hard-edged specular highlight (0 = matte toon, no highlight)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): specular luminance above which the toon highlight shows
Vulkan cel shading (#550): outline width in pixels at a 1080-line output (scaled with the output height, so snapshots match the live view; render scale aware). 0 = no outlines
Vulkan cel shading (#550): outline colour (alpha = opacity)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): brightness multiplier of a coloured outline (linear HDR; black lines are unaffected)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): outlines fade out between half this distance and this distance (metres)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): relative depth jump that draws an outline (inside an avatar, or anywhere in whole-scene mode)
Vulkan cel shading (#550): crease line sensitivity (relative depth second difference; 0 = no crease lines)

Vulkan diagnostic (#549): show the per-pixel avatar mask -- each avatar slot as a colour over the darkened scene (rigged mesh, system body, worn attachments, alpha-blended hair). Same as RenderVKDebugView 22. Allocates the avatar-id target while on

Optional extra limit on skinned (rigged) vertices the GPU-driven renderer reserves buffers for (0 = none: the combined rigged budget, RenderVKRiggedBudgetPct, decides; otherwise minimum 1000000). Buffers follow the rigged meshes actually drawn; past the limit far avatars get coarser rigged detail first, and only then are the farthest rigged meshes left out (the same ones every frame).

Draw worn rigged mesh set to alpha blending as alpha masking when its texture has no alpha channel or only fully opaque / fully transparent pixels (looks the same, sorts correctly, much cheaper with many layered avatars). Soft alpha (hair, lace, overlays) stays blended.

Share of the video memory budget (percent, 2-60) all rigged (skinned) mesh buffers are guaranteed in the GPU-driven renderer: skinned vertices and their temporal anti-aliasing history, pre-skin work lists, skin palettes. While video memory is free they may borrow more (RenderVKRiggedBudgetMaxPct). When video memory runs short the memory ladder lowers it in its own order (on cards with 8 GB or less only after mid texture detail): first far avatars draw simplified copies of their mesh, then coarser creator detail, then the share is lowered.

Vertex budget (thousands) of the avatars that are fully protected in the GPU-driven renderer (allocated first, counted in the rigged memory floor): avatars within RenderVKRiggedProtectMeters or at least 4x RenderVKRiggedProtectPixels tall on screen, largest first, until their full-detail vertices reach it. Avatars past it still keep full detail and their own LOD; only their memory priority differs. 0 = automatic (half of the per-card visible rigged vertex budget).

Avatars closer than this (metres) keep their full rigged mesh detail in the GPU-driven renderer at a crowded place (never simplified, never moved to a lower creator LOD); the protection fades out smoothly to twice this distance.

On-screen height (pixels) where the GPU-driven renderer starts protecting an avatar's rigged mesh detail at a crowded place; the protection grows smoothly to full at 4x this height (no simplification, and creator LODs only where the viewer's own LOD choice for that size would use them). Shorter avatars may be simplified more, and use lower creator LODs only at sizes where they look the same. See also RenderVKRiggedProtectMeters.

Debug (GPU-driven renderer): whether the rigged-mesh performance controller (RenderVKRiggedScreenLOD) may, after its simplified copies are exhausted, also move avatars to lower creator LODs to hold RenderVKRiggedLodTargetFPS. Even when on, an avatar never goes below the creator LOD the viewer would pick for its on-screen size and distance (scaled down to RenderVKReducedAvatarLODScale only for small or distant avatars), so large and nearby avatars keep their full mesh. 0 = never use creator LODs for performance (video-memory shortage may still use them, with the same size floor).

At a crowded place (the screen-size rigged LOD engaged), avatars shorter than this on screen (pixels) are simplified with twice the pixel tolerance, under half of it with four times (toward 1/4 and 1/8 of the triangles). 0 = off.

Screen-size rigged mesh detail at very heavy venues (GPU-driven renderer): when worn mesh takes more graphics card time than RenderVKRiggedGpuBudgetMs while the frame is slower than RenderVKRiggedLodTargetFPS and the graphics card is the bottleneck, or when the memory ladder runs short of video memory, distant avatars draw simplified copies of their mesh whose error stays below a fraction of a pixel to a few pixels on screen; full detail returns as the camera gets closer. Your own avatar and the largest avatars on screen always keep full detail. Ordinary scenes are unaffected.

Per-card budget of visible rigged (skinned) vertices per frame, in thousands. Sizes how much worn mesh the largest avatars on screen may keep at full detail (half of it; RenderVKRiggedProtectVertsK). No longer what makes screen-size rigged detail engage (that is measured GPU time, RenderVKRiggedGpuBudgetMs). 0 = automatic from the video memory budget (about 600 thousand per GB, 3 to 18 million).

Graphics card time per frame (milliseconds) worn mesh may take before screen-size rigged detail (RenderVKRiggedScreenLOD) simplifies distant avatars: skinning plus drawing the rigged meshes, measured on the GPU a few times a second. Only when the frame is also slower than RenderVKRiggedLodTargetFPS and the graphics card, not the processor, is what holds the frame rate back. 0 = automatic: 30% of a RenderVKRiggedLodTargetFPS frame (5 ms at 60).

How far the rigged (worn mesh) buffers may grow past their share (RenderVKRiggedBudgetPct) while video memory is free, in percent of the video memory budget (up to 60). Above the share the memory ladder treats it like any other use: textures give way first. 0 or a value at or below the share = no borrowing.

Headroom (percent, 10-200) the rigged (worn mesh) buffers take over the recent visible demand when they grow, while video memory is not under pressure. More headroom means fewer re-sizes as avatars come into view (each re-size can cost a frame on older cards); under video memory pressure the headroom is 25%.

The rigged (worn mesh) buffers shrink back only when their capacity is more than this share (percent, 150-1000) of what the visible avatars need, for RenderVKRigShrinkHoldSecs. Under video memory pressure they shrink at 200% (125% while the memory ladder's rigged steps are engaged) after about 10 seconds.

Re-size the worn mesh (rigged) buffers, their motion history and the animation tables without waiting for the GPU to go idle, while video memory is not under pressure: the new buffer is allocated next to the old one, which is freed a couple of frames later. Off (or under video memory pressure) every re-size waits for the GPU, which can cost a whole frame on older cards. A diagnostic: leave on.

Seconds (5-600) the rigged (worn mesh) buffers must stay oversized (RenderVKRigShrinkRatioPct) before they shrink, while video memory is not under pressure. Longer = fewer re-sizes while avatars move in and out of view; the memory still follows the demand down eventually.

Seconds (5-600) a scene, skin or animation table must stay under RenderVKTableShrinkPct of its capacity before it shrinks, while video memory is not under pressure (under pressure: 10 seconds under 40%).

A scene, skin or animation table shrinks (to 1.5x its need) only while its need is under this share (percent, 10-40) of its capacity for RenderVKTableShrinkSecs, while video memory is not under pressure.

Frame rate below which screen-size rigged detail (RenderVKRiggedScreenLOD) may engage when the graphics card spends more than RenderVKRiggedGpuBudgetMs on worn mesh and is the bottleneck. Above it full detail is kept, however many avatars are around.

Video memory (MB) for the simplified copies of rigged mesh that screen-size rigged detail draws for distant avatars (the same amount again in system memory). 0 = automatic (3% of the video memory budget, 96 to 1024 MB). Copies nobody has drawn for about a minute are freed.

Screen-size rigged detail (RenderVKRiggedScreenLOD): worn mesh that was uploaded with one level of subdivision smoothing (typical for quad-modelled bodies and heads) gets its quarter-detail copy by undoing that level -- the original cage's corners and faces -- instead of a generic simplification. Meshes without that structure are simplified as before. Changing it rebuilds every simplified copy (for comparison).
Smallest rigged mesh face (triangles) screen-size rigged detail builds simplified copies of; smaller faces always draw as they are.

Vulkan (#719): sky cloud layer. 0 = the classic 2D WindLight / EEP cloud dome (no extra cost; the volumetric resources are freed), 1 = a raymarched volumetric cloud shell between RenderVKVolCloudAltitude and + RenderVKVolCloudThickness, shaped by the region environment's (EEP) cloud coverage, density, scale, scroll, colour and noise texture, with cloud shadows on the ground (RenderVKVolCloudShadows), god rays through the gaps, and reflection probes / water reflections seeing the clouds through a panorama.

Vulkan (#719): volumetric cloud quality (RenderVKVolumetricClouds 1). 1 low (quarter resolution, a quarter of the texels marched per frame, 48 steps), 2 medium (quarter resolution, half the texels per frame, 64 steps), 3 high (quarter resolution, every texel every frame, 96 steps). The temporal reconstruction fills the texels not marched this frame.
Vulkan (#719): altitude (m, region Z) of the volumetric cloud layer's base. EEP has no cloud altitude; this is the viewer's.
Vulkan (#719): thickness (m) of the volumetric cloud shell above RenderVKVolCloudAltitude. GunMetal-DX: 2500.

GunMetal-DX volumetric clouds: how many hand-sculpted cloud bodies (CorvaeOboro's CC0 cumulus volumes) stand among the generated clouds where the region's sky is cloudy, 0 (none) to 1 (about every second 3 km cell).

GunMetal-DX volumetric clouds: the smallest cloud footprint the sky's EEP cloud texture may draw, as a share of the cloud layer's thickness (RenderVKVolCloudThickness; 0.05 = 125 m at 2500 m). Finer texture detail is filtered out of the coverage, so detailed cloud textures (Second Life's Midday sky) give clouds instead of thin vertical columns. It also ties a cloud's height to its width: only a cloud 4 x this wide (500 m) reaches the tall cumulus types, one narrower than 2 x sits low. Smaller = taller narrow clouds. 0 = the coverage as fine as the weather map, heights unlimited.

GunMetal-DX: on a page that scrolls (Preferences tabs and other scrolling panels), the mouse wheel over a combo box or spinner scrolls the page instead of changing the setting. An open combo list still scrolls with the wheel. Off = the old behaviour (the wheel changes the control under the pointer).

GunMetal-DX volumetric clouds: how fast the clouds travel, as a multiple of the region's own cloud scroll (its sky's Cloud Scroll X / Y, which also sets the direction). 1 = the region's speed, 0 = still. A region with its scroll locked stays still at any value.

Vulkan (#719): the volumetric cloud layer casts sun / moon shadows (a top-down transmittance map around the camera, multiplied into the sun light of every lit surface, the RT shadow mask consumer, water and the god rays).
Vulkan (#719): how much of the cloud layer's sun transmittance the ground receives (0 = no cloud shadows, 1 = physical).
Vulkan (#719): multiplier on the horizontal size of the volumetric clouds' weather pattern (the region's EEP cloud scale sets the base size).
Vulkan (#719): multiplier on the volumetric clouds' extinction (on top of the EEP cloud density).
Vulkan (#719): distance (m) at which the volumetric cloud layer has faded into the sky.
Vulkan (#719): temporal reconstruction of the volumetric clouds (reprojection + neighbourhood clamp + adaptive history). Off: every texel is marched every frame without history (noisier, costlier).

Weather (#783): master switch. Off: no weather from any source (your local weather, a parcel's, the region's sky) -- no rain, snow, wind effects, lightning or weather sounds, and no weather cost. The other weather settings keep their values and come back when it is on again. Set from the Weather floater (World > Weather).

Weather (#783): your own local weather, seen only by you. Off (default): no weather -- the renderer runs no weather pass and holds no weather memory once the surfaces have dried. Set from the Weather floater (World > Weather).
Weather (#783): local precipitation type. 0 rain, 1 snow.

Weather (#783): local precipitation intensity 0..1 on the #954 rate ladder (rain 0.25 ~1 mm/h, 0.5 ~5, 0.75 ~23, 1 = 100 mm/h; snow 0.25 ~0.4 cm/h, 0.5 ~1.5, 0.75 ~5, 1 = 15 cm/h). Used while the type's rate setting (WeatherRainFall / WeatherSnowFall) is -1.

Weather (#954): the local rain rate in mm/h (0 .. 200; light below 2.5, moderate 2.5-7.6, heavy 7.6-50, violent above). -1 = from WeatherIntensity on the rate ladder. It drives the drop count and size, the streaks, splashes, the visibility, the wetting speed and the rain sound.

Weather (#954): the local snowfall rate in cm/h of fresh snow (0 .. 360, i.e. up to 1 mm/s; light below 0.5, moderate 0.5-2.5, heavy 2.5-8, blizzard-grade above 8 with wind). Above 30 the look stays a heavy blizzard and only the build-up gets faster. -1 = from WeatherIntensity on the rate ladder. It drives the flake count and size, the visibility and how fast the snow gets deeper (the rate x 0.7: fresh snow settles).

Weather (#954): how strongly the local precipitation rate varies over time, 0 (flat) .. 1: bands of a few minutes, cells of under a minute and now and then a downpour / squall passing (up to ~2.6 x for a minute or two). Deterministic from the source's seed and the synced UTC time (a parcel's pvar= does the same for everyone there).
Weather (#783): direction the local wind blows FROM, degrees clockwise from north (0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west). Drives the rain / snow drift.
Weather (#783): local wind speed, metres per second (0..40).
Weather (#783): how long a weather change takes to settle, seconds (0 = immediate). Every amount eases with a time constant of a third of this.
Weather (#783): rain wets the surfaces that are open to the sky (darker, glossier, ripples on flat ground) and they dry after the rain.
Weather (#783): seconds of full-intensity rain to soak a surface completely (lighter rain takes longer).
Weather (#783): seconds a fully wet surface takes to dry once the rain has stopped.

Weather (#895): after walking / flying / riding into a region or parcel whose weather has no snow (or no weather), the snow and wetness that the previous place's region weather left fade out over this many seconds instead of popping away. 0 = they melt and dry at the normal rates. Local weather and a snowy destination keep everything.

Weather (#895): a teleport inside the same region shorter than this (m) keeps the lying snow, its footprints and the wetness; a longer one (or one to another region) is a new place whose ground starts over.

Weather (#895): after a teleport, a destination whose weather is snowing or raining starts at its steady state (full snow cover with a settled depth, wet surfaces) instead of building up from bare, dry ground over minutes.
Weather (#783 M4): how long covered surfaces keep draining after the rain stops (drips taper off over about this long, and never outlast the surfaces' wetness).
Weather (#783): falling snow settles on upward surfaces that are open to the sky (white, rough, building up in patches) and melts after the snow stops, leaving the surfaces wet.
Weather (#783): seconds of full snowfall for the snow cover to build up completely (lighter snow takes longer).
Weather (#783): seconds a full snow cover takes to melt once the snow has stopped (rain melts it faster). The melt water wets the surfaces.
