Weather (#783): OBSOLETE since #954 -- not read. The lying snow now gets deeper by the snowfall rate (WeatherSnowFall, cm/h) x 0.7 (settling).

Weather (#783): the deepest the snow on open, level ground gets (metres, 0 to 10; drifts against walls pile up to about three times this). It never exceeds this times the snow cover, so it melts away with the cover once the snow stops.

Weather (#783 shared snow depth): when a parcel's weather tag changes its shared snow level (depth= / rate= / since=), or you walk onto a parcel with another one, the lying snow blends to the new level over this many seconds (0 to 120; 0 = at once). Arriving (login, a teleport) always applies it at once.

Weather floater (#783 shared snow depth): Set as parcel weather also writes the snow depth (depth= rate= since=), so everyone on the parcel sees the same snow level whenever they arrived. Off: the tag has no depth and each viewer builds its own snow up from when it arrived.

Weather floater (#783 shared snow depth): the parcel's snow depth on open, level ground (metres, 0 to 10) at the stamped time (WeatherParcelSnowSince). Each viewer caps it at its own WeatherSnowMaxDepth.

Weather floater (#783 shared snow depth): how fast the parcel's snow gets deeper while it snows, in metres per hour (-100 to 100). 0 holds the depth; negative melts it. It replaces the intensity-based build-up for the depth (the intensity still sets how much snow falls).

Weather floater (#954): Set as parcel weather writes the shared depth rate (rate=) from the local snowfall rate (WeatherSnowFall / the intensity's rate, cm/h x 0.7 / 100 m/h: the same build-up every viewer shows locally) instead of WeatherParcelSnowRate. Written explicitly, so viewers older than #954 agree.
Weather floater (#783 shared snow depth): when the parcel's snow depth applied, in unix seconds (UTC), set by Stamp now. Empty: stamped when the tag is written.
Weather (#783): recorded rain, roof, drip, wind and snow sounds that follow the weather, with indoor beds under cover. Off: nothing is loaded or played.

Weather (#1012): hide the repetition of the recorded weather beds -- two playheads over each bed cross-fading to a fresh start point every 10-25 s (loud stretches only), a sparse random layer of drops cut from the light rain / drip beds, and a slow +-1 dB level drift. Off: each bed is one plain loop.

Weather (#894): under cover, the wind is shaped by the openings around you -- windows, doors and gaps facing into the wind make it louder, small gaps whistle, wide openings rush, and the sound comes from the opening. Measured with the room acoustics' rays (ray tracing needed; with AudioAcoustics off a few room rays are traced only while it is windy and you are under cover); without ray tracing, the roof map's openness. Off: one indoor wind bed.
Weather (#783): volume of the weather sounds (0..1), on top of the ambient sound volume.

Weather (#783): scale of the visibility loss the precipitation brings: the precipitation's own extinction (#954, from the rain / snow rate and blowing snow) -- a moving medium in the volumetric fog where it falls (RenderVKVolumetricFog on), else the analytic veil (RenderVKWeatherVeil). One source: no separate extra fog. 0 = none, 0 .. 4.

Weather (#783 M2): how far the wind speed swings around the set speed, 0..1 (0.5 = 50..150 %); the direction wanders slightly with it. Smooth, seeded by the weather's source (region weather: every viewer sees the same gusts).

Weather: how far the wind DIRECTION swings around the set direction, in degrees (0 = only the slight wander that comes with the wind variation, 180 = fully variable). Smooth, seeded by the weather's source (region weather: every viewer sees the same swings); the gustiness adds quicker veers.
Weather (#783 M2): how fast the wind picks up and dies down, 0..1: 0 slow swells over tens of seconds, 1 sharp gusts within 1-2 s.
Weather (#783 M2): thunderstorm amount for your local weather, 0..1 (0 = no lightning). Strikes come more often in heavier rain; heavier storms strike nearer.

Weather (#783 M2): thunder from strikes farther than 6 km arrives after the 6 km delay plus the rest of the sound-speed delay times this (0..1; 1 = real time, up to ~29 s at 10 km). Never under 1 s after the flash.
Weather (#783 M2): use the weather a parcel publishes in its description ([slwx ...] tag, doc/weather_region_protocol.md) when you have no local weather on. Off: a parcel's tag is ignored.
Weather (#783 M2): derive rain from the region's / parcel's shared sky (EEP cloud coverage) when you have no local weather and the parcel publishes none. Off: the region's sky never makes it rain.

Vulkan (#783): weather precipitation particle budget. 0 low (16384), 1 medium (32768), 2 high (65536). The density scales with the intensity inside this cap (#954: the particle box also shrinks toward the top of the rate ladder, and the precipitation veil -- RenderVKWeatherVeil -- carries the distance). #954: 0 also drops the blowing snow and the veil's curtains. #946: 0 (low) also runs the weather's small VRAM tier (coarser snow grids and a cheaper snow mesh; RenderVKWeatherVramTier).
Vulkan (#783): horizontal half extent (m) of the precipitation volume that wraps around the camera (8..64). Larger: rain further out, thinner at the same budget.
Vulkan (#783): a low-resolution top-down depth map around the camera keeps rain and snow out from under roofs and indoors, and keeps sheltered surfaces dry. Off: everything is open to the sky.

Vulkan (#783): frames between refreshes of the weather occlusion map while the camera stays in the same map cell (moving objects, new geometry). The map is also re-rendered whenever the camera crosses into another cell.
Vulkan (#783): animated rain ripples on wet, flat, sky-exposed surfaces.

Vulkan (#783): a high-resolution near cascade of the weather occlusion map around the camera, so the dry patches under roofs, trees and furniture have fine, soft edges. Off: only the coarse map (about half-metre texels).
Vulkan (#783): metres the near weather occlusion cascade covers around the camera (8..64). Beyond it the coarse map takes over with a soft blend.

Vulkan (#946): the weather's VRAM tier. 0 = auto: the SMALL tier on a card whose video memory budget is under 4.5 GB (every 4 GB card), and with RenderVKWeatherQuality 0 (low) on any card -- near maps at most 512 (snow grids 256), outer snow ring at most 128, the snow mesh sized with them, at most 8 avatar shelter layers on the half-height atlas, at most 4 avatar accumulation grids of 16 x 16 x 32, the snow mesh's shadow in the nearest sun cascade only and its edges at full resolution within 10 m (RenderVKWeatherSnowMeshEdgeLod 1): about a quarter of the default memory and GPU time. 1 = always the full tier (the settings' own values), 2 = always the small tier. Applies as each part is next re-created (a tier change starts the lying snow over).
Vulkan (#783): resolution of the near weather occlusion cascade (256..2048, a multiple of 64). 1024 over 32 m is about 3 cm per texel; memory is 2 x res x res x 4 bytes.

Vulkan (#783): the weather occlusion map leans with the wind -- rendered along the falling rain or snow's mean direction (up to 60 degrees), so the dry side of a wall is its lee side, rain blows in under eaves and wind-facing walls get wet. Re-rendered when the direction changes by more than 2.5 degrees. Off: straight down (walls barely wet).

Vulkan (#783): raindrops that hit open ground, roofs, canopies or water near the camera (about 14 m) throw up small, short-lived splashes (a fixed pool of 2048 on the GPU, recycled). Puddles keep their ripple rings as well.

Vulkan (#954): in a strong wind (about 9 m/s, full at 18 m/s) over lying snow, a share of the precipitation particles (up to 35 %, from the same fixed pool) streams along the ground as blowing snow, and the visibility drops (SLWeather blowing). Not on the low weather quality (RenderVKWeatherQuality 0).

Vulkan (#954): with the volumetric fog OFF, the precipitation's loss of visibility (from the rate and blowing snow, x WeatherFogAmount: ~3 km in light rain, ~300 m in a downpour, near whiteout in a blizzard) as a noise-free analytic veil, applied only to surfaces open to the sky (a room seen from a doorway stays clear): one fullscreen pass over the opaque scene and sky (GPU timer g_weather_veil) and the transparent surfaces, water and particles themselves. With the volumetric fog on (RenderVKVolumetricFog) the precipitation is a moving medium in the fog instead and this is not used. Off: the particles alone.

Vulkan (#954): with the volumetric fog on, how strongly the precipitation's medium in the fog moves -- a density field carried by the gusty wind and the fall (rain sheets falling fast, snow swirls, blowing snow along the ground), 0 (even) .. 1. Two noise octaves; one on the small weather VRAM tier, none on the low weather quality (RenderVKWeatherQuality 0).

Vulkan (#783): snow near the camera accumulates where it actually falls -- a persistent snow-cover map around the camera grows on open surfaces while it snows and melts after, so a moved object leaves its old spot bare (it refills), the snow it now stands on stays under it, and sheltered spots stay bare. About 8 MB while snow lies. Off: snow everywhere open to the sky, following the global cover.

Vulkan (#783): moving objects (vehicles, physical and animated objects) carry their own snow: it settles on them while they stand still in the open, rides along with them (patches fixed to the object) and blows off above a few metres per second; it melts with the rest. With RenderVKWeatherSnowDepth they also leave tracks: while they move, the parts that reach the snow (wheels, skids, hulls) press it down and push berms beside the track (RenderVKWeatherSnowMoverPress / MoverBerm); the snowfall refills them. Off: moving objects stay bare and leave no tracks.

Vulkan (#783): how hard moving objects (RenderVKWeatherSnowMovers) press their tracks into the snow depth, 0..1: 1 = down to the object's underside but no lower than the packed layer (~30% of the snow depth: fresh snow packs ~3x), 0.5 = halfway to it, 0 = no tracks.

Vulkan (#783): the share of the snow a moving object actually removes from its track (most of it is packed down: the track keeps ~30% of the depth as packed snow) that is pushed aside into a low lip beside it (and a small bow wave ahead), 0..1. Wheels / bodies compress rather than shovel: ~0.15. A true plough can go higher. A berm never rises above 1.4 x the undisturbed snow depth. 0 = flat tracks.

Vulkan (#783): the most moving object parts (faces / prims touching the snow) that stamp tracks per frame, 16..512. Past it the rest skip that frame (objects outside the near snow field may only take half of it).

Vulkan (#783): the persistent snow cover near the camera also tracks the snow DEPTH (metres) per texel: newly seen ground starts at the current depth of the snowfall, steep surfaces and edges stay thin, and local changes (drifts, footprints) persist while you stay. Needed by the snow mesh, drift / slide / settle and footprints. Off: snow is a surface coating only.

Vulkan (#783): wind blows lying snow along with the mean wind: it piles up against walls and in corners and settles in the lee of obstacles, while exposed spots thin out. Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowDepth.
Vulkan (#783): snow slides off slopes steeper than about 35 degrees into the lower ground next to them. Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowDepth.
Vulkan (#783): lying snow settles a little, so its edges round off into soft mounds. Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowDepth.

Vulkan (#783): snow deeper than about 2 cm near the camera is drawn as real geometry (a raised snow surface that casts and receives shadows), cut cleanly at roof edges and walls; thinner snow and snow beyond the outer ring stay a surface coating. Deferred lighting only (RenderVKDeferredLighting). About 19 MB while it exists (vertices for the near grid and the outer ring, 9 MB of indices).

Vulkan (#783): an outer ring of real snow around the detailed near field (a coarser depth grid, about 0.5 m texels over RenderVKWeatherSnowRingExtent metres, fed by the weather's coarse roof map). The near field hands over to it in a smooth band (no popping as the camera moves), and the ring itself sinks into the snow coating at its edge. About 1 MB of depth (allocated with the snow even when this is off) + 2 MB of mesh vertices at the defaults; while snow is about, the coarse roof map grows to 1.25 x the ring's extent (coarser shelter edges beyond the near field).
Vulkan (#783): the outer snow ring's extent in metres (48 - 192). The snow geometry reaches about 0.43 x this from the camera; the weather's coarse roof map grows to 1.25 x it.

Vulkan (#783): the outer snow ring's grid resolution (64 - 512, rounded to a multiple of 8). Texel = RenderVKWeatherSnowRingExtent / this; the coarse roof map it samples is 256 texels over 1.25 x the extent.
Vulkan (#783): the outer snow ring steps every this many frames (with the time since its last step); at once when it moves a cell or the coarse roof map re-renders.
Vulkan (#783): the snow surface mesh casts sun / moon shadows (drawn into the shadow cascades every frame). Ray-traced shadows and reflections do not see it.

Vulkan (#783 / #87): the snow surface mesh is drawn into the depth pre-pass too (depth, AO normal, camera-only motion), so the motion vectors, the pre-pass AO, the RT shadow mask and the Hi-Z see the snow instead of what it buries (fixes dark avatar-shaped ghosts on deep snow with ray-traced GI). 0 = the old path (G-buffer only), for A/B.
Vulkan (#783): avatars leave footprints in deep snow (their feet press the snow down where they stand and walk); the prints fill in again while it snows. Visual only. Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowDepth.

Vulkan (#783): every limb that reaches deep snow presses into it, not only the feet -- knees and shins when kneeling or wading through drifts, hands and forearms (a crawl, a quadruped's front legs), animated Bento hind limbs and tails, the body when sitting or lying in the snow. The snow packs down first and pushes up a small rim. Avatars and animesh near the camera (RenderVKWeatherSnowLimbRange). Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowDepth.

Vulkan (#783): avatars and animesh within this distance of the camera (m, 0..64; also only inside the near snow field) press their limbs into the snow (RenderVKWeatherSnowLimbs). At most 256 limb boxes per step; past that the rest are skipped and logged. 0 = off.

Vulkan (#783): the angle of repose of lying snow (degrees, 25..43). Deep snow next to a lower spot -- a lee, a track a vehicle or an avatar cleared, a spot a moved object left -- slumps until its slope is no steeper than this (all eight directions, mass conserved), instead of standing as a vertical wall. Also the snow mesh slope at the edge of a covered area (RenderVKWeatherSnowToeReach). Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowSettle or RenderVKWeatherSnowSlide.

Vulkan (#783): how far (m, 0..4; at most 12 snow-grid texels, ~0.75 m near the camera) deep snow may continue as a sloped APRON in under a cover beside it -- a high one too (an airship, a canopy far above); it always ends on the floor (steeper than the repose when the reach is short) -- a roof, a canopy, a table over a deck. The snow maps see only the cover from above, so without it the snow ends in a vertical wall along the cover outline. The apron is one continuous surface at the angle of repose (RenderVKWeatherSnowReposeAngle), ending on the floor the snow lies on (assumed to continue under the cover at the same height), and only while the cover stays 25 cm above it. Against a solid block it is hidden inside it; the maps cannot tell an eave from a wall, so next to a thin wall of a roofed room its end can show inside. (Always on, whatever this says: a 2-texel CLOSURE into every column the snow cannot join -- a deck, step or wall above it, a cover -- so the snow meets that geometry's face with no gap.) #783: the snow depth beside any such column slumps to the repose over 0.7 m (deeper snow is trimmed to ~0.55 m at the outline and rises at the repose behind it), and the apron always reaches at least that far, so values under 0.7 m act as 0.7 m; larger values only lengthen it.

Vulkan (#783): the far snow ring builds deep-snow mesh only on supports at least this far (m, 0..12.7) from their nearest drop -- i.e. raised supports narrower than about twice this (a tree crown or canopy tier, a post, a small ledge) carry no far mesh, only the surface coating. At the far ring's 0.5 m texels a tree crown is one solid patch, and its snow was a flat plate floating in the tree. The near grid still shows the real snow on them up close. 0 = mesh on every support.

Vulkan (#783, debug): paint every static surface by what the snow depth grid says about it -- blue/green/white by depth (2 cm .. 2 m), orange: open top but no depth (only the coating: the depth was zeroed or capped), yellow: something above it in the map (a cover), magenta: a moving object (kept out of the maps), red: under the water line, dark grey: outside the near grid, cyan: covered only per the coarse map. Dark lines: the near snow grid texels; red lines: the coarse map texels. The snow mesh shows its LOD stride per cell: light blue 1, yellow 2, orange 4.

Vulkan (#970): apply the weather (wetness, puddles, ripples, run-off, the snow coating and persistent cover) at ray-traced reflection, GI and RT probe-capture hits, with the same function and weather maps as the main view's surfaces. Off: hits shade their unweathered material (A/B, timing).

Vulkan (#970): ray-traced reflections see the LYING SNOW (the snow mesh): a short height-field march against the snow depth grid backward from each reflection hit finds where the ray entered the snow, so drifts, berms, footprints and trenches show in reflections. Only while the snow mesh is drawn; inner snow grid only (~30 m around the camera; beyond it the snow coating). Off: reflections show the coating on the ground under the snow (A/B, timing).

Vulkan (#946): the snow mesh is rebuilt at least every this many frames while the snow itself changes (falling, melting, footprints); sooner when the snow grid moves, the camera moves more than RenderVKWeatherSnowMeshRebuildMove or turns more than ~8 degrees, or after a teleport / snapshot. Between rebuilds the last mesh is drawn. 1 = rebuild every frame (Beta 5/6 behaviour).

Vulkan (#946): local snow edits (footprints, avatars and vehicles ploughing, limb / body presses, their berms) rebuild only the snow mesh tiles around them on the next frame, between the full rebuilds of RenderVKWeatherSnowMeshInterval. Off = local edits wait for the next full rebuild.

Vulkan (#946): the most snow mesh tiles (8 x 8 snow texels each) one frame's local patch rebuilds (RenderVKWeatherSnowMeshPatch; a footprint touches about 50). More edits than that in one frame wait for the next full rebuild. The small VRAM tier uses at most a quarter of its grid's tiles.
Vulkan (#946): the camera distance (m) that triggers a snow mesh rebuild before RenderVKWeatherSnowMeshInterval runs out (the mesh's level of detail and its hand-over band follow the camera).

Vulkan (#946): how many sun shadow cascades, nearest first, draw the snow mesh (0-4; 4 = all, the default). The farthest cascades' texels are coarser than the snow's relief: 2 saves their draws with little visible change. The small weather VRAM tier uses at most 1.

Vulkan (#783, debug): set to 1 to record ONE snow mesh build (a full build is forced) around the camera's focus -- every texel's snow depth, base, cover, joins, the depth relaxation's pulls, the apron field and every cell's branch, plus the mesh before and after the build -- into logs/snowdump-TIME.bin (the path is logged); resets itself to 0. Read it with scripts/dev/snowdump.py. Alt-click the spot first: the focus centres the window, and its height is the script's default floor.
Vulkan (#783, debug): the snow dump's window, in texels of each snow layer (16..256; the inner grid's texels are about 6 cm, the outer ring's about 0.5 m).

Vulkan (#946): level of detail of snow mesh blocks that hold an edge (a cut, a drop, a closure / apron). 0 = full resolution at any distance (#783 round 8), 1 = full resolution within 10 m and at most stride 2 beyond (the small weather VRAM tier), 2 = like the interior (Beta 4: coarse wall panels at a distance, the cheapest).

Vulkan (#783): smooth the deep-snow mesh -- an edge-preserving filter of the snow depth map before the mesh samples it, and normals from the filtered surface, so the depth map texel grid (terraces, stair-stepped outlines, faceted shading) does not show; sharp contact features (footprints, snow angels) keep their edges.

Vulkan (#783): the far snow ring builds deep-snow mesh only where at least this share (0..1) of a ring texel is the surface the snow lies on. A thin support in a coarse texel -- a tree trunk, a narrow canopy tier, a post, a patchy canopy -- otherwise became a texel-sized slab of snow floating in the tree; below the share the surface coating carries the snow there. 0 = mesh on every ring texel.

Vulkan (#783): avatars press the snow with their real shape -- the lowest surface of the body and what it wears, from the per-avatar shelter map (RenderVKWeatherAvatarShelter) -- instead of boxes around the skeleton's joints: a quadruped's front hooves press as deep as its rear ones, a belly or a tail lying in the snow presses where it is, and every hoof, foot or hand that stands on the ground leaves a footprint. Avatars without a shelter map use the joints. Needs RenderVKWeatherSnowLimbs. Off: the joints only.

Vulkan (#783): a part of an avatar whose underside is this close to the ground under the snow (m, 0..0.5) stands on it -- it packs the snow under it to a footprint's depth and leaves a footprint (RenderVKWeatherSnowBodyContact). Higher parts only push aside the snow they are in.

Vulkan (#783): an avatar's shelter map is used for its snow contact only while the avatar is within this distance (m, 0..4) of where the map was drawn; further (a fast mover between map refreshes) its joints stand in that step (RenderVKWeatherSnowBodyContact).

Vulkan (#783): for avatars pressing the snow with their joints (no shelter map), an arm whose wrist or hand comes within this distance of the snow top (m, 0..1) stands on it like a leg -- a quadruped's front legs press as deep as a foot and leave footprints. 0 = off.

Vulkan (#901): what avatars wear shelters them -- under an umbrella the wearer stays dry and rain splashes on the canopy, a hat keeps the face dry; avatars carry their own snow on what faces up. Each avatar near the camera gets a small top-down map of itself and its attachments (RenderVKWeatherAvatarShelterCount / Range). Off: avatars take the sky like everything else.
Vulkan (#901): how many avatars near the camera get a shelter map (1..16; your own first, then by distance; fewer under VRAM pressure).
Vulkan (#901): avatars within this distance of the camera get a shelter map (m, 2..64).
Vulkan (#901): other avatars whose shelter map is redrawn per frame, in turn (your own every frame).

Vulkan (#901): avatars near the camera accumulate snow and wetness in a small grid over their rest pose, per body part, only while that part is actually exposed (its own umbrella / hat brim and roofs over it, at its current animated pose): a moment of exposure -- an umbrella swaying with a dance -- adds almost nothing, and snow already lying is not removed because the cover swings back. Live. Off: the previous behaviour (the per-avatar top / body values, shown where the instantaneous shelter test says).

Vulkan (#901): the rest-pose accumulation grid's cells (applies when the grids are next allocated, e.g. after a restart): 0 = 16 x 16 x 32 (96 KB an avatar), 1 = 24 x 24 x 48 (324 KB), 2 = 32 x 32 x 64 (768 KB). Three buckets (up / side / down) per cell.

Vulkan (#901): how many avatars (the closest with a shelter layer; the own avatar always) get a rest-pose accumulation grid (1-16; applies when the grids are next allocated). The others keep the per-avatar values.
Vulkan (#901): rest-pose accumulation updates per second for each avatar's grid (staggered, at most 4 grids a frame; each update integrates the time since its last).

Vulkan (#909): an avatar's own surface up to this far (m) above a point of it is NEAR self-cover (a snout over the tongue, a chin over the throat, an arm over the armpit): taken live per pixel, the point shows and gathers no snow. Cover farther above (an umbrella) goes through the rest-pose accumulation only (its sway never flashes). Fades out over 8 cm past it; 0 turns it off. Applies while the accumulation grids are live (otherwise 0.25).

Vulkan (#909): the least height (m) the avatar's own surface must lie above a point of it to count as near self-cover (below: the point's own surface, its slope). Raise it if parts of the body lose their snow wrongly; lower it for very tight mouths.
Vulkan (#909): the height (m) over which near self-cover ramps in above its threshold (soft edges at a mouth's corners, under a chin).
Vulkan (#901): seconds an avatar's rest-pose accumulation grid is kept after the avatar left the camera's shelter range (then freed).

Vulkan (#901): debug view of the rest-pose accumulation: avatar surfaces coloured by their grid -- grey to blue the wetness, white the snow; magenta where the grid has nothing (the per-avatar values apply), orange: no rest position (no skin meta / bind shape for the part yet -- since the #901 / #909 follow-up cluster LOD parts carry theirs); cyan: near self-covered (#909). Also logs every 2 s.

Vulkan (#901): every avatar near the camera keeps its OWN wetness: it gets wet over time while rain falls on it (at the rain's intensity x how much of it is exposed -- an umbrella over it, a roof: slowly or not at all) and dries over time out of the rain (faster in wind and sunshine); top surfaces wet first, the undersides last. Off: avatars take the world's wetness at once, like any surface.
Vulkan (#901): seconds a fully exposed avatar takes to soak through in the heaviest rain (lighter rain: proportionally longer). RenderVKWeatherAvatarWetness.
Vulkan (#901): seconds a soaked avatar takes to dry out of the rain in still, overcast air (wind and sunshine shorten it, up to about half). RenderVKWeatherAvatarWetness.

Vulkan (#901 debug): tint avatar fragments by their shelter map while weather runs -- green: the top of its column (open to the sky), red: under something the avatar wears (an umbrella, a hat brim), blue: snow lying there in the map, magenta: an avatar part with no shelter map (the tint's brightness: the avatar's own wetness, dark = dry); over the rest of the scene, each shelter map's footprint (white border) and, where a map holds a surface over the ground, its height above it in 25 cm bands (yellow low .. red 2 m; rain is hidden under it), green where the point is the top itself, faint blue an empty texel; and log the shelter (layers, per-avatar draws / worn attachments, footprint, wetness, exposure, drops hidden) every 2 s.
Vulkan (#901): the largest square a shelter map covers around its avatar (m, 2.5..12): very large attachments (wings, worn vehicles) are cut off past it.

Vulkan (#901, off by default until reworked): the snow avatars carry on hats, shoulders and umbrellas is a small mesh of its own (domes on small supports, sliding off steep ones), drawn with the ground snow's mesh; off: the coat alone. Needs RenderVKWeatherAvatarShelter and RenderVKWeatherSnowAvatars.

Vulkan (#783): avatars collect their own snow on their shoulders, head and other upward-facing parts while they stand or sit still in the open; it stays on through their animations, melts with the rest and falls off when they run, fly or jump. Their attachments share it. Off: avatars stay bare.

Vulkan (#783): draw lightning flashes -- a brief, soft cool-white light over the scene from the strike's direction, a brighter sky and lit clouds. The weather state decides when and where strikes happen; off draws nothing (thunder is the audio side's).

Vulkan (#783): the weather's cloud cover thickens the cloud layer (the classic dome and the volumetric clouds take the larger of the region's own coverage and the weather's -- the weather never thins a region's sky) and cloud and rain darken the sky a little. Off: the region's sky is left as it is.

Vulkan (#783 M4): run-off -- rain landing on roofs, awnings, tables and other covers runs off and falls from their edges: drips (a share of the precipitation particles) and, where a lot of water collects, thin streams down to the ground; the ground under a drip line gets wet sooner and puddles along it; walls and steep roofs carry rivulets. It starts once the surfaces are wet, keeps draining for a while after the rain (WeatherRunoffDrainSeconds), and melt water runs off the same way. Needs the near occlusion cascade (RenderVKWeatherNearCascade). Off, or dry: nothing allocated, nothing drawn.

Vulkan (#783 M4): resolution of the run-off flow grid over the near occlusion cascade (128 - 512, a power of two; rounded so a whole number of near-map texels make one flow texel). 256 over the default 32 m cascade is ~12.5 cm per texel: where drips leave an edge. Higher: finer edges, more GPU time per roof-map refresh (the flow is only rebuilt then).
Vulkan (#783 M4): edges that drain a lot of roof (an eave in heavy rain) pour as thin continuous streams down to where they land, with splashes there, instead of only dripping.
Vulkan (#783 M4): water trails running down walls, windows and steep roofs -- animated streaks along the slope, from the rain the surface takes and thicker below a roof edge that drains onto it.
Vulkan (#783 M4): the height drop (m) at which the edge of a surface discharges its run-off (an eave, a table edge). Smaller steps (curbs, stairs) let the water flow on.

Vulkan (#718): volumetric fog. 0 off (zero cost: no passes, no memory), 1 on. A camera-aligned froxel grid (RenderVKVolumetricFogQuality) holds a height fog derived from the region's sky (EEP) and the local fog volumes; it is lit by the sun / moon with the shadow cascades (and cloud shadows), the sky ambient and the local lights, filtered over frames by its own temporal pass, integrated front to back and applied to opaque surfaces, the sky, alpha-blended faces, water and particles. LL's haze is kept exactly; the fog adds the haze's shadowed sun shafts (it replaces the god rays pass while on) and the extra fog. Not shown with the camera under water.
Vulkan (#718): volumetric fog grid. 0 low (128x72x48 froxels, ~14 MB), 1 medium (160x90x64, ~30 MB), 2 high (192x108x96, ~64 MB).

Vulkan (#718): view depth (m) the volumetric fog grid covers (32-512). Past it the height fog continues analytically (unshadowed, RenderVKVolumetricFogFarAnalytic); local volumes and shadowed shafts end there.

Vulkan (#718): extinction (per metre) of the volumetric height fog at its base height. Negative = automatic: derived from the region's sky (4 x the EEP haze's Mie extinction, so a hazier sky has a thicker ground fog and a clear sky next to none). 0 = no height fog (only the haze shafts and local volumes).

Vulkan (#718): how fast the volumetric height fog thins above its base height (1 per metre; density x exp(-falloff x height)). Negative = automatic: scale height 2% of the sky's haze ceiling (EEP max altitude), 10-200 m. 0 = uniform.
Vulkan (#718): height of the volumetric fog's base above the region's water level (m). No fog is added below the water surface.

Vulkan (#718): Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy of the fog's scattering (-0.9 back .. 0 even .. 0.95 strongly forward: bright toward the sun). Negative = automatic (0.6, the god rays' value; EEP has no phase parameter).
Vulkan (#718): scattering albedo (colour) of the volumetric height fog, 0-1 per channel. The light tints it; white-ish keeps the sky's mood.

Vulkan (#718): strength of the sun / moon shafts in the haze (the god rays term the fog takes over; 1 = the god rays' default look, 0 = no haze shafts: with RenderVKVolumetricFogDensity 0 too, the frame matches fog-off outside local volumes). Needs shadow cascades (no shafts with shadows off or ray-traced sun).
Vulkan (#718): sky ambient light scale in the volumetric fog.
Vulkan (#718): local light (point / projector) scale in the volumetric fog; 0 = local lights do not light the fog.

Vulkan: shadowed projectors in the volumetric fog (their beams stop at walls). Follows RenderVKProjectorShadows: shadow-mapped projectors take one atlas tap per fog cell; ray-traced ones a stochastic weighted pick + one opaque shadow ray per lit cell (converged by the fog's temporal filter). 0 = off (projector light passes through geometry in the fog), 1 = on. Point lights: RenderVKVolumetricFogPointShadows.

Vulkan: view distance (m) up to which ray-traced projectors and shadowed point lights (RenderVKVolumetricFogPointShadows) trace shadow rays in the volumetric fog (past it they light the fog unshadowed); 0 = the whole fog range. Shadow-mapped projectors are shadowed at every distance.

Vulkan: point lights are occluded by geometry in the volumetric fog (a lamp under a bridge deck or a floor no longer lights the fog above it). Ray traced: point lights join the fog's weighted shadow pick (RenderVKVolumetricFogShadowRays, default 1 ray per lit cell, shared with ray-traced projectors) and the picked light traces one opaque shadow ray; the light's own prim and a small enclosing fixture (RenderVKReSTIRFixtureSize) never shadow it. Needs a ray-tracing frame (any ray-traced shadows / GI); without one, point lights light the fog unshadowed as before. 0 = off (unshadowed), 1 = on except attachment lights (facelights) and except on the low fog quality tier, 2 = on everywhere, attachment lights included. Live.

Vulkan: ray-traced shadow picks per lit volumetric fog cell per frame (1-4), shared by the ray-traced projectors and the shadowed point lights (RenderVKVolumetricFogPointShadows): one weighted pick among them, one shadow ray each; more = less noise with many overlapping lights. Live.

Vulkan: the volumetric fog's sky ambient is occluded per fog cell by one ray-traced sky-visibility ray (cosine-weighted, upward; the temporal pass converges it), so a sealed dark room has dark fog while an open window still lets sky light in. 0 = off (the old global sky ambient everywhere), 1 = while ray-traced GI runs (default), 2 = whenever ray tracing is available.
Vulkan: length (m) of the volumetric fog's ambient sky-visibility ray (RenderVKVolumetricFogAmbientOcclusion); a ray that travels this far unblocked counts as seeing the sky.

Vulkan: with ray-traced sun / moon shadows (no shadow cascades), each lit volumetric fog cell traces one shadow ray toward the sun, so sunlight does not scatter inside rooms. 0 = the old unshadowed sun term.
Vulkan: view-depth limit (m) of the volumetric fog's ray-traced ambient sky visibility and sun shadow rays; cells farther away stay unoccluded. 0 = no limit.
Vulkan (#718): local fog volumes (boxes / ellipsoids with noise-shaped density) are injected into the volumetric fog grid.

Vulkan (#718): history weight of the volumetric fog's own temporal filter (0 = this frame only, noisy; 0.9 ~ 10 frames; max 0.98). Changes outside the jitter noise are rejected by a neighbourhood clamp.
Vulkan (#718): continue the volumetric height fog analytically past the grid's range (RenderVKVolumetricFogRange), up to the draw distance; off = the fog ends at the range.

Vulkan (#718, debug): place this many test fog volumes (0-8; ellipsoids and boxes with scrolling noise, a few tints) in a row 14 m ahead of the camera when the value changes; 0 removes them. Needs RenderVKVolumetricFog and RenderVKVolumetricFogLocalVolumes.

Vulkan (#721): volumetric particles -- smoke / steam / dust-like particle systems put participating medium into the volumetric fog grid (RenderVKVolumetricFog must be on), lit by the sun / moon with shadows, the sky and local lights (shadowed projectors) like the rest of the fog, so light shafts cut through club smoke. 0 = off (sprites only), 1 = smoke-like particles only (heuristic: large, soft, alpha-blended, not saturated stylised sprites, not streaks or beams; glowing / additive ones add emitted light), 2 = every alpha-blended or additive billboard of at least RenderVKVolumetricParticleMinSize (A/B, stylised content may look wrong). Opt-in: the heuristic can misjudge stylised particles.

Vulkan (#721): fraction of an injected particle's sprite coverage that stays drawn as a sprite (0 = replaced by the volume, 1 = sprite unchanged with the volume added on top). Needs RenderVKParticleLighting (the lit particle VS applies the fade); fades back to 1 over the last 30 % of RenderVKVolumetricParticleDistance.

Vulkan (#721): share of an injected particle's coverage (texture mean alpha x tint alpha) that becomes optical depth in the fog grid (mass-conserving: the sphere's projected optical depth equals the sprite's). Sprite 0.35 + density 0.65 keeps the overall opacity; 0 = no volume.
Vulkan (#721): view distance (m, 4 to the fog range) up to which particles are injected into the fog grid; the volume fades out (and the sprite back in) over the last 30 %.

Vulkan (#721): most particles injected into the fog grid per frame (1-4096); past it the nearest are kept (distance-bucketed) and the rest stay plain sprites. Counters: vk_volPartCandidates / vk_volPartInjected / vk_volPartTileOverflow.
Vulkan (#721): smallest particle (m, its larger scale axis) injected into the fog grid; in mode 1 additive / glow sprites need twice this.
Vulkan (#721): gain of the light glowing particles (SL emissive / glow, additive blend) emit into the fog grid; 0 = none (additive particles are then never injected).
Vulkan (#721): amount of noise shaping each injected particle's density (0 = smooth spheres, 1 = fully noise-shaped); the noise moves with the particle.

Sky: off = Classic (the WindLight sky, as other viewers draw it). On = Physical: the sky is computed with Hillaire's physically based atmosphere (multiple scattering, sunsets, altitude), its air derived from the region's WindLight / EEP values so each sky keeps its intent. Haze amount and all surface lighting stay WindLight's.
Physical sky: brightness of the sky (the sun or moon light's illuminance scale).
Physical sky: soft roll-off of the sky's brightest parts (a low sun's glow), as a luminance white point; lower = gentler sunsets. 0 = none.

Physical sky: aerial perspective strength. Distant scenery fades into the sky by the physical air's extinction over this many times its real distance (real air is nearly clear over SL's draw distances), on top of the WindLight haze. 0 = WindLight's haze only.
Physical sky: how much of the sky's ambient colour is added as scattered light (keeps night skies from going black).
Night lighting from the moon's real brightness and phase, a smooth dusk, stars, airglow and night vision (GMDX). Off: the old Second Life night.

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): on a sky that is not one of Second Life's own (a region's or parcel's own EEP environment, a scripted one, a personal sky from inventory), the night exposure lift (GMDXNightExposure*) and the night colour grade (GMDXNightLook, with the Purkinje shift and night noise) are off, so the night keeps the exposure and colours its creator set up; and the light is Second Life's own: the moon at its full EEP strength (no GMDXMoonlightScale, no phase dimming), the sky, clouds, water glint and moon disc lit as with GMDXPhysicalNight off, and Second Life's switch from sun to moon at the horizon instead of physical night's dusk blend. The catalogue stars, Milky Way, planets and the cloud corona stay. Second Life's default skies (Sunrise, Midday, Sunset, Midnight, the default day cycle) and Sky Test keep the full night look. 0 = the night look on every sky. Changes live.

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): at night EEP's ambient light (the sky's fill light on surfaces, the haze, the sky the reflection probes see) follows the moon too, as this multiple of the moon's light fraction (GMDXMoonlightScale x 2 x moon_brightness x the phase), at least 1/256 of the sky's own (starlight on a moonless night). Without it the fill light, set for Second Life's full-strength moon, drowned the dimmed moon: nothing looked moonlit and shadows (cloud shadows too) took nothing away. 0.5: moonlit ground against shadow about twice Second Life's old ratio; 1: Second Life's ratio; lower: darker shadows. The night exposure brings the whole scene back up; on a sky without one (legacy skies, dynamic exposure off) that lift is put into the light instead. Not on a creator's sky (GMDXRespectRegionSky). Changes live.

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): a full moon high in the sky lights the world, the clouds (times GMDXNightCloudLight) and the sky with this fraction of the sun's light (in the viewer's own units: real moonlight is far dimmer, the exposure brings it up). The moon's phase (from where the sun and moon stand) and the sky's moon brightness scale it further; the default moon brightness 0.5 counts as 1.

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): the moon lights the clouds this many times brighter than GMDXMoonlightScale lights everything else, so night clouds read while the moon's disc, the sky and the ground stay as they are. The default 4.5 lights the clouds as GMDXMoonlightScale 0.22 would with the default 0.05. 1 = the clouds lit like everything else. Only the moon's light: the day and dusk while the sun leads are unchanged. Live

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): how the night is shown. 1 = photo: as a night photograph, about one stop under the day for a full moon (clouds readable), a cold blue film grade in the shadows, no Purkinje shift. 0 = eye: as the eye sees it, about two stops under the day, with the Purkinje shift (GMDXNightVisionPurkinje). Live

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): brightness of the moon's disc as a light, a multiple of the moonlight (GMDXMoonlightScale, without GMDXNightCloudLight) (follows the phase and EEP moon_brightness; the EEP moon texture keeps its detail). 1 = far over white on screen, so it clips and blooms (GMDXMoonGlow) like a photographed moon; 0 = Second Life's disc. Only for Second Life's own moon texture: a sky creator's own moon texture (on a sky that is not one of Second Life's) is drawn as Second Life draws it, at its own brightness and without phase shading. Live

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): strength of the night bloom, the soft halo round the bright moon disc (GMDXMoonDisc) and other true highlights, drawn on the final image so cloud in front of the moon blocks it and thin cloud edges glow. Fades in after sunset; the day's bloom is unchanged. Needs the bloom on (RenderBloomStrength above 0); a user bloom threshold (RenderBloomThreshold below 8) takes precedence. 0 = none, 1 = default. Live

Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): the sun's height in degrees where dusk begins. Above it the light is the day's as before; from here down to GMDXDuskSunLow the moon's light fades in while the sun's fades out at the horizon, and the light's direction (and the shadows) turns smoothly from the sun to the moon.
Physical night (GMDXPhysicalNight): the sun's height in degrees (below the horizon) where dusk ends and the moon lights the scene at its full strength. See GMDXDuskSunHigh.

The corona: the bright glow and the faint coloured rings (blue inside, red outside) that thin clouds show around the moon or the sun, from light diffracted by the cloud's water droplets, and the pastel colours (iridescence) on thin cloud edges up to about 20 degrees from them, where the droplets are smaller; strongest where the cloud in front of the light is thin, none in clear sky or behind thick cloud. 1 is the real strength (half of what a droplet scatters goes into this forward peak), 0 off: the clouds exactly as before. Volumetric clouds and the physical sky's cloud layer. Part of physical night: none while GMDXPhysicalNight is off.

The corona (GMDXCloudCorona): the cloud droplets' typical diameter in micrometres. Smaller droplets give larger rings (the first red ring of 15 is about 4 degrees from the light, of 10 about 6). Typical clouds 10 to 20. The thinnest cloud edges use down to 0.3 times this size (the iridescence).

The 22-degree halo: the ring, reddish on its sharp inner edge, that ice-crystal clouds (cirrostratus) show 22 degrees from the moon or the sun. Second Life skies do not say whether their clouds are ice, so it is off by default and, when on, every cloud shows it, faintest where the cloud is thick. 1 is a moderate halo (a tenth of the scattered light in the ring), 0 off. Volumetric clouds and the physical sky's cloud layer. Part of physical night: none while GMDXPhysicalNight is off.

Sky Test (World > Environment > Sky Test...): a test sky for tuning the night look, on your screen only (a personal sky, never sent anywhere). The start sky (GMDXSkyTestBase; by default Second Life's skies blended by the sun's height) with the sun, moon, clouds and haze from the GMDXSkyTest* settings. 0 = back to the region sky. Not kept between sessions. Blocked by RLVa @setenv.

Sky Test: setting this loads a test sky into the GMDXSkyTest* values and turns the test on. 1 full moon high, 2 full moon low, 3 quarter moon, 4 crescent, 5 moonless, 6 dusk (sun -3), 7 deep twilight (sun -8), 8 noon, 9 cloud over a high full moon. At startup (--set) the values you also --set yourself win over the preset.

Sky Test: the sky the test starts from (its colours, ambient, glow, everything the test does not set). 0 the sky in use (the region/parcel sky, or a personal sky you picked, e.g. World > Environment > Midnight), 1 Second Life Sunrise, 2 Midday, 3 Sunset, 4 Midnight, 5 day cycle (the default): Second Life's Midday, Sunset and Midnight blended by the test sun's height, as a day cycle dims them (Midday from +20 degrees, Sunset +8 to +2, Midnight from -9 down).
Sky Test: the sun's height in degrees (-90 to 90; below 0 it has set).
Sky Test: the sun's azimuth in degrees (0 to 360, as Personal Lighting shows it).
Sky Test: the moon's height in degrees (-90 to 90; below 0 it has set).
Sky Test: the moon's azimuth in degrees (0 to 360). With GMDXSkyTestMoonByPhase on, the test sets it from the phase.

Sky Test: place the moon by its phase (GMDXSkyTestMoonPhase): its azimuth is chosen so the sun-moon angle gives that phase at the moon's height. When the two heights cannot give the phase, the nearest phase they can.
Sky Test: the moon's phase angle in degrees: 0 full, 45 gibbous, 90 quarter, 135 crescent, 180 new (the sun-moon angle is 180 minus this). Used while GMDXSkyTestMoonByPhase is on.
Sky Test: cloud coverage (the sky's Cloud Coverage, 0 to 1). Near 1 the cloud field covers the whole sky, the moon too.
Sky Test: cloud density (the sky's Cloud Density, 0 to 3).
Sky Test: cloud scale (the sky's Cloud Scale, 0.01 to 3).
Sky Test: slides the cloud field east-west (the sky's Cloud X, 0 to 1 = one whole tile): with the clouds frozen, puts a cloud in front of the moon.
Sky Test: slides the cloud field north-south (the sky's Cloud Y, 0 to 1 = one whole tile).
Sky Test: the clouds stand still (cloud scroll 0), so a cloud stays where Cloud Shift put it. Off = the start sky's own scroll.
Sky Test: haze density (the sky's Haze Density, 0 to 5).

Vulkan (#1003): fog-like particle systems (large, faint, slow, long-lived, soft-textured, alpha blended: fog machines, smoke, steam, mist) become DENSE local volumetric fog -- their particles keep being simulated but are splatted into local 3D density bricks that are ray-marched, lit, self-shadowed and composited with the volumetric fog; their billboards cross-fade out. Needs RenderVKVolumetricFog and RenderVKParticleLighting. 0 off, 1 on.

Vulkan (#1003): particle fog quality preset over the tuning settings (RenderVKParticleFogSteps / Resolution / NearResolution / ShadowLights hold the medium values). 0 low: half the march steps, 3/4 the resolution, at most 1 self-shadowed light. 1 medium: the settings as they are. 2 high: twice the steps, 1.5x the resolution (full resolution near the camera), 2 more self-shadowed lights (at most 4).
Vulkan (#1003): density multiplier of the particle fog bricks (1 = each particle carries exactly the optical depth its billboard had).

Vulkan (#1003): strength of the particle fog's BASE billow shape -- low-frequency Perlin-Worley noise (advected with the particles' flow) that thresholds the smooth density into lumps with defined edges, thin parts first (0-1.5; 0 = smooth). RenderVKParticleFogErosion erodes their edges further.

Vulkan (#1003): classification score at which a particle system converts to particle fog; it reverts below this minus 0.2, and in between the volume takes a matching share (the billboards keep the rest).
Vulkan (#1003): video memory budget of the particle fog brick atlas (about 8.1 MB per converted system on screen, at most 32); VRAM pressure halves it until it eases.

Vulkan (#1003): debug view -- 1 tints the particle fog by each system's blend (red partial to green fully converted) and draws the bricks' boxes; 2 shows the erosion (unlit: white untouched, red where the noise took density); 3 the ambient occlusion; 4 the local-light term alone (self-shadowed, with its phase). Any non-zero value repeats the VKPartFog log line every 2 s and turns the temporal accumulation off.
Vulkan (#1003): maximum ray-march steps per pixel through the particle fog bricks (8-256).
Vulkan (#1003): particle fog march resolution as a fraction of the render resolution per axis (0.25-1; depth-aware upsampled).
Vulkan (#1003): distance (m) beyond which particle systems stay billboards (they fade back in over the last 20 %).
Vulkan (#1003): frames the particle fog march accumulates (clamped to the current neighbourhood; 1 = none). Short on purpose: the billows move every frame.

Vulkan (#1003): strength of the particle fog's DETAIL erosion -- high-frequency Worley noise (a quarter of the billow size) eating into the lumps' edges more than their cores: cauliflower boundaries -- and of each puff's own lumpy profile (0-2; 0 = smooth lumps, round puffs).
Vulkan (#1003): size multiplier of the particle fog's billows (the base noise scale is 0.3 x the system's sprite size, 0.3-1 m; the detail a quarter of it). 0.25-4.

Vulkan (#1003): how many of the strongest local lights / projectors at each point of the particle fog are shadowed by the fog itself (a short ray through the volume: lit sides glow, far sides fall dark). 0 = off (all local light reaches through the fog), at most 4.

Vulkan (#1003): heavy fog -- converted fog sinks (this x 0.2 m/s; rising smoke and steam, pushed upward by their creator, do not) and on reaching the floor seen in the depth buffer spreads outward from its source in a flat layer, pooling and rolling along the ground. Only the volume moves; the particles themselves are untouched. 0 = off, 1 = heaviest.

Vulkan (#1003): particle fog march resolution (fraction of the render resolution per axis) while converted fog is within about 4 m of the camera -- near billows stay sharp. Not below RenderVKParticleFogResolution; the first switch resizes the march targets once.
Vulkan (#1003): let particle systems on worn attachments become particle fog too (off: they stay billboards).

Vulkan (#208): god rays / volumetric sun and moon shafts through gaps in geometry, marched through the sun/moon shadow cascades and added to the HDR scene before tonemapping. 0 off, 1 low (quarter resolution, 12 steps), 2 medium (half resolution, 16 steps), 3 high (half resolution, 24 steps). With ray-traced sun shadows (RenderVKSunShadows 2) each step traces a shadow ray toward the sun/moon instead, at quarter resolution with 4 / 6 / 8 steps. The march is accumulated over frames (RenderVKGodRaysTemporal), so few steps per frame still converge. Not shown with shadows off or under water.

Vulkan (#208): with ray-traced sun shadows, god ray shadow rays from march points farther than this from the camera (m) treat alpha-mask casters as solid (no per-leaf alpha test) -- the alpha test through stacked foliage is most of a ray's cost. 0 = always alpha test (RenderVKRTSunAlphaDist still applies when nearer).

Vulkan (#208): accumulate the god ray in-scatter over frames at its own resolution (camera reprojection, variance-clamped history) before it is composited, so the shafts' stochastic march (and the ray-traced sun's jittered shadow rays) settles instead of shimmering at the shaft edges. Off: the raw per-frame march is composited and only the main TAA integrates it. With RenderVKGodRaysDenoise (#657) the denoiser replaces this pass where it applies; it needs this on.

Vulkan (#657): god ray DENOISER -- the ray-traced shadow mask's denoiser applied to the shafts, in place of the plain temporal pass (RenderVKGodRaysTemporal must be on; snapshots never use it). The march splits into a 0-1 beam visibility and the noise-free lit in-scatter; the visibility gets an adaptive-length history with a neighbourhood / fast-history clamp (RenderVKGodRaysHistory, RenderVKGodRaysClamp, RenderVKGodRaysSvgf), a moving-caster anti-lag that resets the history fast only where a shadow ray met a moving avatar / vehicle / spinning prim (RenderVKGodRaysAntiLag), an edge-aware a-trous filter keyed on view distance (RenderVKGodRaysAtrous) and a TAA / FSR reactive (RenderVKGodRaysReactive). 0 = off (the plain temporal pass, for A/B), 1 = with ray-traced sun shadows (RenderVKSunShadows 2) only, 2 = also for the shadow-cascade march (no moving-caster detection there). Extra VRAM while it runs: 3 x 8 bytes per march texel (~12 MB at 4K). GPU timer: c_godrays_dn_tmp, c_godrays_dn_sp.

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): longest god ray history, frames (1-64). Longer settles shaft edges with fewer rays per frame; the clamp and the anti-lag cut it back where the shafts actually change.

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): width of the god ray history clamp, in standard deviations of the current 3x3 neighbourhood (0.5-8). Lower reacts faster to changes but lets ray noise through; higher holds edges steadier but can trail. With RenderVKGodRaysSvgf only moving-caster texels use it.

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): moving-caster anti-lag for god rays. The ray-traced march flags texels whose shadow rays met a MOVING caster (avatars, attachments, animesh, moved or spinning prims -- the RT shadow mask's detector); only there a change detector against a ~3-frame running average resets the history at once, so no shaft ghost trails behind a walking avatar or a vehicle while static shafts keep their long history.

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): longest god ray history, frames (1-15), where a moving caster was met (RenderVKGodRaysAntiLag) and no change was detected yet -- e.g. an idle avatar standing in a shaft.

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): SVGF-style god ray history (as RenderVKRTShadowSvgf): static texels clamp the history's luminance to the box of last frame's fast (~3-frame) averages around the texel instead of this frame's raw 3x3 -- a few rays per texel are all-lit / all-blocked by chance at shaft edges, and that box cut the history there (shimmer); and the a-trous filter weighs luminance by the variance left in the accumulated estimate. Off: the plain 3x3 variance box.

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): edge-aware a-trous (SVGF) iterations over the accumulated god rays, 0-4, at the march resolution (5x5 at steps 1, 2, 4, 8). Weighted by view-distance agreement (shafts never mix across silhouettes; the sky only with the sky) and luminance against the remaining variance, so converged shafts keep their detail and fresh / disoccluded texels are smoothed. 0 = no spatial filter (the finalize still runs).

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): gain of the god rays' TAA / FSR reactive (0-15; 0 = off). Where the moving-caster detector (RenderVKGodRaysAntiLag) sees a shaft change, the change x gain marks the pixels reactive (RenderVKReactiveMask), so the resolve does not drag the old shaft behind the mover. Only when the shafts are composited after the alpha (RenderVKGodRaysAfterAlpha).

Vulkan (#657, RenderVKGodRaysDenoise): god ray denoiser debug view, added to the scene like the shafts: 0 off, 1 raw one-frame march, 2 temporal accumulation without the spatial filter, 3 history length (white = RenderVKGodRaysHistory), 4 remaining variance (sqrt x 4), 5 events (red = history length 1: disocclusion / reset / anti-lag snap, blue = this frame's rays met a moving caster, green = the reactive written).
Vulkan (#208): god ray strength (0-4). Multiplies the scattering derived from the sky's haze density, so shafts follow the environment's haze.
Vulkan (#208): forward-scattering of the god ray medium (Henyey-Greenstein g, 0-0.95). Higher concentrates the shafts around the sun / moon; 0 scatters evenly in every direction.
Vulkan (#208): how far from the camera god rays are marched, metres (16-512). Also limited by the shadow cascades' far split.

Vulkan (#842): the haze's sun glow toward the sun (WindLight glow size / focus: the halo around the sun, above its 90-degree level) is not applied to geometry nearer than this many metres, and ramps in to full strength at 6x this distance; off-axis haze is unchanged. An opaque surface in the sun's direction shadows the air in front of it, so LL's unshadowed glow showed as a sun disc on nearby walls and roofs (strongest in heavy haze). 0 = LL behaviour (glow at every distance).

Vulkan sky-view lookup table (#819): 1 = the resolved haze sky colour (skyColor: ~6 exp, a pow, 2 sqrt and the sRGB decode per call) is baked once per frame into a 256 x 128 RGBA16F table (256 KB, created at login) over its two exact coordinates -- the dome direction's height (texels crowded at the horizon) and its angle to the light (crowded toward the sun's glow) -- and the probe-miss sky of the forward / deferred lighting, the water reflection's sky, the far-clip fade target and the RT miss shading read it with one bilinear fetch. The sky pass itself keeps the analytic haze. Exact up to interpolation (the horizon's above / below switch sits on a texel boundary). Pays only where the haze is ALU-bound rather than load-latency-bound, hence default 0 until measured: A/B the deferred lighting (g_defer_* / c_defer_*) and water timers on the GTX 1080 test box. GPU timer of the bake: c_sky_lut (~0.01 ms). Live

Vulkan (#208): shadow samples per god ray per frame (4-96; ray-traced sun shadows 2-96 -- with RenderVKGodRaysDenoise fewer rays per texel still settle). 0 = the tier's count (RenderVKGodRays; ray-traced sun shadows have their own, lower counts).

Vulkan (#208): resolution of the god ray march relative to the render resolution (0.25, 0.5 or 1). 0 = the tier's (RenderVKGodRays). Snapshots march at full resolution with 4x the steps (ray-traced: at least half resolution, 3x the steps, at most 24).
Vulkan: reclaim mesh geometry no live instance has referenced for ~1 min, once resident geometry exceeds RenderVKGeometryBudgetMB (or the mesh allocator is under pressure).

Vulkan: resident mesh geometry (MB) above which unreferenced geometry is reclaimed (RenderVKGeometryGC). This is the floor used under memory pressure; while RAM and video memory have room the budget scales to min(VRAM budget / 8, RAM / 32).

Vulkan: seconds an asset is kept after the last live object stops using it, before it is released (#737): material entries, terrain records, bindless texture slots and their images (outside VRAM pressure), and mesh geometry (slots, then their LOD groups, the CPU mirror and the packed GPU buffers). Release follows liveness, not memory pressure: a left sim's assets go about this long after its objects are gone. 5..600; memory pressure still reclaims sooner.
Vulkan: wall-clock time per frame (ms) the geometry GC's budget pass walks the mesh asset table (the pass is spread over as many frames as it needs).

RAM (#262, Linux/glibc, read at startup): allocations of at least this many KB are mmap-backed and go back to the OS as soon as they are freed (pins glibc's dynamic threshold, which otherwise grows and keeps freed decode buffers resident in per-thread arenas). 0 = glibc default. Needs RenderMemoryGovernor.

RAM (#262): memory (MB) the memory governor tries to leave available for other programs. 0 = automatic: max(1536 MB, 12% of physical RAM). Loading slows down (never stops) when available memory approaches this.

RAM (#883): every this many minutes, log one MemTrend line: process RSS and its change since the last report and per hour since the first, the malloc heap (in use / free but retained, Linux), the largest tracked containers and caches (entries, bytes, cap, peak) and the ones that grew most since the first report. Long AFK sessions: grep MemTrend in the log of the session that grew. 0 = off.
RAM (#883): how many containers each MemTrend line names, by size and by growth.

RAM (#883, Linux): when a MemTrend report finds more than this many MB free but retained in the malloc heap, hand it back to the OS (malloc_trim on a worker thread). Gradual frees from many subsystems never reach the texture-drop trim. 0 = never.
RAM (#262): after login (world init) and each teleport start, log the process RSS and memory-governor state every 250 ms for this many seconds (MemGov tag), plus the window peak and VmHWM. 0 = off.

RAM (#262): pace texture decodes, mesh decodes and HTTP concurrency by available system memory, and trim retained CPU texture copies sooner when memory is short or they exceed a RAM-scaled allowance, so loading bursts do not push other programs into swap.

Vulkan: byte budget (MB, min 16) for the raw compressed mesh-asset LOD bytes kept for re-decoding; least recently used are evicted and re-requested from the mesh repository (disk cache) if needed again.

Vulkan: sun/moon shadow cascade updates. 0 Realtime (every cascade every frame), 1 Balanced (nearest every frame, farther ones every 2/4/8 frames), 2 Performance (every 4/16/32). Cached cascades re-render early when the view outgrows them or the light jumps. Live.

Vulkan: the probe-face and shadow-view rigged culls (clean_probe_rigcull / clean_shadow_rigcull) compact their draw lists with a subgroup prefix scan. Used only where the device supports full compute subgroups (computeFullSubgroups) and subgroup arithmetic; otherwise, or with this off, the shared-memory scan runs (same output, slower). Off = rule the subgroup scan out when diagnosing a crash / device lost around avatars (rigged-cull crash, TheSlowly report). Live.

Vulkan (#564): cull rigged (avatar) shadow casters per shadow view -- each sun cascade and projector shadow tile draws only the avatars whose bounds reach it, instead of every avatar into every view. Lossless. Off = the old whole-list draws (diagnostics). Live.

Vulkan (#564): shadow-caster LOD for rigged mesh. A shadow view (sun cascade / projector tile) draws an avatar mesh's coarsest #561 decimated step whose geometric error stays under this many of THAT view's shadow texels at the wearer -- below what the map resolves, so near / fine cascades keep the full mesh. 0 = off (full detail in every shadow view). Live.

Vulkan (#564): GPU index memory for the shadow-caster LOD (decimated steps re-indexed onto their source mesh), allocated only once a slow frame draws shadow-mapped avatars; least-recently-used entries are evicted, unused ones freed after ~30 s. 0 = none. Read at allocation.

Vulkan (#564): per shadow view and rigged list, the most culled draws kept (capped by the rigged work capacity). A list with more draws in one view is drawn unculled that frame (never missing). Memory: 20 views x 5 lists x 2 x stride x 20 B. Applied at the next rigged buffer re-size.

Vulkan (#564): under load only (frame slower than RenderVKRiggedLodTargetFPS for ~2 s; released after ~5 s comfortably fast), at most this many projector shadow tiles per frame re-draw their avatar casters, stalest and most influential first. Projectors lighting the area near the camera always refresh. 0 = never limit. Live.

Vulkan measurement (needs RenderVKGpuTimers): log every frame's GPU total next to the staggered jobs it carried ("FRAMEJOB gpu=... jobs=0x...": bits 0-3 sun cascades re-rendered, 4-7 overlay cascades, 8-11 projector tiles re-rendered, 12 realtime probe, 13-15 scheduled probe face slot, 16 a far cascade re-render deferred (RenderVKShadowDeferFrames), 17 a projector tile held a frame behind a far cascade). For finding uneven frames. Live.

Vulkan measurement aid (restart or settings change that builds a new spec set): also build the uber lighting kernel with local lights / reflections / atmosphere (and all three) compiled out, with the live spec constants, never bound, so RenderVKPipelineStats logs what each feature costs in registers ("lightProbe ..." VKPipeStats lines).

Vulkan measurement aid (needs RenderVKGbufRegProbe at startup): draw the static G-buffer with probe variant N (1 no terrain, 2 no hex, 3 no debug, 4 no legacy bump, 5 all; #821 slim G-buffer VS probes with the real G-buffer FS: 11 no texture animation / texgen, 12 no tangent, 13 no encloses-camera test, 14 no rest-pose output, 15 no cel word, 16 no attachment / spin pose, 17 all six) to time its occupancy gain. Renders those features WRONG. 0 = normal. Live.

Deferred G-buffer draws (static and rigged) use a reduced vertex shader with only what the G-buffer fragment shader reads: no previous-frame pose (second instance row, previous joint table / skinned positions, second spin pose) and no pick outputs. Fewer registers, higher vertex-stage occupancy. Bit-identical position to the depth pre-pass (same source lines, invariant), so the EQUAL test still matches. Live A/B: both pipeline sets are built (0 = the full world vertex shader).

Deferred G-buffer: draw terrain with its own pipeline (terrain-only fragment shader, built hex tiling off / on and bound to match SlipstreamRenderTerrainHexTiling) and every other static opaque / mask surface with a terrain-free one. The terrain branch otherwise sets the register count, and so the occupancy, of every G-buffer fragment (Pascal: 112 vs 48 registers). The main cull also writes its terrain draws to a list of their own; every other pass draws the buckets as before. Same image. Live A/B (0 = the single G-buffer pipeline).

Terrain bake (#811): render each region's blended terrain surface (all four terrain materials, hex tiling, normal / ORM / emissive) once into per-region textures and draw far terrain from them with a slim G-buffer shader; near terrain keeps the live shader, crossfaded over RenderVKTerrainBakeBand metres. Probe and mirror captures use a ready bake at every distance. Unbaked regions (not baked yet, over the budget, under VRAM pressure) draw with the live shader. Live (0 = every terrain pixel blends its materials every frame, as before).

Terrain bake (#811): texels per edge of the nearest regions' bakes (256 to 4096, a power of two; 2048 = 8 texels per metre on a 256 m region, 22 MB with mips for legacy terrain, 45 MB for PBR). Farther regions bake smaller (the resolution their distance needs, RenderVKTerrainBakeAuto), down to 256.

Terrain bake (#811): metres from the camera within which terrain is always drawn with the live shader (the start of the crossfade to the bake). The crossfade also starts no nearer than where a bake texel covers one screen pixel (RenderVKTerrainBakeAuto), so the switch keeps the detail the live shader would show.
Terrain bake (#811): width in metres of the crossfade from the live terrain shader to the bake.

Terrain bake (#811): parity factor between a bake texel and a screen pixel. The crossfade starts at max(RenderVKTerrainBakeNear, Auto x texel size / pixel angle), and farther regions bake at the resolution that distance needs. 1 = the bake is as sharp as the live shader where it takes over; 0.5 = up to one mip softer (the switch moves nearer, more terrain is baked); 0 = the fixed near distance and RenderVKTerrainBakeRes everywhere.

Terrain bake (#811): VRAM budget in MB for the terrain bakes (nearest regions first; a farther region's bake is freed for a nearer one). Halved while the texture / VRAM pressure ladder is engaged, 0 at its geometry rung (every bake freed, the live shader draws all terrain, the setting untouched).
Terrain bake (#811): thousands of bake texels rendered per frame (whole rows; a 2048 x 2048 bake at 256 takes 16 frames). Lower spreads the bake cost thinner.

Vulkan measurement aid (restart): also build the static G-buffer pipeline with terrain / hex tiling / debug views / legacy bump compiled out (and all four), never drawn, so RenderVKPipelineStats logs what each costs in registers ("gbufProbe ..." VKPipeStats lines); #821: also the slim G-buffer VS with texture animation / tangent / encloses-camera / rest pose / cel word / attachment + spin pose compiled out (and all six), with the G-buffer FS ("gbufVsProbe ..." lines; compare with the slim VS, kWorldVertGbufSpv, ~95 registers).

Vulkan: bound each bucket indirect draw's max draw count by the live instances of its bucket class (lossless). Off = every bucket draw passes the full list capacity. Pascal-era NVIDIA pays for the max draw count, so this is worth ~15 ms a frame at 4K on a GTX 1080. Live.

Vulkan (#564): with cached sun cascades (RenderVKShadowUpdate 1 / 2), cache only the static world and redraw avatars into every cascade each frame (a static-caster copy per cascade, ~4 x resolution^2 x 4 B). Off = cached cascades keep avatars where they stood when rendered. Live.

Vulkan: with the dynamic-caster overlay (RenderVKShadowDynamicOverlay, cached sun cascades), the two far cascades (2 and 3) redraw their moving casters / avatars every N frames, alternating, and keep the last result in between (a re-rendered or invalidated cascade always refreshes; #825: a frame that re-renders a far cascade skips the other one's scheduled redraw, which then follows a frame later -- at most N + 1 frames). 1 = every cascade every frame. The near cascades always refresh. Live.
Vulkan: sun/moon shadow cascade resolution (square, per cascade; 4 cascades). Prefs "Shadow quality": 256 Low, 512 Medium, 1024 High, 2048 Ultra. Live.
Vulkan: shadow-map rasterizer constant depth bias (acne vs peter-panning). Applied at renderer init.

Vulkan sun / moon shadow cascades: the largest depth bias a caster gets, in normalized shadow depth (0.001, default: about half a metre in the nearest cascade, a few metres in the farthest). The slope-scaled bias (RenderVKShadowBiasSlope) grows without limit as a face turns edge-on to the sun, so at sunset a hill's crest was pushed metres back and god rays and late shadows leaked through the land. 0 = no cap. Read when the renderer starts.
Vulkan: shadow-map rasterizer slope-scaled depth bias. Applied at renderer init.
Vulkan: extra shadow-map compare bias in normalized light depth, subtracted at sampling (0 = rely on raster + normal-offset bias).

Vulkan: sun/moon shadow-map receiver fit (flickering acne streaks / wedges on flat ground in the far cascades, camera high or zoomed out). 1 = the filter taps (Medium / High Gaussian, Ultra PCSS) allow the receiver plane a slope tolerance (RenderVKShadowPlaneTolerance) proportional to their distance from the pixel, PCSS compares every gathered texel against the plane at that texel's own centre, its filter radius is capped in metres (RenderVKShadowPCSSMaxRadius), and past the nearest cascade the normal offset grows with the sine of the light angle. 0 = the old receiver (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (RenderVKShadowReceiverFit 1): how far, in metres of light depth per metre of filter-tap offset, the real surface may depart from the receiver plane the shadow filter extrapolates (the plane comes from the interpolated vertex normal, which on smoothed meshes and terrain is tilted from the true facet). Scales with each cascade's texel; zero at the pixel's own position and not applied in the nearest cascade, so contact shadows are kept. At 0.5 a far-cascade tap 2 texels out (~1.2 m) forgives ~0.6 m of depth: low objects (curbs, benches) can lose their shadow at that range -- lower it to 0.25 if they do. 0 = exact plane. Live.

Vulkan (RenderVKShadowReceiverFit 1, shadow filter Ultra / PCSS): largest penumbra filter radius in world metres (also bounds the blocker search) -- in the far cascades 16 texels spanned up to ~10 m of ground. 0 = no cap (16 texels). Live.
Vulkan diagnostic: disable the GPU cull's frustum test (every instance passes)

Object cache look-ahead (#479, grid path only): while the camera moves faster than RenderVKVOCacheLookAheadMinSpeed, also select and prioritise cached objects around the point it reaches in RenderVKVOCacheLookAheadSeconds.
Object cache look-ahead (#479): how far ahead along the camera's velocity to select, in seconds of travel (0.1 to 5; capped at the draw distance).
Object cache look-ahead (#479): camera speed (m/s) above which the look-ahead engages.
Object cache outcome metrics (#479): log a VOCacheMetrics summary every 5 s (pop-in latency, missing-on-screen, cull CPU time, objects created per second, waiting list, sampled invariant check).

Debug (#479, Develop > Rendering > Freeze culling camera): freeze the camera used for object-cache selection, the GPU cull frustum, mesh LOD and texture streaming at its current pose, while the view stays free; draws the frozen frustum and cache-entry boxes by state.
Frozen culling camera overlay (#479): draw cache-entry boxes within this many meters of the frozen camera.
Frozen culling camera overlay (#479): at most this many cache-entry boxes per frame.
Vulkan: VRAM budget (MB) for UI textures (previews, map tiles, icons); least-recently-bound are released (what is on screen is never released)

Vulkan: UI textures not drawn for this many seconds (closed floaters, scrolled-away thumbnails, old map tiles) release their VRAM; they are uploaded again from the CPU copy when drawn. 0 = only the RenderVKUITexCacheMB budget releases them
Vulkan: VRAM budget (MB) for world textures; textures keep the mips their on-screen size needs and a global mip bias fits the total under this. 0 = 60% of the GPU's memory budget
Debug: every 5 s, log the largest world object near the camera (VKHuge) with its registered instances and a CPU replay of the cull. Walks the whole object list; off by default.

Most Vulkan pipelines that may compile at once (shader warm-up at the login screen and after updates). 0 = automatic: hardware threads - 1. How many actually run together is decided by free memory: each pipeline's learned compile cost (or a per-driver default, 3 GB on AMD's Windows driver) is admitted against the memory available (#471). Lower it only if compiling still fills memory. Automatic mode compiles ONE at a time on Intel's Windows driver (parallel pipeline creation crashes it, #876) and, for 3 sessions, after a session that crashed while compiling shaders (#876/#890); any value above 0 overrides that.

Testing (#471): a fixed memory budget in MB for parallel Vulkan pipeline compiles, in place of the live free memory the scheduler normally admits them against. 0 = automatic. A low value (e.g. 1024) simulates a memory-starved machine: compiles serialize (one always runs). Delete vk_pipeline_cache.bin to force a cold compile.
Log texture/mesh fetch progress every 2 s for the first 5 minutes after login, plus when it settles (#484: comparing fetch strategies such as concurrency settings from a cold cache).
Vulkan ray tracing foundation (VK_KHR_acceleration_structure + ray_query): 0 off, 1 auto (enabled when the GPU supports it). Read at device creation: restart to apply

Vulkan ray tracing: total RT memory budget in MB (BLAS + TLAS + working buffers). 0 = auto: no percentage cap, RT may use the GPU memory budget's free room (what it holds plus what is free, minus a reserve for textures). Over budget RT evicts static BLAS and, with no room for its working buffers, falls back to shadow-mapped projectors. Avatars leave RT shadows only under real video memory pressure (the VRAM ladder), temporarily. RT also yields before textures under VRAM pressure.
Vulkan ray tracing: maximum static BLAS builds per frame (lazy, for LOD slots the TLAS pass selected)
Vulkan ray tracing: maximum triangles (thousands) of static BLAS built per frame
Vulkan ray tracing: instances whose bounding sphere is farther than this (m) from the camera are left out of the TLAS (terrain and water always in); 0 = no limit

Vulkan ray-traced projector shadows (RenderVKProjectorShadows 2): maximum number of shadowed projectors per frame (most important first; 1..256). No atlas budget applies; the cost is one ray per pixel per shadowed projector touching it

Softness of ray-traced shadows, 0..1 (Preferences > Graphics > Advanced > Shadow softness). Projectors: light source radius in metres at the apex (RenderVKRTShadowSamples jittered rays per pixel). Sun / moon: angular radius of the disc, softness * 5 degrees (0.01 = 0.05 degrees). With TAA the ray pattern changes every frame and the resolve averages it. 0 = hard shadows
Deprecated, migrated to RenderVKUpscaler (at startup, or whenever it is set to a non-zero value).

Vulkan upscaling (#184), AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 3.1: 0 off (native), 1 Native AA (1/1), 2 Quality (render at 1/1.5 of the window), 3 Balanced (1/1.7), 4 Performance (1/2), 5 Ultra Performance (1/3), 6 custom (RenderVKRenderScale). FSR replaces the TAA resolve (TAA turns on by itself); sharpening follows RenderCASSharpness. A device that cannot run FSR, or a frame where it fails, uses the TAA resolve at the same scale. #870 / #962 NVIDIA DLSS (needs the user-installed shim, see RenderVKDlssShim): 7 DLAA (native), 8 Quality, 9 Balanced, 10 Performance, 11 Ultra Performance -- fixed render sizes chosen by the network. Which network runs (Super Resolution, or Ray Reconstruction = denoise + upscale) is RenderVKDlssRayReconstruction. When DLSS is unavailable or cannot run a frame, FSR 3.1 runs at the matching preset (7 = 1, 8 = 2, ... 11 = 5). (Before #962, 7-11 always meant Ray Reconstruction: such settings are migrated once to RenderVKDlssRayReconstruction 1, see RenderVKDlssSettingsVersion.)

Vulkan DLSS (RenderVKUpscaler 7-11): while DLSS runs, run GI, the RT shadow mask and the stochastic denoiser at the full render resolution, overriding RenderVKGIScale, RenderVKRTShadowMaskScale and RenderVKDenoiseScale -- cleaner edges for DLSS to work from (less upsampled silhouette noise), at about 4x the cost of half resolution. 0 = off (default: the scale settings the user chose apply), 1 = on, 2 = auto: on only for the top GPU class (hardware ray tracing and 16 GB or more). The VRAM budget can still lower them. Live.

#962 which DLSS network the DLSS upscaler modes (RenderVKUpscaler 7-11) run: 0 Off = DLSS Super Resolution (upscale / anti-alias; our own RT denoisers stay on), 1 On = DLSS Ray Reconstruction (denoise + upscale: replaces the RT denoisers, RenderVKDlssRawSignals), 2 Auto (default) = Ray Reconstruction while at least one noisy ray-traced signal is on (RT reflections, ray-traced GI, ReSTIR DI), Super Resolution otherwise (ray tracing off, or only RT shadows / RTAO); a change of Auto's answer is adopted after it holds 2 s. A network whose NVIDIA library is missing is replaced by the other (Off without Super Resolution falls back to FSR 3.1). Switching re-creates the network before the next frame and restarts its history once. Live.
