#962 internal: the DLSS settings migration done (1 = RenderVKUpscaler 7-11 from before #962, which were Ray Reconstruction modes, moved to RenderVKDlssRayReconstruction 1 once). Do not change.

#962 debug: how DLSS Super Resolution gets the exposure. 0 (default) = the unexposed scene plus the resolved exposure (RenderExposure x the dynamic exposure) as the network's exposure image; 1 = the colour pre-exposed by us and the output divided back (the Ray Reconstruction path's handling). Flip only if Super Resolution looks too dark / bright, ghosts on exposure changes or blows out highlights. Live.

#870 / #962 DLSS (Super Resolution and Ray Reconstruction): 1 (default) = at startup, load the user-built slip_nr shim (libslipstream_ngx.so / slipstream_ngx.dll, contrib/ngxshim) when it is present (RenderVKDlssShimPath, then the viewer's library folder) and, on an NVIDIA GPU, enable the Vulkan extensions it needs; 0 = never load it. Restart required.

#870 raw signal routing while DLSS Ray Reconstruction is reconstructing (never under DLSS Super Resolution, #962: our denoisers stay on there): the deferred lighting consumes these RT signals RAW (our denoiser's spatial / temporal filter skipped) so the network denoises them. Bits: 1 the RT shadow mask's sun / moon (off by default: the forward-lit transparents read the same mask and reach the network through the transparency overlay, which it does not denoise), 2 stochastic projector shadows, 4 RT reflections (the resolve keeps each pixel's own ray; off by default: the rays are sparse -- density gradient / strength lattice -- so own-ray pixels next to filtered ones form a screen-space pattern, which the network cannot denoise), 8 ray-traced GI, 16 the merged RT shadow pass's sun / moon channel, 32 also signals running below the render extent (RenderVKRTShadowMaskScale, RenderVKDenoiseScale, RenderVKGIScale under 1: their raw samples reach the network as 2x2-correlated noise, so by default they stay denoised). 0 = every signal keeps our denoisers (A/B).

#870 DLSS Ray Reconstruction transparency overlay (needs the shim built from this viewer's contrib/ngxshim, version 1.1+): the network's colour input is the opaque scene (copied after the lighting) and pass 2's transparents -- alpha-blended hair / fur / feather cards, particles, glass, water -- go in as an overlay it upscales WITHOUT denoising. Their pixels have no guide data of their own (the guides show what is behind them), so denoising them smears their texture. Off: the final scene is the colour input (A/B).

#870 DLSS Ray Reconstruction responsivity hint on live media / animated-texture faces (the no-history masks, #605): -1..1, positive = less history (no trails on changing textures), 0 = no mask handed over. Needs the shim 1.1+. #962: DLSS Super Resolution takes the same mask as its bias-current-colour mask (positive values only; 0 or below = none).

#870 debug: show one DLSS Ray Reconstruction input instead of the reconstruction (the network does not run; Ray Reconstruction only, ignored under Super Resolution). 0 off, 1 colour input (pre-exposed; the opaque scene with the overlay on), 2 diffuse albedo, 3 specular albedo, 4 world normal (x 0.5 + 0.5), 5 roughness, 6 specular hit distance (log: black 0 m .. white 256 m, magenta = none / 65504), 7 motion (red |x|, green |y|, full at 8 render pixels; blue = moving left), 8 transparency overlay colour, 9 its alpha (pass 2b coverage), 10 responsivity, 11 depth. Live.

#870 debug: the sign of the projection jitter handed to DLSS (Ray Reconstruction and Super Resolution; 1 = as applied to the projection, the SDK's convention; -1 = negated). Flip only if the image shakes or fine detail stays fuzzy.
#870: maximum length (m) of the guide pass's screen-space march that estimates the specular hit distance where the RT reflection trace did not run (0 = none: those pixels report no hit).
#870: steps of that march (quadratically spaced; max 128).

#870 / #962: folder holding the user-built DLSS shim (libslipstream_ngx.so / slipstream_ngx.dll) and NVIDIA's feature libraries (Super Resolution: libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.* / nvngx_dlss.dll; Ray Reconstruction: libnvidia-ngx-dlssd.so.* / nvngx_dlssd.dll; either or both), or the shim's full path. Empty = the "dlss" folder in the viewer's user data folder (~/.slipstreamviewer/dlss, %APPDATA%\SlipstreamViewer\dlss; where contrib/ngxshim/build.sh installs), then the viewer's own library folder. Restart required.
FSR 3.1 (RenderVKUpscaler 1-6): 1 = the FidelityFX debug view (dilated motion vectors, reactive / lock masks, dilated depth, history viewports over the upscaled image).

Vulkan numeric HDR probe (FSR / TAA brightness): logs (VKFSR, about once a second) the linear HDR value at the RenderVKFSRDebugProbeX / Y pixel, the exposure, and per-image outlier statistics (largest channel, NaN / Inf count, pixels above exposed 16 / 256, 64x64-grid mean exposed luma). FSR frames: its colour input, its pre-RCAS internal upscaled colour and its output, with the exposure fed to FSR. Every resolved frame (FSR or TAA): the HDR target the post chain (bloom, exposure, tonemap) reads. Switch RenderVKUpscaler (or RenderFSAAType 3 with it off) and compare. Debug only (one extra compute dispatch per probe point).
RenderVKFSRDebugProbe: the probed pixel's horizontal position, 0 (left) .. 1 (right) of each image's own extent (render or display size). 0.5 = screen centre.
RenderVKFSRDebugProbe: the probed pixel's vertical position, 0 (top) .. 1 (bottom) of each image's own extent. 0.5 = screen centre.

FSR 3.1: transparency-and-composition mask value on the water surface (0..1). Its reflections and animated normals do not follow the surface motion; higher = FSR relies less on locked history there (less ghosting, a little more shimmer).
FSR 3.1: cap on the reactive mask fed to FSR (alpha-blended faces / particles, RenderVKReactiveMaskGain); AMD recommends staying below 1 (0.9).

Diagnostic (#190): log every targeted particle source every ~2 s (VKParticleDiag): flags, target key and whether it resolved, source / target positions, the source's distance from its owner avatar, accel, max age, burst settings.

Diagnostic (#693): every ~2 s log each script particle source (VKParticleAudit): pattern / flags / burst settings, LL's expected particles per second at the current frame time vs the bursts the source fired, the particles kept by LL's throttles, handed to the GPU and actually emitted (young particles in a pool snapshot), live particles vs the expected steady state, the largest per-frame source move and the live-attachment-transform vs LL render-position gap. Costs a whole-pool readback every ~2 s.

Vulkan particles: 1 (default) lights every live particle ONCE per frame at its centre in a compute pass (sun / moon + shadow, probe ambient, clustered local lights, haze), and the particle fragment shader only applies that record -- the standard per-particle lighting of modern engines. 0 = the old per-pixel lighting (the full lit-surface stack per particle fragment; costly with large sprites near the camera at high resolution).

Vulkan particles (RenderVKParticleLighting 1): near-camera fade by screen footprint. A sprite whose height exceeds this fraction of the view height starts fading out (alpha-blended and additive pairs only); fully gone at RenderVKParticleNearFadeEnd. End <= Start or Start 0 = off.
Vulkan particles: footprint (fraction of the view height) at which the near-camera fade reaches zero -- the sprite is then not rasterised at all. See RenderVKParticleNearFadeStart.

Vulkan particles (RenderVKParticleLighting 1, full-resolution draws): fragment shading rate. 0 = auto (2x2 from 1440p up, 2x1 below), 1 = full rate, 2 = 2x1, 4 = 2x2 pixels per shaded fragment. Coverage and blending stay per pixel. Sprites smaller than RenderVKParticleSmallPx always shade at full rate. Needs variable-rate shading support.

Vulkan particles: reduced-resolution particle pass (needs RenderVKParticleLighting 1). Sprites of the blend pairs that compose exactly (alpha, additive, premultiplied) are drawn into an offscreen target at RenderVKParticleResScale against a downsampled depth and composited with a depth-aware upsample (bilinear over the half-resolution texels whose depth agrees, nearest-depth where none does), glow and TAA reactive mask included. Sprites smaller than RenderVKParticleSmallPx stay at full resolution. 0 = off, 1 = always, 2 = adaptive (default): only while the estimated particle overdraw exceeds RenderVKParticleLowResEnter shaded layers per pixel, back to full resolution below RenderVKParticleLowResExit.
Vulkan particles: resolution of the reduced-resolution particle pass (RenderVKParticleLowRes) per axis. Below 0.75 = half resolution (0.5, the default); 0.75 and above = the pass never runs.
Vulkan particles (RenderVKParticleLowRes 2): estimated particle layers per pixel (sum of the on-screen sprite areas over the render area) at which the reduced-resolution pass switches on.
Vulkan particles (RenderVKParticleLowRes 2): estimated layers per pixel below which (for about half a second) the particles go back to full resolution.

Vulkan particles (#879; RenderVKParticleLighting 1): size routing. A sprite whose on-screen size (its larger side, in render pixels) is below this draws at full resolution and full shading rate: it never goes into the reduced-resolution pass (RenderVKParticleLowRes) nor gets the coarse rate (RenderVKParticleShadingRate), and does not count toward the reduced-resolution switch -- distant sprites a few pixels wide stay sharp instead of turning into blurry blocks. Ribbons always count as small. The large sprites keep the cheap paths. 0 = off (every sprite takes them, the old behaviour). Live.

Diagnostic (#879): every ~2 s log (VKParticles "routing:") how many on-screen particle sprites the size routing (RenderVKParticleSmallPx) kept at full resolution and full shading rate vs the large ones, where the large ones went (the reduced-resolution target size, or the full-resolution shading rate), and the coverage estimates the reduced-resolution switch reads.

Vulkan (#39): particles cast sun/moon shadows. Alpha and premultiplied-alpha sprites only (additive glows and fire add light, they don't block it); the texture's alpha shapes the shadow. With RenderVKTranslucentShadows they cast partial, tinted shadows (smoke thins the light), otherwise alpha-tested hard ones. Not cast by ray-traced sun shadows or into projector shadows. Cost: every live alpha particle is drawn once more per shadow cascade rendered that frame (up to 4), no extra culling -- small at typical particle counts, it grows with heavy particle scenes.

Vulkan: render the world at this fraction of the window resolution (0.25-1) and upscale it (#181). Only used while RenderVKUpscaler is 6 (FSR Custom). FSR 3.1 does the upscale (TAA turns on by itself); the post chain, selection, HUD and UI stay at full resolution. 1 = native (no extra work). Snapshots always render native. Switchable live

Vulkan (#195): trace ray-traced sun / moon and projector shadows for opaque surfaces in a separate compute pass after the depth pre-pass (a screen-space shadow mask), instead of inside the main lit shader. Pass 1 then runs the lighter lit shader without ray queries. Needs RenderVKDepthPrepass. Transparent surfaces and particles still trace inline.

Dynamic reflection probe capture (Vulkan): draw avatars (rigged meshes and worn attachments) only into the cube faces their bounds touch, as LL's per-face camera cull does. Off = every face draws every avatar the main view skinned.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan): sort each face's opaque and alpha-mask draws front to back from the probe origin before drawing (early depth rejection). Costs two single-workgroup sorts per face; with the mask pre-pass on it rarely pays at probe resolution.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan): when the LOD level chosen for the probe face is not resident, draw the nearest resident level (coarser first). Off = the highest resident level, as the main view falls back.
Reflection probe capture (Vulkan, #124): resolve alpha-mask cutouts with a depth-only pass first, then light each pixel once (depth EQUAL). Off = light every see-through cutout layer.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan, #829): draw the probe faces with the capture-only lit shader (no probe / SSR / mirror / AO / debug terms, the nearest 16 lights of the probe's list, one hard sun ray when the sun is ray traced). Live; off = the full forward lit shader the planar mirror uses (A/B).

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan, #833): draw the probe faces' opaque / mask / rigged geometry into a probe-resolution G-buffer and light it in one compute pass (the capture shader's lighting: the probe's nearest lights, the sun / one hard sun ray, no probe walk), instead of lighting every fragment in the forward capture shader. Water, cluster LOD avatars and blended alpha stay forward. Live; off = the forward capture faces (A/B). GPU timers: pr_gbuf (sky + G-buffer pass) / pr_light (realtime: pr_rt_gbuf / pr_rt_light); pr_face then holds only the water and the cluster LOD avatars.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan, #834): blended alpha (glass, translucent prims, alpha hair) in the probe captures. 0 = none, 1 = the realtime probe and scheduled probes near the camera (RenderVKProbeAlphaDist), 2 = every capture. The water and alpha-mask content (foliage, fences) are always drawn; mirrors always keep alpha. Live; also drops the blend layer of ray-traced captures.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan, #834, RenderVKProbeAlpha 1): a scheduled probe keeps its blended alpha while the camera is within this many metres of the probe's influence sphere (inside it = always). Live.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan, #124): objects (and avatars) whose bounding sphere projects to fewer face texels across than this on a probe cube face are not drawn into it (diameter over depth, at the face resolution); probe LOD follows the face resolution. 0 = draw everything.
Vulkan (F7): the HUD attachment cull walks a CPU-kept list of the HUD instances instead of re-reading every instance row (same rows, order and output). Off = the full-scan HUD cull.

Vulkan (S2 / I-2): the realtime reflection probe's six faces are culled in one pass (one per-instance cull, one scan, one emit into every face's own region) and their alpha-blend draws sorted once from the probe origin and split per face, instead of a compaction and an alpha sort per face. Needs RenderVKProbePrivateCull and RenderVKProbeSharedCull, and RenderVKProbeFrontToBack off. Off = the per-face path.

Vulkan (S2): with RenderVKMultiViewCull, the frame's scheduled reflection-probe face is culled in the realtime probe's pass (a second test per instance from its own origin) and its alpha sorted in the same dispatch, instead of its own cull and sort. Off = its own per-face cull. #832: works with the GPU-driven probes (#478) -- the scheduled face's cull entry is patched on the GPU from the scheduled job (origin, clips, dynamic flag, empty job), as the realtime job's is. Only in frames where the realtime probe runs all six faces multi-view; otherwise the scheduled face culls on its own. Live (A/B: pr_cull vs pr_rt_cull).

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan): the RenderVKProbeMinPixels size of a static instance is the widest it can look (the middle of its three oriented extents), so long thin faces -- rails, trims, poles, wires -- drop once they are under the cutoff across. Off = the diagonal of its world box (any long face was kept).

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan): an instance is drawn into the cube faces its bounds (padded 0.25 m) touch. Off = the 1 m-padded cull box plus a 4 m box around the object origin, which also drew every instance near a face edge into the neighbouring face.

Reflection probe capture (Vulkan): the probe alpha sort moves the water draws out of the alpha list, so the capture water and alpha passes each draw only their own geometry. Off = both draw the whole alpha bucket and discard the other's fragments.

Ray-traced reflection probes (Vulkan, RenderReflectionProbeDetail 3): each capture texel also traces the nearest alpha-blend surface in front of the opaque hit (a second ray over the alpha-blend class only) and composites it over the hit by its alpha -- one transparency layer (glass, foliage cards, beams); layers behind it are lost. Off = alpha-blend surfaces are invisible in ray-traced captures (cheaper).

Vulkan (F2): the main alpha sort moves water surfaces and water-exclusion prims (invisiprims) out of the alpha lists into their own lists, so the water, water-exclusion and alpha passes each draw only their own geometry (the planar mirror drops the other's geometry in the vertex shader). Off = water and invisiprims stay in the post-water alpha list and every pass draws the whole list, discarding the other fragments.

Vulkan TAA (F5): post-water alpha and particles write their coverage into a reactive mask that the TAA resolve reads, instead of a second copy of the scene after the water that the resolve diffs against (removes the copy and the split of the alpha pass). Off = the copy.

Vulkan TAA (F5, RenderVKReactiveMask): the reactive value is the covering alpha / particle coverage times this gain (clamped to 1). Higher = less history (and less trailing) under transparent surfaces, more aliasing shimmer.

Keeps media on prims (web pages, video) sharp with temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) or FSR upscaling on: those surfaces show only the current frame instead of blending it with earlier ones, so videos do not smear and scrolling text does not leave trails. The rest of the scene stays anti-aliased. Changes apply immediately.

The same as RenderVKMediaNoTemporal for scripted texture animations (scrolling, rotating or flip-book textures): with temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) or FSR upscaling on, those surfaces show only the current frame, so fast animations do not smear. Off by default: slow animations look smoother with the anti-aliasing. Changes apply immediately.
Reflection probe capture (Vulkan): cull every face of a capture in one pass over the instances (a face mask per instance), then compact each face from it. Off = a full cull per face.

Vulkan ray tracing (#194): bake alpha-mask cut-outs into opacity micromaps (VK_EXT_opacity_micromap) so the RT hardware resolves them; only edges fall back to the shader alpha test. Used when the device supports it and the start-up self-test passes.

Vulkan ray tracing (#1032): alpha-mask faces whose alpha test can never fail (no base texture, or a base texture without alpha, and face alpha at or above the cutoff -- e.g. blend faces auto-demoted to mask because their texture has no alpha) are traced as opaque: rays commit them in hardware instead of returning to the shader for an alpha test. Their shadow class (facing rules, coloured foliage transmission) is unchanged. 0 = trace them as cut-outs (previous behaviour, A/B). Live.

Vulkan ray tracing (#1032): also build opacity micromaps for static alpha-blend faces with an alpha texture -- transparent-only: regions whose alpha is exactly 0 are skipped by the RT hardware, everything else still goes to the shader (translucent shadows, coloured transmission and reflections unchanged). Needs opacity micromap support (RenderVKRTOpacityMicromaps). Costs micromap memory and build time for blend surfaces. 0 = alpha-mask faces only (previous behaviour). Live.

DEBUG (#194): stop opacity-micromap work after a stage and discard the result -- 1 bake, 2 + micromap build, 3 + micromap BLAS build; 4 live but forced 2-state, 5 live with micromaps disabled per instance, 6 live and accumulating but never referenced by the TLAS. 0 = normal.
DEBUG (#194): give each opacity micromap its own buffer instead of the shared RT arena.
Vulkan ray tracing (#194): highest opacity micromap subdivision level (4^level micro-triangles per triangle; 6 = 4096, 1 KB each). Higher = fewer edge fallbacks on large alpha cards, more memory.

Vulkan (#195): resolution of the ray-traced shadow mask relative to the render resolution (0.25-1). 0.5 traces a quarter of the rays; pass 1 upsamples it depth-aware (no bleeding across silhouettes). 1 = one traced pixel per rendered pixel.

Vulkan (#1086): below full mask resolution (RenderVKRTShadowMaskScale < 1), a pixel none of whose 4 mask taps lies on its own surface (a hair strand, the rim of an ear or a horn) takes the brightest tap close behind it instead of the closest-depth one -- which was the shadow that thin receiver casts on what is behind it (flickering dark specks on avatars, amplified by DLSS / FSR). Off = the closest-depth tap (A/B).

Vulkan (#1086): below full mask resolution, the smallest depth difference (mm, 1-1000) at which the RT shadow mask's plane-aware upsample still counts a mask texel as this pixel's surface (beyond 1.5 % of the distance). 30 = the previous 3 cm. Lower separates close-up layers -- hair cards over the scalp -- so one does not blend the other's shadow in (A/B).

Vulkan: denoiser for the ray-traced shadow mask (sun / moon and ray-traced projectors, RenderVKRTShadowMask). On: temporal accumulation in 16-bit float with a neighbourhood variance clamp and an adaptive history length (RenderVKRTShadowHistory, RenderVKRTShadowClamp; fast reset on disocclusion and moving casters), an R2 frame-sequence noise phase, an edge-aware penumbra blur sized by the blocker distance (RenderVKRTShadowSpatial) and a depth-plane-aware upsample. Off: the previous fixed 0.75 blend (A/B; set RenderVKRTShadowHint on as well for the exact old behaviour).

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise): longest temporal history of the ray-traced shadow mask, in frames (1-64). Longer = smoother soft / translucent shadows where nothing moves; moving casters and disocclusions reset it through the neighbourhood clamp regardless, and with RenderVKRTShadowSvgf a moving sun (time of day) shortens it. Was 16 before #85.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise): moving-caster anti-lag for the ray-traced shadow mask. The trace flags texels whose shadow rays met a MOVING caster (avatars, worn attachments, moved or spinning prims; this frame or last), and only there a change detector (centre sample and 3x3 mean both outside the fast history noise band) snaps the history to the current frame and drops the fast-history box widening, so a walking avatar shadow on static ground appears at once and leaves no trail. Static casters (grass, fences) keep the long, widened history. Off: the previous behaviour everywhere (A/B).

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise, TAA / FSR with RenderVKReactiveMask): where the moving-caster detector (RenderVKRTShadowAntiLag) saw a shadow move this frame, mark the pixels reactive for the TAA / FSR resolve (a shading change on a static receiver, whose zero motion vector otherwise lets the resolve keep the old shadow). RenderVKRTShadowReactiveGain scales it. Off: A/B.
Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowReactive): reactive strength per unit of shadow change (0-15.9; 2 = a half lit-to-shadow change is fully reactive).

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise): longest mask history, in frames (1-15), of HARD shadows (penumbra about one mask texel) cast by MOVING casters; contact shadows go to 1 frame and wide penumbrae up to RenderVKRTShadowHistory. With Shadow softness 0 moving-caster shadows take no mask history at all (TAA / FSR integrate the jitter). Static casters keep their own 4-frame floor.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise): width of the history clamp box of the ray-traced shadow mask, in standard deviations of this frame's 3x3 neighbourhood (0.5-8). Lower = less ghosting behind moving casters but more residual shimmer in penumbrae; higher = smoother but slower to follow.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise): largest radius, in shadow-mask texels, of the edge-aware penumbra blur (0 = no spatial pass, 16 max). The radius follows each penumbra's own width on the receiver (blocker distance x light size, stretched toward grazing sun angles), so hard / contact shadows are never blurred; fully lit and umbra texels are never touched.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise, #85): SVGF-style spatial filter for the ray-traced sun / moon shadow mask: this many edge-aware a-trous iterations (5x5 B3-spline at step 1, 2, 4, 8; 1-4) weighted by the receiver's depth plane, its slope and luminance against the temporal / spatial variance, filtered along with the variance; gated by the penumbra radius (RenderVKRTShadowSpatial caps it) so contact shadows and fully lit / umbra texels stay exact. No extra video memory (last frame's history slot is the scratch). 0 = the single penumbra disc blur (previous behaviour). Ray-traced projector shadows run the same iterations when RenderVKRTShadowProjDenoise is on (#666; else they keep the disc blur). Default 3 (#85; was 0). Live.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise, #666): ray-traced projector shadows get the full sun / moon denoiser. Each projector keeps its own shadow history length and short running average, its still shadows are only reset when they really changed (as RenderVKRTShadowSvgf for the sun), moving casters and moving lights shorten its history, and the RenderVKRTShadowAtrous filter smooths its soft edges by how noisy each spot still is. Needs RenderVKRTShadowSvgf. Off: the previous projector path (shared history length, one-frame clamp box, penumbra disc blur; A/B). Costs 16 B per shadow-mask pixel of video memory and scales with the ray-traced projectors in view. Live (a switch restarts the shadow history).

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise, #666): the ray-traced shadow denoiser keeps its temporal history whatever the anti-aliasing (FXAA, SMAA or none, not only TAA / FSR). Keeps the motion-vector plumbing TAA uses (last frame's camera, motion vectors, previous object positions) while the shadow mask is in use, without TAA's jitter or resolve. Off: the previous coupling -- without TAA / FSR the mask has no temporal accumulation and soft shadows show their one-frame noise (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#1050, A/B): while DLSS Ray Reconstruction reconstructs the frame, the ray-traced shadow mask's denoiser (the separate sun shadow path: "Trace sun and projector shadows together" off) stabilises the sun / moon itself as it does without TAA / FSR -- the full RenderVKRTShadowHistory on static shadow edges and the exact history reprojection (RenderVKRTMaskExactReproj) -- instead of leaving the jittered edge for a resolve to average: Ray Reconstruction is a denoiser, not such a resolve, and static shadows vibrated in place (strongly at Ultra Performance, a little under DLAA). TAA, FSR, DLSS Super Resolution and no AA are unchanged. 0 = the old behaviour. Live.

Vulkan (#674 fix, A/B; 0 = the old biased reprojection): the ray-traced shadow denoiser's history reprojection uses the exact render pixel each reduced-resolution shadow-mask texel traced, instead of an estimate that is a quarter texel off at RenderVKRTShadowMaskScale 0.5. With TAA / FSR the jitter averages that error out; without them (FXAA, SMAA, none) a still shadow's history slides sideways every frame, gets clamped back and slides again (shadows gliding back and forth). Only applies while the view is not jittered, or jittered under DLSS Ray Reconstruction (RenderVKRTShadowRrHistory): TAA / FSR are unchanged. Live.

Vulkan (#674 diagnostic): log (category VKShadow) this many frames of what the shadow passes see -- the sun / moon direction and its step since the previous frame, the camera and its step, whether the sun is ray traced this frame, the RT shadow mask state (ping-pong set, resolution, history), and the temporal / jitter state. One run per change of the value (set 0, then N again to repeat; max 2000). 0 = off.

Vulkan RT shadow mask: how far a receiver's shadow-ray origin leaves its surface to cover the depth buffer's sub-pixel position error, in render-pixel footprints scaled by the sine of the view's grazing angle (0 off, 1 = 1/8, 2 = 1/4, 3 = 1/2). Without it, far ground / large flat prims seen at a grazing view self-shadowed in sharp shards and screen-row combs (still camera). Sub-pixel, so no visible gap at any distance. Live.

Vulkan RT shadow mask, smooth terrain (#211): a receiver pixel that the drawn terrain shows but the ray-traced terrain covers (the two surfaces disagree there by up to 10 cm along the normal: a geomorph step, a coarser BLAS stand-in) starts its sun rays on the ray-traced surface instead, found by one short terrain-only ray toward the camera. Without it such receivers self-shadowed in long streaks along a low sun. Only moves the ray origin up onto the traced terrain (never down), so contact shadows and terrain self-shadowing from real relief are kept. Live.

Vulkan (#674 fix, A/B; RenderVKRTShadowSvgf): measure the sun / moon's movement between frames exactly. The old measure read float rounding of the light direction as up to ~0.02 degrees of movement on random frames, which cut the ray-traced shadow history short there and made still shadow edges pulse without TAA / FSR. 0 = the old measure. Live.

Vulkan (#674, RenderVKRTShadowAntiLag): after a ray-traced shadow's rays last met a moving caster (avatar, attachment, moved prim), the spot keeps the moving-caster treatment (short history, change detection, no static clamp widening) for this many more frames (0-7). Stops moving avatars' shadows leaving a fading trail where the shadow just left. 0 = the old one-frame flag (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#674): when the camera zooms or moves in, the ray-traced shadow denoiser shortens its history in proportion to how much bigger things got on screen, so shadows don't visibly settle in afterwards. 0 = off (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#674, RenderVKRTShadowAntiLag): where a moving caster (avatar, attachment, moved prim) newly covers a spot, its ray-traced shadow is taken at once instead of fading in from the lit history over a few frames (the light, mottled leading edge of a walking avatar's shadow). Only when this frame's rays met the mover and the spot got darker beyond the ray noise. 0 = off (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#674, RenderVKRTShadowAtrous + RenderVKRTShadowSvgf): spots a moving caster's shadow just reached (only a frame or two of history) get one pass of the spatial shadow filter even where the shadow edge is sharp, smoothing the dotted ray pattern inside a fresh avatar shadow. 0 = off (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#674, RenderVKRTShadowSvgf + RenderVKRTShadowAtrous): where a moving caster's ray-traced shadow has just arrived, the spatial shadow filter no longer fills the spot from the long-settled (still lit) ground around it -- that fill is meant for freshly uncovered ground, and on a walking avatar's shadow it blended the leading edge into the lit area in front. 0 = the old fill (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#674, RenderVKRTShadowAntiLag): the longest temporal history (frames, 1-15) a ray-traced shadow keeps where its rays meet a moving caster (avatar, attachment, moved prim), soft wide penumbrae included -- they used to climb back to the full RenderVKRTShadowHistory, so a walking avatar's soft shadow faded in at its leading edge. The spatial filter smooths the extra noise. 0 = the old behaviour (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#674, RenderVKRTShadowAntiLag): where a moving caster's ray-traced shadow is certain this frame -- every shadow ray of the spot blocked (or every one clear) and its neighbourhood agreeing -- the denoiser shows this frame's result directly instead of blending in older history, so no light from where the shadow was a moment ago bleeds through a walking avatar's shadow. Soft edges still use the history. Static casters are not affected. 0 = off (A/B). Live.

Vulkan (RenderVKRTShadowDenoise, #85): steadier soft sun / moon shadow edges. On: the shadow history of still objects is only reset when the shadow really changed (checked against a short running average of the neighbourhood, not one noisy frame), so the faint outer edges of soft shadows keep their full history; history is also dropped where the surface turned, and is shortened while the sun moves (time of day) so shadows don't lag. The spatial filter (RenderVKRTShadowAtrous) then smooths by how noisy each spot still is: freshly uncovered ground (an avatar moving off it) is smoothed hard right away, settled areas keep their detail. Off: the previous behaviour (A/B). Live.

Vulkan RT shadow denoiser debug view (#85), shown through the sun / moon term of the lighting: 0 off, 1 raw one-frame trace, 2 temporal accumulation (no spatial filter), 3 history length (white = RenderVKRTShadowHistory frames), 4 variance (sqrt x 4; with RenderVKRTShadowSvgf the variance left after filtering), 5 final mask, 10 (#674) per texel: red = how far the temporal result was pulled away from this frame's raw trace (full red = 0.25 or more), green = moving-caster path, blue = certainty bypass took the raw, 9 (#674) per texel: red = the history length the temporal pass used (white = RenderVKRTShadowHistory), green = the moving-caster path, blue = the change detector, 6 history events (red = no history: newly uncovered or first frame, green = history clamped because the shadow changed, the stronger the more, blue = a moving object's shadow moved), 7 the short running average the history is checked against, 8 shadow-terminator diagnostics (#664; every RT shadow -- sun and projectors, mask and inline -- shown through its light, in the terminator band: PRE-PASS TRIANGLE path red / yellow / white = red, green = Hanika lift length (5 mm = full), blue = escape check shortened (half) / cancelled (full) the lift; CAMERA-PROBE path blue / cyan (green = lift), magenta = probe hit rejected (no lift); black = outside the band). 11 self-hit detector (the raw trace; red = a sun ray blocked within 5 cm of its origin, blue = within 50 cm -- specks on open ground that turn red are rays hitting their own receiver; best with RenderVKRTShadowCache 0). 12 smooth-terrain receiver gap (#211; the raw trace, smooth terrain on): pixels whose drawn surface lies UNDER the ray-traced terrain show red rising to yellow with the gap along the normal (2 cm full red, 10 cm yellow), every other pixel the raw value at quarter brightness -- red patches mean the RT terrain does not match the drawn one there (RenderVKRTTerrainOriginSnap hides it). 1-7, 11 and 12 need RenderVKRTShadowMask; 8 reads best unfiltered (RenderVKRTShadowMask off, or RenderVKRTShadowAtrous 0). Live.

Vulkan forward lit surfaces (alpha-blend glass / water prims / transparent pools, forward opaque): 1 (default) = their local lights are found through the froxel light masks the deferred lighting uses (RenderVKLightCulling 2: about 64 px tiles x 48 depth slices at 4K, every light kept) -- the same light-list quality as opaque surfaces. 0 = the coarse 16 x 9 x 24 cluster lists (about 240 px tiles at 4K, at most 64 lights each; A/B). Needs RenderVKLightCulling 2 (otherwise the cluster lists are used). Mirror and reflection-probe captures keep their own lists. Live.

Vulkan ray-traced projector shadows (RenderVKProjectorShadows 2) on ALPHA-BLENDED surfaces (glass, water prims, transparent pools). The RT shadow mask and the stochastic projector sampler (RenderVKProjStochastic) only cover surfaces in the depth pre-pass, so a blended surface had to trace one shadow ray (plus a terminator probe) per ray-traced projector at every shaded fragment -- a screen-filling transparent surface under a few projectors cost milliseconds. 0 (default) = blended surfaces take ray-traced projectors unshadowed (no ray; as water and the reflection captures). 1 = trace them inline per fragment (the previous behaviour, exact shadows on glass). Shadow-map projector records (RenderVKProjectorShadows 1) are unaffected. Live.

Vulkan ray-traced projector shadows (#85 phase 2): 0 = exact (the RT shadow mask traces every ray-traced projector at a pixel: the first 4 in their own slots, every further one folded into a light-weighted REST visibility slot), 1 = stochastic + denoised: per pixel the deferred lighting picks RenderVKProjStochasticSamples of ALL the ray-traced projectors reaching it by importance, traces one shadow ray each and the diffuse / specular denoiser filters the result (every projector shadowed; cheaper in clubs with many projectors). Needs ray tracing, RenderVKProjectorShadows 2 and the split deferred lighting; water and captures keep the projectors unshadowed while it runs (alpha-blend surfaces: RenderVKRTBlendProjShadows, in either mode). GPU timers: c_defer_pstoch, c_dn_tmp, c_dn_sp. Live.

Vulkan merged ray-traced shadows (#195 + #85): when the sun / moon (RenderVKSunShadows 2) AND the projectors (RenderVKProjectorShadows 2, RenderVKProjStochastic 1) are both ray traced on a split deferred frame, ONE pass traces each pixel's sun / moon ray (its own ray: soft disc, contact edges, moving-caster tracking as the RT shadow mask) beside its stochastic projector pick, and ONE denoiser filters both (the sun / moon as its own channel with the mask's history rules and a penumbra-gated filter). The RT shadow mask does not run then and the lighting stays deferred. GPU timers: c_defer_shadowmerge, c_dn_tmp, c_dn_sp (instead of c_rtmask, c_rtmask_tmp, c_rtmask_sp, c_defer_pstoch). Every other combination of sun / projector shadow settings keeps its separate path. 0 = always the separate passes. Live.

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (#85 / #869 Phase 1): the stochastic projector pass and the merged RT shadow pass (RenderVKProjStochastic, RenderVKRTShadowMerge) run on the GENERIC SHADOW CORE -- one receiver setup per pixel, one light-sample loop (sun / moon, then the projector picks), one shadow-ray walk for every light type (6 ray-query sites in the merged kernel instead of 16, less than half its size). The sun / moon is traced exactly as before; projector rays gain the receiver bias the RT shadow mask always gave them (the shadow-terminator lift on smooth low-poly meshes, the cluster-LOD avatar lift and the view-slope offset): less shadow acne on projector-lit avatars and curved surfaces. 0 = the per-light-type kernels. Live (the core kernels compile at login; until they land the per-light-type kernels run).

Vulkan ray-traced sun / moon shadows (#771 Phase 2): SUN EXPOSURE CERTIFICATES -- a world-space cache that proves a surface cannot see the sun for any sun direction along the next stretch of the sun's path (a few degrees of its arc; a cone around it for a sky that does not move), so the merged RT shadow pass skips the sun ray there (interiors, clubs, under roofs) and keeps skipping while the sun moves. Certificates expire only when the sun really leaves their arc (minutes), a static object near them changes, a ray proves them wrong, or they reach RenderVKSunCertMaxAge. The image is the same as without it. Needs the merged RT shadow pass on the generic shadow core (RenderVKRTShadowMerge, RenderVKProjStochastic, RenderVKShadowGenericCore). 0 = off, 1 = on. Live.

Sun exposure certificates (RenderVKSunCert) debug view, drawn as the sun's colour: 1 = what each pixel did (green skipped, cyan spot check, orange traced in a certified cell's unseen part, blue traced: not certified, yellow certifying, magenta no table entry, grey not considered, red a lit ray revoked the cell); 2 = certificate age (green new to red at RenderVKSunCertMaxAge, blue none). 0 = off.

Sun exposure certificates: degrees of the sun's arc per certified bin (~80 s of the default 4 h day per 2 degrees). Larger = fewer renewals, more rays per certificate and more cells that cannot certify. Changing it re-certifies everything.
Sun exposure certificates: how far (degrees) beside its current arc the sun may wander before the arc is re-anchored (a day-cycle keyframe kink re-certifies everything).
Sun exposure certificates: bins certified ahead of the sun's current one per round (0-31). More = rarer renewals (the next round starts when the sun reaches the last bin), more rays per round.
Sun exposure certificates: certification rays per bin per round (4-64; the 4 wedge corners first). A bin is certified only when every one of them hits static opaque geometry.
Sun exposure certificates: the finest world cell's edge (m); a cell doubles until it holds RenderVKSunCertCellPixels render pixels across.
Sun exposure certificates: render pixels across a cell at least (the level choice).

Sun exposure certificates: 1 in N pixels that could skip trace anyway, and a lit result revokes the cell and its neighbours (a gap narrower than the certification rays). Rounded down to a power of two; 1 = every pixel traced (validation: SXC certifies but never skips), 0 = no spot checks.
Sun exposure certificates: seconds a certificate is used before it is re-certified (a safety net for changes nobody reported; renewed before it runs out).
Sun exposure certificates: table entries (64 B each; 65536 = 4 MB). Fixed size: idle entries are evicted (RenderVKSunCertIdleSecs, sooner while the table is nearly full).
Sun exposure certificates: pixels of a cell that trace certification rays per frame (one ray per certified bin each).
Sun exposure certificates: certification rounds started per frame at most (a teleport's cold start spreads over several frames instead of a ray burst).
Sun exposure certificates: an entry nobody looked at for this long is evicted (halved repeatedly while the table is over 85 % full).
Sun exposure certificates: frames a static change (moved, edited, rezzed, deleted object; LOD swap) keeps revoking the cells its sweep toward the sun crosses (a new BLAS can land a few frames late).
Sun exposure certificates: frames between two certification rounds of a cell at least; x4 per recent revocation by a lit ray (hysteresis: a marginal cell settles on traced instead of flickering).
Sun exposure certificates: a sun / moon step above this many degrees in one frame re-certifies everything.
Sun exposure certificates: while the sun moves faster than this many degrees per frame (an environment transition) nothing is skipped or certified; 30 calm frames later everything re-certifies.

Sun exposure certificates: the VKSunCert log line every ~5 s (skip %, traced reasons, certification rays, rounds, revocations by cause, epochs by cause, cells live / cap / peak, the sun's speed, GPU ms).

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (RenderVKReSTIRDI 2+, RenderVKReSTIRDenoiseIters above 0): pixels whose SURFACE moved on its own since the last frame by more than this many shadow-denoiser texels (an animated avatar or animesh, a moving prim: the motion vectors disagree with the camera's reprojection) never take the converged shortcut -- their light pick may be stable, but a still lamp's shadow slides over a breathing / walking body, so the full spatial filter stays on (no crawling grain on avatars). Static geometry is never affected. 0 = off (the old rule: avatars could take the shortcut). 0.25 .. 3.75 in quarter steps. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (RenderVKReSTIRDI 2+, #85): a-trous iterations the shadow denoiser gives a pixel whose diffuse visibility has CONVERGED (its reused light pick stands for 8+ frames and its history is 8+ frames long) -- the reservoir already did most of the noise work, so the spatial filter can stop early (less blur, less cost). Only where one light holds 90 %+ of the pixel's light (see RenderVKReSTIRConvMultiLight). 0 = every pixel takes all RenderVKDenoiseAtrous iterations. 1 .. 7. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#1052, A/B): which pixels may take the RenderVKReSTIRDenoiseIters converged shortcut. Off (default) = only pixels where one light holds 90 %+ of the light: elsewhere a long-standing reused light pick is still one light's on/off shadow per frame, shared by its whole neighbourhood, and the shortened spatial filter left organic blotches with hard rims in the stochastic light shadows. On = the old rule (any pixel with a long-standing reused pick; less denoiser cost, the blotches back). Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (A/B): 1 = cut the shadow denoiser's history and the reservoirs' reuse whenever the sum of the lights reaching the pixel's 1 m light-grid cell changes by 25 % (the original rule: any moving light in the cell, or the camera moving a pixel into the next cell, restarted the history -- grainy shadows near moving lights). 0 (default) = no such cut: reused lights are re-weighed with their current position and colour each frame, a light switching off drops out at once, and the denoiser's neighbourhood clamp limits the lag. Live.

Vulkan merged RT shadows (RenderVKRTShadowMerge 1, A/B): 1 (default) = pixels whose shading normal faces away from the sun / moon still trace one sun ray (their real visibility, mostly self-shadowed) instead of being written 'lit'. Those pixels are never lit by the sun themselves, but the sun shadow denoiser and its upsample blend them into their neighbours: written 'lit' they drew thin BRIGHT lines along normal seams, mane strands and wing edges of a mesh avatar in sun shadow (a dark room). 0 = the old 'lit, no ray' rule. Costs one extra ray on the turned-away pixels whose facet is within the terminator slack (most others are self-shadowed without a ray). Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, A/B): the MOVING-LIGHT shadow rule. A moving light's shadow moves every frame, but the shadow denoiser reprojects its history with the camera only, so that history is wrong wherever the shadow moved (grain under moving party / club lights). 1 (default) = pixels lit by a light that moved since the last frame (more than RenderVKReSTIRMoveEps) keep only RenderVKReSTIRMoveHistory frames of shadow history in proportion to that light's share, always take the full spatial filter (no RenderVKReSTIRDenoiseIters shortcut), and that light's shadow sample traces RenderVKReSTIRMoveRays rays. 0 = the old behaviour. Debug: RenderVKDenoiseDebug 7 draws white stripes over such pixels. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, RenderVKReSTIRMoveCut 1): frames of shadow history a pixel keeps when the lights reaching it moved since the last frame (scaled by their share: full at half of its light). Shorter = less lag behind the moving shadow, more noise for the spatial filter. 1 .. 15. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, RenderVKReSTIRMoveCut 1): pixels lit by a light that moved since the last frame evaluate this many of their candidate lights, each with its own shadow ray, instead of one picked light (the ReSTIR reservoir's pick, which neighbouring pixels share and which is all-or-nothing visible). More real samples where the short shadow history cannot average them -- removes the crawling 'water' blotches under moving club lights. Costs up to this many shadow rays per such pixel (instead of 1); lights that do not reach the pixel trace nothing. 0 = off (one pick). 0 .. 15 (at most the RenderVKReSTIRCandidates window). Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, RenderVKReSTIRMoveCut 1): shadow rays a moved light's sample traces across its disc (RenderVKReSTIRPointRadius) instead of one, where its short history cannot average the penumbra. Only pixels picking a moved, soft light pay; adaptive early-outs stop after 2 rays where they agree. Used only where RenderVKReSTIRMoveLights is 0 (the dense evaluation traces one ray per light: a few-cm disc has little penumbra to resolve). 1 .. 15. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (RenderVKReSTIRDI 1+): how a pixel takes its RenderVKReSTIRCandidates light samples (and the moving / flickering-light rule its RenderVKReSTIRMoveLights) from its light-grid cell's RenderVKReSTIRCellSamples. The cell's samples are ordered by brightness share, so a strong light fills a long run of them. 1 (default) = evenly spaced samples across the whole list: every light is represented about in proportion to its brightness, and the dense evaluation shadows several DIFFERENT lights. 0 = a contiguous run (the old way: often the same light repeated -- e.g. four rays of a fire and none of the lamp beside it, which showed as dark blotches in soft multi-light shadows near a flickering fire). Both are unbiased. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, needs RenderVKReSTIRMoveCut 1): the FLICKERING-LIGHT shadow rule. The shadow denoiser filters ONE visibility per pixel for all the shadowed lights reaching it, weighted by their brightness; when one light's brightness or colour changes every frame (a scripted fire, a blinking club light) beside other lights, the remembered visibility belongs to the old brightness mix, and a flaring fire shone through its own shadow (bright flickering streaks and crawl on an avatar by a campfire). 1 (default) = pixels whose light mix such a light can shift take the moving-light rules: short history (RenderVKReSTIRMoveHistory), several lights evaluated per pixel (RenderVKReSTIRMoveLights), the full spatial filter -- in proportion to how much of the mix can shift (a lone light never: its visibility does not depend on its brightness). 0 = off. The 'ReSTIR DI' stats line counts the flickering lights. Live.
Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, RenderVKReSTIRFlickerCut 1): how much a light's colour / intensity or radius must change between two frames (relative, 0.02 = 2 %) to count as flickering. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (#869, RenderVKReSTIRMoveCut 1): how far (metres) a light's centre (a projector's apex, or its axis turning) must move between two frames to count as moving. Sub-millimetre jitter of a still light is ignored. Live.

Vulkan (#91, emissive surfaces as lights; needs RenderVKReSTIRDI 1+, RenderVKProjStochastic 1 and ray-traced projector shadows): 1 = EMISSIVE SURFACES LIGHT THE WORLD -- every ReSTIR frame each static object face whose material emits (PBR emissive, or legacy FULLBRIGHT + GLOW; fullbright alone and glow alone never) above RenderVKReSTIREmissiveMin becomes a set of EMISSIVE TRIANGLE lights (its mesh triangles in world space, each with its own texture colour; up to RenderVKReSTIREmissiveTriangles of them, 4096 emitting objects). A receiver is lit by every triangle whose front it faces (exact form factor, clipped to its horizon -- no box, no cut-off line on whatever stands on a large emitter), coloured by the emissive texture under the light it sees (a rainbow track tints what stands on each stripe). ReSTIR DI samples them together with the lights (one shadow ray to a point on the triangle: soft shadows, denoised), and the lighting adds their diffuse light x the denoised visibility; with GI on, GI rays stop taking those emitters' emission (RenderVKReSTIREmissiveGISplit) so nothing is lit twice. Works even in a scene without lights. Counted in the 'ReSTIR DI' VKGpu line (emitters, triangles, cells, texels, rays); GPU timer c_rs_emissive (emitters + triangles + grid) and pass 15's. 2 = build the records and grid cells only (no light: the cost A/B). 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): the radiance luminance (linear) a face's material needs (averaged over its texture) to become an emissive light; its triangles on dark parts of the texture (under 2 % of this) are no light. Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): how strongly a LEGACY fullbright + glowing face emits -- radiance = its colour x tint x texture x glow x this (a face needs both fullbright and glow). 0 = legacy faces never emit (PBR emissive only). Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): how strongly a PBR emissive face emits as a light -- radiance = its emissive factor x emissive texture x this; the PBR counterpart of RenderVKReSTIREmissiveGlowScale (applied before RenderVKReSTIREmissiveMin). 1 = the material's own emission (physically right for LDR content: neon and signs light only faintly and close by); higher = brighter, longer-reaching light from every PBR emitter. An emitter that takes over its prim's point light (RenderVKReSTIREmissiveLightTakeover) takes that light's strength instead. 0 = PBR faces never emit. Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): 1 = LIGHT TAKEOVER -- a prim with an SL POINT light (not a projector, not worn / attached) whose own faces emit (PBR emissive, or legacy fullbright + glow, as for any emitter) lights the world FROM THOSE FACES at its light's strength: a lamppost's lantern glass becomes the light (soft shadows from the frame bars; the light's colour with the glass texture's variation), and its point light goes out where the glass's light replaces it (the deferred lighting of opaque surfaces; forward / alpha surfaces, water, fog, probe captures and the RT reflection / GI hits keep the point light -- the emitters do not light those, so nothing is lit twice). Calibrated so a white surface facing the lamp at a third of the light's radius gets the same light as from the point light, falling off to the radius as the SL light does (physical closer than a ninth of it). Decided each frame on the GPU: a light whose glass cannot be listed whole (the RenderVKReSTIREmissiveTriangles cap), or that reaches past the light grid, keeps its point light. Emitting faces on OTHER prims of the linkset are not part of it. Counted in the 'ReSTIR DI' VKGpu line (light takeover: lights, taken over, refused). 0 = off (the emitters at their own strength beside the point light). Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): where an emissive surface's light ENDS -- the distance at which a white surface facing the whole surface would reflect less than this (linear radiance; its luminance x area / (pi d^2)), smoothly faded to 0 there (measured from each triangle). Smaller = longer reach (more triangles per grid cell, more cost); larger = tighter pools. Live.
Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): the longest reach (metres) of any emissive surface's light, whatever its brightness (0.5 .. 128). Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): emissive triangles kept per light-grid cell (1 .. 8). A cell reached by no more than this many keeps them all (exact, noise-free unshadowed light); with more, it keeps its strongest (all but a quarter of the slots) exactly and lights the rest with one stable aggregate per cell (the remaining slots only spread the shadow rays over the rest). Each pixel evaluates them all (a form factor + one texture read each): cost scales with it. Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1): the most emissive triangles lit per frame (256 .. 16384, the fixed buffer's size). While all emitting objects' triangles fit, every triangle is a light; past it, every object keeps every s-th triangle (the same s for all, a fixed offset per object: no frame-to-frame change) at s times its brightness -- about the same light, coarser. Cost: the per-frame build and the grid cells' candidate walk grow with it. Live.

Vulkan (#986, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1/2): an emitting object whose transform, material, texture average and geometry did not change since the last build keeps its triangle lights (copied, not rebuilt). Texture-animated faces and light-takeover faces are always rebuilt, and every object is rebuilt at least every 16 builds. 0 = rebuild every triangle every frame (A/B only). Live.

Vulkan (#986, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1/2): the grid cells find their emissive triangles through per-cell candidate lists (each triangle visits only the cells it reaches; up to 1M cell-triangle pairs, past that the old walk for that frame). 0 = every cell walks the triangles near its workgroup (the pre-#986 build, much slower with many emitters: A/B only). Live.

Vulkan (#986, with RenderVKReSTIREmissiveCellLists 1): a grid cell with more than 32 candidate emissive triangles (near a big emitter: often thousands) is built by a whole workgroup instead of one thread walking its list twice, which set the whole pass's time. Same result. 0 = one thread per cell (A/B only). Live.

Vulkan (#1009, with RenderVKClusterLOD on): a static object traced on its cluster LOD ray-tracing cut still lights the scene from its emissive faces (ReSTIR DI emissive lights) -- its triangles come from its legacy geometry at the level the cluster-off path would trace, so the light matches RenderVKClusterLOD off. 0 = such statics are left out of the emissive lights (the old behaviour; A/B only). Live.

Vulkan (#1009, diagnostic, with RenderVKReSTIREmissiveCellLists 1 and the GPU timers' ReSTIR DI log line): counts the objects whose material emits but which the emissive light build leaves out, by reason -- rigged (legacy / cluster cut), a cluster-traced static without a legacy row, a worn or own-avatar attachment, not in the ray-tracing scene this frame. Costs one coarse texture fetch per such object per build. Live.

Vulkan (#1006, with RenderVKReSTIREmissiveCellLists 1): the emissive light grid re-gathers only the cells whose emitting triangles changed (an emitter moved, appeared, vanished, changed its geometry or LOD); the others keep last frame's result with their triangle references carried to this frame's records. Colour and brightness changes (animated textures, glow, flicker) need no re-gather. A teleport, a settings change or the first frame rebuild everything. 0 = rebuild every cell every frame (the old behaviour, A/B). Live.

Vulkan (#1006, with RenderVKReSTIREmissiveIncremental 1): the most changed emissive grid cells re-gathered per frame, oldest change first; the rest wait (their light references stay valid, only a new candidate is missing meanwhile). Cells whose content cannot wait (a vanished triangle, a cell with a sampled far field, cells new to the grid) are always re-gathered at once. 0 = no cap. Live.

Vulkan (#1006, with RenderVKReSTIREmissiveIncremental 1): an emissive grid cell with more candidate triangles than slots (its far field sampled per frame, its aggregate colour following animated textures) is re-gathered every this many frames. 1 = every frame (the look of the full rebuild); higher values save time near large emitters but hold their far-field samples and colour between refreshes. Live.

Vulkan (#1006, with RenderVKReSTIREmissiveCellLists 1): an emitter whose power (its average emitted luminance x its area) is below this is listed in a 2x coarser overlay grid instead of the finest grid level (it lights only a metre or two; the finest cells cost the most to fill). The light itself is unchanged: its triangles are still evaluated exactly. 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan (#91, RenderVKReSTIREmissive 1 with RenderVKGI): GI rays that hit an emissive surface ReSTIR DI already samples drop its emission (DI carries that light, sharp and shadowed; GI keeps its reflected light), so it is not counted twice. An emitter past the caps keeps its emission in GI. 0 = GI keeps every emission (double light near emitters: A/B only). Live.

Vulkan (#439, point light shadows WITHOUT ray tracing): 1 = choose the most important point lights for cube shadow maps each frame (RenderVKPointShadowMapMax of them, brightness x apparent size, 512 / 256 / 128 px by size) and log the selection with its planned VRAM. The cube-map render path itself is not implemented yet, so the lights stay unshadowed; with ray tracing, point lights are shadowed by ReSTIR DI instead (RenderVKReSTIRDI + RenderVKReSTIRLights 1). 0 = off. Live.
Vulkan (#439, RenderVKPointShadowMaps 1): the most point lights given cube shadow maps per frame. Live.

Vulkan ray-traced global illumination (#87; needs ray tracing and the split deferred lighting): bounce light from every surface, sky and light, replacing the reflection probes' flat diffuse ambient where it has an estimate. 0 = off (probe ambient). 1 = one bounce: one ray per GI pixel, its hit lit by the sun, the local lights and the hit's own ambient (RenderVKGIHitAmbient). 2 = + temporal reuse (ReSTIR GI: each pixel keeps its best bounce sample from last frame, re-connected with the proper geometry term; much less noise). 3 = + spatial reuse (last frame's samples of neighbouring pixels on the same surface, each checked with one visibility ray: no light through walls). Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): the GI resolution relative to the render resolution: 0.5 (default, half), 0.25 (quarter: about a quarter of the trace and denoiser cost, softer GI) or 1 (full). Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): multiplier of the GI diffuse light (1 = physically matched to the probes' units). Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): a floor under the GI ambient, as a fraction of the old probe ambient (0 = none: a sealed room without lights goes dark, as the GI says; 0.1 keeps a navigable minimum). Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): the longest GI ray (m); past it the sky / environment stands. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): a GI ray hit's own indirect light. 0 = none (strictly one bounce: interiors darker, no sky leak), 1 = the reflection probes there (the probe capture's sky can leak into sealed rooms), 2 = the GI radiance cache there, else the probes (default: multi-bounce; RenderVKGICache 1), 3 = the radiance cache, else nothing (multi-bounce without probe leaks). The ray-traced reflections' hits follow the same rule on GI frames (RenderVKRTReflectionsHitOcclusion). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): the brightest single GI sample (luminance) before it is scaled down -- tames rare bright hits (a lamp seen through a gap) that the denoiser cannot spread. With reuse (RenderVKGI 2 / 3) the reservoir keeps the scaled-down weight too, so a clamped sample is not handed on to the neighbours at full strength. 0 = no clamp. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3): the smallest angle cosine to the surface a GI sample may arrive at to be kept in the reuse reservoirs. A sample that skims the surface (grazing) gets a huge weight which a neighbouring pixel facing it head-on multiplies into a bright sparkle -- the single-pixel fireflies along edges and curved silhouettes. Below this cosine the sample is not used (it carries 0.25 % of the light at 0.05). 0 = the old behaviour. 0 .. 0.5. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3, RenderVKGILightChangeCut): how many times brighter a reused GI sample may become when it is re-shaded because a changed light reaches it. The reuse weight was chosen for the old (often dark) colour, so a sample whose light switches from dim to bright is multiplied by the ratio: the single-pixel sparkles along edges under club lights (cyan in RenderVKGIDebug 9). Brighter re-shades are scaled down to this gain; fresh samples catch up within the light-change history. 0 = no limit (the old behaviour). 0 .. 16. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3, RenderVKGILightChangeCut): how much a changed light must matter at a reused GI sample's point before that point is re-shaded. The changed lights' unshadowed light there (the larger of before and after the change, so a light that switches off or sweeps away counts too) against the sample's stored brightness: below this fraction the sample is kept as it was (no extra ray) and the GI denoiser keeps its full history there. A faint far light or a small light next to a bright one no longer re-shades everything in its radius. Higher = fewer re-shades (cheaper), small changes take longer to show in the bounce light; 0 = re-shade wherever a changed light reaches (the old behaviour). Debug: RenderVKGIDebug 8 (dim green = a re-shade skipped); the GI stats line (GPU timers on) counts the skipped re-shades per ray. 0 .. 4. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3, RenderVKGILightChangeCut): how far a light must move, as a fraction of its radius, before GI counts it as changed (its projector axis: this many radians of turn). Measured from where it was when GI last counted it, so slow drift still adds up, while a worn light swaying a few millimetres with an avatar's idle or dance animation does not re-shade the GI around it every frame. Never below RenderVKReSTIRMoveEps. ReSTIR DI's own moving-light rule is unchanged. 0 = RenderVKReSTIRMoveEps per change (the old behaviour, but against the last counted position). 0 .. 1. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): the GI denoiser's spatial boost for pixels whose history is shorter than this many frames -- what camera motion uncovers (zooming / panning: the outlines of hair strands, tails, limbs, the body). Such a pixel holds only a 1-few sample estimate; it is now blurred with its neighbours weighted by how settled they are (a settled neighbour counts up to 8x), with a wider brightness tolerance and the variance of a few-sample estimate, fading out as its history reaches this length. Without it the speckles along silhouettes after a zoom took about a second to fade. 0 = off (the old behaviour). 0 .. 7. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): when a pixel's position last frame does not land on the same surface (moving the camera across thin strands or a silhouette, where the GI's reduced-resolution samples shift by less than a texel), the best-matching texel next to it (depth, normal) supplies the history -- for both the reservoir reuse (RenderVKGI 2 / 3) and the GI denoiser -- instead of starting the pixel over. 1 (default) = on, 0 = off (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3): extra neighbour samples, within 3 texels, for a pixel that found no usable sample from last frame (camera motion uncovered it, or a thin strand). They let it start from several reused samples instead of one fresh ray (a speckle until its history builds up). Applies at RenderVKGI 2 too. Costs a few buffer reads on those pixels only; still one visibility ray. 0 = none (the old behaviour). 0 .. 8. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI, RenderVKGIScale below 1): the upsample of the reduced-resolution GI to full resolution also compares surface normals, not only depth -- a hair strand lying on the body no longer averages its GI with the body's -- and where none of the 4 nearest GI texels lies on the pixel's surface (a strand thinner than a GI texel) the best-matching texel nearby is used rather than one across the silhouette. 1 (default) = on, 0 = depth only (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): a GI ray whose first surface is the BACK of a single-sided face stops there and brings back no light (it started inside geometry or slipped into a seam). 1 (default): removes light leaking in at contact edges and corners -- SL builds' overlapping prims and hairline gaps, a moving avatar's surface a hair off its ray-traced copy -- the bright single-pixel sparkles along edges that DLSS Ray Reconstruction smears into crawling colour noise. 0 = the old behaviour (back faces are passed through, and RenderVKGICullBackFaces culls them in hardware). Debug: RenderVKGIDebug 9 (magenta = a ray stopped this way). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): point lights at the surfaces GI rays hit join the hit shadow-ray budget (RenderVKGIHitShadowRays: that many of the brightest lights at each hit get a shadow ray). 1 (default): a point light no longer lights hidden spots unshadowed -- under tables and boxes, inside crevices, behind walls -- which made bright GI samples (sparkles) at contact edges. 0 = point lights unshadowed at GI hits (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3): lights that moved (RenderVKGILightMoveRel) or whose colour / brightness / radius changed (RenderVKReSTIRFlickerEps) since GI last counted them as changed -- colour-cycling club lights, fires, moving lamps. A GI sample remembered from an earlier frame carries the colour its point had then; 1 (default) = when such a sample is the one a pixel reuses and such lights are significant at its point (RenderVKGIReshadeThreshold), the point is re-shaded with this frame's lights (one extra ray + hit shading, only on those pixels), so the reuse keeps converging but the colour is current; and the GI denoiser keeps at most RenderVKGILightChangeHistory frames of history where such lights carry the bounce light. Removes the crawling pink / green blotches under colour-changing club lights. 0 = the old behaviour. Debug: RenderVKGIDebug 8; the GI stats line (GPU timers on) counts re-shades and changed lights per frame. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGILightChangeCut 1): frames of GI denoiser history a pixel keeps where the bounce light comes from lights that changed since the last frame (scaled by their share; only where they are significant, RenderVKGIReshadeThreshold). Shorter = the bounce follows a colour change faster, more noise for the spatial filter. 0 = no cap (only the reuse rule). 1 .. 15. Live.

#1087 Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3, RenderVKGILightChangeCut 1): GI keeps treating a light as moved for RenderVKGILightChangeHold frames after it last moved (RenderVKGILightMoveRel), instead of only on the frames it is counted as moved (a moving lamp is counted only every few frames). Colour / brightness changes alone stay with RenderVKGILightChangeCut's re-shade. While it does: reused GI samples it is significant at keep at most RenderVKGILightMoveMCap frames of confidence, so this frame's fresh samples take over quickly instead of averaging light from the lamp's old position; the GI denoiser keeps its light-change history cap through the whole motion; and the radiance cache around the light's old and new position keeps a short mean (RenderVKGILightChangeCacheFrames). Removes the noise on objects and avatars near scripted / animated moving lights, worst at half GI resolution. Areas no changed light reaches are unaffected (no extra cost there). 0 = the old behaviour. The GI stats line (GPU timers on) counts the hot lights per frame. Live.

#1087 Vulkan GI (RenderVKGILightMoveFix 1): frames a light stays "moved" for GI after it was last counted as moved. Longer = smoother under lights that move in steps or slowly; shorter = full GI reuse returns sooner once a light stops. 0 = only the frame it is counted (close to the old behaviour). 0 .. 600. Live.

#1087 Vulkan GI (RenderVKGILightMoveFix 1): the confidence (in frames, like RenderVKGIMCap) a reused GI sample keeps where a recently moved light is significant at its point. Low = the bounce light follows a moving light within a few frames (the reuse still averages several samples); high = more stale light from the light's old position survives. 0 = no clamp (only the hold's denoiser and cache rules). 0 .. 64. Live.

#1087 Vulkan GI (RenderVKGILightMoveFix 1, RenderVKGICache 1): the longest mean, in frames, of a GI radiance-cache cell inside a recently moved light's radius (at its old or new position), instead of RenderVKGICacheFrames. The cache then follows a moving light (the bounce of the bounce, and the fill of newly revealed pixels) instead of averaging the light's path. Its samples are kept, never restarted. 0 = no change (RenderVKGICacheFrames everywhere). 0 .. 1024. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): spatial (a-trous) iterations of the GI denoiser, 1 .. 5. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): the GI denoiser's longest history (frames). Longer = smoother, slower to follow lighting changes. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): the GI denoiser's neighbourhood clamp width (sigmas) -- its anti-ghosting. Lower = faster response, more noise. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): GI ray hits take their local lights from the world-space light grid's samples (builds the grid while GI runs) instead of walking every light in range. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI): ray-traced projector shadow rays per GI hit (0 .. 4; the brightest projectors at the hit get one each, the rest are unshadowed there). Live.

Vulkan GI debug view (RenderVKGI on): 1 the denoised GI irradiance, 2 this frame's raw GI samples, 3 the GI denoiser's history length, 4 its variance, 5 the reservoirs (red = a fresh sample, green = reused from last frame, blue = from a neighbour; brightness = its confidence M), 6 the radiance cache at each pixel (green = a cached value, red = no cell, yellow = a cell without samples yet), 7 the sky visibility the specular occlusion uses (white = open sky, black = enclosed), 8 changed lights and clamps (red = the share of the pixel's bounce light from lights that changed since the last frame -- what shortens the GI history, RenderVKGILightChangeCut; green = the reused sample was re-shaded because such a light reaches it; blue = the firefly clamp scaled the pixel's sample down), 9 sparkle causes (pixels whose GI is over 4x their neighbourhood's: red = a fresh ray that hit nothing / sky, orange = a fresh ray skimming the surface, yellow = a fresh hit, green = reused from the last frame, blue = from a neighbour, cyan = re-shaded; magenta = a ray stopped at a back face, RenderVKGIBackFaceStop; other pixels dim grey). 0 = off. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2+): how many frames a reused GI sample may stand for (the M cap). Higher = less noise, slower to follow lights and moving objects. Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 3): neighbouring pixels whose last-frame GI samples each pixel also weighs (0 .. 6). Live.
Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 3): how far the spatial neighbours are taken from (GI pixels, 1 .. 64). Live.

Vulkan GI radiance cache (RenderVKGI on): a world-space grid of irradiance filled by the GI itself, read by the GI ray hits (RenderVKGIHitAmbient 2 / 3) for multiple bounces (default on). It stays valid while the camera moves; objects that move, appear or vanish invalidate the cells they touch. Fixed memory (RenderVKGICacheSlotsLog2). Live.
Vulkan GI radiance cache: the table's size as a power of two (12 .. 22; 18 = 262144 cells, 12 MB). Live (re-created on change).
Vulkan GI radiance cache: the cell edge near the camera (m); it doubles with each RenderVKGICacheLevelDistance step of distance. Live.
Vulkan GI radiance cache: the camera distance (m) after which the cells double in size (and again at each doubling of it). Live.
Vulkan GI radiance cache: the longest averaging window of a cell (frames). Live.
Vulkan GI radiance cache: a cell nobody wrote for this many frames is freed for others. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI on): occlude the probe / screen-space / legacy env specular reflections with what the GI rays saw, so an enclosed room does not reflect the sky. 0 = off (the probes' reflections everywhere), 1 = by the sky visibility (the fraction of GI rays that escaped; default), 2 = by the larger of that and the GI / probe ambient ratio (keeps more reflection in rooms lit by lamps). Forward (alpha) surfaces use the ratio from the GI radiance cache. Pixels the RT reflections trace keep their reflections. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI on): trace a GI ray for 1 pixel in N per frame (1, 2 = checkerboard, 4 = a 2 x 2 rotation); the others reuse their reservoirs (RenderVKGI 2 / 3) or keep their history. 2 / 4 roughly halve / quarter the trace cost (most of GI's cost) at some extra noise and lag. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI on): a GI ray that reaches its length (RenderVKGIRayLength) without a hit takes the reflection probes' far field along it -- what lies beyond, as the probes captured it -- instead of the raw sky. Lets the ray length shrink (cheaper misses) without far buildings and terrain turning into sky light. Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI on): the atmospheric haze's sky-coloured in-scatter on a lit surface is scaled by how much of the sky GI sees from it (twice its sky visibility, capped at 1: a wall under open sky sees half the sky and keeps all its haze), so a sealed room's walls take no sky-lit haze -- no teal or blue glow filling a closed room. The haze's dimming with distance is kept. 0 = the haze everywhere (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan (#87): with ray-traced GI, cel shading's ambient flatten reference (the sky ambient its flattened ambient and its rim light are pulled toward) is scaled by GI's sky visibility, so a cel-shaded avatar in a dark room gets no sky-lit rim glow. 0 = the old unoccluded sky reference, for A/B.

Vulkan (#87): pixels the ray-traced reflections handle no longer skip the GI specular occlusion; it scales the probe reflection their RT splice left in place (rays that missed, no ray on the pixel's plane at thin silhouettes, the fades), and candidates the RT pass did not take are occluded fully. 0 = the old rule (RT-roughness pixels keep their whole specular), for A/B.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI on): GI rays cull single-sided back faces in the ray-tracing hardware (the same faces the shader skipped by re-tracing past them; cheaper traversal). 0 = the shader's rule only. Live.

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (the split generic shadow core's sun and light-sample kernels, RenderVKShadowSplitKernels): alpha-tested and translucent casters are sampled at an ISOTROPIC texture level -- the receiver pixel's footprint as a constant ray width over the caster triangle's texel density -- instead of projecting the anisotropic footprint onto every caster (fewer registers in the shadow walks, faster). Cut-out shadows may differ slightly at grazing angles. 0 = the anisotropic footprint (the fused kernels always use it). Live.

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (the generic shadow core: the merged sun / moon and the stochastic light samples): each shadow ray first asks the ray-tracing hardware for an OPAQUE caster alone (no alpha tests, no translucency); only a ray that finds none walks the alpha-tested / translucent / foliage layers, over that geometry only. Same visibility (an opaque caster blocks whatever lies in front of it); the penumbra size estimate behind an opaque caster no longer counts translucent layers in front of it. 0 = the full walk for every ray (default: in an open sunlit scene most rays come back clear and pay for two traversals; measured ~0.2 ms slower on an RTX 5090). Live.

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (the generic shadow core: RenderVKShadowGenericCore, ReSTIR DI, the split lights): run the stochastic shadow pass as separate kernels -- one choosing each texel's light samples (candidates, reservoir reuse; a 64 B descriptor per denoiser texel of VRAM), one tracing the sun / moon, one tracing the light samples, a thread each (8 B per sample slot and denoiser texel for the job list and the visibilities: 64 B at the default settings), one combining the lights' terms with those visibilities -- so the shadow walks run in kernels that hold only their samples' working set (fewer registers, more warps hiding the traversal's latency). Same image. 0 = the single fused kernel (also the fallback while the buffers cannot be allocated). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI on): run the GI trace as separate stages -- the rays' traversal, the hit shading, the reservoir reuse, the re-shades -- that hand each other compact per-texel records (96 B per GI texel of VRAM), so each kernel holds only its own working set (fewer registers, more warps hiding the traversal's latency, less instruction-cache thrashing). Same image. 0 = the single fused GI kernel (also the fallback while the records cannot be allocated). Live.

Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI and RenderVKGISplitKernels on): split the GI hit shading further -- the traversal stage sorts its rays into a hit list and a miss list, a small kernel shades the misses (sky + probes), and the hits run as a material kernel (surface, textures, weather) handing a 64 B record to a lighting kernel (sun ray, local lights, cache / probes). Each kernel runs only over its own rays and holds only its own working set. No extra VRAM (the lists and records live in the split stages' buffer). Same image up to the record's rounding (normals 2 x 16-bit octahedral, colours fp16). 0 = the single shading stage. GPU timers: c_gi_miss, c_gi_hitmat, c_gi_hitlight (1) vs c_gi_shade (0). Live.

#1038 Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3, temporal anti-aliasing / upscaling on so motion vectors exist): the GI's reused samples from the last frame follow each surface's own motion (the motion vectors), not only the camera's. A walking or dancing avatar used to look up the last frame at the spot where its body was NOT (the background behind it), so its pixels lost all their reused samples and fell back to one fresh ray each for as long as it moved -- the grain on moving avatars, and the slow settle after one walks out from behind something. Static scenery is unaffected. Costs one motion-vector read per GI pixel. 0 = the camera-only lookup (the old behaviour). Live.
