#1038 Vulkan GI (RenderVKGI 2 / 3 with RenderVKGICache): a GI pixel that has nothing to reuse from the last frame (just uncovered -- an avatar stepping out from behind a wall, a camera pan -- or a history reset) blends in the GI radiance cache's value at its position as up to this many extra samples, instead of showing a single noisy ray. The cache entry is the average of many pixels over many frames, so the newly visible area starts close to its final brightness and settles in a few frames without the noise burst. Pixels with reused samples (the steady state) are unaffected; the cache itself still receives the raw estimate. 0 = off (the old behaviour). 0 .. 16. Live.

#1038 Vulkan denoisers (the GI denoiser with RenderVKGIDisoccFix above 0, the local-light shadow denoiser with RenderVKDenoiseDisoccFix above 0): extra help for pixels whose history was just lost when a WHOLE surface appears at once -- an avatar walking out from behind a wall, whose body has no settled neighbours to borrow from. Such a pixel starts from the average of its same-surface 3x3 neighbourhood instead of its own single sample, and while young its blur accepts more of a curved / normal-mapped body (relaxed normal test) and reaches further (wider steps). Pixels with an established history are filtered exactly as before. 0 = off (the old behaviour). Live.

#1038 Vulkan denoisers (GI, local-light shadows): when a surface moved on its own since the last frame (a walking or running avatar, a moving object), its history is accepted even if its distance to the camera changed by up to about as much as it moved sideways (at most 25 % of the distance; the surface-direction test still applies). The depth check assumed only the camera moves, so an avatar moving toward or away from the camera lost its history every frame and stayed grainy. Static surfaces are unaffected. 0 = off (the old behaviour). Live.

#1038 Vulkan local-light shadow denoiser (ray-traced projectors / ReSTIR DI): the spatial boost for pixels whose history is shorter than this many frames -- what an avatar walking out from behind a wall or a camera pan uncovers. Such a pixel holds only a 1-few ray estimate; it is blurred with its neighbours weighted by how settled they are, with a wider brightness tolerance, fading out as its history reaches this length (the GI denoiser's RenderVKGIDisoccFix, for the local-light shadows). Pixels with an established history: unchanged. 0 = off (the old behaviour). 0 .. 7. Live.

#1038 Vulkan ReSTIR DI (RenderVKReSTIRDI 2+, motion vectors on): the light choices reused from the last frame follow each surface's own motion (the motion vectors), not only the camera's, so a moving avatar keeps its reused light samples instead of starting over every frame (less grain in local-light shadows on moving avatars). Static scenery is unaffected. 0 = the camera-only lookup (the old behaviour). Live.

Vulkan ray tracing: the visibility queue (#1039), a bit mask. 1 = the RT hit shading's sun rays (GI with RenderVKGIShadeSplit, RT reflections with RenderVKRTReflectionsShadeSplit) leave the lighting kernels: the material kernel writes each hit's sun ray as a request, one lean walk kernel traces them all, the lighting kernel reads the results (it holds no sun walk any more: fewer registers). 2 = every hit ray leaves them (overrides 1): + the RT reflection hits' occlusion ray and the hit shadow-ray budget's projector / point-light rays (the material kernel walks the local lights unshadowed and queues the budget's rays), + the RT reflections' blend layers in a kernel of their own -- the lighting kernels hold no ray query at all. 4 = the GI reuse's visibility rays (with RenderVKGISplitKernels; combines with 1 or 2): the REUSE kernel queues each reused pick's visibility ray instead of tracing it, the walk kernel traces them, and a lean VIS TAIL kernel finishes those texels from the picks REUSE stored and the results (the queue holds every GI texel or the frame uses the old REUSE). 8 = the stochastic shadow pass's light-sample visibility (with RenderVKShadowSplitKernels; combines with the others): the sun / moon and the local-light samples are prepared by one kernel (receiver, sample, terminator / rig probes) and written as requests, a lean walk kernel per light kind traces each sample's rays and stores its visibility for the combining kernel (the sun: every denoiser texel or the old kernel that frame; the light samples: up to 2 per texel, the rest by the old kernel). 16 = one frame-level walk (with any of the above): the lighting chain records every queued consumer's request kernels first (the shadow pass, the RT reflections, the GI), then all their walks back to back between two barriers, then their resolves -- fewer barriers, and the walks of different consumers overlap. Same image (the walk runs the same functions on the same rays; the shadow pass's requests round a few inputs: see clean_vis_queue.glsl). Higher bits are reserved for the later steps. 0 = the rays inside the lighting kernels. GPU timers: c_gi_walk / c_defer_rtrefl_walk (+ c_defer_rtrefl_layers with 2); c_gi_hitmat / c_defer_rtrefl_mat then include the requests (with 2 the requests and the local-light walk are their own kernel: c_gi_hitreq / c_defer_rtrefl_req), c_gi_hitlight / c_defer_rtrefl_light the resolve; with 4 c_gi_reuse_walk and c_gi_vistail (the VIS TAIL that finishes the queued texels); with 8 c_defer_shadowsungen / c_defer_shadowvisgen (the requests) and c_defer_shadowsunwalk / c_defer_shadowviswalk / c_defer_shadowvistail in place of c_defer_shadowsun / c_defer_shadowvis (c_defer_pstoch* without merged shadows); with 16 c_vq_begin (the queue headers), c_vq_prod (the last producer up to the walk wave), then the walks' own marks (overlapping completion points). Live.

Vulkan ray tracing (RenderVKVisQueue): the visibility queue's video memory cap in MB (per queued hit 64 B with RenderVKVisQueue 1; with 2, at one hit shadow ray, 224 B per RT reflection ray and 144 B per GI texel -- more per extra shadow ray; with 8, 64 B per denoiser texel for the sun and 48 B per queued light sample; the hits past it take the old path). 0 = by the GPU's video memory size: 896 MB above 24 GB, 192 MB above 12.5 GB, 64 MB above 8.5 GB, else 32 MB (allocated by demand). Live.

Vulkan stochastic RT projector shadows (RenderVKProjStochastic): the WALL-BLEED fix in the denoiser. A frame whose projector pick carried no light at a pixel (a black gobo texel) used to count as 'fully lit', so other projectors leaked through walls at the share of such picks. With this on it is a weight-0 sample: the pixel keeps its history (or takes its neighbours' estimate when it has none) and stays a full tap of every filter -- no extra noise around moving avatars; geometric edge-stops keep the filters from crossing walls. See RenderVKDenoiseDebug 1 (raw: magenta = no information this frame, dark blue = no RT projector), 2 (history length) and 4 (denoised). The turned-away gate is RenderVKProjStochFacingGate. 0 = the old behaviour (no-light picks count as lit). Live.

Vulkan stochastic RT projector shadows (RenderVKProjStochastic): a pixel whose visible surface faces away from a projector beyond normal-map slack is shadowed by its own surface, with no shadow ray (the ray's origin would be pushed through a single-plane wall and the back of the wall came out lit). The RT shadow mask's own rule; geometric, no noise. 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan merged RT shadows (RenderVKRTShadowMerge): trace ONE stochastic sun / moon disc ray per pixel per frame (as the projectors do) and let the denoiser integrate the soft edge, instead of RenderVKRTSunSamples rays with the adaptive early-out. Outdoor A/B only: halves the sun rays on lit / umbra pixels, more penumbra noise. 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan merged ray-traced shadows (RenderVKRTShadowMerge): the weak sun / moon threshold -- the active light's colour luminance x the sun scale. Below it no sun / moon shadow ray is traced (night, a dim moon cost nothing); from it to twice it the shadow fades in smoothly (never pops). 0 = always traced. Live.

Vulkan stochastic projector shadows (RenderVKProjStochastic 1): projectors sampled (one shadow ray each) per denoiser texel per frame, 1-2. A texel with no more candidates than this traces all of them exactly. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI stochastic light shadows (#869): visibility-aware light lists. A small world-space cache of surface patches (0.25 m near the camera, coarser with distance; the two sides of a wall are separate patches) learns which lights every shadow ray from a patch found blocked for 8 frames in a row; those lights are left out of the patch's light set entirely (no shadow ray, no share of the shared shadow ratio, no light) -- so many blocked club projectors behind a wall no longer darken the next room's own lights in sweeping bands. A few probe rays per patch keep re-testing them: one visible ray (a door opens, a light swings into view) re-admits the light the next frame. Every patch tracks the whole light set (a count per light), so a hundred blocked projectors are handled like one. Stats: the ReSTIR DI VKGpu line (RenderVKGpuTimers 1), "occlusion cull: ...". 6.25 MB fixed. 1 = the SOFT cull (#1052): only traced rays blocked by something farther than the patch size count (never a surface's own terminator / self-shadow), a light starts leaving after 12 such frames and fades out over 4 more, and the patch verdict is dithered (shadow pass) / blended (lighting) across neighbouring patches -- no hard-edged rectangles. 2 (default since 2026-10-25) = the first version's rules (8 frames, any zero sample counts, a hard verdict per patch box). The soft cull's neighbour blending let lit patches leak light into fully shadowed ones (bright rectangles inside a table's shadow), so the hard cull is the default until that is fixed. 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan ReSTIR DI (A/B for RenderVKReSTIROcclusionCull): how a POINT light the occlusion cull holds blocked at a patch is handled. Off (default) = it stays in the patch's shadow ratio with an exact zero visibility (no shadow ray, no noise) and the lighting gives it the ratio like any other light, so the ratio means the same light set inside and outside culled patches and the denoiser can blend them. On = the old rule: it is taken out of the ratio and the lighting entirely, so a culled patch's ratio is over a different light set than its neighbours' and its own history -- the denoiser's blend of the two drew the patches as dark / light rectangles. Projectors always use the old rule. Live.

Vulkan stochastic light shadows (RenderVKProjStochastic 1, #869): the strongest lights per denoiser texel (by their unshadowed light there, with hysteresis so near-equal lights never swap) that get their OWN shadow ray and their own denoised visibility every frame; every other light shares one visibility ratio estimated over the others only. Stops a projector behind a wall from painting its gobo through it with the visible lamps' ratio, and a blocked projector from darkening those lamps. 0 = one shared ratio for every light (the old path), 1-4. Cost: up to this many shadow rays more per lit texel, +64 B per denoiser texel (+80 B without the merged sun channel). Live.

Vulkan diffuse / specular lighting denoiser (#85 phase 2): its resolution relative to the render resolution, 0.5 (half, depth-aware upsample; default) or 1 (full). VRAM 112 B per denoiser pixel (~103 MB at 2560x1440 half, ~412 MB full); steps down to half when it does not fit. Live.
Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: a-trous spatial iterations (1-5; steps 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 texels). The specular takes fewer on smooth surfaces. Live.
Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: the longest diffuse history (frames, 1-63). Live.
Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: the longest specular history on rough surfaces (frames, 1-63). Live.
Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: the specular history of a mirror-smooth surface (frames; rises to RenderVKDenoiseSpecHistory with roughness). Live.
Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: neighbourhood clamp width (standard deviations of the current 3x3); smaller = less ghosting, more noise. Live.
Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: the a-trous luminance edge-stop in standard deviations of the signal (larger = smoother, softer light edges). Live.

Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser: relative change of a pixel's unshadowed light (a projector switched, dimmed, recoloured or moved) above which its history is cut (fully at twice this); 0 = off. Live.

Vulkan diffuse / specular denoiser debug view (RenderVKProjStochastic 1; replaces the lit image): 0 off, 1 raw projector visibility (one frame: the diffuse shadowed / unshadowed ratio, white = lit, no filtering), 2 history length (red diffuse, green specular, of their maximum; blue the specular a-trous depth / 7), 3 variance (red diffuse, green specular: standard deviation relative to the signal), 4 denoised diffuse visibility, 5 denoised specular visibility, 6 denoised diffuse visibility (left half) beside the lit image (right half), 7 the ReSTIR view (each texel's chosen light), 8 the split lights (RenderVKProjStochasticSplitK: one colour per light, several split lights in alternating diagonal bands; near-black = none), 9 the same colours x each split light's denoised visibility. With split lights on, 1 / 4 / 5 show the shared ratio of the OTHER lights. Live.

Vulkan soak-test switch (0 = off): while the projector denoiser's images are held (stochastic RT projector shadows with ray-traced projectors in view), flip its sun / moon channel every N seconds so the denoiser re-allocates on demand -- the Beta 5 Windows NVIDIA DEVICE_LOST trigger. With RenderVKResizeAtFrameStart on the re-allocation happens before the next frame's recording (the fix); off, mid-recording (the old path). Each flip is logged. Live.

Vulkan: re-create / free the projector denoiser's images, the split deferred lighting intermediates and the rigged-mesh buffers (pre-skin work lists, skinned vertices, palettes, the joint / skin-meta / skin-cache tables, the GPU animation tables and the rigged motion history) before the frame's command buffer begins (the frame that asks keeps its current images or buffers, lights with the uber kernel once, or skips the GPU animation once). Off = the old path that re-allocated them in the middle of the frame's recording (a DEVICE_LOST on Windows NVIDIA); for A/B tests only. Live.

Vulkan soak-test switch (0 = off): every N frames (at least 2) while rigged meshes are drawn, re-create the rigged palettes, pre-skin work list and skinned-vertex buffer at their current size -- the rigged re-size and descriptor-set re-point seen 1-3 frames before the Beta 4/5 DEVICE_LOSTs. With RenderVKResizeAtFrameStart on it happens before the frame's recording (the fix); off, inside it (the old path). Each forced re-size is logged ("rigged re-size STRESS", "rigged buffers re-sized ... [stress]"). Live.

Vulkan ray-traced shadows, shadow-terminator lift (RenderVKRTShadowTerminatorOffset, #664): where the receiver's triangle comes from. 1 (default) = the PRE-PASS TRIANGLE: a pass right after the depth pre-pass (same draws, depth EQUAL) evaluates the Hanika lift on the exact rasterized triangle (its three vertices via VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric) into an R32G32_UINT target (8 bytes per render pixel, resident only while RT shadows trace), read by the RT shadow mask and the inline lit pass -- no camera-ray probe, no wrong-surface picks in creases or at weld seams. 0 = the old camera-ray probe (A/B, kept for one release). Without fragment-shader barycentrics, for alpha-blend receivers and in mirror / probe views the probe always serves. Switchable live

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (sun / moon, ray-traced projectors, reflection-probe sun rays): shadow-terminator fix (Hanika 2021). Smooth-shaded low-poly meshes (garments, bodies, sculpts) are lit by their interpolated vertex normals but shadow rays leave the flat triangle, so near the terminator whole triangles self-shadow (faceted dark patches). On: within the near-grazing band the ray origin is lifted onto the surface the vertex normals describe (tangent planes of the triangle's three vertex normals, barycentric blend; flat-shaded geometry gets no lift), escape-checked so it never jumps a layer or a touching caster, and the facing gate / penumbra stretch use the smooth normal. One probe per pixel shared by the sun and every projector. Shadow mask, inline lit-FS traces and probe captures. Off = old behaviour (A/B). Switchable live

Vulkan sun / moon lighting: bump shadow-terminator term (Chiang, Li & Burley 2019, "Taming the Shadow Terminator"). Where a normal map tilts the shading normal toward the sun past the surface's interpolated normal, the light used to end in a hard cut at the shadow line (the sun shadow -- ray-traced or cascades -- follows the smooth surface, not the normal map). On: the sun term fades smoothly to zero over that band (G = min(1, Ng.L / (N.L Ng.N)), -G^3 + G^2 + G). No effect without a normal map. Complements RenderVKRTShadowTerminatorOffset, which fixes the low-poly facet terminator of the shadow rays. Switchable live

Vulkan ray-traced soft sun and projector shadows (sun: RenderVKRTShadowSoftness > 0; projectors: their RT softness): near the shadow terminator, soft-disc rays that would leave the receiver lower than the centre (hard) ray are lifted to min(N.L, this x disc radius) above its surface, so smooth-shaded low-poly meshes (avatars, sculpts) don't self-shadow in a stipple the hard ray never shows. In disc radii, 0..4; 0 = off (A/B). Receivers more than (1 + this) disc radii from grazing are unaffected

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (sun / moon, ray-traced projectors, probe-capture sun rays): grazing fade for smooth-shaded low-poly meshes (#664). Where the light skims the surface (smooth N.L near 0, e.g. a projector straight down a nearly vertical leg), shadow rays are decided by millimetre facet detail and print a sawtooth of spikes along the triangles. On: within the shadow-terminator band, the shadow is blended toward lit as the interpolated-normal N.L falls from w to 0, w = this x the triangle's vertex-normal deviation (sine, capped 0.25), so the light fades out smoothly by N.L. Fine meshes are barely affected. In steps of 0.5, 0..3.5; 0 = off. DEFAULT OFF and A/B only: the fade also lightens shadows cast by other objects in that thin band (bright lines on curved limbs), and the RT shadow denoiser already removes the grazing sawtooth. Needs RenderVKRTShadowTerminatorOffset. Switchable live

Vulkan: ray-traced shadow mask ray-skipping hint -- a texel whose accumulated history is uniformly lit / blocked stops after the first ray that agrees. Saves rays in settled areas, but at moving penumbra edges it can lock a stale 0 / 1 (blocky, lagging soft edges) and biases the denoiser's clamp. Off by default.

Vulkan (#771): ray-traced sun / moon shadow cache. A GPU tile classifier re-traces only the shadow-mask tiles whose sun shadow can have changed -- no reprojected history, shadow edges / penumbrae / tints, moving casters, receivers inside the sun-swept volume of a MOVING avatar / animesh / object or of an edited / rezzed object, the shadow range's fade band, the progressive refresh slice -- and the rest reuse their accumulated (fully lit / fully shadowed) history without tracing the sun. Projector shadows are always traced. Off (default for now: the measured win is small until per-tile carry / projector skip land): every mask texel is traced every frame. Log: VKRTCache.
Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): tile size of the classifier in shadow-mask texels, 8 or 16. Larger tiles classify cheaper but re-trace more around each reason.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): safety refresh -- every tile is re-traced at least once per this many frames (a hashed round-robin slice per frame), bounding what no signal reports (alpha textures or LODs streaming in) to that period. 1 = trace every tile every frame.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): the refresh period while the sun / moon drifts (time of day) below RenderVKRTShadowCacheSunJump per frame. Shadow edges are traced every frame anyway; this re-traces the uniform areas progressively.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): a sun / moon step larger than this (degrees per frame) re-traces every tile that frame. Smaller steps refresh progressively (RenderVKRTShadowCacheSunRefreshFrames).

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): a texel's accumulated sun visibility counts as uniform (reusable) when every channel is within this of fully lit or fully shadowed, over its whole 3x3 history neighbourhood (accumulated, pre-spatial). A reused texel's raw input is then exactly 1 or 0 -- what its rays return -- so the result converges as without the cache. Max 0.05.
Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): the shortest accumulated history (frames) a texel needs before it may be reused.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): STATIC CARRY -- while the camera is exactly still and no ray-traced projector exists, reused shadow-mask tiles skip ALL mask work (no receiver rebuild, no temporal / spatial filtering): last frame's per-texel results are carried over. Off: reused tiles still rebuild their receivers and run the filters.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): longest shadow (m) a moving caster's or changed object's box is swept along the sun; tiles whose receivers lie in that swept volume re-trace (the ground under it, minus RenderVKRTShadowCacheFloorMargin, ends it sooner).
Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): metres below the terrain under a caster that its shadow footprint still reaches (receivers in a dip / downhill).

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): a character whose pose is unchanged counts as a MOVING caster only when its root moved (translation + rotation x size) more than this many shadow-mask texels at its distance. Held / still characters never count.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): when more than this share of the mask is re-traced for 3 frames in a row, the classifier is skipped (the plain full trace, as without the cache) and probed again every 30 frames until the share drops 0.15 below. Above 1 = never.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): GPU side, per frame -- when more than this share of the mask's blocks is traced, the trace runs as one plain full dispatch in raster order instead of the block lists.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): GPU spinners (llTargetOmega). 0: the volume a spinner's shadow can reach (its sphere swept along the sun) is re-traced every frame -- correct for any shape. 1: only when its sphere moved since last frame; inside it, texels whose rays meet the spinner and the shadow-edge ring still re-trace, but a fast, asymmetric spinner (a windmill blade) can leave its new shadow positions untraced (missing / flickering blade shadows) until the refresh slice.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): a moving avatar's / animesh's caster box is LL's extents united with its position, padded RenderVKRTShadowCacheBoxPad (animesh: plus its root object's own radius). Off: the culling box (+-2 m around the position, 1 m + 25 % padding, animesh at least 4 m) -- a small fish then sweeps an 8 m cube along the sun. A slightly small box only delays a leading shadow edge by one frame (the rays' moving-caster bits re-trace it after).
Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCacheTightBoxes): padding (m) around a moving character's tight caster box.

Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): frames an edited / rezzed / deleted / re-registered object keeps the tiles whose sun corridor it touches re-tracing (its new geometry can reach the ray-tracing structure a few frames after the change).
Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): margin (m) added around a moving caster's / changed object's swept volume (plus the sun disc's penumbra spread) when testing a tile's receivers against it.
Vulkan (#771, RenderVKRTShadowCache): every ~5 s log the tiles traced / reused and why (VKRTCache), with the mask's GPU ms when RenderVKGpuTimers runs.

Vulkan (#212): translucent (alpha-blend) objects cast tinted, partial shadows: more opaque blocks more light, and coloured glass colours the light passing through it (stained glass). Texels LL's shadow pass makes solid (alpha 0.88 and up: leaves, fences, grilles) still cast full, sharp shadows as in Firestorm; only the lower-alpha parts tint. Off: LL's shadow-pass rule throughout (texture alpha under 0.598 casts nothing, under 0.88 a 50% shadow). Shadow maps keep a half-resolution colour layer per sun/moon cascade; ray-traced sun, moon and projector shadows tint along each ray. With Avatar shadows "Full" rigged alpha-blend mesh casts this way too.

Vulkan sun / moon shadows (#185): 1 shadow maps (cascades), 2 ray traced -- rays toward the sun / moon against the scene TLAS, pixel-exact with soft edges (RenderVKRTShadowSoftness, RenderVKRTSunSamples, RenderVKRTShadowBias). 2 needs the ray tracing foundation (RenderVKRayTracing + VK_KHR_ray_query) and falls back to shadow maps without it, over the RT memory budget, or on a frame without a valid TLAS. Shadows still need RenderShadowDetail >= 1. Switchable live

Vulkan ray-traced sun / moon shadows: past this camera distance (m) sun rays treat alpha-mask casters as solid (no per-leaf alpha test) -- cheaper, but leaf cards shadow as full rectangles. 0 = always alpha test (default)

Vulkan (#735): light through foliage in ray-traced sun / moon shadows and RT god rays (also probe captures). Shadow maps cull the back faces of single-sided casters, so leaf cards facing away from the sun cast nothing there, while shadow rays met both sides and made dense canopies solid. 0 = off (every leaf face occludes), 1 = cull: single-sided alpha-mask leaf faces turned away from the light pass it, as in the shadow map (free; opaque, double-sided, worn and rigged casters stay solid), 2 = tinted: as 1, plus one transmission ray per lit receiver that colours the light by the leaves it passes (RenderVKRTFoliageTransmissionStrength / Tint / Layers). Live 3 = auto (default): 2 when translucent shadows (RenderVKTranslucentShadows) are on, else 1; 0 / 1 / 2 force a mode.
Vulkan (#735, RenderVKRTFoliageTransmission 2): fraction of the light one leaf passes (0..1). Live

Vulkan (#735, RenderVKRTFoliageTransmission 2): how much of the leaf texture's hue the transmitted light takes (0 = grey, 1 = full hue; the brightness comes from the strength alone). Coloured only with RenderVKTranslucentShadows. Live
Vulkan (#735, RenderVKRTFoliageTransmission 2, debug): the transmission ray stops after colouring the light by this many leaves (1..8). Live
Vulkan (#735, debug / A/B): invert the leaf facing convention of RenderVKRTFoliageTransmission (the light-facing faces pass instead). Off in normal use. Live

Vulkan (projector shadows): whether a shadowed projector's AMBIANCE term takes the projector's shadow like its direct light. Ambiance is LL's fake bounce light: a soft, unshadowed fill in the light's colour, which builders use for mood lighting (even from projectors buried underground) but which also paints a soft copy of the image past walls. 0 = never (LL behaviour), 1 = always, 2 = auto (default): shadowed only while ray-traced GI runs (GI provides the real bounce light), LL behaviour otherwise. The direct light is always shadowed. Live.

Vulkan (ray-traced shadows; A/B): 1 (default) = a surface whose geometric face, on the side the camera sees, faces away from a light is shadowed by its own surface -- no shadow ray -- and every shadow ray leaves from the visible side. Applies to the sun / moon and ray-traced projectors in every RT path (shadow mask, stochastic projector sampler, inline forward shading, probe captures); the RT shadow mask also records a turned-away projector as shadowed instead of leaving it unshadowed. Fixes projector light from the next room leaking through single-plane / thin walls onto the wall's far side. Smooth-shaded terminators keep the terminator lift (RenderVKRTShadowTerminatorOffset). 0 = the old rule (the ray origin flipped to the light's side of the surface). Live

Vulkan (debug / A/B): ray-traced sun / moon shadows treat single-sided rigged meshes (bodies, worn rigged clothing, animesh) and worn attachments as the shadow map does -- faces whose front side faces away from the light do not occlude (inverted-hull outlines stop shadowing the face they wrap). Double-sided materials occlude from both sides. 0 = every avatar face occludes from both sides (the old behaviour). Live

Vulkan ray-traced sun / moon shadows on TRANSPARENT receivers (alpha-blend faces, traced inline in the alpha pass): within this camera distance (m) their opaque-only sun ray keeps the alpha test of alpha-mask casters; beyond it every opaque-class caster is solid (cheaper through stacked foliage). Without it an alpha-blend avatar overlay (blush, makeup layer) a few mm under a mostly cut-out alpha-mask layer (freckles, skin details, lashes, hair) was shadowed by that layer's whole triangles. 0 = never (all casters solid); 0..255. Live

Vulkan ray-traced shadows (sun, moon, projectors, RT probe faces): EXTRA shadow-ray origin offset in metres along the receiver's geometric normal, on top of the automatic one. The shaders already move every origin off its surface by the float error of its coordinates (a few ULPs, Wachter and Binder; ~0.1-0.25 mm inside a region) and of the depth reconstruction (~5e-7 x camera distance), so 0 (default) is correct for geometry that matches what is drawn. Raise only to hide a real geometry mismatch (self-shadowing speckle); a few millimetres already jump the stacked layers of mesh avatars and detach contact shadows.

Vulkan ray-traced projector shadow diagnostic (RenderVKProjectorShadows 2): 0 off; N focuses the N-th ranked traced projector and logs (VKRTFLICKER) record-assignment changes, TLAS membership near its apex (per-class counts, instances entering/leaving), and with RenderVKDebugView 15 its per-frame visibility + blocking instances
Depth of field focuses on whatever is under the mouse cursor (Black Dragon free focus).
Depth of field keeps its current focus point (Black Dragon locked focus).
Third person: the camera focus follows head motion and the camera tilts with head roll (Black Dragon cinematic head tracking).
Cinematic camera: how strongly head roll is damped back to level, 0..1 (1 = never roll).
Cinematic camera while sitting: roll damping, 0..1 (1 = never roll).
Third person: pin the camera focus to this skeleton joint number plus the preset focus offset (-1 = off). Black Dragon bone camera.

Vulkan ambient occlusion style: TRUE = standard (diffuse ambient multiplied by AO, as UE/Filament/Frostbite); FALSE = LL/Alchemy parity (softenLightF adjustIrradiance: blend towards RenderSSAOEffect * min(irradiance * RenderSSAOIrradianceScale, RenderSSAOIrradianceMax)).

Vulkan ambient occlusion, standard style only (RenderVKAOStandard): occluder bias as a slope of the sample distance (default 0.1 ~ 5.7 degrees; below ~0.1 terrain-patch seams self-occlude above the receiver's tangent plane) plus a depth epsilon, capped at LL's fixed 5 cm. Lets small creases (under the chin, inside a helmet, ears) occlude; LL's 5 cm bias rejects them at any radius or factor. 0 = LL's fixed 5 cm bias.

Vulkan ambient occlusion (SSAO: standard style only; GTAO: always): tests occluders against each triangle's real (depth-derived) surface, removing self-occlusion faceting on smooth low-poly meshes. Legacy capped path (RenderVKAODepthMips off): the facet normal IS the AO normal (steps at triangle edges once the radius is large, #648). Depth-MIP path: the smooth unperturbed vertex normal orients the AO and the facet plane only fades out taps that barely rise above the receiver's own triangle (slope RenderVKAOContactSlope), so it stays continuous across edges.
Vulkan ambient occlusion strength: exponent applied to the occlusion term (1 = as computed; 2 = partly occluded areas darker; fully lit and fully occluded unchanged). Range 0.1 to 8.

Vulkan ambient occlusion method (RenderDeferredSSAO on): 0 = SSAO (LL aoUtil port), 1 = GTAO (ground-truth AO, Jimenez 2016; RenderVKGTAO* settings), 2 = RTAO (#86: ray-traced AO on RT GPUs -- short cosine-weighted rays against the scene, sees off-screen and hidden occluders; RenderVKRTAO* settings; falls back to GTAO on any frame that cannot trace: no RT GPU, RT off, RT standing down for memory). Live; the AO kernel's GPU time is sub-mark g_ssao / g_gtao / g_rtao (RenderVKAOHalfRes: g_ssao_half / g_gtao_half / g_rtao_half) in the 'GPU sub ms/frame' log (the depth MIP build before it: g_ao_depthmip).

Ray-traced AO (#86, RenderVKAOMethod 2): occlusion radius in metres -- the rays' length. 0 (default) = the same as GTAO (RenderVKGTAORadius), for a like-for-like A/B; 0.5-2 m typical (longer finds more off-screen occluders, costs more on the GPU and darkens interiors more). Live.

Ray-traced AO (#86): the outer fraction of the radius over which an occluder's weight fades linearly to 0 (as GTAO's falloff; done by randomizing each ray's length, so it stays a cheap first-hit ray). 0 = a hard cut at the radius. Live.

Ray-traced AO (#86): rays per AO texel per frame (1-16; with RenderVKAOHalfRes one texel per 2 x 2 pixels). The AO temporal accumulator and blur integrate them over frames: 1 is the intended setting on any RT GPU, 2-4 converge faster after disocclusion at 2-4x the trace cost. Live; sub-mark g_rtao / g_rtao_half.

Ray-traced AO (#86): GTAO contact blend radius in metres. GTAO (at most 2 slices x 4 steps) computes the near field up to this distance -- screen-space detail such as creases and pixel-sized contact -- and the rays start there and cover the rest of the radius; the two visibilities multiply (no distance band counted twice). 0 = rays only (pure RTAO: also catches hidden occluders right at contact, noisier there). Live.

Ray-traced AO (#86): extra ray-origin offset along the surface's geometric normal, in metres, on top of the automatic float-precision offset. Raise only if flat surfaces show speckled self-occlusion. Live.
Ray-traced AO (#86): ray-origin offset for the depth reconstruction error at grazing views, in render pixels of footprint (as RenderVKRTShadowSlopeBias for the RT shadow mask). 0 = off. Live.
Ray-traced AO (#86): avatars (rigged meshes, animesh and worn attachments) occlude. A character's stale pose never occludes itself (throttled-animation rule of the RT shadows). Live.

Ray-traced AO (#86): texels whose AO rays met a MOVING caster this frame (avatars, attachments, moved or spinning prims) keep at most this many frames of AO history (RenderVKAOHistory), so contact occlusion follows a walking avatar instead of trailing it. 0 = off (the full history everywhere). Live.

Ray-traced AO (#86): the AO blur's tap spacing for RTAO, as a multiple of the GTAO / SSAO spacing (RenderShadowBlurSize). A few rays per texel are noisier than GTAO's slices; the wider, depth- and plane-aware blur covers new or disoccluded areas until the temporal history converges (converged texels use only the nearest taps). Live.

Vulkan alpha-mask coverage per mip (#648): the alpha used for the cutoff TEST is scaled by 1 + mip level x this (Golus' anti-aliased alpha test), so masked foliage / shell grass / fences keep their level-0 coverage at distance instead of thinning out where the lower mips average alpha below the cutoff (seen as a sharp AO / depth line at a fixed camera distance on dense shell grass). Applied identically in the depth pre-passes and the lit pass; blending keeps the real alpha. 0 = off (plain alpha test; GunMetal-DX default: RenderVKAlphaCoverageMips already keeps a cut-out's solid area in its mips, and both together over-cover -- far and grazing views drew trees and fences as pale blobs), 0.25 typical with the coverage mips off, max ~3.9. Live.

GTAO with RenderVKAODepthMips on (#648): also apply the facet self-occlusion test (RenderVKAOGeometricNormal). Off (default): GTAO integrates against the smooth vertex normal only -- the test was made for SSAO, GTAO shows no self-faceting without it, and on layered alpha content (shell grass) it faded real occluders into a lighter band at a fixed camera distance. The legacy capped path is unchanged. Live.
Vulkan AO denoise (the depth-aware separable blur after the AO kernel; #648 A/B). 0 = pass the raw AO through (noisy; for diagnosis). Live.

Vulkan AO blur plane tolerance in metres (#648): a tap is averaged only if it lies within this distance of the receiver's plane (+ a float-precision floor of 0.05% of depth and a 1-degree slope over the tap's in-plane distance), never looser than LL's. 0 = LL's tolerance, 0.7% of view depth, which merges layered alpha content (shell grass layers a few cm apart) past a fixed camera distance -- a sharp line with per-blade AO detail before it and smooth, lighter AO after. Live.

Vulkan AO depth MIP chain filter (#648, RenderVKAODepthMips on): 1 = plain mean of each 2x2 (coverage-weighted; distance-consistent on layered alpha content such as shell grass), 0 = XeGTAO depth-aware weights (drop nearer layers once their view-depth gap exceeds the falloff band, which banded shell grass at a fixed camera distance). Live.

Vulkan AO temporal accumulator (#843; both methods, full and half resolution). The AO kernel's noise varies every frame (GTAO: the Hilbert-curve R2 temporal index; SSAO: a re-hashed reflection tile) and a reprojected per-texel history integrates it over RenderVKAOHistory frames, with or without TAA / FSR: depth-tested disocclusion, a clamp to the raw 3x3 neighbourhood so moving occluders do not ghost, reset on camera cuts / teleports / region crossings. The blur then uses its short kernel on converged texels. Needs the motion-vector / previous-camera plumbing (kept alive for it without TAA / FSR). Sub-mark g_ao_temporal; 2 x 4 B per AO texel. Off = the per-frame AO + blur, as before. Live.

Vulkan AO temporal accumulator (#843, RenderVKAOTemporal): the longest history in frames (1..32). Longer = smoother, slower to follow an AO change the neighbourhood clamp does not catch. Texels at half this length or more (at least 4) get the short blur. Live.

Vulkan AO (#648, RenderVKAODepthMips on): taps blend between the two depth MIP levels around their fractional level (no jumps at log2 thresholds), the facet self-occlusion test is a ratio (no elevation threshold that turns into a distance band), and GTAO fades in over 1-2 px of projected radius. 0 = the previous behaviour, for A/B. Live.

Vulkan AO (#648): distance-invariant radius. Both methods read a linear view-depth MIP chain (XeGTAO-style prefilter, sub-mark g_ao_depthmip; R32F, ~5.3 B per render pixel, freed when off) at a level chosen by tap distance, so the world radius no longer shrinks close to the camera (no pixel cap: RenderSSAOMaxScale is ignored, RenderVKGTAOMaxPixels 0 = none); taps reconstruct at exact texel centres and the blur's plane test uses the depth-derived normal. Off = the legacy capped path, for A/B. Live.

Vulkan AO (#828): build the RenderVKAODepthMips view-depth chain with 64x64-pixel tiles per workgroup (SPD-style: 16x fewer workgroups, two barriers, gathered level-0 reads) instead of the #648 16x16 tiles. Identical chain contents; sub-mark g_ao_depthmip either way. Off = the #648 build, for A/B. Live.

Vulkan GTAO quality tier (#828; RenderVKAOMethod 1). 0 = full (RenderVKGTAOSlices / RenderVKGTAOSteps as set, the default). 1 = at most 2 slices x 4 steps. 2 = at most 1 slice x 4 steps with single-level depth taps (no RenderVKAOTapBlend): ~1/6 of the depth fetches, for slow GPUs; noisier, the image changes. Caps only: lower slice / step settings still apply. Live; kernel sub-mark g_gtao / g_gtao_half.

Vulkan GTAO slice / step noise (#843; RenderVKAOMethod 1). 0 (default) = interleaved gradient noise (Jimenez 2014): every 3 x 3 neighbourhood spans the range, no coarse repeat. 1 = XeGTAO's Hilbert-curve R2 sequence (A/B): its 64 x 64 tile can show as a grid of boxes. Live.

Vulkan GTAO per-frame noise (#843; RenderVKAOMethod 1). 1 (default) = the slice / step noise (RenderVKGTAONoise) advances every frame on the AO's own frame counter (XeGTAO temporal index) whenever something integrates it: the AO temporal accumulator (RenderVKAOTemporal, any AA mode) or the TAA / FSR resolve; with neither the spatial pattern stays static (it would only crawl). 0 = static pattern always (A/B). Live.
GTAO: slice directions per pixel (1 to 8). Cost scales linearly.
GTAO: horizon-search steps per side of each slice (1 to 32). Cost scales linearly.

GTAO: occlusion search radius in metres (world space, projected to pixels per depth). With RenderVKAODepthMips on it is the same at every camera distance; off (legacy), it is capped by RenderVKGTAOMaxPixels and shrinks close up.

GTAO: cap on the projected search radius, in pixels at native render scale; a capped close-up surface searches a proportionally smaller world radius (#648). 0 = automatic: no cap with RenderVKAODepthMips on (the depth MIP chain bounds the cost), the old 192 px on the legacy path. Any other value is an explicit safety cap on both paths.
GTAO: fraction of the radius over which an occluder's weight fades to zero at the radius edge (0.01 to 1; larger = softer edge, fewer halos).
GTAO: thin-occluder compensation (XeGTAO): extra weight on the view-depth offset in the falloff, so thin objects far in front of / behind a surface stop darkening it. 0 = off.
GTAO: multi-bounce approximation (Jimenez 2016) with this constant albedo (0 = off; 0.5 typical). Brightens occlusion the way interreflection would.

Vulkan ambient occlusion (both methods) at HALF resolution: the AO kernel and its blur run once per 2x2 pixel block (~1/4 of the cost; GPU sub-marks g_ssao_half / g_gtao_half) and the AO targets are a quarter of the size. Each block is represented by one real pixel -- on a checkerboard the closest depth of the block, else the farthest non-sky one -- whose exact depth and normals the AO is computed at; every lighting read upsamples it (RenderVKAOUpsample). 0 = full resolution. Live (a toggle re-creates the AO targets)

Vulkan half-resolution AO (RenderVKAOHalfRes) upsample in the lighting: 1 = depth-aware -- each pixel blends the 4 nearest AO texels bilinearly, weighted by how far it lies from each texel's surface plane (tolerance RenderVKAOBlurTol + 0.05 % of the view depth + a slope term) and by normal similarity, taking the closest-surface texel when none matches (no AO bleeding across silhouettes; + 2 B per render pixel for the per-texel plane), 0 = plain bilinear (cheapest; AO halos ~1 px wide at silhouettes). Live

Vulkan setting specialization (RenderVKSpecPipelines): after a graphics-setting change whose specialized pipelines are not ready, the previous configuration keeps rendering while they compile in the background; after this many seconds the new setting applies on the generic (run-time branch) pipelines until they land. 0 = apply at once on the generic pipelines. Live

Vulkan setting specialization (RenderVKSpecPipelines): the most compile threads one specialized-set build (a setting change, or the configuration at login) uses. 0 = automatic (the pipeline compile thread count, shared with every other compile). Prewarm builds always use one. Live

Vulkan setting specialization (RenderVKSpecPipelines): budget, in MB, for the specialized pipeline sets kept resident (least recently used configurations are released first; the current one never is) and, separately, for their per-configuration cache files on disk (vk_spec_*.bin next to vk_pipeline_cache.bin). Minimum 16. Live

Vulkan: compile the heavy lit shaders (forward / deferred lighting, water, particles) with the current graphics settings as specialization constants, so the paths those settings disable are removed from the shaders (fewer registers, less spilling). Off = the generic shaders, which test every setting at run time. Live

Vulkan setting specialization (RenderVKSpecPipelines; #818): 1 (default) = the current sky's lighting mode -- classic (a legacy sky without auto-adjust: LL's sRGB-space ambient / sunlight recombination) or linear -- is a specialization constant of the lit shaders (forward lit FS, deferred uber / split kernels, water, per-pixel particles), so only that mode's path is compiled and the driver allocates registers for it alone; the AO upsample mode (RenderVKAOHalfRes / RenderVKAOUpsample) is specialized alongside. A sky change (teleport, region / parcel / personal sky) switches to the generic pipelines at once until the other mode's set is built; that set is prewarmed in the background, so the switch is normally instant. 0 = both sky paths compiled, chosen per frame (A/B). Same image. Log: VKSpec key text 'sky classic / linear / runtime'; VKPipeStats register counts of the spec kernels show the saving. Live

Vulkan: at login, the progress screen stays up until the shaders needed to draw the world are compiled ("Compiling shaders (N / M)"; a cold driver cache after an update or driver change), at most this many seconds -- then the world shows anyway (logged). With a warm cache there is no wait. 0 = never wait.

Vulkan setting specialization (RenderVKSpecPipelines): while idle, compile ahead 0 nothing, 1 the configuration before the last setting change (flipping it back applies at once), 2 that plus the one-setting neighbours of the current configuration (shadow filter, screen-space reflections, mirrors, cel shading; at least 30 s apart), within RenderVKSpecCacheMB. Prewarm compiles on one low-priority thread and pauses while logging in, teleporting or while frames run slow. Live
Vulkan: with ambient occlusion on, also occlude environment reflections (specular IBL) from the AO term, NdotV and roughness (Lagarde 2014). Off = LL behaviour (AO darkens diffuse ambient only).

Vulkan debug: check every descriptor-set bind for single image descriptors whose view was destroyed or whose view handle now belongs to another image (a set not rewritten after a render target was re-created -- the snapshot DEVICE_LOST class). Each one is logged once as "STALE DESCRIPTOR bound" with the image's name and created / freed frame. Costs a hash lookup per bound image descriptor; on by itself while RenderVKDebugSnapshotStress runs. Not persisted.

Vulkan repro aid: every N frames render an offscreen snapshot (as the Snapshot floater / 360 snapshots do), cycling 700x381, the window size, 512x512 with HUD, a half-size depth snapshot and 1.25x the window -- the size round trips that re-create the shared screen targets. 0 = off. Not persisted.

Vulkan repro aid (texture freed while in use / DEVICE_LOST): every N texture passes run a texture pool compaction plan whatever the slack and hysteresis rules say (any block a packing frees, no headroom, no settle time), and move up to 64 MB / 384 images per pass -- exercises the move + retire path and VMA's block frees as often as possible. Watch the log for "retire guard" lines. 0 = off. Not persisted.

Vulkan repro aid (texture freed while in use / DEVICE_LOST): run the bindless texture eviction sweep every texture pass with a window of N passes (at least 12) instead of every 120 passes with the grace window -- textures of anything briefly out of view are released and re-uploaded constantly (expect texture pop-in). 0 = off. Not persisted.

Vulkan testing aid (#135): simulate a graphics device loss without touching the driver. 1 = the next queue submit, 2 = the next fence / semaphore wait, 3 = the next present reports VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST (the work is not submitted / presented). Runs the whole device-lost path: the report in the log and logs/slipstream_gpu_lost.txt, the message box, the logout and clean exit, and the next launch's notice. One-shot: resets to 0. Not persisted.

Vulkan testing aid (#672): the next N pipeline creations report VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY without calling the driver, exercising the recovery path: requeue with backoff, the compile concurrency cap halving (floor 1), retries, and -- when N exceeds the retries -- giving the pipeline up (its feature off, a one-time notice) instead of crashing. Read at Vulkan start-up (set it, then restart; delete vk_pipeline_cache.bin for a cold start): then only the background shader warm-up batch counts (the login screen UI stays real). Also read every frame: set in-world it counts every creation (batch, synchronous, UI, compute) -- e.g. before enabling depth of field. One-shot: resets to 0.

Region crossings (#607, #850): the shortest time a deferred kill of another avatar (or its attachments / animesh / vehicle) that is only probably crossing (near a region edge) waits for the new region before it is applied. With SLCrossingKeepAdaptiveGrace the wait grows with the handoff times actually observed, up to SLCrossingKeepGraceMaxSeconds. Avatars that log out or teleport away near an edge vanish this much later.

Region crossings (#850): the near-edge wait (SLCrossingKeepGraceSeconds) follows observed handoffs: 1.25 x the longest of the last 32 (within 10 minutes), measured as the time until the new region re-sent a waiting avatar, or re-created one whose wait ran out. Never below SLCrossingKeepGraceSeconds or above SLCrossingKeepGraceMaxSeconds. Off = fixed SLCrossingKeepGraceSeconds.
Region crossings (#850): the longest the adaptive near-edge wait (SLCrossingKeepAdaptiveGrace) can grow to. Avatars that log out or teleport away near an edge can vanish up to this much later.

Region crossings (#607): how long a deferred kill waits when the crossing is certain (our own attachments / vehicle, or an attachment whose avatar already moved to the new region). Attachments can arrive many seconds after their avatar.

Region crossings (#850): when the region we are in removes the vehicle we sit on while it is near an edge with a connected region across it (SLCrossingKeepEdgeMargin plus 1 s of its speed), wait up to SLCrossingKeepOwnVehicleEdgeSeconds for the crossing instead of unseating us at once: the vehicle is handed to the next region before its riders. CrossedRegion or the new region re-sending the vehicle ends the wait. Never applies to attachments or away from such an edge. Off = remove it at once, as before.

Region crossings (#850): how long SLCrossingKeepOwnVehicleEdge waits for the crossing before the vehicle is removed after all (kept short: a vehicle really removed or ejected near an edge disappears this much later). Max 10.
Region crossings (#607): another avatar killed by its region counts as crossing when it is within this many meters of an edge with a connected region across it (plus 1 s of its horizontal speed).

Clean-pipeline self-registration sweep budget: number of objects re-ingested per frame by selfRegisterSweep (registerCleanFace over their faces). MUST be well below the region object count so the sweep amortizes over frames instead of re-registering the whole world every frame (which pins the CPU and starves the GPU). Lower = faster frames, slower geometry self-heal/LOD catch-up; higher = quicker heal, more per-frame CPU. Clamped to >=16.

Night exposure (GMDXPhysicalNight): at night only (fading in as the sun sinks from half GMDXDuskSunLow to GMDXDuskSunLow; by day the exposure is the stock one), once the scene is darker than a quarter of RenderDynamicExposureCoefficient (where the stock auto exposure stops brightening), the eye gives back this fraction of every stop the scene loses, down to GMDXNightExposureKnee. 0.5 = a scene 4 stops darker shows 2 stops darker. 1 = nights shown as bright as dusk; 0 = the stock curve (nights darken stop for stop). Changes live.

Night exposure (GMDXPhysicalNight): stops below the night start where GMDXNightExposureAdapt gives way to GMDXNightExposureDeepAdapt. Around a moonlit night's level; darker than this is moonless or deep shadow at night.
Night exposure (GMDXPhysicalNight): the fraction of every stop given back past GMDXNightExposureKnee, so a moonless night stays dark but readable instead of black. Changes live.

Night exposure (GMDXPhysicalNight): the most the night curve brightens over the stock auto exposure's maximum, in stops (6 = 64x). Below that the screen darkens stop for stop again, so near-black stays black and noise is not amplified. The lift is also never more than physical night took from Second Life's moon (log2 of 1 / (GMDXMoonlightScale x 2 x moon brightness x phase): 4.3 stops for the default full moon), so a night that was dark in the old Second Life night stays dark. Changes live.

Night vision (GMDXPhysicalNight): strength of the Purkinje shift, the blue cast and loss of colour as the eye's rods take over in low light (Kirk and O'Brien's model as used in Ghost of Tsushima). Faded in by how dark the scene the eye has adapted to is (GMDXNightVisionLuminance), so moonlight tints a little and a moonless night a lot; it changes colour only, never brightness. 0 = off. Changes live.

Night vision (GMDXPhysicalNight): candelas per square metre for one renderer unit of scene brightness, which places the night in the eye's mesopic range (5 down to 0.005 cd/m^2, where the Purkinje shift fades in). Higher = night vision starts later and stays weaker; lower = it starts sooner. Changes live.
Night vision (GMDXPhysicalNight): low-light grain and loss of sharpness, scaled by how dark the scene is, as the eye sees in the dark. 0 = off (the default), 1 = strongest. Changes live.

#485 asset fetch: hard cap on keep-alive connections to the asset CDN host, summed over textures, mesh and large mesh (8 + 8 + 2 by default). TextureFetchConcurrency / Mesh2MaxConcurrentRequests stay the per-class targets and are scaled down together when they add up to more. Live.
#485 asset fetch: steady pacing of texture request starts (token bucket, at most ~100 ms worth at once). 0 = no pacing. About the peak rate measured against the CDN (~245 GETs/s). Live.
#485 asset fetch: steady pacing of mesh request starts (headers and LODs are small GETs). 0 = no pacing. Live.

#485 asset fetch: on 429 / 503 / gateway errors / timeouts, pause ALL new asset requests of that class for the server Retry-After (0.5-30 s) or an exponential delay from 0.5 s up to this. 0 = off. Live.

#485 asset fetch: texture requests handed to the HTTP layer at once (sent or about to be sent). Everything else waits, holding no data, in the priority queue where it can be re-ranked or dropped. Should be a few more than the texture connections. Live.
#485 asset fetch: mesh requests handed to the HTTP layer at once (same idea as SLFetchMaxInFlight). Live.
#485 mesh: retry-delayed mesh requests count against the dispatch budget for at most this many (they hold no HTTP slot), so a few requests walking their back-off can never stop fresh dispatch. Live.
#485 mesh: delayed requests beyond this many count against the dispatch budget in full (back-pressure for a wall of failing requests). Live.

#585 RAM: once the renderer has captured a mesh LOD, free LL's shared copy of its vertex / index / tangent / weight arrays (face counts, bounds and rigging tabs are kept). Off = keep LL's copy (new loads only; released LODs fill again on their next delivery). Live.
#485 mesh: cap on unsent mesh LOD / skin requests waiting on the main thread. Over it the lowest-scored are dropped and re-issued per object once the list is under 3/4 of the cap (minimum 256). Live.
#485 mesh: cap on remembered (gated / cap-dropped) mesh loads waiting to be re-issued; past it deferrals are refused and counted (the renderer re-requests on its own as a backstop). Live.

#485 mesh: do not request mesh LOD / skin for objects whose horizontal (X/Y) distance from the agent exceeds the network draw distance (AgentUpdate Far) plus their radius and SLMeshNetGateMargin; drop queued unsent ones and re-issue when back in range. Own attachments / HUDs exempt. Live.
#485 mesh: metres added to the network draw distance (plus the object radius) for the mesh request gate. Live.

#485 RAM: most texture fetch workers alive at once. A finished worker keeps its decoded image until its texture deletes it; over this, the oldest idle / finished workers are deleted first (in-progress ones are bounded by SLFetchMaxQueued and the in-flight / decode limits). Live/peak in the RAM log line (workers N (peak P cap C)). Min 1024. Live.
#485 RAM: seconds a texture fetch worker with no work (result taken by its texture, or dropped unsent) is kept before it is deleted (a texture that wants more data simply starts a new one). Live.
#485 RAM: seconds a finished texture fetch worker whose texture has not taken the result is kept before it is deleted with its decoded image (refetched from the disk cache if still wanted). Live.
#485 RAM: most texture fetch workers the 1 Hz worker sweep deletes per pass (oldest first), so a large backlog drains over a few seconds instead of in one frame. Min 64. Live.

#951: log the texture fetch pipeline (workers by state and why, the oldest per stage, HTTP slots, decode admission, J2C store index / reads / writes) every 10 s while fetches are in progress (60 s otherwise), and a "texture pipeline stalled" warning when nothing progresses for 30 s. Live.
#485 RAM: most MB of decoded / encoded image data held by idle and finished texture fetch workers; over it, the oldest go first whatever their age. Min 64. Live.

#485 network draw distance fetch gate: textures whose every world-object user is farther from the agent HORIZONTALLY (X/Y; height ignored) than the network draw distance (AgentUpdate Far, 192 m in fast flight) plus its radius and SLFetchNetDDGateMargin are not requested, and queued requests for them are withdrawn before sending. Own avatar / attachments / HUDs, bakes and UI textures are never gated; what is loaded stays. Live.
#485: metres added to the network draw distance (and each object's radius) for the texture fetch gate (SLFetchNetDDGate). Live.

#485 asset fetch: most texture requests waiting to be sent (each holds only a ~1.5 KB worker, no data); beyond it the lowest priority ones are dropped unsent and come back if still wanted, so keep it well above a busy view. 0 = no cap. Live.

#485 asset fetch: an unsent texture request is dropped once the renderer has not asked for that texture for this many seconds (it left the view, e.g. flying fast). Boosted textures (avatars, UI, sculpts) are exempt. 0 = off. Live.
#485 asset fetch: log a FetchGate stats line every few seconds while anything is queued or in flight.

DEBUG (Vulkan, #238): check every pipeline layout's push constants against this many bytes instead of the device's maxPushConstantsSize (128 = what AMD Polaris / RX 470-590 exposes, the Vulkan minimum). Violations are logged as ERROR at startup; layouts are still created on the real device. 0 = off. Takes effect after restart.

GPU breadcrumbs for crash diagnosis (NVIDIA diagnostic checkpoints / AMD buffer markers): when the graphics device is lost, the log names the last render passes the GPU reached. Small per-frame cost. Takes effect after restart.

GPU debug labels for crash and capture tools (#973): every GPU breadcrumb (one per render pass) is also recorded as a VK_EXT_debug_utils command-buffer label, and GPU objects carry their debug names, so Radeon GPU Detective, RenderDoc and similar tools name the pass the GPU was in. One label per pass (about a hundred per frame), recorded on the CPU only: no measurable cost. Takes effect after restart.

Ray tracing debug A/B (#973): rigged (avatar) BLAS are rebuilt from scratch every frame they change instead of refit. Tests whether refits produce a broken BVH on a driver (a GPU hang / device lost in the RT shadow pass). Costs GPU time on crowded sims. A rebuild that does not fit this frame's build scratch budget still refits. 0 = normal (refit).

Ray tracing debug A/B (#973): skip static BLAS compaction (the compacted-size queries and the compacting copies). Tests whether compaction copies corrupt a BLAS on a driver. Static BLAS then keep their full build size (more VRAM). 0 = normal (compact).

Ray tracing debug A/B (#973): KB of guard band after every BLAS allocated while this is non-zero (e.g. 64), filled with a pattern; every 30 frames up to 1024 bands are read back and checked, and an overwritten band is logged with the BLAS before it (the one that wrote past its end) and the one after it. The last checks are also reported when the graphics device is lost. Applies to newly created arena chunks only (set it before logging in, or wait for the RT idle release). Costs VRAM (band size x BLAS count). 0 = off.

Ray tracing crash diagnosis (#874): every frame the TLAS instance records just built are copied to host memory (about 80 bytes per scene instance), so when the graphics device is lost the report checks every BLAS reference, the slot-address tables and the fault address against the GPU address registry and names a bad reference. Small per-frame cost.

Debug, one shot (#874): run the ray tracing scene audit of the DEVICE_LOST report now, on a healthy device, and write it to the log (look for "RT scene audit"). Needs RenderVKRTLostAudit. Resets itself.

Ray tracing crash guard (#874 / #889): the ray-traced shadow mask checks every index it reads through the ray tracing tables (instance ids, rig groups, triangle and vertex indices, texture slots, light records) against the real bounds and skips an out-of-range read instead of letting the graphics card fault; the first offender of each frame is logged (look for "RT read guard") and included in the device-lost report. A couple of compares per hit. Turn off only to compare against the unguarded behaviour. Takes effect after restart.
Debug (#874): log every frame in which the ray tracing read guard (RenderVKRTGuard) skipped a read, with its per-site counts and first offender, instead of once per distinct offender.

Debug (#889): insert a full GPU memory barrier (all commands, all memory) before every ray tracing BLAS build or refit, before the TLAS build and before the ray-traced shadow mask. Slower; for testing whether a graphics device loss with ray-traced shadows is a synchronisation problem (no crash with it on = a missing barrier).

Video memory accounting (#407): when the driver offers VK_EXT_device_memory_report, it tells the viewer what it allocates for itself (pipelines, descriptor and command memory, queues), shown in the VRAM breakdown log line and bug reports. Diagnostic only, negligible cost. Takes effect after restart.

Vulkan (#695, needs restart): on an integrated GPU with a BIOS carve-out (AMD APUs), the most of the system RAM the VRAM budget may count on top of the carve-out, in percent of physical RAM (capped by the shared heap the driver reports; at most 90). The rest is left to the viewer's CPU side and the system memory governor's reserve for other programs. 0 = budget the carve-out alone (the old behaviour).

Video memory (#411): suballocate texture and UI images from shared memory blocks (Vulkan Memory Allocator pools) instead of one driver allocation each. The driver rounds every allocation up to its page size (64 KB on NVIDIA), which wasted about 1 GB on small textures in busy regions. Off = every image gets its own allocation (the old behaviour). Takes effect after restart.

Video memory (#411): block size in MB of the small-texture slab pools (images up to the driver's allocation granularity, 64 KB on NVIDIA). A block is only released when every texture in it is gone, so smaller blocks return memory sooner after unloads; larger blocks mean fewer driver allocations. Takes effect after restart.

Video memory (#614): texture pool compaction. Textures in the emptiest texture-pool blocks are copied on the GPU into free slots of fuller blocks so the sparse blocks are freed (unloads and mip-downs leave partly used blocks behind). Runs in the background (RenderVKTexCompactMBPerFrame) while the reclaimable slack exceeds RenderVKTexCompactMinSlackMB, and as the first answer to VRAM pressure (RenderVKTexCompactPressureMBPerFrame) before the VRAM ladder lowers anything visible.
Video memory (#614): background texture pool compaction budget, MB of textures moved per frame (at least one texture per frame while there is work).

Video memory (#614): background texture pool compaction runs only once the reclaimable pool slack (blocks a perfect packing would free, beyond one block of allocation headroom per pool) has stayed at least this many MB for 10 seconds; a block allocated into within the last 20 seconds is not moved. Projector / particle / water textures (pinned) are never moved.
Video memory (#614): texture pool compaction budget under VRAM pressure (the pre-step that runs before the VRAM ladder's first rung), MB of textures moved per frame.

Video memory (#614): the longest the VRAM ladder waits for the texture pool compaction pre-step, in seconds (1.5 s at most while usage is inside the reserve). A failed allocation that still does not fit never waits.

Video memory (#411): textures whose memory requirement is above the small classes and at most this many KB are suballocated from the medium (TLSF) pool; larger ones keep their own allocation. 0 or anything at or below the granularity disables the medium pool. Large values keep more memory stranded in partly used blocks after unloads (measured: 4096 KB with 64 MB blocks freed less VRAM than no pooling after a 50% unload). Default 2048 (2026-10-09: the 256K-2M band held ~640 dedicated textures / ~570 MB in a home sim). Takes effect after restart.
Video memory (#411): block size in MB of the medium texture pool (raised to at least twice RenderVKTexturePoolMediumMaxKB). Takes effect after restart.

Video memory (#587): size classes in KB for textures between the small slab classes and RenderVKTexturePoolMediumMaxKB. Each class gets its own pool of equal-size slots, so a freed slot is always reusable and no space is stranded between mixed sizes. An image goes to the smallest class within 12.5% of its size, otherwise to the medium (TLSF) fallback pool. Empty or "auto" = classes probed from the driver's memory requirements for power-of-two textures with mips (RGBA8 and BC formats); "default" = the built-in list measured on NVIDIA (90,177,352,698,1392,2780); "none" = fallback pool only (the old behaviour); or KB values separated by commas, which can be combined with "auto" or "default" (e.g. "auto,1500"). The VKMem "top sizes" log line marks each common size s (slab class), f (fallback) or d (dedicated), with KB rounded up, and suggests values for sizes the classes miss. Takes effect after restart.

VR (#1073, beta): start in VR through the active OpenXR runtime (e.g. SteamVR). Read once at startup (restart to apply); the command line option --vr and the login screen's Start in VR button turn it on for one launch. Off, the OpenXR loader is never loaded. No runtime or no headset: the viewer starts on the desktop with a notice.

VR (#1074): the per-eye render size as a multiple of the VR runtime's recommendation (1 = the runtime's size; 0.25 - 2, within the headset's maximum). Read when the VR session starts (restart to apply). VR only.

VR (#1075, layered stereo; experimental): render one image per eye -- each from its own located eye pose and FOV, as layers of one recording -- instead of M1's one mono image for both eyes. The eyes go out through one 2-layer array swapchain (or one per eye) with the depth layer where the runtime offers it. Read when the VR session starts (start the viewer with --set SlipstreamVRStereo 1). Effects not yet converted to layers are off in stereo (see the log line "stereo: ..."). VR only.
VR (#1074): the near clip plane in metres while the headset is the camera (0.01 - 0.5; the desktop camera keeps its own). VR only.

VR (#1074): your standing eye height in metres (0.5 - 2.5). At that real height your view is at the avatar's eyes; lower (crouching, sitting) moves the view down. Recenter VR View replaces it with your current height. Also the floor estimate when the VR runtime offers no floor-level reference space. VR only.

VR (#1074): smoothing time (seconds, half-life) of the avatar eye position the head-tracked view is attached to, against the animation's head bob (walking, idle). 0 = attached rigidly to the avatar's head. Does not smooth your own head tracking. VR only.

VR (#1076): protect against low frame rate -- when the headset misses frames, temporarily lower draw distance and other costly settings until the frame rate recovers (settings are not changed). Off by default for now (2026-10-27: it judged pacing against SteamVR's throttled rate and oscillated; #1137) -- a fixed VR baseline caps the draw distance at 256 m during a session instead. A safety preference (Preferences > Safety), kept across sessions. VR only.

VR (#1076): the right thumbstick turns smoothly (90 degrees a second) instead of in 30-degree snaps. Smooth turning is a common cause of motion sickness; snap turning is the default. A comfort preference (Preferences > Safety), kept across sessions. VR only.

VR (#1076) diagnostic, not saved: what the headset frame submits, to pin a UI wall that looks different in each eye / moves with the head. 0 = normal. 1 = the UI wall layers only (no world: if the wall is then steady and sharp, the wall layers are right and the world's projection layer is what disagrees with them). 2 = the wall as ONE flat quad (1.6 m wide, the whole UI image) at the wall's centre instead of the facets. 3 = the world declared as rendered (the M1 declaration: the whole mono image at the symmetric render FOV and the head orientation for both eyes) instead of each eye's own FOV and pose with its part of the image. Every placement logs the exact layer poses once (tag VR). VR only; live.

VR (#1122): extra gain in dB on world audio and voice while they play on the VR headset's own output during a VR session (headset DisplayPort / HDMI audio is usually quieter than desktop outputs). Clamped to -20..+12. Applied only during the session, removed when it ends. Above 0 dB the OpenAL output limiter is asked for so loud peaks are compressed instead of clipped.

VR dictation (#1118, right thumbstick press held while a text field on the UI wall has focus): the spoken language. "en" uses the English speech model; any other Whisper language code ("de", "fr", "ja", ...) or "auto" (detect) uses the multilingual model. The English model is chosen by CPU: "small.en" (264 MB, more accurate) on CPUs with 24 or more hardware threads, else "base.en" (82 MB); the multilingual model is 82 MB. Each is downloaded on first use, after asking.

VR dictation (#1118): your own names and terms, comma-separated (for example "Powy, Gemini, Noms"), that the speech model should spell correctly. They are passed to the speech model as a hint on this computer only, together with the names of avatars within chat range and the region / parcel name. Nothing is logged or sent anywhere.

#1122: the output device for all of the viewer's audio (world sounds and voice), by its name. Empty = the system default. A voice output device picked in the voice device settings still wins for voice; a VR session's headset output sits on top temporarily. A device that is not connected leaves audio on the system default until it is back.

#1122: the input device (microphone) for the viewer's audio (voice), by its name. Empty = the system default. A voice input device picked in the voice device settings still wins; a VR session's headset microphone sits on top temporarily.
